title: DIRECTOR, FIRST-YEAR ENGINEERING AND SENIOR DESIGN PROGRAMS #00098504
description:
Hiring Department

College of Engineering and Computing

Job Description

The College of Engineering and Computing (CEC) seeks a director to lead two high-visibility undergraduate initiatives that span the full arc of the engineering student experience: the college's required first-year introductory engineering course and a new interdisciplinary senior design program.

The Director will oversee the first-year introductory engineering course — a one-credit-hour course required for most first-year students in the college, enrolling nearly 1,000 students each fall semester. This includes coordinating instructional staff, ensuring consistent course delivery and assessment, and maintaining the course's role as students' foundational introduction to engineering.

The Director, in close partnership with academic departments across the college, will also build a new interdisciplinary senior design program and will launch and lead an annual senior design student expo that showcases student work and engages industry partners and other external stakeholders. This includes enhancing senior design and capstone activities college-wide through competitions, structured validation processes, business and market insight, and increased visibility for student work.

This position coordinates staff and faculty involvement across departments to ensure the success of these programs and serves as a contact for industry partners and external stakeholders who want to engage in these activities.

Key Responsibilities

First-Year Engineering Course

  • Oversee day-to-day administration of the first-year introductory engineering course, including staffing, scheduling, and section coordination for an enrollment of nearly 1,000 students each fall semester
  • Ensure consistency in course content, delivery, and assessment across sections and instructors
  • Recruit, train, and supervise instructional staff (faculty, instructors, and/or teaching assistants) supporting the course
  • Monitor course outcomes and use data to drive continuous improvement

Interdisciplinary Senior Design Program

  • Work with academic departments to review current senior design practices, outcomes, and accreditation requirements
  • Design and launch a new interdisciplinary senior design program in partnership with academic departments across the college
  • Establish shared standards, structures, and support systems for senior design and capstone experiences college-wide
  • Introduce competitions, structured validation processes (e.g., design reviews, testing/verification milestones), and business/market insight components to strengthen capstone outcomes
  • Work with departments to coordinate faculty and staff across discipline areas to ensure smooth execution of interdisciplinary design teams

Senior Design Expo & External Engagement

  • Plan and launch an annual senior design student expo showcasing capstone and senior design projects
  • Serve as the primary point of contact for industry partners, sponsors, and other external stakeholders involved in senior design and the expo
  • Cultivate and maintain relationships with industry to support project sponsorship, judging, mentorship, and recruitment opportunities
  • Increase the visibility of senior design work internally and externally through the expo and other channels

General

  • Coordinate closely with department chairs, faculty, and staff to align efforts
  • Report regularly to the Associate Dean for Undergraduate Education on program status, outcomes, and opportunities for improvement

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education and experience and at least 6 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessary

title: Scientist - Soil Health Assessment Center/Soil & Plant Testing Lab
description:
Hiring Department

Soil Health Assessment Center/ Soil & Plant Testing Lab

Job Description

The University of Missouri's Soil and Plant Testing Lab (SPTL) and Soil Health Assessment Center (SHAC) are seeking a Scientist to conduct applied soil fertility and soil health research and support the integration of research activities within SPTL and SHAC. This position will provide scientific leadership, oversee research and laboratory operations, and contribute to grant development and publications. Responsibilities include independently planning and executing field, greenhouse, and laboratory studies; developing and validating methods and standard operating procedures (SOPs); analyzing and interpreting data; maintaining quality assurance and quality control (QA/QC) standards; preparing publications, reports, Extension products, and presentations; and coordinating assigned phases of research projects.

The initial appointment will be a 60/40 split, 60% (3-day/week) at SHAC and 40% (2-day/week) at SPTL, but this may be adjusted as needed to support lab operations.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Designs and conducts replicated field, greenhouse, incubation, and laboratory research in soil fertility, nutrient management, soil testing, and soil health.
  • Analyzes, integrates, and interprets research and laboratory data using appropriate statistical, geospatial, and reproducible data-management methods; evaluates uncertainty and data quality.
  • Develops, validates, documents, and improves sampling and analytical methods, SOPs, instrument calibrations, and QA/QC processes for the SHAC, SPTIL, and research projects.
  • Prepares peer-reviewed manuscripts, technical and sponsor reports, Extension publications, figures, tables, abstracts, posters, presentations, and other scientific deliverables.
  • Coordinates assigned projects and major project phases, including work plans, field and laboratory schedules, collaborators, sample logistics, documentation, milestones, and problem resolution.
  • Assist with proposal development, outreach activities, Extension programs, field demonstrations, stakeholder communication, and collaborative research with faculty, agencies, and industry partners.
  • Train and mentor research staff, technicians, graduate students, undergraduate students, and temporary employees; coordinate project activities and schedules.
  • As with all positions, involvement with other duties and responsibilities may be expected in order to support the mission and purpose of the University of Missouri.

Shift

Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. (40 hours per week).

However, this position requires periodic travel to off-campus research and Extension locations, including occasional extended work hours and overnight travel during the field season, as needed to support time-sensitive research, laboratory, and Extension activities.

Minimum Qualifications

A Bachelor's degree in related/ relevant area and at least 3 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessary.

Preferred Qualifications

A bachelor's degree in soil science, agronomy, crop science, environmental science, chemistry, or a closely related field is required. A Ph.D. in a relevant field is strongly preferred because of the independent research, method-development, statistical analysis, and publication responsibilities.

Three years of progressively responsible experience in soil fertility, soil health, agronomic research, or soil/plant laboratory analysis is required. Experience must include experimental design, field/laboratory methods, statistical analysis, QA/QC, technical writing, and project coordination. Relevant graduate education may substitute for experience; doctoral research may satisfy the experience requirement.

A valid driver's license and ability to meet MU vehicle-use requirements are required for travel to research sites.

Certified Crop Adviser or a similar credential is preferred.

Salary Range: $53,976.00 - $70,000.00 per year

title: BTS Plasterer
description:
Hiring Department

Construction Services

Job Description

At the University of Missouri, Campus Facilities Operations is dedicated to creating a safe, efficient, and inspiring environment that fosters education, research, and service excellence. Our team manages campus facilities and infrastructure through services including Engineering, Custodial Operations, Maintenance, Construction, Inventory Management, Sustainability, and Project Management, ensuring seamless daily operations. Join us to make a meaningful impact on the university community and help shape the future of Mizzou with a commitment to quality and continuous improvement.

Nature and Level of Work
Perform skilled work on a journey level in the application of plaster to wall and ceiling surfaces, lath and other framework installation and dry wall finishing. All work is subject to spot-checking and inspection for conformance to specifications and accepted standards of the trade. Functional contacts include co-workers, other service department employees and other University staff and students.

Key Responsibilities
• Install lath and other framework; plaster wall and ceiling surfaces. Apply coats of plaster or other material to lath or other framework, add additional coats and topping and finishes to desired thickness.
• Perform plastering patchwork by removing old plaster, applying new plaster in amounts sufficient to fill in cracks and holes and finishes to match existing surface.
• Finish dry wall by applying appropriate materials to seams, indentions, corners and low areas. Tape seams, apply finishing coats and sand topping to desired finish.
• May occasionally perform general tasks such as the following: move and/or cover furniture and equipment for protection, carry supplies, set up scaffolding and ladders, tear out old walls, mix plaster (and other mixtures), and clean up job site on completion of work.
• May fabricate, repair and/or install decorative plaster pieces; may utilize spraying equipment in application of plastering materials.
• May perform or assist with preparation of cost estimates, material orders, reports and maintenance of records.
• Perform other duties as assigned.

Shift

7:30 am. – 3:30 p.m., Monday - Friday

Minimum Qualifications

• A high school diploma or an equivalent combination of education and experience from which comparable knowledge and abilities can be acquired is necessary; demonstrated skills may offset requirements.
• Experience sufficient to qualify as a journey level, with a minimum of four years of actual work in the trade, including apprenticeship or vocational training.
• Knowledge of and skill in the maintenance and use of tools, equipment and materials of the trade.
• Good physical health and coordination; sufficient strength to perform some heavy lifting and ability to work on ladders, scaffolding and staging.
• A valid driver’s license may be required for certain positions.
• Depending on the nature of work performed, the incumbent may be required to wear a respirator or self-contained breathing apparatus (SCBA) as outlined in the “Industrial Standard for Respirator Use”.

Preferred Qualifications

A valid State of Missouri Driver’s License must be held and maintained by incumbents in the position.

title: Counseling Health/Welfare/Wellness SR-RSVP Clinician
description:
Hiring Department

The MU Counseling Center - MU Student Health and Well-Being

Job Description

POSITION IS ALSO POSTED AS A PSYCHOLOGIST UNDER JOB ID #61306. ONLY ONE WILL BE HIRED.

The MU Counseling Center is part of the MU Student Health and Well-Being unit, which includes the Counseling Center, Student Health Center, and Wellness Resource Center. The Center is an APA-accredited doctoral internship site and serves the MU student community. The Relationship and Sexual Violence Prevention Program (RSVP) is a program embedded within Student Health and Well-Being. RSVP case management and clinical services are embedded within the Counseling Center, while outreach and prevention efforts are embedded within the Wellness Resource Center. The staff seek professionals to join a team who are engaged in efforts to enhance campus services to better support all students.

The successful candidate will promote the well-being of Mizzou students through the provision of high-quality case management and clinical services (including brief individual therapy, group therapy, and crisis counseling) for university students with a special focus on survivors of sexual assault, relationship violence, and stalking. These presenting concerns often overlap with various psychological, academic and interpersonal concerns. The RSVP clinician will work collaboratively with other mental health providers, medical staff, and outreach and health promotion staff in Student Health and Well-being. Competence and experience in the treatment of a wide variety of diagnoses and life problems in addition to relationship and sexual violence is required.

Job Duties Include:

  • Provide confidential case management, brief individual therapy, group counseling, and crisis intervention services to students, with a special focus on survivors of sexual assault, relationship violence, and stalking as part of the Relationship and Sexual Violence Prevention Program (RSVP).
    • Conduct RSVP Brief Screening assessments for students seeking RSVP related clinical services and connect to appropriate case management and on-going clinical services as needed.
    • Provide case management services depending on individual needs of the student, including but not limited to safety planning, assisting with referral needs, providing resources, and trauma-specific psychoeducation.
    • Provide brief therapy to students referred for on-going clinical services.
    • Perform crisis and consultation services during regular business hours that require complex clinical decision-making.
    • Maintain timely, accurate, and complete documentation of all service contacts as required by Center policies and procedures and state laws.
    • Develop and facilitate RSVP related group therapy.
  • Provide prevention and outreach services centered around relationship violence, sexual assault prevention, impacts of interpersonal violence, and other related topics.
    • Work closely with the RSVP Health Educator at the Wellness Resource Center (WRC) and other WRC Health Educators and staff to develop and provide prevention and outreach services on campus.
    • Foster relationships with key campus contacts for the purpose of developing and implementing programmatic interventions that result in student participation.
  • Coordinate with other campus offices that work with survivors – such as the Student Health Center, MU Police Department, Student Accountability and Support, Care Team, and Office of Institutional Equity (OIE).
  • Coordinate with community partners who also serve survivors in the larger Columbia area and make referrals and connections as needed.
  • Become familiar with the Clery Act (20 U.S.C. 1092(f)) and the Violence Against Women Act (VAWA) and related federal requirements for universities and colleges, including programming, service provision, and reporting.
  • May conduct supervision and training for post-doctoral residents, doctoral interns in our APA-accredited doctoral internship, post-MA fellows, and graduate students in training (as allowed by licensure status).
  • Contribute as a member of the MUCC team to the development and implementation of goals, philosophies, policies, and procedures that support the psychological needs of Mizzou students and cultivate a culture of well-being on campus. Serve on relevant MUCC and/or University committees as requested.

The successful candidate will possess strong interpersonal, oral, and written skills; value a multifaceted approach involving linked clinical and training efforts; demonstrate the ability to work collaboratively with colleagues, campus partners, and student groups; exhibit interpersonal flexibility with a sense of humor; understand the importance of life balance and have a strong commitment to the developmental perspective of counseling services.

Shift

Monday through Friday, 8:00am - 5:00pm

This position may require evening and weekend hours supporting activities and programs within the department. Occasionally division and campus projects may require additional hours outside of your normal schedule.

Minimum Qualifications

Master's degree in psychology, counseling, marriage and family therapy, or social work and relevant licensure (or eligible to be licensed within 12 months) within the State of Missouri.

Preferred Qualifications

Two or more years of post-degree experience working with sexual assault, relationship violence, and stalking. Must be fully licensed to practice independently as an LPC or LCSW in the state of Missouri and licensure must be maintained as a requirement for employment. Provisional Licensure is not accepted.

While candidates should not exclude themselves from consideration for a position, preference will be given to applicants who also have extensive experience providing case management and clinical services to survivors of relationship and sexual violence. Additionally, a minimum of one year of clinical experience working in a college counseling center (this may include practica, internship or post-MA fellowship experience) or with a college aged population is desired.

Anticipated Hiring Range

Salary Range: $70,000 - $115,000 per year
Global Grade: GGS 010
University Title: Senior Counselor Health/Welfare/Wellness

Internal applicants can determine their university title by accessing the Talent Profile tile in myHR.

title: Heart of MO RPDC Special Education Improvement Consultant
description:
Hiring Department

Heart of Missouri Regional Professional Development Center

College of Education and Human Development

Job Description

PURPOSE

The Special Education Improvement Consultant provides training, coaching, and technical assistance to Local Education Agencies (LEAs) to implement evidence-based practices that improve academic achievement and postsecondary outcomes for students with disabilities, with a focus on college and career readiness.

EXPECTED OUTCOMES

Support Missouri LEAs in improving outcomes for students with disabilities, including increased achievement in English Language Arts (ELA) and/or Math and improved postsecondary readiness and outcomes.

REQUIRED SKILLS

  • Systems change, implementation, and continuous improvement
  • Data analysis and data-based decision making
  • Adult learning and professional development
  • Coaching, consulting, facilitation, and presentation
  • Effective meeting management and collaboration
  • Conflict resolution and problem-solving
  • Leadership and mentoring
  • Technology-enhanced professional development
  • Development and delivery of high-quality professional development
  • Accurate, timely reporting and documentation

REQUIRED KNOWLEDGE/EXPERIENCE

Knowledge and/or experience in:

  • State and federal special education requirements, including Part B of IDEA, the Missouri State Plan for Special Education, SPP/APR, and SSIP
  • Missouri Learning Standards (MLS), Dynamic Learning Maps (DLM) Essential Elements, Missouri Model Curriculum, Missouri Assessment Program (MAP/MAP-A), and Missouri School Improvement Plan (MSIP)
  • Standards-based IEPs, specially designed instruction, co-teaching, accommodations, modifications, and effective teaching and learning practices
  • Response to Intervention (RTI), Multi-Tiered Systems of Support (MTSS), School-Wide Positive Behavior Supports (SW-PBS), and other evidence-based interventions
  • Implementation, scaling, and district continuous improvement practices
  • Data-based decision making and Early Warning Systems
  • Science of Reading/literacy
  • High-quality professional development for adult learners
  • Post-secondary transition planning and college/career readiness
  • Missouri Educator Standards and Quality Indicators
  • Cultural awareness, collective teacher efficacy, and interpersonal/intrapersonal skills

CORE RESPONSIBILITIES

The Special Education Improvement Consultant will:

  • Provide training, coaching, consultation, and technical assistance to LEA staff.
  • Support implementation of evidence-based instructional practices and programs that improve student achievement, graduation, dropout, and postsecondary outcomes.
  • Assist districts with college- and career-ready planning and effective transition from school to post-school activities.
  • Deliver high-quality professional development using DESE-approved materials.
  • Participate in district/school improvement planning and collaborative activities with RPDC and DESE staff.
  • Mentor new Improvement Consultants and assist with development or revision of training materials as requested by DESE.
  • Attend required DESE, RPDC, and professional development meetings, trainings, and conferences, including the annual Postsecondary Transition Training Institute (PTTI).
  • Participate in the development and implementation of the FY27 consultant credentialing process, including pilot activities and feedback, as requested by DESE.

REPORTING REQUIREMENTS

  • Complete monthly consultant logs and submit required data through the DESE-designated system by the 5th of each month for the preceding month.
  • Submit training attendance records to DESE by the 5th of each month for the preceding month.

TRAVEL

Regular travel is required in the consultant's assigned region (Mid-Missouri). There could also be travel in the neighboring RPDC regions for DESE-required activities, meetings, and conferences.

Shift

Monday-Friday, 8:00am to 5:00pm

12 month appointment. 40 hours per week.

Minimum Qualifications

A Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education and experience and at least 4 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessary.

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelors Degree in Education/Special Education

Three years of classroom experience, elementary/secondary content-specific teaching certificate are preferred.

Experience in special education instruction, intervention, and assessment practices.

MO Teaching Certification

Current MO Drivers License

Salary Range: $51,875 - $57,000 per year (Grant Funding)

title: Office Executive
description:
About The Role:

OCS are looking for an enthusiastic and capable individual to form a key part of the team. Office Executives play a critical role in ensuring the smooth, efficient, and professional operation of the office environment. Acting as a central point of contact for clients, visitors, and internal teams, they support day-to-day administrative, operational, and organisational functions while delivering a high standard of customer service and maintaining a safe and compliant workplace.

Working Hours
Monday-Friday , 6am-3pm

Key Responsibilities:

Front of House & Visitor Management

  • Provide a professional and welcoming front-of-house service to all visitors, clients, and stakeholders.
  • Maintain vigilance at the reception area by actively monitoring the front entrance for arrivals.
  • Greet visitors promptly, ensuring a positive first impression at all times.
  • Register visitors in the appropriate system and manage check-in and check-out processes.
  • Ensure all visitors and contractors complete required site inductions before access is granted.
  • Maintain a clean, organised, and clutter-free reception area that reflects a professional environment.

Security & Access Control

  • Create and issue access cards for new starters in a timely manner.
  • Deactivate access cards for leavers to maintain security compliance.
  • Manage visitor and contractor passes, ensuring proper authorisation and usage.
  • Conduct monthly audits of the access control system to ensure accuracy and compliance.
  • Perform daily CCTV checks to monitor security and report any irregularities.
  • Maintain key management systems including key safes and logs.
  • Monitor and ensure all Security Industry Authority (SIA) licences are valid, conducting monthly checks.

Communications & Customer Service

  • Act as a key communication point, managing incoming calls, emails, and Microsoft Teams messages.
  • Respond promptly and professionally to all communications, ensuring queries are addressed or escalated appropriately.
  • Share relevant information with team members to maintain effective internal communication.
  • Provide excellent customer service to both internal and external stakeholders.

Scheduling & Meeting Room Management

  • Manage shared calendars, ensuring accurate scheduling of meetings, subcontractor works, deliveries, and events.
  • Coordinate meeting room bookings, ensuring adequate time is allocated for setup and turnaround.
  • Prepare meeting rooms to required specifications, including equipment and materials such as flip charts, stationery, refreshments, and audio-visual setup.
  • Ensure meeting spaces are maintained to a high standard before and after use.

Administrative Support

  • Raise and manage purchase orders, including amendments where necessary.
  • Handle invoice queries in collaboration with finance teams and suppliers.
  • Raise, monitor, and close reactive and planned preventative maintenance (PPM) work orders within required timeframes to maintain 100% compliance.
  • Conduct monthly audits across service lines such as cleaning, waste management, and pest control.
  • Upload and maintain compliance documentation in line with company and client requirements.
  • Ensure all site files and records are kept accurate, up-to-date, and audit-ready.

Stock Control & Supplies Management

  • Perform regular stock checks on office and kitchen supplies including milk, tea, coffee, fruit, stationery, cleaning consumables, and hygiene products.
  • Liaise with cleaning teams and suppliers to ensure adequate stock levels are maintained.
  • Place and manage orders in line with operational requirements and budgets.

Building Inspections & Facilities Support

  • Conduct daily building inspections, including plant rooms and communal areas, identifying and reporting any issues.
  • Communicate relevant updates or concerns to the security team and other stakeholders.
  • Maintain a visible and proactive presence across the site to support client engagement.
  • Carry out routine tasks such as daily cleaning and maintenance of coffee machines.

Policies & Compliance

  • Maintain a thorough understanding of client and company policies and procedures, including:
    • Visitor management
    • Post handling
    • Clear desk policy
    • Workplace conduct (e.g., dogs in the office)
  • Ensure all daily activities are carried out in compliance with these policies.

Personal Specification:

Training & Development

  • Complete all mandatory training requirements, including:
  • Security Industry Authority (SIA) Licence
  • Emergency First Aid at Work
  • IOSH (Institution of Occupational Safety and Health

    Team Support & Cover

  • Provide flexible support to cover team absences due to sickness or annual leave. In addition, the role will require on occasion to work outside normal working hours when required to ensure service continuity

    Skills, Qualifications & Experience:

  • Participate in ongoing in-house training across a variety of operational and compliance topics.
  • Attend external training sessions where required.
  • Collaborate closely with team members to ensure seamless operational coverage.
  • Requirements & Skills
  • Essential Skills & Experience
  • Proven administrative or office support experience.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, Word, Outlook, and Teams.
  • Strong organisational and time management skills with the ability to prioritise tasks effectively.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
  • High attention to detail and accuracy.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
  • Professional and proactive approach with a strong customer service mindset.

MU Extension is an academic division consisting of approximately 1500 faculty and staff throughout the state within 22+ organizational departments throughout Cooperative Extension and Continuing Education. School of Humanities and Social Sciences

The Dean’s Office in the School of Humanities and Social Sciences (SHSS) at UMKC is seeking a Student Services Coordinator to join their team.

title: Senior Project Manager
description:
About The Role:

We are looking for an experienced Senior Project Manager to join our Frameworks Division, delivering refurbishment and building services projects across our national government frameworks.

You will manage multiple projects concurrently across the contract, with individual project values up to £5 million. Projects will include office refurbishments, fit-outs, HVAC upgrades, mechanical and electrical installations, and building fabric works within live operational buildings.

Experience delivering refurbishment and upgrade projects within existing, occupied buildings is essential. Candidates whose experience is solely in new-build construction will not meet this requirement.

Working closely with the Operations Manager, Regional Operations Director and Pre-Construction team, you will manage projects from initial client brief through design development, tendering, construction, commissioning and final handover.

Key responsibilities

  • Manage multiple projects concurrently, balancing programmes, budgets, resources and client priorities.

  • Develop client requirements into clear scopes of work, design briefs and contractor proposals.

  • Coordinate design development through the relevant RIBA stages alongside the Pre-Construction team.

  • Lead site surveys and design coordination meetings, identifying existing building constraints and operational requirements.

  • Plan phased refurbishment works around occupied buildings, managing access, service interruptions and business continuity.

  • Manage subcontract tender packages, procurement schedules and supply chain appointments.

  • Prepare and maintain project execution plans, risk registers and construction phase plans.

  • Develop, monitor and update construction programmes throughout the project lifecycle.

  • Lead direct employees, subcontractors and supply chain partners across mechanical, electrical and building fabric works.

  • Ensure teams have the necessary skills, training and resources to deliver safely and effectively.

  • Deliver projects on time, within budget and to the agreed quality standards.

  • Coordinate commissioning, snagging, certification and final handover.

  • Chair project progress and client meetings, recording decisions and tracking agreed actions.

  • Monitor project costs, forecasts and commercial performance.

  • Manage variations and contractual changes, ensuring they are recorded, assessed and reported promptly.

  • Identify efficiencies and opportunities to improve margins while maintaining service quality.

  • Work closely with Commercial, Procurement and Health & Safety teams.

  • Maintain appropriate health and safety controls, technical compliance and project records.

  • Build effective client relationships and apply lessons learned to improve future delivery.

Essential experience and skills

  • A minimum of five years’ relevant construction project delivery experience.

  • A mechanical, electrical or building fabric background, or experience across these disciplines.

  • Proven experience delivering refurbishment, fit-out or building services upgrade projects within existing buildings, with project values up to £5 million.

  • Experience managing multiple projects concurrently, including responsibility for budgets, programmes, resources and subcontractors.

  • Experience working in live or occupied environments and delivering phased works with minimal disruption.

  • Strong understanding of the RIBA design process and pre-construction activities.

  • Ability to develop and manage construction programmes throughout the project lifecycle.

  • Strong commercial awareness, including cost control, forecasting, procurement and change management.

  • Experience leading and developing direct and subcontracted teams.

  • Excellent communication, client relationship and stakeholder management skills.

  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Project, Excel, Word, Outlook, Teams and PowerPoint.

  • Understanding of health, safety and legislative requirements relevant to construction project delivery.

  • Willingness to travel between project sites across the UK.

Desirable experience

  • Experience delivering projects within government estates or national framework contracts.

  • Knowledge of NEC and other construction contract arrangements.

  • Experience delivering multidisciplinary projects combining M&E, HVAC, fit-out and building fabric works.

About you

You will be organised, proactive and focused on finding practical solutions. You will be comfortable managing competing priorities, making sound decisions under pressure and recognising when additional support or resources are needed.

You will bring a professional, collaborative approach, with a commitment to client satisfaction, safe delivery and the development of your team.

Applications are welcome from experienced Project Managers and Project Engineers ready to progress, provided they can demonstrate the required refurbishment and project delivery experience.

title: Field Specialist in 4-H Youth Development – Platte County
description:
Hiring Department

University of Missouri (MU) Office of Extension and Engagement

University of Missouri Extension 4-H Youth Development program

Job Description

MU TITLE: Assistant/Associate/Full Extension Professional

LOCATION: : Kansas City, Missouri, primarily serves Platte County along with Clay and Jackson counties in the Urban West Region, with additional service across the state as needed.

Specialist Emphasis

University of Missouri Extension 4-H youth development programs help children and teens become caring, capable, competent, and contributing through a series of progressive experiences over time with caring adults during non-school hours. 4-H youth development programs focus on the broader developmental needs of youth rather than preventing single issues or problems. 4-H youth development programs use a human ecological approach, recognizing that young people are part of systems, including family, school, community, and society.

Program specialization: The Field Specialist in 4-H Youth Development is responsible for planning, implementing, and evaluating positive youth and volunteer development programs.

This position is a 12-month, ranked, non-tenure track appointment at the rank of assistant, associate, or full Extension Professional. Rank will be determined at the time of appointment based on qualifications and experience in accordance with the MU Extension faculty standards. This position will hold the working title of Field Specialist in 4-H Youth Development.

As a Field Specialist, your workload distribution at appointment will be 90% Extension Teaching and 10% Traditional Service.

This appointment is renewable annually at the discretion of the University and workload distribution may change at the discretion of Extension leadership. Circumstances affecting continued employment include, but are not limited to, work performance, fund availability, and educational priorities.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Implement community-based 4-H PYD programs, in-school and after-school programs, short-term interest (SPIN) Clubs, and enrichment activities.
  • Use and recommend research-based curriculum and teaching methods.
  • Secure a culture of high-quality service for all the 4-H members and volunteers
  • Provide leadership to 4-H councils and committees
  • Recruit, develop, and train youth and adults to assist as leaders with implementing the 4-H program.
  • Conduct evaluations of the Missouri 4-H programs (evaluations provided).
  • Ensure that all the youth and adults in the county have the opportunity to participate in extension programs.
  • Apply for and administer local grants and other funding sources.
  • Provide supervision and development to program associate(s).
  • Other duties as assigned.

CORE DUTIES OF MU EXTENSION SPECIALISTS

MU Extension Specialists deliver the University of Missouri to all Missourians. They serve all Missourians by bringing research-based solutions to work on local problems. MU Extension Specialists teach new and foundational concepts, link people to resources, support partner organizations, participate in research, train volunteers, evaluate programs, foster innovation, and serve communities. MU Extension Specialists work as a team to expand educational attainment, foster economic development, and improve health outcomes. These core duties fall into three major areas:

Educate, Create, and Connect.

  • Educate. MU Extension specialists design, conduct, and evaluate educational programs. MU Extension specialists teach research-based information via meetings, in-person and online courses, continuing education classes, technical assistance, volunteer training, media, websites, consultation, and other educational methods. They provide educational programs that support Missouri's learners and clients' individual, organizational, and community goals.
  • Create. MU Extension specialists develop innovative and research-informed educational products, services, materials, and other scholarly works. These include curricula, publications, presentations, educational tools, websites, and similar resources. MU Extension specialists obtain and use extramural funding to support creative works. MU Extension specialists contribute to the scholarship of Extension and Engagement by evaluating programs that result in learning and behavior changes that impact individuals and communities.
  • Connect. MU Extension specialists engage with learners, stakeholders, volunteers, and communities, including county extension councils, government officials and agencies, partners, and University and professional organizations. MU Extension specialists listen and respond with care. MU Extension specialists intentionally foster engaged partnerships and robust connections to the vast array of programs offered by the University of Missouri System.

Professional Expectations

  • Engage with stakeholders in all counties to identify educational needs and then collaborate with appropriate internal and external partners to meet those needs.
  • Create an annual plan of work that reflects local needs and aligns with statewide program area efforts. Provide a monthly report to county extension councils, supervisors, county commissioners, and others regarding programmatic efforts. Attend at least one county extension council each month and provide an oral update on program efforts at that meeting.
  • Collaborate with campus-based specialists on research projects and then deliver findings from those efforts via demonstrations, field days, courses, workshops, consultations, publications, and appropriate media.
  • Effectively work with supervisors, other specialists, and local leaders to complete administrative tasks as needed.
  • Demonstrate competency in communication, educational programming, subject matter knowledge, educational delivery, volunteer management, grant acquisition, teamwork, interpersonal relations, organization knowledge, leadership, and professionalism.
  • Offer timely, research-based information during times of natural disasters or similar events.
  • Represent the University of Missouri on boards and committees as assigned.
  • Participate in professional development events to improve both technical and leadership skills.
  • Other duties and responsibilities as assigned to support the mission of MU Extension.

Additional Expectations

  • MU Extension Specialists regularly travel throughout Missouri and occasionally to out-of-state locations. MU Extension requires specialists to have a valid Missouri driver’s license, a legally operating vehicle, and wireless telephone/data service for University use. MU Extension specialists receive reimbursement for approved travel expenses, per University of Missouri policy.
  • MU Extension programs often occur outside of regular business hours. MU Extension Specialists should expect to attend these events as needed to meet the needs of learners, clients, and stakeholders.

MU EXTENSION LEADERSHIP RECEIVED

The Senior Program Director for 4-H Youth Development provides overall programmatic leadership. Programmatic supervision comes from the Assistant Director of Missouri 4-H (Education Director) for the Missouri 4-H and administrative oversight from the Regional Director.

MU EXTENSION INFORMATION

The University of Missouri (MU) Office of Extension and Engagement’s distinct land-grant mission is to improve lives, communities, and economies by producing relevant, reliable, and responsive educational strategies throughout Missouri. Our dedicated and knowledgeable specialists and staff collaborate with researchers and community leaders to develop and deliver programs that address the needs of Missourians, including educational attainment, economic development, and healthy people. For more information about MU Extension and Engagement, please visit .

UNIVERSITY INFORMATION

The University of Missouri, also known as Mizzou and MU, is the Flagship University of the four-campus University of Missouri System. It is one of the state’s land-grant universities. MU’s comprehensive undergraduate and graduate, professional, and research programs attract an annual enrollment of more than 30,000 students. MU Extension and Engagement programs are located on all four campuses and in 114 counties and St. Louis city.

Qualifications

An earned PhD or master’s degree at time of appointment.

Candidates will be evaluated on:

Hours of upper-level coursework in one or more of the following areas: child, adolescent, and adult human development; education, learning theory, and learning strategies; organizational systems and human resource management; community development/partnerships; and volunteerism.

title: Senior Applied Research Economist
description:
Hiring Department

Rural & Farm Finance Policy Analysis Center (RaFF) - Division of Applied Social Sciences

Job Description

This Senior Applied Research Economist position combines applied economic research with leadership of the Early Warning System of Farm Financial Stress (EWS). This role will advance RaFF's research and stakeholder engagement activities focused on farm financial conditions, agricultural lending, and financial stress in the farm sector.

The role develops analytical tools and models, conducts applied research on farm finance and agricultural credit markets, and leads EWS activities across participating states. Working with producers, lenders, policymakers, researchers, and Extension professionals, the position integrates economic analysis and stakeholder intelligence to identify emerging risks and deliver actionable insights that support decision-making across the agricultural finance sector.

Responsibilities

  • Lead the implementation and improvement of the Early Warning System of Farm Financial Stress (EWS).
  • Engage producers, lenders, Extension professionals, researchers, policymakers, and other stakeholders to monitor emerging financial risks and conditions.
  • Coordinate EWS stakeholder meetings, manage project activities, and oversee development of consensus reports and related outputs.
  • Synthesize stakeholder input, economic data, and analytical findings into reports, presentations, and decision-support materials.
  • Develop and enhance models used for farm income projections, agricultural lending analysis, farm financial stress assessment, and policy evaluation.
  • Conduct applied research on farm finance, agricultural credit markets, and related policy issues.
  • Contribute to Farm Income Outlook reports, Missouri Agricultural Outlook publications, and other RaFF products.
  • Present findings to policymakers, producers, lenders, industry groups, and professional audiences.
  • Lead collaborative projects and pursue external funding opportunities that support RaFF's mission.
  • Mentor graduate students, postdoctoral fellows, and research staff as appropriate.

Candidates will be evaluated on:

  • Knowledge of U.S. agricultural policy, commodity markets, farm finance, and agricultural lending.
  • Experience conducting applied economic analysis and developing decision-support tools.
  • Ability to integrate quantitative analysis with stakeholder input to assess emerging conditions and risks.
  • Experience leading collaborative projects and stakeholder engagement activities.
  • Quality and impact of applied research, policy analysis, reports, and presentations.
  • Strong written and oral communication skills for technical and non-technical audiences.

Shift

Monday - Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM

Minimum Qualifications

A Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience, and at least 5 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessary.

Preferred Qualifications

  • PhD in Agricultural Economics, Applied Economics, Economics, or a related field with 2+ years of post-PhD experience; OR Master's degree with 5+ years of relevant experience; OR Bachelor's degree with 10+ years of relevant experience.
  • Deep knowledge of agricultural markets, farm finance, agricultural credit systems, and agricultural policy.
  • Experience with applied economic modeling, econometrics, forecasting, or policy analysis.
  • Experience leading stakeholder engagement, consensus-building processes, or multi-state initiatives.
  • Proficiency with R, Excel, and other analytical software.

description:
Hiring Department

University of Missouri (MU) Office of Extension and Engagement

4-H Center for Youth Development - Mercer County

Job Description

MU TITLE: Educational Program Associate III

LOCATION: Mercer County - Princeton, MO

The University of Missouri (MU) Office of Extension and Engagement’s distinct land-grant mission is to improve lives, communities, and economies by producing relevant, reliable, and responsive educational strategies throughout Missouri. Our dedicated and knowledgeable faculty and staff collaborate with researchers and community leaders to develop and deliver programs that address the needs of Missourians including: educational attainment; environmental concerns; community, economic, business and workforce development; global food systems; and health systems. For more information about MU Extension and Engagement, please visit

The University of Missouri Extension 4-H Center for Youth Development provides leadership and expertise with developing communities of young people across Missouri who are learning citizenship, leadership, and life skills. 4-H is publicly supported by county, state, and federal partners, as well as private resources to enrich the learning experiences of both youth and adults. For more information about 4-H, visit

This position will assist in the planning, management, and support of 4-H Youth Development programs in assigned geographic area, under the guidance and supervision of the 4-H Youth Development Specialist/Educator.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES

  • Advocate for positive youth development in the community and MU Extension.
  • Work as a member of the leadership team to coordinate and/or conduct educational events, contests, camps, and programs utilizing a positive youth development approach.
  • Build and expand external local partnerships to grow the 4-H program in Mercer County, including but not limited to Schools, Community Centers, and other Youth serving organizations.
  • Build and expand internal partnerships to grow the 4-H program in Mercer County, including partnerships among other UM Colleges and Missouri Extension programs: Agriculture & Environment, Business and Community, Health and Human Science.
  • Lead the coordination and planning, management, marketing, implementing (including teaching) and evaluation (including reporting) of researched based curriculum that has an emphasis on Leadership and Civic Engagement, STEM, Healthy Living, Agriculture and Natural Resources, as well as other career exploration topics. Including curriculums offered face to face activities and online.
  • Build capacity amongst volunteers and community partners, fostering developmental relationships to contribute to program growth.
  • Engage and empower volunteers and community partners to effectively implement 4-H programs across all delivery modes.
  • Develop leadership capacity among youth.
  • Assist in the management of financial and in-kind resources.
  • Coordinate and/or conduct educational events, contests, camps, and programs utilizing a positive youth development approach.
  • Contribute to the statewide effort to impact the lives of all Missourians positively including promotion of state and national events and contests.
  • Report accomplishments and impacts to appropriate sources including supervisor, funders, and stakeholders.
  • Assist with record keeping and report preparation of 4-H Youth Development Programs.
  • Ensure that individuals in the county can participate in extension programs.
  • Participate in training and professional development opportunities for continued in knowledge, skills, and abilities as it is related to the 4-H Youth Development program.
  • Ability to travel and work flexible hours, including some evenings and weekends, is required to fulfill assigned responsibilities.
  • As with all positions, involvement with other duties and responsibilities may be expected in order to support the mission and purpose of MU Extension.

LEADERSHIP RECEIVED AND EXERCISED

Administrative supervision is received from the assigned Field Specialist/Educator in 4-H Youth Development. This position is not responsible for supervision.

CORE ATTRIBUTES FOR MU EXTENSION STAFF

  • Exhibit a high personal standard of excellence, be an effective team player, and demonstrate civility and respect for all.
  • Engage stakeholders and learners; maintain positive interpersonal relationships and exhibit effective written and oral communication skills.
  • Operate with minimal guidance and be a self-directed learner who is flexible and adaptable to changing environments.
  • Ensure all youth and adults in the county have an ability to participate in extension programs which offer a safe environment.

UNIVERSITY INFORMATION

The University of Missouri, also known as Mizzou and MU, is the Flagship University of the four-campus University of Missouri system. It is the state’s land-grant university and one of the most comprehensive universities in the United States. MU’s broad undergraduate programs and its’ graduate, professional and research programs attract annual enrollment of more than 30,000 students. MU is centrally located in Columbia, MO, which is consistently ranked as one of America’s most livable cities. MU Extension and Engagement programs are located on all four campuses and in 114 counties and St. Louis city.

Shift

Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m. - 1:00 p.m. (20 hours a week)

Ability to travel and to work flexible hours, including some evenings and weekends, is required to fulfill assigned responsibilities.

Minimum Qualifications

An associate degree or an equivalent combination of education and experience and at least 6 months of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessary.

Preferred Qualifications

A minimum of six hours in one or more of the domains of the 4-H Professional, Research, Knowledge and Competency Taxonomy (PRKC) for youth development. Domains are youth and adult development, learning strategies and education, organizational systems and resource management, community partnerships and volunteerism.

Experience in group work that involved direct care and interaction with children, such as YMCA, day care, schools, recreational facilities etc. may be substituted on a year-for-year basis for the stated education.

Individual must be self-motivated, be willing to take initiative and have the ability to work with minimum supervision.

ASSOCIATES WILL BE EVALUATED ON

  • A yearly Plan of Work based on locally identified needs.
  • Ability and willingness to learn and implement hands-on learning that has an emphasis on emphasis on Leadership and Civic Engagement, STEM, Healthy Living, Agriculture and Natural Resources, as well as other career exploration topics.

  • Ability to effectively use social media and information technology including a variety of Windows based computer software programs.
  • Ability to remain organized, accurate, and dependable with a positive attitude and willingness to work as part of a team.
  • Demonstration of strong communication skills when identifying and working with partners, youth, volunteers, and community members/organizations to provide a quality program.
  • Marketing, promotion, and evaluation of programs offered.
  • Use of creativity, problem solving and the ability to think on your feet.
  • Ability to understand, synthesize and communicate relevant information to various audiences.
  • Ability to recruit, develop and train youth and adults as volunteer leaders to assist with the implementation of the 4-H program.

Position Overview: We are seeking a dedicated and experienced Behavior Analyst to design, implement, and monitor behavioral intervention programs for children ages 18 months-21 years with autism spectrum disorders and other developmental disabilities using applied behavior analysis (ABA) methods. This primarily consists of clinic-based service delivery although there may be opportunities for community-based service delivery. The behavior analyst will provide treatments focused on skill building (e.g., intensive behavioral intervention program) and behavior reduction (e.g., severe behavior clinic).

  • Train and supervise staff in the application of ABA methods and techniques, ensuring best practices and quality care.
  • Maintain detailed records and documentation, including data collection, progress reports, and treatment modifications.

Reporting to the Associate Athletics Director for Development, this position is responsible for securing philanthropic support for Mizzou Athletics through the identification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship of major gift prospects. The Director of Development will manage a regional portfolio of alumni, donors, and prospective supporters while serving as a frontline fundraiser for the department.

The Director will build meaningful donor relationships, execute strategic fundraising plans, and consistently advance prospects toward significant philanthropic investments. In addition to fundraising responsibilities, this position will assist with premium seating initiatives and provide a high level of customer service and stewardship to Mizzou Leadership Circle members and other key Athletics supporters.

Key Responsibilities
1. Major Gift Fundraising & Portfolio Management (70%)
• Manage a regional portfolio of major gift prospects and donors.
• Identify, cultivate, solicit, and steward donors capable of making leadership and major philanthropic commitments.
• Conduct regular in-person donor visits and meaningful prospect interactions.
• Develop individualized strategies to move prospects through the fundraising pipeline.
• Solicit gifts supporting scholarships, capital projects, annual giving, endowments, and sport-specific priorities.
• Recruit, retain, and upgrade donors into the Mizzou Leadership Circle (MLC).
• Maintain accurate fundraising activity, proposals, and donor strategies within the CRM.

2. Regional Development, Premium Seating & Collaboration (15%)
• Serve as the primary development officer for an assigned geographic region.
• Collaborate with University Advancement and Foundation colleagues on shared prospects and principal gift opportunities.
• Participate in campaign initiatives and departmental fundraising strategies.
• Assist with premium seating sales initiatives, including the cultivation and solicitation of prospective premium seating donors, while identifying opportunities to increase philanthropic support.
• Provide exceptional customer service to Mizzou Leadership Circle members, premium seating holders, and assigned donors by ensuring timely communication, stewardship, and fulfillment of donor benefits.

3. Donor Engagement & Stewardship (15%)
• Represent the Mizzou Athletics Fund at donor events, athletic contests, alumni functions, and community events.
• Assist with donor cultivation events, Mizzou Leadership Circle programming, and stewardship initiatives.
• Build meaningful, long-term relationships that encourage continued philanthropic investment in Missouri Athletics.
• Promote the mission and philanthropic priorities of Missouri Athletics.

description:

The Director, Internal Audit is a key leader within Waters Corporation's Internal Audit function, responsible for advancing a risk-based assurance program that strengthens governance, risk management, and internal controls across the organization. Reporting to the VP, Internal Audit, this role provides leadership over operational, financial, compliance, and risk assessment activities, while supporting the Company's Enterprise Risk Management process and serving as a trusted advisor to business and functional leaders.

You will help shape the future of Internal Audit at Waters by identifying emerging risks, advancing innovative audit approaches, delivering practical insights that support business objectives and strengthen organizational performance, and contributing to the development of a modern, scalable Internal Audit function aligned with the Global Internal Audit Standards.

• Develop and manage the global Internal Audit roadmap and strategy, including the annual risk assessment process, maintenance of the audit universe, and development of a risk-based audit plan focused on the Company's highest-risk areas• Lead the continued maturation of the Internal Audit function through the implementation of leading practices, enhancement of audit methodologies, development of quality assurance processes, and alignment with the Global Internal Audit Standards• Direct and oversee the planning, execution, and reporting of operational, financial, compliance, and advisory engagements to ensure timely completion and adherence to Internal Audit standards and methodologies• Collaborate cross-functionally on a global basis to expand Internal Audit services beyond internal control compliance, promoting innovation, continuous improvement, and enhanced risk management practices• Manage relationships with co-sourced providers and external specialists to ensure effective delivery of audit services, appropriate subject matter expertise, and alignment with Internal Audit objectives• Support the VP, Internal Audit in preparing and facilitating Audit and Finance Committee reporting, including communication of audit results, emerging risks, and the status of audit remediation activities• Partner with the VP, Internal Audit to facilitate the annual Enterprise Risk Management process, including risk identification, assessment, reporting, and monitoring activities

• Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related discipline

• CPA, CIA, CISA or equivalent professional certification required• Demonstrated experience leading operational audits, financial audits, risk assessments, and SOX compliance programs• Strong knowledge of SOX, COSO Internal Control Framework, risk management principles, and the Global Internal Audit Standards• Proven ability to build relationships and influence stakeholders at all levels of the organization• Excellent communication, presentation, and executive presence, with the ability to influence and engage stakeholders at all levels of the organization, including senior leadership and the Audit Committee• Experience managing external service providers and co-sourced audit relationships• Domestic and international travel is required; approximately 30-40%• Experience within life sciences, biopharma including medtech, or broader industrial manufacturing• Experience supporting global organizations operating in a regulated environment• Familiarity with Optro, or similar governance, risk, and compliance platforms

Guided by our mission to improve outcomes for young children and their families, we envision a future where all children thrive in nurturing, supportive environments.

Working at the Center means being part of a passionate, collaborative team committed to impact. title: Mobile Technician (Food & Distribution)
description:
About The Role:

Working Pattern

40 hours over six days

Location: Mobile across contract sites (primarily Morrisons) — UK-wide travel required

Reports to: Regional Operations/Engineering Supervisor

Contract: Full-time

Working pattern: Shift-based, including some early mornings, evenings, and occasional weekends

Driving requirement: Full UK driving licence (van provided)

Role Purpose

OCS are looking for a hands-on Mobile Technician role that bridges operational cleaning support with basic mechanical troubleshooting and fixes for machinery used across our food production and distribution contracts. You’ll help keep our equipment safe, clean, and running by completing hygiene tasks, first-line fault finding, minor repairs, and supporting planned maintenance, all while maintaining high standards of food safety and site compliance.

This is not an industrial cleaning role and not a manufacturing role - it’s an on-the-ground, mobile operational support role focused on equipment uptime, hygiene, and quick-turn resolution.

Key Responsibilities

• Perform targeted cleaning of production and distribution equipment in line with SOPs, including hygiene resets and documentation.

• Use and store chemicals safely under COSHH requirements and maintain correct PPE use.

• Support deep‑clean activities during shutdowns and peak periods.

• Diagnose and complete minor mechanical fixes such as belt adjustments, sensor cleaning, and clearing jams.

• Assist with simple PPM tasks including lubrication, inspections, and filter changes.

• Escalate issues outside scope and support engineers or contractors during call‑outs.

• Record all work accurately in maintenance logs or CMMS systems.

• Work within food‑site rules including GMP, allergen control, tool control, and hygiene zoning.

• Follow LOTO, permit‑to‑work processes, and complete dynamic risk assessments and near‑miss reporting.

• Maintain van stock of consumables, parts, and cleaning materials.

• Build effective working relationships with production, engineering, hygiene, and QA teams.

• Use mechanical skills confidently with hand tools and basic component replacement.

• Travel between sites with flexibility for shifts and varied environments; full UK licence required.

• Work safely with chemicals, in chilled or ambient warehouse settings, and undertake physical tasks up to 20kg.

• Advantageous experience includes basic electrical checks, LOTO awareness, CMMS use, Food Safety Level 2, and FLT/MEWP or PAT certification.

Tools, Equipment & PPE Provided

• Company van

• Basic tool kit and consumables.

• Uniform and task-appropriate PPE.

• Induction covering food site rules, GMP, allergen awareness, COSHH, manual handling, and LOTO awareness.

• Task training for site-specific equipment, SOPs, and documentation standards.

• Shadowing period with experienced technicians/engineers/hygiene leads.

title: Service Delivery Manager
description:
About The Role:

We are currently recruiting for a Service Delivery Manager to join our Technical Services team in Liverpool.

The Service Delivery Manager will be responsible for the day-to-day delivery of technical services at the site, leading the engineering team and ensuring planned and reactive maintenance is delivered safely, efficiently and in line with contractual requirements.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Responsible for the day-to-day management and supervision of the site-based engineering team, ensuring all planned and reactive maintenance is completed to the required standards and in line with agreed service levels.
  • Manage the operational performance of technical services across the site, ensuring contractual KPIs and client expectations are consistently achieved.
  • Build and maintain a strong working relationship with the client, acting as a key point of contact for technical service delivery.
  • Coordinate effectively with the Helpdesk and engineering team to ensure tasks are fully closed out with clear and comprehensive job sheets and compliance documentation.
  • Lead, support and develop the engineering team, driving performance, standards and continuous improvement.
  • Act as a point of escalation for operational and technical issues, ensuring problems are managed through to resolution.
  • Work through technical issues and challenges to identify practical and effective solutions.
  • Supervise and manage the team to deliver a consistently high standard of service to the client.
  • Maintain a good commercial understanding of the contract and wider business requirements.
  • Promote a proactive, ‘can-do’ approach, ensuring tasks within the team’s capabilities are completed safely and in a timely manner.

Essential Hiring Criteria:

  • Applicants must have the right to work in the UK.
  • Technically qualified with a strong understanding of building services and technical infrastructure.
  • Previous experience supervising or managing an engineering maintenance team.
  • Experience of driving continuous improvement in engineering and maintenance standards.
  • Good understanding of Health & Safety, Environmental and Quality Assurance procedures.
  • Experience of supervising, supporting and developing operational teams.
  • Good IT skills, including MS Office and relevant technical software.
  • Experience using CAFM systems.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Strong problem-solving and planning skills, with the ability to take ownership of issues through to resolution.
  • Confident working with clients and stakeholders, managing expectations and representing technical service delivery at client meetings.
  • A strong team leader with the ability to set standards, motivate others and create a positive and proactive working environment.

Personal Attributes:

  • High attention to detail.
  • Methodical and structured approach to problem-solving.
  • Patient and professional communication style.
  • Collaborative approach when working with different teams and stakeholders.
  • Good understanding of client requirements and business drivers.
  • Excellent communication skills at all levels.
  • Adaptable and flexible to changing priorities.

description:
Hiring Department

Department of Psychiatry

Job Description

The Center for Child Well-Being, housed within the Department of Psychiatry in the University of Missouri School of Medicine, seeks an Educational Resource Coach to support Early Childhood Programs, including the Infant & Early Childhood Mental Health (iECMH) Initiative and Child Care Inclusion Services.

This position will be based regionally in the Kansas City area and will require regular travel both regionally and statewide.

We are seeking a candidate with a strong background in special education and/or extensive experience working with children ages 0–5 who have atypical mental, behavioral, and/or physical development.

About the Center for Child Well-Being

The Center for Child Well-Being drives positive change for children and families through innovative programs, collaborative community partnerships, and strategic capacity building. Guided by our mission to improve outcomes for young children and their families, we envision a future where all children have a strong foundation for lifelong health.

Working at the Center means being part of a passionate, collaborative team committed to impact. Staff are supported in their professional growth, empowered to contribute meaningfully, and engaged in work that is purpose-driven and community-centered. Join us in shaping a more responsive and resilient childhood systems landscape across Missouri!

Key Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

  • Provide on-site consultation and coaching to early childhood programs in North Central Missouri, focused on social-emotional learning within a Multi-Tiered System of Support (MTSS) framework.
    • Support implementation of Tier 1 (universal supports), Tier 2 (targeted supports), and Tier 3 (individualized intensive interventions).
  • Maintain up-to-date knowledge of best practices, state mandates, and emerging trends in early childhood mental health and education in Missouri.
  • Develop and deliver in-person and virtual training sessions for stakeholders on early childhood mental health and social-emotional learning.
  • Conduct research on evidence-based practices to support training and inform project development and implementation.
  • Contribute to project management and project development initiatives as assigned.
  • Maintain clear and accurate documentation for all activities, including coaching visits, training sessions, and technical assistance efforts.
  • Contribute to project reporting
  • Other duties as assigned.

Shift

Monday – Friday
8:00 a.m. – 5:00 p.m.
Occasional nights and weekends to accommodate trainings.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and experience and at least 2 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessary.

Preferred Qualifications

Education: Master’s degree in Early Childhood Education, Special Education, Psychology (clinical or developmental), or other related field.
Credentials: State certification or licensure in education, mental health, or a related field
Years of Experience: 3 or more years of experience in early childhood education settings preferred
Additional Training: Experience with evidence-based frameworks such as the Pyramid Model, Conscious Discipline, trauma-informed care, etc.

description:
Hiring Department

The Wang Lab at the University of Missouri-St, Louis and Danforth Plant Science Center

Job Description

The Wang Lab at the University of Missouri-St, Louis and Danforth Plant Science Center seeks to hire a self-motivated Postdoctoral Researcher to work on lipid signaling in plant stress responses. The projects use multidisciplinary research strategies, including protein-lipid interactomes, metabolite profiling, lipidomics, and multiplex genomic editing. Working knowledge in mass spectrometry is highly desirable. Competitive salary, fringe benefits, and travel support to conferences will be provided. The appointment will be made initially for two years with the option to renew.

Responsibilities:

  • Design and conduct experiments in biochemistry, metabolomics, and molecular biology.
  • Maintain precise records of research findings and analyze data statistically.
  • Write reports as required and prepare manuscripts for publication.
  • Communicate findings and present research at professional meetings.
  • Mentor others and work collaboratively in the lab to learn and aid in other projects.
  • Other lab and research duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Ph.D. in biochemistry, cellular/molecular biology, plant biology or related fields

Required knowledge, skills, and abilities:

  • Able to organize, multitask time efficiently, and work independently and collaboratively.
  • Able to use integrated methods for data analysis and thinking quantitatively.
  • Write effectively and have good communication skills.
  • Have prior research experience in biochemistry, molecular biology, and plant biology.

Familiarity with mass spectrometry and metabolomic analyses is critical.

Application Materials

1. Cover letter describing past research experience and future interests
2. CV
3. Contact information for three professional references

Employment visa sponsorship is not available for this position.

As such, education is focused on both traditional and nontraditional students, student retention, providing academic supports, and graduation of the most diverse college-educated work force of any university in the state. title: Senior Business Intelligence Specialist – Center for Child Well Being
description:
Hiring Department

Department of Psychiatry

Job Description

The Center for Child Well-Being, housed within the Department of Psychiatry in the University of Missouri School of Medicine, seeks a Senior Business Intelligence Specialist to support our Center and programmatic-level impact through our Data, Systems, and Evaluation domain.

The ideal candidate is a data professional who cares about the people behind the metrics and the impact of the programs they work with. The candidate will be able to translate technical expertise into practical insights for grant-funded community programs. The candidate will be comfortable helping colleagues build understanding and application of data, communicating findings clearly, and working collaboratively with program teams to solve problems together. They will be growth-oriented and look for ways data can support the team’s efficiency and help move program goals forward.

Experience and technical skill with some of the following is preferred, though candidates need not have expertise in all areas:

- data analysis tools (e.g., R, Python, SPSS, SAS)

- data visualization tools (e.g., Power BI)

- data collection platforms (e.g., REDCap or other survey tools)

- web UI/UX experience

- experience with social or human service organizations, particularly in systems or program management

This position requires the ability to manage multiple competing priorities while maintaining accurate documentation, timely follow-through, and a high level of service. A strong understanding of data structures, cleaning, and validation is essential.

About the Center for Child Well-Being

The Center for Child Well-Being drives positive change for children and families through innovative programs, collaborative community partnerships, and strategic capacity building. Guided by our mission to improve outcomes for young children and their families, we envision a future where all children have a strong foundation for lifelong health.

Working at the Center means being part of a passionate, collaborative team committed to impact. Staff are supported in their professional growth, empowered to contribute meaningfully, and engaged in work that is purpose-driven and community-centered. Join us in shaping a more responsive and resilient childhood systems landscape across Missouri!

Key Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

  • Provide technical assistance and guidance on data collection processes, tools, and best practice. Including development of user guides and training materials.
  • Partner with program staff to assess data needs and translate program goals into effective data collection systems.
  • Perform ongoing system maintenance, including data cleaning, validation, and management, and help modify data systems as needs change.
  • Support website management, including page and resource development, under the guidance of the supervisor.
  • Analyze data sets to identify trends, outcomes, and areas for program improvement.
  • Help translate data findings into actionable insights that support program leads and leadership’s decision-making.
  • Support design and implementation of program evaluation plans, providing technical assistance as needed.
  • Apply appropriate quantitative and qualitative methods to help assess program effectiveness and impact and contribute to evaluation elements of reports.
  • Develop reports, dashboards, and visualizations that translate data into clear narratives for stakeholders.
  • Support data quality monitoring across programs, including validation, auditing, and quality improvement efforts.
  • Help maintain documentation related to data governance, standard operating procedures, and compliance, under supervisor guidance.
  • Support a culture of accountability and continuous improvement within the Center.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Shift

Monday – Friday
8:00 a.m. – 5:00 p.m.
Occasional nights and weekends

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience is necessary

Preferred Qualifications

Years of Experience: Experience with some of the following is preferred, though candidates need not have expertise in all areas: data analysis tools (e.g., R, Python, SPSS, SAS), data visualization tools (e.g., Power BI), and data collection platforms (e.g., REDCap or survey tools). A strong understanding of data structures, cleaning, and validation is important. Prior web UI/UX experience and experience with social or human service organizations are both a plus.
