title: Executive Strategic Communications Specialist - UMKC Chancellor's Office
description:
Hiring Department

UMKC's Chancellor's Office and the Office of Strategic Marketing Communications

Job Description

UMKC is seeking a highly experienced and versatile writer to produce polished executive communications primarily for the Chancellor but also for other members of the executive leadership team. The Executive Strategic Communications Specialist will focus on a range of written materials and presentations for internal and external audiences. Speeches and scripts consume the majority of work hours, but there also will be talking points for meetings and events, digital emails, announcements, memos and other correspondence.
This individual will be housed in the Office of the Chancellor and will work very closely with the Vice Chancellor of Strategic Marketing and Communications in executing high level work in a fast-paced environment, learning the Chancellor’s voice and preparing communications that strategically deliver key messages and information to campus and community.

The successful candidate will be a creative, inspiring writer who is naturally prolific, and – in drafting speeches – shows a knack for telling compelling stories that draw on rigorous research. This person should be a curious thinker, broad reader and quick writer who is comfortable working as part of a team, and who is also comfortable with a number of communications channels and technologies, including digital email and web writing.

The ideal candidate will have the following capabilities:

  • Strategic focus: Demonstrated ability to create written product that meets strategic messaging goals for university, working closely with Vice Chancellor of Strategic Marketing and Communications to develop broad and targeted communications.
  • Strong writing and editing: Write and edit high-level communication materials for Chancellor and other executive leaders for UMKC, including reports, talking points, certain newsletters, presentations, scripts, and briefing documents that reinforce our mission, goals, and priorities.
  • Excellent skills in storytelling and synthesis. Distill information from interviews, meetings, documents and various sources to convey compelling messages that align with our mission, goals, and priorities.
  • Strong practices in content verification and review. Adhere to current division of Strategic Marketing and Communications practices in place that include rigorous editing and review of content for quality, accuracy, AP style, UMKC style and other best practices as well as achieving goals for messaging and voice that are specific to executive communications. Further, executive communications must be well coordinated with overall university communications to achieve optimal impact.
  • Analysis and goal setting: In partnership with other communication team members, create metrics and routinely analyze the impact of communication vehicles and messages, and refine as necessary.

Minimum Qualifications

A Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education and experience and at least 4 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessary.

Preferred Qualifications

  • A Bachelor's Degree in English, Journalism, Communications or a closely related field and at least three years of professional writing experience, preferably in an academic environment is required.
  • Exceptional, dedicated writer with the ability to write for the spoken word, written and digital media alike.
  • Strong project management and time management skills including the ability to work quickly and creatively, sometimes under pressure when content needs to be developed in a tight timeframe.
  • Demonstrated proficiency with Microsoft Office tools (especially Word and PowerPoint) and digital email tools as well as familiarity with Adobe Suite, social media platforms like Instagram and Facebook and editing in cloud-storage tools (Box, Sharepoint).
  • Ability to research, collect, and organize information from diverse sources.
  • Strong interpersonal skills including capacity to collaborate with others.
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to adhere to stringent processes for editing and review of written material with key internal partners and coordination for staging cues and other relevant checks and balances.
  • A capacity to respond receptively to feedback.
  • Experience in a professional setting preferred.

Anticipated Hiring Range

The anticipated hiring range for this position has been established as $61,000 - $70,000 annually.

Salary is determined by a variety of factors, including but not limited to, the individual’s particular combination of education, skills, and experience, as well as organizational requirements.

Your total compensation goes beyond the number on your paycheck. The University of Missouri provides generous leave, health plans, and retirement contributions that add to your bottom line.

title: Cleaning Team Leader
description:
About The Role:

As a Cleaning Team Leader, you’ll lead the day-to-day delivery of cleaning services for a leading UK broadcasting company, ensuring high standards of cleanliness, presentation and customer service are maintained.

You’ll supervise the cleaning team, manage workloads, rotas, stock and equipment, and ensure services are delivered safely and in line with contractual requirements.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead and support the cleaning team to ensure services are delivered to agreed standards and specifications.
  • Allocate workloads and resources effectively, ensuring cleaning schedules and rotas are maintained.
  • Respond promptly to service issues and reactive cleaning requests, following the appropriate helpdesk processes.
  • Ensure all activities comply with OCS and client Health & Safety requirements, including COSHH, risk assessments, method statements and PPE.

  • Manage cleaning stock, consumables, equipment and machinery, ensuring appropriate levels are maintained and equipment remains safe and operational.

  • Good knowledge of professional cleaning methods, standards and practices.
  • Strong understanding of Health & Safety and COSHH requirements.
  • Confident managing and motivating teams to deliver high standards of service.
  • Strong organisation and attention to detail.
  • Good communication and customer service skills.
  • Comfortable using basic IT systems and completing administrative tasks.

  • Ability to prioritise workloads and respond effectively to changing operational requirements.
  • Professional and presentable when dealing with customers and stakeholders.

About You

You’ll be a confident and approachable team leader with a hands-on attitude and a strong focus on delivering excellent service. You’ll communicate effectively with colleagues, customers and stakeholders and take pride in maintaining high standards across the site.

title: Usher
description:
Hiring Department

Touhill Performing Arts Center at the University of Missouri-St. Louis

Job Description

The Touhill Performing Arts Center at the University of Missouri-St. Louis creates opportunities for the people of our region to experience, appreciate and embrace the transformational power of the performing arts. It is a welcoming place, a leading cultural partner in our community and a symbol of this University's commitments to integrate education, innovation and excellence.

The Usher provides direct customer-focused guest services to patrons of the facility.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES

[Customer Focus] – 30%

The Usher is primarily responsible for ensuring that guests and patrons of the Touhill are met with courteous and attentive service whether assisting in wayfinding, welcoming patrons to the facility, or wishing guests a good night.
The Usher is the individual utilized in fulfilling the Touhill’s mission of being a “welcoming place”.

[Event Support] – 30%

Pleasantly directing patrons to amenities and seating.
Handing out programs or other materials on behalf of the client to patrons.
Enforcing Touhill policies regarding proper theater decorum, seating issues, and disruptive patrons while maintaining a welcoming and friendly demeanor.

[Emergency Reporting and Response] – 25%

Remaining vigilant for any emergent issue (such as hazards, suspicious activity or items, or that may arise, seeking the safety and security of patrons and guests as priority.
Reporting observed issues to House Managers for resolution if warranted.
Executing public safety procedures when necessary and directed by the House Manager.

[Training] – 5%

Completing University-mandated training as required.
Completing Touhill-specific training (and/or Touhill qualification(s)) as required.

As with all positions, may perform other job-related responsibilities as needed to support departmental and campus-wide needs.

Shift

Variable depending on event needs

Minimum Qualifications

High school diploma or equivalent and some work experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessary

Preferred Qualifications

  • Communicates professionally in both verbal and written formats.
  • Ability to work long and unusual hours, including late at night.
  • Willingness to work hard and take direction.
  • Experience with House Management or front-of-house operations.
  • An understanding of theatrical terminology, equipment, and usages.
  • Good communication skills and customer service experience are recommended.

Anticipated Hiring Range

$17.50/hr

title: Field Specialist in 4-H Youth Development – St. Charles County
description:
Hiring Department

University of Missouri (MU) Office of Extension and Engagement

4-H Youth Development program

Job Description

MU TITLE: Assistant/Associate/Full Extension Professional

LOCATION: : St. Peters, Missouri serving St. Charles County in the Urban East Region, with additional service within the region and across the state as needed.

Specialist Emphasis

University of Missouri Extension 4-H youth development programs help children and teens become caring, capable, competent, and contributing through a series of progressive experiences over time with caring adults during non-school hours. 4-H youth development programs focus on the broader developmental needs of youth rather than preventing single issues or problems. 4-H youth development programs use a human ecological approach, recognizing that young people are part of systems, including family, school, community, and society.

Program specialization: The Field Specialist in 4-H Youth Development is responsible for planning, implementing, and evaluating positive youth and volunteer development programs.

This position is a 12-month, ranked, non-tenure track appointment at the rank of assistant, associate, or full Extension Professional. Rank will be determined at the time of appointment based on qualifications and experience in accordance with the MU Extension faculty standards. This position will hold the working title of Field Specialist in 4-H Youth Development.

As a Field Specialist, your workload distribution at appointment will be 90% Extension Teaching and 10% Traditional Service.

This appointment is renewable annually at the discretion of the University and workload distribution may change at the discretion of Extension leadership. Circumstances affecting continued employment include, but are not limited to, work performance, fund availability, and educational priorities.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Implement community-based 4-H PYD programs, in-school and after-school programs, short-term interest (SPIN) Clubs, and enrichment activities.
  • Use and recommend research-based curriculum and teaching methods.
  • Secure a culture of high-quality service for all the 4-H members and volunteers
  • Provide leadership to 4-H councils and committees
  • Recruit, develop, and train youth and adults to assist as leaders with implementing the 4-H program.
  • Conduct evaluations of the Missouri 4-H programs (evaluations provided).
  • Ensure that all the youth and adults in the county have the opportunity to participate in extension programs.
  • Apply for and administer local grants and other funding sources.
  • Provide supervision and development to program associate(s).
  • Other duties as assigned.

CORE DUTIES OF MU EXTENSION SPECIALISTS

MU Extension Specialists deliver the University of Missouri to all Missourians. They serve all Missourians by bringing research-based solutions to work on local problems. MU Extension Specialists teach new and foundational concepts, link people to resources, support partner organizations, participate in research, train volunteers, evaluate programs, foster innovation, and serve communities. MU Extension Specialists work as a team to expand educational attainment, foster economic development, and improve health outcomes. These core duties fall into three major areas:

Educate, Create, and Connect.

  • Educate. MU Extension specialists design, conduct, and evaluate educational programs. MU Extension specialists teach research-based information via meetings, in-person and online courses, continuing education classes, technical assistance, volunteer training, media, websites, consultation, and other educational methods. They provide educational programs that support Missouri's learners and clients' individual, organizational, and community goals.
  • Create. MU Extension specialists develop innovative and research-informed educational products, services, materials, and other scholarly works. These include curricula, publications, presentations, educational tools, websites, and similar resources. MU Extension specialists obtain and use extramural funding to support creative works. MU Extension specialists contribute to the scholarship of Extension and Engagement by evaluating programs that result in learning and behavior changes that impact individuals and communities.
  • Connect. MU Extension specialists engage with learners, stakeholders, volunteers, and communities, including county extension councils, government officials and agencies, partners, and University and professional organizations. MU Extension specialists listen and respond with care. MU Extension specialists intentionally foster engaged partnerships and robust connections to the vast array of programs offered by the University of Missouri System.

Professional Expectations

  • Engage with stakeholders in all counties to identify educational needs and then collaborate with appropriate internal and external partners to meet those needs.
  • Create an annual plan of work that reflects local needs and aligns with statewide program area efforts. Provide a monthly report to county extension councils, supervisors, county commissioners, and others regarding programmatic efforts. Attend at least one county extension council each month and provide an oral update on program efforts at that meeting.
  • Collaborate with campus-based specialists on research projects and then deliver findings from those efforts via demonstrations, field days, courses, workshops, consultations, publications, and appropriate media.
  • Effectively work with supervisors, other specialists, and local leaders to complete administrative tasks as needed.
  • Demonstrate competency in communication, educational programming, subject matter knowledge, educational delivery, volunteer management, grant acquisition, teamwork, interpersonal relations, organization knowledge, leadership, and professionalism.
  • Offer timely, research-based information during times of natural disasters or similar events.
  • Represent the University of Missouri on boards and committees as assigned.
  • Participate in professional development events to improve both technical and leadership skills.
  • Other duties and responsibilities as assigned to support the mission of MU Extension.

Additional Expectations

  • MU Extension Specialists regularly travel throughout Missouri and occasionally to out-of-state locations. MU Extension requires specialists to have a valid Missouri driver’s license, a legally operating vehicle, and wireless telephone/data service for University use. MU Extension specialists receive reimbursement for approved travel expenses, per University of Missouri policy.
  • MU Extension programs often occur outside of regular business hours. MU Extension Specialists should expect to attend these events as needed to meet the needs of learners, clients, and stakeholders.

MU EXTENSION LEADERSHIP RECEIVED

The Senior Program Director for 4-H Youth Development provides overall programmatic leadership. Programmatic supervision comes from the Assistant Director of Missouri 4-H (Education Director) for the Missouri 4-H and administrative oversight from the Regional Director.

MU EXTENSION INFORMATION

The University of Missouri (MU) Office of Extension and Engagement’s distinct land-grant mission is to improve lives, communities, and economies by producing relevant, reliable, and responsive educational strategies throughout Missouri. Our dedicated and knowledgeable specialists and staff collaborate with researchers and community leaders to develop and deliver programs that address the needs of Missourians, including educational attainment, economic development, and healthy people. For more information about MU Extension and Engagement, please visit .

UNIVERSITY INFORMATION

The University of Missouri, also known as Mizzou and MU, is the Flagship University of the four-campus University of Missouri System. It is one of the state’s land-grant universities. MU’s comprehensive undergraduate and graduate, professional, and research programs attract an annual enrollment of more than 30,000 students. MU Extension and Engagement programs are located on all four campuses and in 114 counties and St. Louis city.

Qualifications

An earned PhD or master’s degree at time of appointment.

Candidates will be evaluated on:

Hours of upper-level coursework in one or more of the following areas: child, adolescent, and adult human development; education, learning theory, and learning strategies; organizational systems and human resource management; community development/partnerships; and volunteerism.

Anticipated Hiring Range

This position offers a minimum starting salary of $58,000, with the final salary determined based on the candidate’s qualifications and experience.

title: ELECTRONICS TECHNICIAN III #00079804
description:
Hiring Department

Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering

The Mechanical & Aerospace Engineering Department is one of the largest academic units at Missouri S&T and supports both undergraduate and graduate education. The department conducts instruction, laboratory activities, and sponsored research across a broad range of engineering areas and secures substantial research funding to support these efforts. Facilities provide opportunities for hands-on learning and research engagement, contributing to both instructional and scholarly activity. Ongoing and future initiatives, including the Protoplex building, expand research and collaboration space for students, faculty, and industry partners.

Job Description

The Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering at Missouri S&T is seeking an electronics technician to serve various roles, including setting up and maintaining the instructional lab equipment at the MSU campus, based on the course schedule. The technician will also be responsible for assisting in the development of new equipment and experiment systems for the mechanical engineering cooperative program at MSU. As time allows, the technician will assist in development, construction and maintenance of both instructional lab and research lab equipment for the S&T campus Mechanical and Aerospace department. Therefore, the successful candidate must be a motivated, independent, electronics technician capable of handling multiple tasks and projects in multiple locations.

This position will require frequent travel to the MSU campus labs and coordination between his duties on the two campuses.

Primary duties and attributes:

  • Work as part of a team to construct, install, set-up and maintain instructional and research lab equipment in the Mechanical Engineering department, in labs both on the S&T campus and on the MSU campus.
  • Have some mechanical skills as well as a good base in electronics and computers.
  • Schedule tasks to ensure that experiments are set up and ready to run at the appropriate time and that all the required materials and supplies are in place.
  • Work on construction, updating, troubleshooting and repairing a wide variety of laboratory equipment from simple mechanical systems to delicate electronic instrumentation to CNC machine tooling to laser systems, and everything in between.
  • Spend time both on the S&T campus and the MSU campus (Plaster center) each week. The amount of time will be dependent on what is going on at any one time, but expect to go to Springfield at least one day per week.
  • Work directly with students and faculty to evaluate problems and suggest and implement solutions to complex problems.
  • Assist with development, construction, installation and maintenance of instructional and research laboratory equipment as directed.

Minimum Qualifications

An Associate's degree or an equivalent combination of education and at least 1 year of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessary

Anticipated Hiring Range

The anticipated hiring range for this position has been established as $17.40-$23.85 hourly.

Salary is determined by a variety of factors, including but not limited to, the individual’s particular combination of education, skills, and experience, as well as organizational requirements.

Your total compensation goes beyond the number on your paycheck. The University of Missouri provides generous leave, health plans, and retirement contributions that add to your bottom line.

Grade: GGS 7

To review the University of Missouri’s Staff Compensation Structure you can view the Job Code detail page. Internal applicants can determine their university title by accessing the Talent Profile tile in myHR.

Application Deadline

Applications will be accepted until this position is filled.

Community Information

University Information
Missouri S&T is one of the nation's leading research universities with over 100-degree programs in 39 disciplines. It was founded in 1870 as one of the first technological institutions west of the Mississippi River. Located about 100 miles west of St. Louis in the vibrant community of Rolla, Missouri S&T is an accessible, safe, and friendly campus surrounded by Ozarks' scenery. Missouri S&T offers undergraduate degrees in engineering, the sciences, liberal arts, humanities, and business, with M.S. and Ph.D. programs available in many of the science and engineering programs. With over 7,000 students and 300 faculty, Missouri S&T is big enough to accommodate a broad population, yet small enough for individuals to build high visibility and impactful careers.

COLLEGE of ENGINEERING & COMPUTING (CEC)
Missouri S&T’s College of Engineering and Computing is the largest of three colleges at S&T, accounting for approximately 80% of the total enrollment (about 4,500 undergraduates and 800 graduate students). The college includes more than 170 ranked faculty members who serve in 16 undergraduate programs, all with master’s and doctoral equivalents organized into nine academic departments. title: Programmer Analyst
description:
Hiring Department

Department of SOM Chief Information Officer

Job Description

*****This role requires regular, in-person presence at our Columbia, Missouri location to effectively support departmental operations and collaborate with internal stakeholders. Candidates must be able to work onsite; this position is not eligible for remote work.*******

The MU School of Medicine is seeking an intermediate-level Programmer Analyst/Application Developer to design, develop, enhance, deploy, and support modern web applications and technology solutions that advance the School of Medicine's clinical, academic, administrative, and data management needs.
This position will play an important role in the School of Medicine's long-term technology strategy, including expanding the use of artificial intelligence, modernizing applications for cloud environments, improving application security, and increasing automation across existing and future systems.
The successful candidate will work as part of an Agile development team supporting and developing applications used by students, faculty, staff, and other stakeholders across the School of Medicine and MU Health. The position requires strong full-stack application development skills, particularly with C#, React, and TypeScript, as well as foundational knowledge and practical experience with artificial intelligence, cloud application deployment, application security, and containerization.
The ideal candidate will be able to quickly integrate into an established development team, contribute to existing applications, and help identify opportunities to improve development processes and introduce new technologies.

Duties and Responsibilities

Duties include, but are not limited to:

  • Design, develop, enhance, test, deploy, and maintain web-based applications supporting the MU School of Medicine's academic, administrative, clinical, reporting, and data management functions.
  • Develop modern web applications using technologies including C#, .NET/ASP.NET, React, TypeScript, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, SQL, and related frameworks and technologies.
  • Participate in the modernization and migration of existing applications to cloud-based environments, including designing applications and deployment processes that support scalability, reliability, maintainability, and security.
  • Apply artificial intelligence technologies to improve existing systems and develop new capabilities, including:
    • AI-powered workflow automation
    • AI agents
    • AI chatbots and conversational applications
    • AI-assisted software development and code testing
    • AI-supported application and cybersecurity solutions
  • Evaluate opportunities to integrate AI capabilities into existing School of Medicine and MU Health applications while considering security, privacy, reliability, maintainability, and responsible use of AI.
  • Assist with strengthening application security and implementing development practices designed to mitigate traditional and AI-enabled cybersecurity threats.
  • Develop and maintain secure integrations between applications, databases, APIs, cloud services, and other institutional systems.
  • Work with relational database technologies such as Microsoft SQL Server, MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, or similar platforms, including SQL programming, stored procedures, data modeling, and application/database integration.
  • Participate throughout the software development lifecycle, including requirements gathering, technical design, implementation, testing, code review, deployment, troubleshooting, and production support.
  • Identify, analyze, and document application and business requirements by collaborating with students, faculty, staff, technical teams, and other stakeholders.
  • Translate business requirements into practical technical solutions that improve and automate business processes, data collection, reporting, and application workflows.
  • Troubleshoot, debug, and resolve application, integration, database, deployment, and performance issues.
  • Participate in Agile development processes, including sprint planning, backlog refinement, daily team collaboration, code reviews, testing, deployment, and continuous improvement activities.
  • Work with modern development and deployment practices, including source control, automated build and deployment processes, and CI/CD pipelines.
  • Utilize or support Docker and other containerization technologies for application development, deployment, and environment consistency.
  • Maintain appropriate technical documentation for applications, architecture, integrations, deployment processes, and operational procedures.
  • Provide estimates for development efforts and assist with evaluating project feasibility, technical approaches, priorities, risks, and dependencies.
  • Conduct research and development on emerging technologies, particularly artificial intelligence, cloud computing, cybersecurity, software development frameworks, and development automation.
  • Identify opportunities to improve existing applications, development processes, system architecture, security, maintainability, and overall user experience.

Shift

Monday – Friday
8:00 a.m. – 5:00 p.m.

Minimum Qualifications

A Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education and experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessary.

Preferred Qualifications

Education: BS in Computer Science
Years of Experience: 3-5 years

Skills and Abilities

  • Strong knowledge of and practical experience developing applications using C# and ASP.NET Core, as well as experience developing modern front-end applications using React.
  • Strong knowledge of TypeScript and JavaScript.
  • Experience with one or more of the following:
    • AI automation
    • AI agents
    • AI chatbots
    • AI-assisted code testing or software development
    • AI security or cybersecurity applications
  • Experience working within an Agile software development team and participating in iterative development and deployment processes.
  • Experience designing, developing, testing, and supporting full-stack web applications.
  • Strong understanding of relational databases, SQL programming, and application/database integration.
  • Experience deploying or supporting applications in a cloud environment.
  • Understanding secure software development principles and application security practices.
  • Experience using modern source control and collaborative development practices, such as Git and pull-request-based development.

Interpersonal & Behavioral Competencies

The successful candidate should demonstrate:

  • Growth-minded and curious about emerging technologies.
  • Ability to step into the current team and make an immediate impact.
  • Ability to communicate clearly with both technical and non-technical resources and collaborate effectively across disciplines, skills, job roles.
  • Thrives in an agile environment and embraces uncertainty.

description:
Hiring Department

Department of Psychiatry

Job Description

The Center for Child Well-Being, housed within the Department of Psychiatry in the University of Missouri School of Medicine, seeks a Program Lead to support the Missouri Child Psychiatry Access Project (MO-CPAP).

The ideal candidate is an experienced program leader with progressive responsibility for developing and implementing large-scale, statewide programs, preferably within complex, multi-million-dollar initiatives. They will bring strong leadership skills, including team building, delegation, professional development, accountability, and the ability to translate strategic priorities into effective program operations.

Excellent communication, sound judgment, and the ability to navigate complex challenges are essential. This position exercises independent judgment in guiding program implementation and day-to-day operations while ensuring alignment with funding requirements, project goals, and organizational priorities.

This position is a full-time, grant-funded, exempt, on-site position.

About the Center

The Center for Child Well-Being drives positive change for children and families through innovative programs, collaborative community partnerships, and strategic capacity building. Guided by our mission to improve outcomes for young children and their families, we envision a future where all children have a strong foundation for lifelong health.

Working at the Center means being part of a passionate, collaborative team committed to impact. Staff are supported in their professional growth, empowered to contribute meaningfully, and engaged in work that is purpose-driven and community-centered. Join us in shaping a more responsive and resilient childhood systems landscape across Missouri!

Key Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

Program Leadership and Strategy

  • Serve as Program Lead for the for the Missouri Child Psychiatry Access Project (MO-CPAP).
  • Work closely with the Principal Investigators (PIs) and Medical Director to translate project goals, funding requirements, and organizational priorities into effective program strategy and implementation.
  • Collaborate with other Program Leads in the Psychiatry Access Programs domain (e.g., the Maternal Health Access Project) to ensure seamless service transfer between programs.
  • Exercise delegated authority for day-to-day program operations and maintain oversight of program activities, deliverables, timelines, and staff.
  • Lead strategic planning and implementation to expand program reach, impact, and sustainability. Translate organizational and funding priorities into actionable program goals, strategies, and operational plans, and monitor progress toward established outcomes.
  • Monitor program performance using data-informed approaches and adjust strategies as needed to improve program effectiveness and achieve project goals.

Program Operations and Implementation

  • Maintain responsibility for day-to-day program management, including oversight of workflows, service delivery, quality assurance, and operational processes.
  • Establish and maintain standardized processes that support effective, consistent, and sustainable program implementation.
  • Manage program timelines, milestones, deliverables, and reporting requirements.
  • Ensure program activities align with regulatory, contractual, and institutional requirements in collaboration with appropriate Center and University partners.
  • Develop and monitor the program budget, track expenditures and budget performance on a minimum of a monthly basis, and identify and address variances and emerging financial needs with support from appropriate financial administrators.
  • Identify operational challenges and develop/implement solutions.

Team Leadership and Supervision

  • Supervise a team of professional employees, currently 3–6 full-time staff.
  • Foster a collaborative, high-performing team culture grounded in accountability, communication, and continuous improvement.
  • Maintain clear and consistent communication with team members regarding program priorities, expectations, changes, and operational needs.
  • Participate in program and Center meetings and communicate relevant information and decisions to team members.
  • Provide coaching, performance feedback, and accountability; address performance concerns appropriately; and support professional development and growth.
  • Support workforce planning, hiring, onboarding, and team development in collaboration with Center leadership and appropriate University partners.
  • Delegate responsibilities effectively and establish clear expectations, roles, and accountability within the team.
  • Build effective working relationships with internal colleagues and external partners to support coordinated services and program operations.

Rural Expansion and Systems Development

  • Lead the expansion of the MO-CPAP into rural communities across Missouri in alignment with Rural Health Transformation Project contractual requirements & priorities.
  • Develop and implement strategies that support sustainable growth while maintaining program quality, consistency, and fidelity.
  • Support program sustainability planning and funding development by identifying opportunities, contributing to grant proposals and applications, and developing strategies to sustain and expand program services.

Stakeholder Engagement and Partnerships

  • Build and maintain strong relationships with external stakeholders, including behavioral health professionals, state agencies, healthcare organizations, and community partners.
  • Serve as a key organizational representative for the program and facilitate collaboration, coordinated care, and program integration across partners and systems.
  • Represent the program in meetings, presentations, and other professional settings.
  • Communicate program goals, progress, challenges, and opportunities effectively to internal and external stakeholders.

Data, Evaluation, and Reporting

  • Partner with the evaluation team to understand program data collection and management, monitor program performance, assess outcomes and impact, and use data to inform program decisions and improvements.
  • Work collaboratively with evaluation partners to ensure program data and performance information accurately reflect program activities and outcomes.
  • Utilize program data and evaluation findings to support continuous quality improvement and stakeholder communications.
  • Lead required program deliverables and reports.
  • Ensure deliverables are comprehensive, accurate, professionally written, aligned with project requirements, and submitted in a timely manner.

Other

  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Work Hours: This position may occasionally require work outside of standard business hours, including evenings or weekends, based on program needs, stakeholder meetings, travel, or events associated with the expansion of services across Missouri.

Shift

Monday – Friday
8:00 a.m. – 5:00 p.m.
Occasional nights and weekends

A Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education and experience and 3 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessary

Preferred Qualifications

Education: Bachelor's degree in public health, healthcare administration, social work, behavioral health, business administration, or a related field; master's degree preferred.
Years of Experience: Progressive experience in program leadership, development, implementation, or management. Demonstrated experience leading complex programs involving multiple stakeholders, sites, or geographic regions. Experience supervising and developing professional staff. Experience working with healthcare, behavioral health, maternal health, public health, or community-based systems is preferred. Experience working with state agencies, healthcare organizations, or community partners is preferred.

Office of Financial Success

Job Description

The Program Manager for the Office of Financial Success (OFS) manages and coordinates the functions of OFS supporting the Mizzou community. The Program Manager assists the Senior Program Manager with all duties, including operational services and as the center’s secondary representative. This position will be primarily responsible for supervision of the student worker staff of OFS. Additionally, the Program Manager will assist the Senior Program Manager in establishing and building relationships with campus leaders and programs. This position will also be required to perform financial counseling in accordance with established standards, conduct financial wellness seminars/workshops, manage table events, and develop learning content to support these functions.

Specific duties include:
-Assist with the planning, management, and implementation of financial counseling programs, financial wellness workshops/presentations, and recruitment activities in alignment with student needs and campus strategic priorities
-Assist with planning and supervising the OFS table at special events and in pre-determined admissions recruitment events
-Create, develop, and manage financial wellness education content
-Utilize platforms such as myZou, MU Connect, MU Engage, etc. to track touchpoints and program engagement
-Analyze program data with Microsoft 365 Tools such as Microsoft Excel to assess effectiveness and inform strategic decision-making
-Other job-related duties as assigned

Monday - Friday 8:00am-5:00pm. Some evening and weekend hours may be required.

Minimum Qualifications

A Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education and experience and at least 2 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessary.

-Bachelor's Degree in Personal Finance, Family Economics, Finance, Business or any Finance related field

description:
Hiring Department

Campus Facilities Management (CFM)

Learn more about our team here: https://www.umkc.edu/finadmin/campus-facilities/

LOCATION: UMKC Volker Campus

Job Description

As a UMKC employee within the BTS Locksmith trade, you’ll belong to an engaged, diverse community and will get to interact and engage with faculty, staff, and students from a variety of backgrounds daily. UMKC offers many competitive benefits, including health, dental, life and other insurance plans; a comprehensive retirement program; and educational assistance and tuition reduction programs for employees and their spouse/dependents. You will have a assorted amount of work in the locksmith trade and you will have the opportunity to broaden your skillsets with the Campus Facilities Department as you will work side by side with the skilled trades such as HVAC, electrical, carpentry, and plumbing when needed. There is never a dull, typical day on campus as we have a wide variety of buildings that range from over 100 years old to just under 2 years old, and some of our most iconic buildings have great history in Kansas City, for example Scofield Hall. This job could be just the refreshing change and new opportunity you are looking for, and we encourage you to apply and start a new adventure in your career.

Perform skilled work on a journey level involving the installation, maintenance, service and repair of a wide range of locking mechanisms, door closers and exit devices; and in the fabrication, issuance and accountability for keys for such equipment. Work is subject to spot checking and inspection for conformance to specifications and accepted standards of the trade. Functional contacts include co-workers, other service department employees, and other university staff and students.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Install, maintain, repair, reset, adjust and/or replace all types of locking mechanisms and/or door closers
  • Make keys from duplicate pattern keys on manually and automatically operated key cutting machines. Make keys manually from codes, by observing pin settings in locking devices and by impression models.
  • May issue and receive keys. Maintain necessary access rosters and lists, card files, receipts and other records to account for keys issued, received, and maintained in key vault. Maintain file of combinations for combination locking devices
  • As directed by proper authority, open locks for which no key is available, utilizing prescribed lock-picking procedures and lock-picking tools. May maintain and repair coin vending devices serviced by the university. May lock and unlock various rooms and offices as assigned.
  • May perform or assist with preparation of cost estimates, material orders, reports and maintenance of records.

7:30am-4:00pm, Monday through Friday

Minimum Qualifications

  • High school graduate or equivalent; demonstrated skills may offset requirements and a minimum of 4-years of actual experience in the trade, including apprentice or vocational training.

  • Valid driver’s license required.

title: M&E Lead Engineer
description:
About The Role:

Shift Pattern: Monday to Friday, some weekend overtime may be required as part of an on call rota.

The M&E Lead Engineer is responsible for leading a team of mechanical and electrical engineers, overseeing planned preventative maintenance (PPM) and reactive works, and ensuring compliance with statutory and contractual obligations. Supported by a Workplace Co-Ordinator, this role collaborates closely with the helpdesk team, reviews contractor performance, prepares client quotes, and maintains critical trackers to support operational efficiency and client reporting. In addition to leading the governance of M&E service delivery, the role would require practical hands-on support to ensure work delivered is compliant with regulations, OCS safe working practices and policies, and contractual KPI’s.

Key Responsibilities

1. Team Management and Leadership

· Lead a team of engineers with diverse skill sets, assigning tasks, monitoring performance, and ensuring workload balance.

· Conduct regular team briefings to align on priorities, address challenges, and maintain high standards of service delivery.

· Provide technical guidance and mentoring to engineers, fostering skill development and problem-solving capabilities.

2. Collaboration with Helpdesk Team

· Work closely with administrative support to review PPM and reactive work requests, assigning appropriate resource to ensure job completion in timely and compliant manner.

· Provide input on task prioritisation and resource allocation to ensure efficient job completion and minimal downtime.

· Working collaboratively with administrative support and engineering resource to ensure CAFM system is reporting real-time status and updates of open works.

3. Contractor Quote Review and Benchmarking

· Ensure value for money and providing the Client with the most efficient, cost effective, and operationally suitable solutions.

· Monitor Contractor performance in line with OCS expectations of service delivery.

4. Quote Preparation and Tracking

· Utilising administrative support, prepare detailed and accurate quotes for client approval for additional works, repairs, or upgrades, whilst ensuring transparency and value for money.

· Track and report on the status of quotes, including those pending submission to the client and those awaiting approval, using the variable work tracker.

· Follow up with the client or Account Manager to expedite approvals and ensure timely project initiation.

5. Compliance and Certificate Management

· Review certificates from contractors (e.g., compliance certificates for PPM, safety tests) to verify accuracy, completeness, and adherence to statutory regulations.

· Ensure all compliance documentation is filed correctly and available for audits or client reviews.

· Escalate any non-compliance issues to the Account Manager promptly, proposing corrective actions.

6. Compliance Tracker Management

· Use and manage the compliance tracker to monitor PPM schedules, reactive works, and statutory deadlines for M&E assets (e.g., HVAC, electrical systems, fire safety).

· Keep tracker data updated with completion dates, certificate statuses, and any overdue risks, ensuring real-time accuracy.

· Collaborate with the Account management team to maintain 100% compliance across all tracked tasks.

7. Support for Monthly Business Reporting

· Conduct task analysis (e.g., completion rates, overdue tasks, contractor performance) and provide data to the Account Manager for inclusion in monthly business reports.

· Highlight key M&E activities, compliance updates, and risks in a concise format to support client reporting.

· Assist in identifying trends or recurring issues to inform strategic recommendations.

8. Technical Oversight

· Leverage qualified M&E expertise to diagnose complex issues or verify contractor work quality on an as-needed basis.

· Support the Engineering resource to ensure works delivered are compliant, time appropriate, and with resolute solutions.

· Ensure all work complies with safety standards and is documented appropriately.

· Technical knowledge and familiarity with M&E systems expected to be found in a corporate office space and workplace environment. The Lead Engineer will need to work closely with SME’s in the SCP to ensure robust resilience and response to specialist systems.

· Knowledge and familiarity of SFG-20 and maintenance strategies, task descriptions and frequencies.

9. Process Improvement and Risk Mitigation

· Identify and champion innovative ideas and improvements to service delivery as part of continuous improvement plans.

· Proactively flag risks (e.g., aging assets, delayed approvals) and recommend mitigation strategies to the Account Manager.

· Support the implementation of new processes or tools to streamline compliance and reporting.

Skills and Qualifications

Essential:

· Qualified Mechanical and/or Electrical Engineer (e.g., NVQ Level 3, HNC, or equivalent) with proven technical expertise.

· Experience in leading a team of engineers in a facilities management or maintenance environment.

· Strong understanding of PPM, reactive works, and statutory compliance requirements (e.g., F-Gas, electrical safety).

· Proficiency in analysing data, and using tracking/reporting tools.

· Excellent communication and collaboration skills to work with helpdesk, contractors, and clients.

Desirable:

· Previous experience in a client-facing role.

· Knowledge of facilities management software (e.g., CAFM systems).

· Previous/current appointment, and capability for re-appointment, as a Low Voltage Authorised Person.

Working Conditions

· Monday to Friday, however some weekend overtime may be required as part of an on-call rota.

· Office/site-based, with regular interaction across the client premises.

· Willingness to work “on-the-tools” as and when required to support M&E service delivery.

· Flexibility to respond to urgent issues outside standard hours if required.

description:
About The Role:

We are seeking an experienced Senior Mechanical Project Manager to join our Projects Division. The successful candidate will be responsible for leading mechanical building-services projects from initial scope and design development through to installation, commissioning and final handover, ensuring projects are delivered safely, on time, within budget and to the highest quality standards.

This is a project-delivery role focused on physical mechanical works, including heating, ventilation, cooling, pipework, plant replacement and associated building-services installations.

You will manage the technical, commercial and operational delivery of projects while coordinating clients, engineers, subcontractors, suppliers and internal teams.

Key Responsibilities

  • Manage mechanical installation, replacement, upgrade and refurbishment projects.
  • Lead projects from initial scope and design development through to final handover.
  • Develop project programmes, delivery plans and resource schedules.
  • Review technical drawings, specifications and scopes of work.
  • Coordinate engineers, subcontractors, suppliers and site activities.
  • Monitor project progress and address potential delays or delivery risks.
  • Manage budgets, variations, forecasts and WIP with the Commercial team.
  • Ensure compliance with technical standards, client requirements and CDM Regulations.
  • Produce and review RAMS and other project documentation.
  • Lead project meetings and provide progress reports to clients and stakeholders.
  • Manage testing, commissioning, snagging and final handover.
  • Ensure all health, safety and environmental procedures are followed.

Qualifications and Experience

Essential

  • Significant experience managing mechanical engineering or building-services projects.
  • Strong knowledge of heating, ventilation, cooling, pipework, pumps and plantroom systems.
  • Experience delivering projects from initial planning through to handover.
  • Experience managing budgets, forecasts, variations and WIP.
  • Ability to interpret mechanical drawings and technical specifications.
  • Experience managing subcontractors, suppliers and site teams.
  • SMSTS or an equivalent five-day Site Management Safety qualification.
  • Valid CSCS card.
  • Strong leadership, commercial and communication skills.
  • Full UK driving licence.

Desirable

  • HNC, HND or degree in Mechanical Engineering, Building Services or Construction Management.
  • Recognised mechanical trade or engineering qualification.
  • PRINCE2, APM or equivalent project-management qualification.
  • IOSH or NEBOSH qualification.

description:

University of Missouri-Kansas City, Planning, Design, and Construction

Job Description

Responsibilities:

  • Manage contracted construction projects to assure compliance with Contract Documents, laws, standards, practices, and University objectives and requirements. Maintain project cost and schedule information and continually monitor progress and status as the project design develops.
  • Provide active direction to consultants and stakeholders to align deviations.
  • Ensure coordination of work and communication construction of University new building construction, and/or renovation or remodel of existing University facilities
  • Monitor and manage Architects and Engineers on design and construction projects, approving payments, and assuring deliverables from all parties on each project.
  • Coordination with other campus departments, and non-university companies, as related to construction projects to ensure understanding of scope of work, impact of construction on departments and/or private companies (Utility companies, private businesses, or private homeowners).
  • Conduct reviews of contract documents for accuracy, completeness, coordination of disciplines, conformance to industry standards, campus design standards, and building codes.
  • Interpret, administer, and enforce the construction contract and all associated agreements for professional services.
  • Assume primary manager of the project during the construction phase; ensure projects are completed on schedule, within budget, and in accordance with the requirements of the contract documents.
  • Manage all contract budget expenditures and transactions for University construction projects.
  • Monitor MBE/WBE contract compliance as it relates to the General Contractor and their Subcontractor/Material Suppliers.
  • Other Duties as Assigned

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

  • Possesses an in-depth conceptual and practical knowledge in the CSM Operations function and begins to acquire knowledge in other related functions
  • Has knowledge of best practices and concepts in the CSM Operations function and how own area integrates with other functions
  • Strategically executing projects on a campus/within buildings that are occupied and in regular use
  • Creating and maintaining positive relations with all the third party partners (Ex; Maintaining relationships with our third party partners preserves a stable list of partners that UMKC can work with)
  • Creating and maintaining positive relations with internal clients (Ex; Clients may have desires for the scope of their project that exceed their budget. This person will strive to manage expectations and build consensus)

title: Electrical Supervisor
description:
About The Role:

Working Pattern

08.00 - 17.00 Monday to Friday, one hour unpaid lunch

A Qualified Supervisor is the electrically competent person with specific responsibility for the safety, technical standard and quality of electrical installation work completed under their supervision.

A Qualified Supervisor is responsible for:

  • Ensuring that the results of inspection and testing are recorded correctly on the appropriate certificates or reports.
  • Ensuring that the business’ premises, equipment, documentation, and records are available for inspection when required by NICEIC.
  • Supervisory duties for all electrical operatives
  • Safeguarding all unused NICEIC forms of certification and reporting any loss, theft or misuse.

A proposed Qualified Supervisor should:

  • Be available to the business on a full-time basis.
  • Have at least two consecutive years supervisory or managerial responsibility for the standard of electrical installation work.
  • Satisfy the technical training and/or experience requirements.
  • Understand the Electricity at Work Regulations, current edition of BS 7671, and the Codes of Practice and guidance documents relevant to the range of electrical work undertaken.
  • Understand the inspection, testing, verification, certification and reporting procedures for the range of electrical work undertaken.

Key Duties & Responsibilities

  • Demonstrate competence / experience as an electrician.
  • Work across a wide range of electrical installation types and materials.
  • Demonstrate competence of electrical testing and completion of electrical installation certificates (NICEIC). Including appropriate collation of reports, software, correct application of testing equipment etc.
  • Participate in the supervisory on call rota and maintain the Engineers on call rota.
  • Demonstrate a reasonable working knowledge of other building service systems.
  • Willing to work overtime to support the needs of the Business.
  • Verification of subcontractors reports and other in-house reports within the contract.
  • These duties and responsibilities may be changed in accordance with the needs of the company, in particular the post holder may be required to provide support to holders of other posts according to changes in workload and patterns of working.

Essential

  • Full UK Drivers Licence
  • 18th Edition IET Wiring Regulations
  • Knowledge of Microsoft Word, Excel and Outlook
  • Must be able to qualify for role within NICEC.
  • Experience in in service test and inspection of electrical installations.

Desirable but not essential

  • Experience in Maximo system
  • Experience of working in a busy large office environment
  • Previous supervisory experience.
  • Experience using NIEC Click Software.

Key Person Criteria

  • Excellent communication skills both written & verbal.
  • Strong customer facing skills.
  • Proactive and flexible team player.
  • Ability to react under pressure.
  • Has no problem receiving or delivering instructions.
  • Flexible approach to working hours.
  • Good organisational skills.
  • Good time keeping.

title: Senior Project Manager
description:
About The Role:

We are looking for an experienced Senior Project Manager to lead refurbishment and building services projects, overseeing a project portfolios worth up to £3 million.

You will manage multiple projects concurrently, with individual project values typically ranging from £10,000 to £500,000. Works will include office refurbishments, fit-outs, HVAC upgrades, mechanical and electrical installations, and building fabric improvements within live operational buildings.

Experience delivering refurbishment and upgrade projects within existing, occupied buildings is essential. Candidates must demonstrate relevant refurbishment experience alongside any new-build project experience.

Working closely with the Operations Manager, Regional Operations Director and Pre-Construction team, you will take responsibility for delivery from initial client brief through scoping, design development, pricing, procurement, construction, commissioning and final handover.

Key responsibilities

  • Lead multiple projects across an account portfolio worth up to £3 million, with individual works typically valued between £10,000 and £500,000.

  • Maintain oversight of programmes, budgets, resources, risks and commercial performance across the portfolio.

  • Act as a senior point of contact for clients, managing expectations, resolving escalations and maintaining effective working relationships.

  • Develop client requirements into clear scopes of work, design briefs and contractor proposals.

  • Lead design coordination and pre-construction planning appropriate to each project.

  • Oversee site surveys, identifying existing building constraints and operational requirements.

  • Plan phased refurbishment works within occupied buildings, managing access, service interruptions and business continuity.

  • Manage subcontract tender packages, procurement schedules and supply chain appointments.

  • Ensure project execution plans, risk registers and construction phase documentation are prepared and maintained.

  • Develop and monitor construction programmes, addressing delays and resource conflicts promptly.

  • Lead and support project teams, direct employees, subcontractors and supply chain partners.

  • Ensure personnel have the competence, training and resources required to deliver safely and effectively.

  • Deliver projects on time, within budget and to the agreed quality standards.

  • Oversee commissioning, snagging, certification and final handover.

  • Chair client and project progress meetings, ensuring decisions and actions are recorded and followed through.

  • Monitor costs, forecasts and margin performance alongside the Commercial team.

  • Manage variations and contractual changes, ensuring timely assessment, reporting and agreement.

  • Identify efficiencies and opportunities to improve commercial returns while maintaining quality.

  • Work closely with Commercial, Procurement and Health & Safety teams.

  • Maintain effective health and safety controls, technical compliance and project governance.

  • Develop team capability and apply lessons learned to improve delivery across the contracts.

Essential experience and skills

  • A minimum of five years’ relevant construction project delivery experience.

  • Proven experience as a Project Manager or Senior Project Manager with responsibility for multiple concurrent projects.

  • A mechanical, electrical or building fabric background, or experience across these disciplines.

  • Demonstrable experience delivering refurbishment, fit-out or building services upgrades within existing buildings.

  • Experience managing project portfolios, including budgets, programmes, resources, subcontractors and commercial performance.

  • Experience delivering phased works within live or occupied environments with minimal disruption.

  • Strong understanding of design development, pre-construction activities and the relevant RIBA stages.

  • Ability to develop, manage and challenge construction programmes throughout the project lifecycle.

  • Strong commercial capability, including estimating, cost control, forecasting, procurement and change management.

  • Experience leading and developing direct and subcontracted teams.

  • Strong client relationship, communication and stakeholder management skills.

  • Ability to resolve delivery issues, manage escalations and make sound decisions under pressure.

  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Project, Excel, Word, Outlook, Teams and PowerPoint.

  • Understanding of health, safety and legislative requirements relevant to construction project delivery.

  • Willingness to travel between contract sites as required.

Desirable experience

  • Experience managing projects ranging from £10,000 to £500,000 within an account portfolio worth up to £3 million.

  • Experience within government, broadcasting or other complex operational estates.

  • Knowledge of NEC and other construction contract arrangements.

  • Experience delivering multidisciplinary projects combining M&E, HVAC, fit-out and building fabric works.

About you

You will be an organised, commercially minded leader who can manage several projects at different stages while maintaining clear oversight of delivery, risk and client expectations.

You will bring a practical, collaborative approach, supporting your team, resolving problems promptly and recognising when additional resources or specialist input are needed.

You will be committed to safe delivery, high-quality workmanship, client satisfaction and the continued development of your team.

title: DATA ARCHITECT - HYBRID
description:
Hiring Department

Division of Information Technology

Job Description

The Data Architect provides technical architecture leadership for Enterprise Data & Analytics (ED&A), helping design and implement the foundational data capabilities that support reporting, analytics, and institutional decision-making across the University of Missouri System.

This role is responsible for enterprise data architecture, reusable data products, semantic models, Common Data Layer (CDL) development, and Microsoft Fabric solutions. The Data Architect works closely with business stakeholders, analysts, analytics engineers, data engineers, and technology partners to translate business needs into scalable, secure, and sustainable technical solutions. The position serves as a hands-on architect who moves comfortably between strategy, solution design, and implementation while establishing reusable patterns and standards that can be leveraged across the institution.

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

• Lead the design and implementation of enterprise data architecture, reusable data products, semantic models, and Common Data Layer capabilities.

• Provide technical architecture leadership for strategic reporting, analytics, and data modernization initiatives.

• Design scalable and supportable solutions using Microsoft Fabric technologies, including lakehouses, warehouses, data pipelines, semantic models, and Power BI.

• Translate business requirements into technical architectures, implementation plans, and reusable solution patterns.

• Collaborate with analysts, analytics engineers, data engineers, and business partners to deliver enterprise data solutions.

• Establish architecture standards, data modeling practices, and technical guidance that promote consistency, reuse, and long-term sustainability.

• Support the design and implementation of enterprise data governance, metadata, lineage, and data access capabilities.

• Develop proofs of concept, reference architectures, and foundational components that reduce technical risk and accelerate delivery.

• Provide technical mentorship and architecture guidance across project teams.

• Evaluate emerging technologies and recommend approaches that enhance the University's enterprise data and analytics capabilities.

Shift

Monday - Friday, 8am - 5pm

Minimum Qualifications

• Must live within the state of Missouri

• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, or related field.

• Five (5) years of experience in data architecture, data engineering, analytics, business intelligence, or related disciplines.

• Experience with data modeling, SQL, data warehousing, and enterprise analytics solutions.

• Experience with cloud-based data platforms such as Microsoft Fabric, Azure, Snowflake, Databricks, or similar technologies.

• Knowledge of data governance, security, and enterprise data architecture principles.

• Experience translating business requirements into scalable technical solutions.

Preferred Qualifications

• Master's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Information Technology, Data Management, Engineering, or a related field.

• Experience in higher education, healthcare, government, or other large, complex organizations.

• Experience with Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, Azure, or similar cloud-based data and analytics platforms.

• Experience with enterprise data architecture, semantic modeling, data governance, reusable data products, or business intelligence solutions.

• Relevant certifications such as: Fabric Analytics Engineer Associate (DP-600) or Fabric Data Engineer Associate (DP-700)

title: Break Operations and Facilities Assistant (Student)
description:
Hiring Department

MU Housing

Job Description

MU Housing provides a world-class housing experience that engages residents within an innovative and educational environment that supports best on-campus housing practices and promotes success.

This position is designed to be operations-centered during the academic year break periods. This appointment requires commitment from students to remain available and responsive during a period of reduced staffing and commit to little to no travel during the designated break periods (e.g. Thanksgiving, Winter Break). This position primarily focuses on supporting desk operations, conducting facility walk-throughs, and performing room inspections across MU residential halls.

Housing Operations & Facility Assistants are a consistent presence in the halls during academic breaks. They are responsible for setting and role modeling expectations by abiding by and enforcing Housing and University guidelines and procedures. They must have a thorough understanding of emergency protocols and operational procedures.

MU Housing is a 365/24/7 operation, and the presence of Housing Operations & Facility Assistants is required to provide exceptional services and experiences for our residents during fall, winter, and spring break. This position will ONLY be scheduled during breaks, therefore requiring availability over academic break periods.

Essential Functions

The Housing Operations & Facility Assistant will perform all duties listed below as assigned in conjunction with other staff members:

  • Desk operations include answering the desk telephone, taking messages, processing mail and packages, assisting with check-in and check-out, answering questions from residents, and other duties as assigned.
  • Maintain a communication log.
  • Conduct resident room inspections as residents move out, documenting any and all damages or issues with the condition of the room.
  • Conduct full facility walk-throughs (interior and exterior) for safety, security, and weather preparedness. Submit work orders and incident reports for all found issues as appropriate.
  • Assist with building security and foster resident safety.
  • Assist with emergency facility situations as necessary and in emergent situations as applicable.
  • Maintain a high level of confidentiality at all times.

Additional Responsibilities

  • Provide operational and administrative support for MU residence halls.
  • Understand, abide by, and enforce policies and procedures for MU Housing.
  • Submit work orders to support residence hall cleanliness and facility safety and security.

Required Attendance and Participation

Housing Operations & Facility Assistants are expected and required to participate in the following:

  • November 18-19, 2026: Mandatory Training
  • November 21, 2026: First Scheduled Day of Work
  • Break Schedules:
    • November 23–30, 2025 (Thanksgiving Break)
    • December 21, 2025 – January 15, 2026 (Winter Break)
    • March 22–29, 2026 (Spring Break)
    • Scheduled team meetings

Campus operations are closed on December 25 and January 1.

Anticipated Hiring Range

$16.40 per hour, paid on a bi-weekly basis

Staff will provide essential hall presence through desk operations, facility checks, and inspections during break periods, committing to little to no travel during these breaks to ensure essential coverage.

Shift

  • Staff are expected to work an average of 35-40 hours per week.
  • This position does not include on-call duties.
  • Staff must report to work even during inclement weather.
  • This position operates during all university breaks throughout the academic year.

This position may require evening and weekend hours supporting activities and programs within the department. Occasionally division and campus projects may require additional hours outside of your normal schedule.

Minimum Qualifications

To be eligible for a student title, an individual must be enrolled at the University of Missouri. Enrollment in the summer session is not required if the student was enrolled in the Spring semester and is pre-enrolled for the Fall semester. Selection is contingent upon results of a review with the Office of Institutional Equity, Office of Student Accountability & Support, Office of the Vice Chancellor for Student Affairs, previous MU appointment history, and reference checks

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in housing or related field.
  • Prior Resident Advisor, Facility Security Assistant, and/or Desk Attendant experience preferred.
  • Preference given to students who live on campus.
  • Strong organizational skills, good time-management skills, reliability, a sense of commitment to the workplace, and the ability to work with a variety of people.
  • Have a positive and friendly disposition and demonstrated ability to professionally and articulately communicate.
  • Critically think through a variety of complex situations.
  • Availability to work a varied schedule (mornings, nights, weekends).

Benefit Eligibility

This is a student position and is not eligible for University benefits.

Equal Employment Opportunity

The University of Missouri is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

To request ADA accommodations, please call the Director of Accessibility and ADA at 573-884-7278.

title: Casual Security Officer
description:
About The Role:

Days of Working: This is a mobile, multi-site role, requiring flexibility to support operational needs around Plymouth, shift patterns will vary depending on site requirements.

As a Casual Security Officer, you will play a key role in maintaining a safe, secure and welcoming environment across a range of court and tribunal buildings within a defined area. - Oversees and performs very complex tasks in the area(s) of cataloging, acquisitions, circulation, reserve, reference and instruction

title: Senior Flight Test Aircraft Engineer
description:
Company Overview

Imagine a piloted air taxi that takes off vertically, then quietly carries you and your fellow passengers over the congested city streets below, enabling you to spend more time with the people and places that matter most. At Joby, we've been working to make that dream a reality since 2009 and we're now in the final stages of certifying our aircraft with the FAA. With plans to launch our aircraft in the US and Dubai, we're now scaling manufacturing and preparing for the launch of our commercial service.

Overview

As a Senior Flight Test Aircraft Engineer, you are the technical authority assigned to the Flight Test aircraft assets. Joining Joby’s Flight Test department, you will become integral to managing the experimental S4 fleet of aircraft routinely operated for research and development, show compliance and exhibition purposes. A Flight Test Aircraft Engineer interfaces directly with Maintenance, Engineering, Production, Quality, Airworthiness and Certification teams as the representative for the aircraft to coordinate work and troubleshoot technical challenges. The Aircraft Engineer plays a critical role in the Flight Test team being responsible for controlling the aircraft configuration and directly contributes to the safety and airworthiness of the platform.

Responsibilities

  • Serves as the aircraft’s primary technical liaison and the interface between the Flight Test team and the supporting engineering disciplines
  • Responsible for approving the hardware and software configuration changes on the aircraft and maintains the master Bill of Materials (BOM) and system configuration record
  • Coordinates, tracks and approves all work, including modifications, performed on the assigned aircraft
  • Manages the configuration documentation to ensure traceability to engineering specifications
  • Works collaboratively with Aircraft Quality Control and Certification Engineering to maintain conformity required for FAA Type Inspection Authorization (TIA)
  • Manages the aircraft weight and balance records to produce artifacts used for dispatch
  • Supports conformity and certification activities by providing accurate aircraft and equipment configuration data
  • Facilitates resolution of cross-functional technical issues affecting the aircraft
  • Represents and communicates the aircraft’s status and operational/test readiness to Flight Test operations and air crew
  • Manages the Safety of Flight compliance status of the as-configured aircraft and systems
  • Technical reviewer of all open non-conformances and discrepancies for Safety of Flight implications
  • Provides operational support whilst the assigned aircraft is dispatched to coordinate troubleshooting and facilitate on-demand configuration changes required for specific testing
  • Works directly with the Airworthiness team to ensure compliance to FAA Special Airworthiness Certificate requirements and manage the associated limitations
  • Conducts on-aircraft functional tests as well as rigging and actuator calibration procedures

Required

  • Bachelor of Science (Aerospace, Mechanical, Electrical Engineering or other technical field) degree or equivalent experience and training
  • Minimum of 8 years experience working in an aerospace environment
  • Experience working in or interfacing with aircraft maintenance, Flight Test and systems engineering functions
  • Excellent interpersonal skills to effectively communicate with colleagues across a wide range of technical disciplines
  • Exhibits strong technical leadership and ownership
  • Must be able to work both independently and on a team
  • Read and speak English proficiently
  • Able to accommodate required travel approximately 30% of duty

Desired

  • Experience as an Aircraft Manager on an experimental Flight Test Program, preferably including VTOL or STOVL and fly-by-wire platforms
  • Civil aircraft certification experience including use of ARP 4754 processes for requirements and FAA AC 23-8C or AC 27-1B for flight test
  • Familiarity with FAA Order 4040.26C
  • Familiarity with DO-178C and DO-160
  • Experience in managing a technical team and projects is highly desired

Additional Information

Compensation at Joby is a combination of base pay and Restricted Stock Units (RSUs). The target base pay for this position is $144,100 - $193,400/yr. The compensation package will be determined by job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.

Joby also offers a comprehensive benefits package, including paid time off, healthcare benefits, a 401(k) plan with a company match, an employee stock purchase plan (ESPP), short-term and long-term disability coverage, life insurance, and more.

Joby is an Equal Opportunity Employer
