title: Graphic Designer
description:
Hiring Department

Enrollment Management Communication

Job Description


Enrollment Marketing & Communications is seeking an experienced graphic designer to create compelling visual work that engages prospective students and supports the University of Missouri’s enrollment goals. This position will develop creative for integrated campaigns across print and digital channels, helping strengthen how students and families experience the Mizzou brand throughout the recruitment process.

The ideal candidate is a self-motivated designer who brings strong creative judgment, manages projects effectively and works well within a collaborative team.

This is an on-campus, in-person position.

Key Responsibilities:
1. Creative Development and Production
Develop original design concepts and produce creative materials for recruitment and enrollment initiatives. Projects may include print publications, direct mail, digital advertising, email graphics, social media content, signage, presentations and other marketing materials.

2. Project Execution and Creative Refinement
Translate project goals, audience needs and creative direction into effective visual communications. Manage assigned projects from initial concept through revisions, production and final delivery, incorporating feedback while maintaining the strength and purpose of the design.

3. Team and Campus Collaboration
Partner with EMC team and other department stakeholders to develop cohesive campaign materials. Contribute ideas during creative planning, follow established workflows and communicate clearly throughout each project.

4. Brand Stewardship and Quality Assurance
Apply university brand standards consistently while identifying opportunities to make enrollment communications distinctive and engaging. Review work carefully for visual quality, accuracy, consistency, accessibility and alignment with project objectives. Prepare files according to the technical requirements of each channel or vendor.

5. Creative Growth and Innovation
Stay informed about emerging design practices, creative technologies and trends across higher education, consumer marketing and digital media. Explore new tools, formats and approaches that can improve creative quality, strengthen collaboration and keep the team’s work fresh and relevant.

Shift

40 hours/week, some evening and weekend responsibilities may be required

Minimum Qualifications

A Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education and experience and at least 3 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessary

Preferred Qualifications

Prior graphic design experience is preferred

Anticipated Hiring Range

Salary: $$54,000-$58,000 per year.
Grade GGS - 10
University Title : Senior Strategic Communications Associate
To review the University of Missouri’s Staff Compensation Structure you can view the Job Code detail page. Internal applicants can determine their university title by accessing the Talent Profile tile in myHR.

Application Materials

Cover letter, resume, and design portfolio are required

Sponsorship Information

Employment visa sponsorship is not available for this position.

Community Information

Columbia offers small-town friendliness with big city features and a high quality of life for people of all ages and interests. Founded on education and known as an ideal college town, its location also makes it an attractive spot for businesses and travelers. Located on Interstate 70 and U.S. Highway 63, Columbia is right in the middle of the state and the nation. Just a couple hours’ drive from St. Louis and Kansas City, Columbia is Boone County’s largest population center offering big-city culture, activities, and resources with a low cost of living. Columbia is home to a variety of restaurants and entertainment venues and hosts more than a dozen festivals each year. title: Field Specialist in Agronomy – Franklin County, MO
description:
Hiring Department

University of Missouri (MU) Office of Extension and Engagement

MU Extension's Plant Health & Technology program

Job Description

MU TITLE: Assistant/Associate/Full Extension Professional

LOCATION: Union, Missouri, and primarily serves Franklin, Ste. Genevieve, St. Francois, and Washington

Counties in the East Central Region along with Jefferson, St. Louis Counties in the Urban East Region,

with additional service across the state as needed.

SPECIALIST EMPHASIS

The emphasis area for this position is agronomy, which includes the science of crops, forages, soils, weeds, insects, and pathogens. The position involves planning, implementing, and evaluating educational programs. Examples of agronomic programs in MU Extension include soil testing, precision agriculture, crop and hay production, pest monitoring, grazing systems, pesticide application, weed management, and disease management. The position also involves interacting with the farming community, including agronomic commodity groups, industry representatives, farm families, other university colleagues, and local and statewide elected officials

This position is a 12-month, ranked, non-tenure track appointment at the rank of assistant, associate, or full Extension Professional. Rank will be determined at the time of the appointment based on qualifications and experience in accordance with the MU Extension faculty standards. This position will hold the working title of Field Specialist In Agronomy.

As a Field Specialist, your workload distribution at appointment will be 90% Extension Teaching and 10% Traditional Service.

This appointment is renewable annually at the discretion of the University and workload distribution may change at the discretion of Extension leadership. Circumstances affecting continued employment include, but are not limited to, work performance, fund availability, and educational priorities.

CORE DUTIES OF MU EXTENSION SPECIALISTS

MU Extension Specialists deliver the University of Missouri to all Missourians. They serve all Missourians by bringing research-based solutions to work on local problems. MU Extension Specialists teach new and foundational concepts, link people to resources, support partner organizations, participate in research, train volunteers, evaluate programs, foster innovation, and serve communities. MU Extension Specialists work as a team to expand educational attainment, foster economic development, and improve health outcomes. These core duties fall into three major areas:

Educate, Create, and Connect.

  • Educate. MU Extension specialists design, conduct, and evaluate educational programs. MU Extension specialists teach research-based information via meetings, in-person and online courses, continuing education classes, technical assistance, volunteer training, media, websites, consultation, and other educational methods. They provide inclusive educational programs that support the individual, organizational, and community goals of Missouri’s learners and clients.
  • Create. MU Extension specialists develop innovative and research-informed educational products, services, materials, and other scholarly works. These include curricula, publications, presentations, educational tools, websites, and similar resources. MU Extension specialists obtain and use extramural funding to support creative works. MU Extension specialists contribute to the scholarship of Extension and Engagement by evaluating programs that result in learning and behavior changes that impact individuals and communities.
  • Connect. MU Extension specialists engage with learners, stakeholders, volunteers, and communities, including county extension councils, government officials and agencies, partners, and University and professional organizations. MU Extension specialists listen and respond with care. MU Extension specialists intentionally foster engaged partnerships and robust connections to the wide array of programs offered by the whole University of Missouri System.

Professional Expectations

  • Engage with councils, commissions, legislators, and stakeholders in all coverage counties to identify educational needs and then collaborate with appropriate internal and external partners to meet those needs.
  • Create an annual plan-of-work that reflects local needs and aligns with statewide program area efforts. Provide a monthly report of impact to county extension council assigned, supervisors, county commissioners and others, regarding programmatic efforts. Attend at least one county extension council meeting each month and provide an oral update on program efforts.
  • Collaborate with campus-based specialists on research projects and then deliver findings from those efforts via demonstrations, field days, courses, workshops, consultations, publications, and appropriate media.
  • Work in collaboration with other specialist in counties of responsibility to serve the needs of the headquartered county, ensuring counties receive promotional materials in advance of programming.
  • Effectively work with supervisors, other specialists, and local leaders to complete administrative tasks as needed.
  • Demonstrate competency in communication, educational programming, subject matter knowledge, educational delivery, volunteer management, grant acquisition, teamwork, interpersonal relations, organization knowledge, leadership, and professionalism.
  • Offer timely, research-based information during times of natural disasters or similar events.
  • Represent the University of Missouri on boards and committees as assigned.
  • Participate in professional development events to improve both technical and leadership skills.
  • Other duties and responsibilities as assigned to support the mission of MU Extension.

Additional Expectations

  • MU Extension programs often occur outside of normal business hours. MU Extension Specialists should expect to attend these events as needed to meet the needs of learners, clients, and stakeholders.
  • MU Extension Specialists travel regularly throughout Missouri and occasionally to out-of-state locations. MU Extension requires specialists to have a valid Missouri driver’s license, a legally operating vehicle, and wireless telephone/data service for university use. MU Extension specialists receive reimbursement for approved travel expenses, per University of Missouri policy.

MU EXTENSION LEADERSHIP RECEIVED

The Senior Program Director for Agriculture & Environment provides overall programmatic leadership. Programmatic supervision comes from the Education Director for the Plant Health & Technology program area and administrative oversight from the Regional Director for the East Central region.

MU EXTENSION INFORMATION

The University of Missouri (MU) Office of Extension and Engagement’s distinct land-grant mission is to improve lives, communities, and economies by producing relevant, reliable, and responsive educational strategies throughout Missouri. Our dedicated and knowledgeable specialists and staff collaborate with researchers and community leaders to develop and deliver programs that address the needs of Missourians, including educational attainment, economic development, and healthy people. For more information about MU Extension and Engagement, please visit .

UNIVERSITY INFORMATION

The University of Missouri, also known as Mizzou and MU, is the Flagship University of the four-campus University of Missouri System. It is one of the state’s land-grant universities. MU’s comprehensive undergraduate programs and its graduate, professional, and research programs attract an annual enrollment of more than 30,000 students. MU Extension and Engagement programs are located on all four campuses and in 114 counties and St. Louis city.

Qualifications

An earned master’s or Ph.D. with appropriate coursework demonstrating knowledge of Agronomy, Plant Sciences, Crop Sciences, Soil Sciences at the time of appointment.

Candidates will be evaluated on:

Oral and written communication skills.

Anticipated Hiring Range

Minimum starting salary of $58,000.00, salary will be commensurate with qualifications and experience of the applicant.

Application Materials

Complete the brief online application and be prepared to upload:

• Cover Letter

• Resume/CV

• Copies of all unofficial academic transcripts, and

• a list of 3-5 references

For questions regarding the online application process contact MUHR@missouri.edu or call 573.882.7976. For technical problems with the online application process contact Helpdesk@missouri.edu or call 573.882.5000.

description:
About The Role:

Working Hours: Monday to Friday, 08:00 - 16:30

About the Role

We are looking for a skilled and motivated Refrigeration & Air Conditioning Engineer to join our mobile technical services team. You will be responsible for the maintenance, repair and some installation works of a wide range of air conditioning, refrigeration, and mechanical systems across commercial sites.

Key Responsibilities

As a Mobile Refrigeration & Air Conditioning Engineer, you will be responsible for delivering high-quality technical services across a range of commercial environments. Your duties will include:

Technical Service & Maintenance

  • Carry out planned and reactive maintenance, servicing, and repairs on:
  • Split air conditioning systems
  • VRV/VRF systems
  • Air Handling Units (AHUs) and heat pumps
  • Commercial refrigeration equipment, including chilled cabinets, multidecks and light commercial systems
  • Diagnose faults and perform repairs on F-Gas infrastructure, electrical, and mechanical components, ensuring systems are restored to full functionality.

Compliance & Standards

  • Work in accordance with industry regulations, technical standards, and manufacturer guidelines.
  • Ensure all work complies with F-Gas & ODS regulations, Permit to Work procedures, and Health & Safety protocols.
  • Maintain safe working practices at all times, including when working at heights or in confined spaces.

Documentation & Reporting

Accurately complete:

  • Service documentation
  • Inspection reports
  • Maintenance logs
  • Remedial work records
  • Use handheld devices (PDA or mobile apps) to update job status, record findings, and communicate with internal teams.

Communication & Collaboration

  • Liaise professionally with clients, site contacts, and internal teams to ensure clear communication and minimal disruption to operations.
  • Work independently on assigned tasks and collaborate effectively within a small, supportive team.

Emergency Support

Requirements

  • Time-served apprenticeship in Air Conditioning/Refrigeration
  • City & Guilds Level 2/3 NVQ or equivalent in HVAC, Refrigeration, or Mechanical Engineering
  • F-Gas & ODS Regulations (Category 1 – 2079)

title: EDUCATIONAL RESOURCE COACH #00032897
description:
Hiring Department

South Central Regional Professional Develop Center

The Education Department at Missouri S&T prepares future educators through hands-on teacher education programs, bridging the gap between K-12 and university learning. Known for its collaborative, social atmosphere, the department encourages open communication, flexibility, and community-building through traditions like “Taste-test Tuesdays.” Faculty & Staff support one another through shared teaching insights, flexible schedules, and a strong emphasis on work-life balance. With resources like the Child Development Center and the South Central RPDC, the department provides opportunities for travel, professional growth, and community impact. Faculty engage in educational research and active learning, guiding students to become reflective, high-standard educators who contribute meaningfully to local schools and beyond.

Job Description

The purpose School-wide Positive Behavior Support (SW-PBS) Consultant is to assist Local Education Agencies (LEAs) in establishing and maintaining effective social/behavioral systems to improve academic performance and social behavior for all students. The expected outcome for this effort is to build the capacity of district level personnel, district and building administrators, and teachers to develop and sustain the SW-PBS framework by providing effective training, materials, and support services. In doing so, district leadership teams (DLTs) and building leadership teams (BLTs) will be formed. Teams will receive just-in time, just-as-needed training and support as they build multi-tiered systems of behavioral support.

Consultants/Specialists will:

  • Collaborate with DESE and SW-PBS Consultants throughout the state to provide consistent and high-quality standards for implementing the SW-PBS framework in districts and schools.
  • Collaborate with other DESE initiatives (e.g. DCI and DCI-MTSS) to provide effective and efficient supports to districts and schools.
  • Ensure all districts/buildings identified for recognition are districts/buildings that have signed partnership agreements and are currently implementing the work of the initiative. Professional Development Activities
  • Provide training and support to identified districts and schools implementing the MO SW PBS framework.
  • Assist identified districts and schools in monitoring and evaluating the fidelity and implementation level of the DW-PBS and/or SW-PBS framework using DESE-approved tools.
  • Assist LEAs in determining training needs and in procuring Regional Professional Development Center (RPDC) center personnel to provide High-Quality Professional Development (HQPD) for training on the identified set of effective educational practices.
  • Assist identified districts and schools in the collection and analysis of data.
  • Provide support, as indicated by LEA need, in leadership components of PBS.
  • Provide training and coaching, using DW-PBS and/or SW-PBS materials and resources collaboratively planned and coordinated with other RPDC consultants for identified district and school improvement.
  • SW-PBS Consultants may be expected to serve on a DCI Coaching Support Team (CST) to provide training and coaching on SW-PBS activities, as assigned by DESE. All Trainings: All trainings provided must be advertised using the same title and description provided by DESE to ensure consistency across the state. Individuals are expected to participate in developing, refining, and/or revising training and support materials when requested by the SW-PBS State Coordinator or DESE. Individuals are expected to participate in team coaching practices including coaching preparation, facilitation of feedback and solution dialogue, and adhere to an established plan of coaching.
  • Participate in trainings for newly hired SW-PBS consultants, as requested by SW-PBS State Coordinator. Attend and actively participate in statewide monthly resource, support, and training meetings, as designated by the master calendar. Attend, participate, and present at the annual Summer Institute as requested. Participate in state professional development opportunities applicable to SW-PBS as requested and approved.

Required Travel: Positive Behavior Support Consultantsw are limited to travel inside their region and neighboring RPDC regions with the exception of attendance at DESE-required activities/meetings/conferences.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and experience and at least 2 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessary.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Psychology, behavior analysis, and factors that affect application of behavior principles in schools for all students
  • Classroom management
  • Function-based thinking (FBT) and Functional Behavior Assessment (FBA)
  • Behavior Intervention Plans (BIP) Effective meeting management and processes/protocols
  • Curriculum development
  • Coaching, presenting, consulting, and facilitating skills
  • Conflict resolution and problem-solving processes
  • Leadership skills
  • Use of technology to enhance professional development including virtual technologies and synchronous, online instruction
  • Development of high-quality professional development
  • Accurate and timely preparation of reports and progress logs o Effective communication skills including face-to-face, virtual communication, and use of social media o Family and community involvement

Anticipated Hiring Range

The anticipated hiring range for this position has been established as $53,976 - $69,576 annually.

Salary is determined by a variety of factors, including but not limited to, the individual’s particular combination of education, skills, and experience, as well as organizational requirements.

Your total compensation goes beyond the number on your paycheck. The University of Missouri provides generous leave, health plans, and retirement contributions that add to your bottom line.

Community Information

University Information
Missouri S&T is one of the nation's leading research universities with over 100-degree programs in 39 disciplines. It was founded in 1870 as one of the first technological institutions west of the Mississippi River. Located about 100 miles west of St. Louis in the vibrant community of Rolla, Missouri S&T is an accessible, safe, and friendly campus surrounded by Ozarks' scenery. Missouri S&T offers undergraduate degrees in engineering, the sciences, liberal arts, humanities, and business, with M.S. and Ph.D. programs available in many of the science and engineering programs. With over 7,000 students and 300 faculty, Missouri S&T is big enough to accommodate a broad population, yet small enough for individuals to build high visibility and impactful careers.

KUMMER COLLEGE
Established in 2022, The Kummer College serves as a pathbreaking model for social impact, technology transfer, and interdisciplinary collaboration within a future-oriented STEM-focused university. Supported by the Kummer Institute Foundation at Missouri S&T, this unique college integrates key academic, co-curricular, and administrative activities related to technology commercialization, business innovation and entrepreneurship, systems thinking, and economic development. Within The Kummer College lives several departments: Department of Business and Information Technology (BIT), Department of Economics, Department of Engineering Management and Systems Engineering (EMSE) and Kummer Student Programs.

COLLEGE of ENGINEERING & COMPUTING (CEC)
Missouri S&T’s College of Engineering and Computing is the largest of three colleges at S&T, accounting for approximately 80% of the total enrollment (about 4,500 undergraduates and 800 graduate students). The college includes more than 170 ranked faculty members who serve in 16 undergraduate programs, all with master’s and doctoral equivalents organized into nine academic departments. The college recently added a bachelor’s degree in biomedical engineering and a Ph.D. in bioengineering, both starting in fall 2024. Missouri S&T, supported by the College of Engineering and Computing, is nationally recognized for its career outcomes and ROI.

COLLEGE of ARTS, SCIENCES, & EDUCATION (CASE)
The College of Arts, Sciences, and Education is a catalyst of innovation, creativity, and discovery, where students and faculty work side-by-side to create and share knowledge and understanding. From arts and humanities to the natural and social sciences, the College of Arts, Sciences, and Education has a program for everyone. The College of Arts, Sciences, and Education (CASE) is made up of eleven units including Air Force ROTC, Army ROTC, Arts, Languages and Philosophy, Biological Sciences, Chemistry, English and Technical Communication, History and Political Science, Mathematics and Statistics, Physics, Psychological Science, and Education. The college is home to over 90 tenured/tenure-track and 44 non-tenure-track faculty members. CASE offers more than 85 different academic options including certificates, minors, bachelor’s, master’s, and doctoral degrees.

About Rolla
Rolla, Missouri offers several great advantages that help individuals enjoy a high quality of life. Rolla is an ideal place for families, with its low cost of living, excellent schools, safe neighborhoods, and a range of recreational activities suitable for all ages. The Ozark Scenic Riverways and beautiful landscapes offers abundant opportunities for outdoor enthusiasts of every lifestyle. With its vibrant community, Rolla hosts multiple events, concerts, art exhibitions, and theater performances throughout the year. The university’s Leach Theatre showcases nationally renowned performers for campus and community alike. Overall, living in Rolla offers a high quality of life with a supportive community, affordable living, beautiful natural surroundings, and numerous opportunities for personal and professional growth.

The Department of Management in the Trulaske College of Business at University of Missouri (MU)

Job Description

The Department of Management in the Trulaske College of Business at University of Missouri (MU) invites applicants with excellent teaching credentials in the areas of Analytics, Operations, and/or Supply Chain Management (SCM) to join our team at all levels for a non-tenure track (NTT), full-time teaching position. The person selected must be available to start teaching undergraduate and/or master’s level courses no later than August 2027. The successful candidate is expected to assume active service roles related to undergraduate and MBA curriculum development and academic program performance at department and college levels.

Qualifications

Candidates must have a PhD in a relevant discipline, or a Masters Degree and work experience of at least five years in the related field or function. Highest degree earned should be from an AACSB-accredited business school or other closely related program (e.g., Industrial Engineering). Prior industry and professional knowledge/experience in the areas of Analytics, Operations and/or SCM; a record or demonstrable evidence of excellence in teaching; industry experience; evidence of collaborative team participation. Relevant industry or professional certifications.

Candidates will be evaluated on key skills sought including: ability to engage students in both large and small section formats and in both face-to-face and 100% online formats; effective use of a variety of assessment methods; currency in analytics, operations management, and/or supply chain management; effective training of and coordination

Letter of Interest, Curriculum Vita and evidence of teaching effectiveness. title: Behavioral Resource & Referral Specialist Lead – Center for Child Well Being
description:
Hiring Department

Department of Psychiatry

Job Description

The Center for Child Well-Being, housed within the Department of Psychiatry in the University of Missouri School of Medicine, seeks a Lead for the Behavioral Resource and Referral Specialist Team in Psychiatry Access Programs.

The ideal candidate will be an experienced team leader who has progressive experience in delivering behavioral health services. They will be skilled at building relationships with patients, families, providers, and community partners. They will have strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills, with the ability to assess individual needs and identify appropriate behavioral health resources.

Excellent communication, sound judgment, and the ability to navigate complex challenges are essential. This position exercises independent judgment in guiding program implementation and day-to-day operations while ensuring alignment with funding requirements, project goals, and organizational priorities.

About the Center

The Center for Child Well-Being drives positive change for children and families through innovative programs, collaborative community partnerships, and strategic capacity building. Guided by our mission to improve outcomes for young children and their families, we envision a future where all children have a strong foundation for lifelong health.

Working at the Center means being part of a passionate, collaborative team committed to impact. Staff are supported in their professional growth, empowered to contribute meaningfully, and engaged in work that is purpose-driven and community-centered. Join us in shaping a more responsive and resilient childhood systems landscape across Missouri!

Key Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

Team Leadership and Supervision

  • Supervise a team of professional staff (currently 4-6 full-time employees) responsible for responding to MHAP/MO-CPAP calls and requests, completing intake and triage, coordinating referrals, and conducting follow-up with patients and families.
  • Foster a collaborative, high-performing team culture grounded in accountability, communication, and continuous improvement.
  • Maintain clear and consistent communication with team members regarding program priorities, expectations, changes, and operational needs.
  • Participate in program and Center meetings and communicate relevant information and decisions to team members.
  • Provide coaching, performance feedback, and accountability; address performance concerns appropriately; and support professional development and growth.
  • Support workforce planning, hiring, onboarding, and team development in collaboration with Center leadership and appropriate University partners.
  • Delegate responsibilities effectively and establish clear expectations, roles, and accountability within the team.
  • Build effective working relationships with internal colleagues and external partners to support coordinated services and program operations.

Program Operations and Workflow Management

  • Oversee day-to-day Resource & Referral team operations to ensure timely and appropriate response to calls, requests, intakes, referrals, and follow-up activities
  • Monitor team workload, coverage, and workflow and make adjustments as needed to maintain service responsiveness and program capacity.
  • Identify operational challenges, develop & implement solutions.
  • Support implementation of program changes, new workflows, and process improvements and ensure team members understand and consistently apply updated expectations.
  • Maintain and reinforce standardized processes that support efficient, consistent, and high-quality service delivery.
  • Serve as a point of escalation for complex referrals, challenging situations, service barriers, and other issues requiring additional consultation or judgment.
  • Collaborate with the Program Leads and Center leadership to address operational issues and support effective program implementation.

Quality Assurance and Compliance

  • Monitor team performance and work products to promote accuracy, timeliness, consistency, and quality.
  • Ensure staff maintain accurate, timely, and HIPAA-compliant electronic case documentation, including referral, follow-up, and outcome information.
  • Support adherence to HIPAA, health and safety regulations, contractual requirements, and organizational policies and procedures.
  • Identify trends, gaps, and opportunities for improvement in service delivery and documentation and work with staff to address them.
  • Participate in quality improvement activities and contribute to the development and refinement of program processes, resources, and procedures.

Service Delivery and Program Support

  • Maintain sufficient working knowledge of MHAP/MO-CPAP services, workflows, referral processes, and statewide mental and behavioral health resources to effectively supervise and support the team.
  • Provide consultation and problem-solving support to staff related to screening, triage, referrals, provider scheduling, follow-up, and complex resource needs.
  • Periodically participate in direct service activities, calls, or other program functions as needed to maintain operational knowledge, support coverage, and respond to program needs.
  • Support staff in developing individualized resource options based on patient and family needs, geographic location, and available mental health, behavioral health, and substance use resources.
  • Promote a responsive, respectful, and service-oriented approach that supports engagement and satisfaction among patients, families, and referral partners.

Resources, Data, and Process Improvement

  • Oversee team efforts to maintain accurate and current statewide mental and behavioral health resource information, including identifying, vetting, and updating available resources
  • Support the development and maintenance of program resources, materials, policies, data, and processes.
  • Monitor team-level data and performance information to identify trends, inform workflow decisions, and support continuous quality improvement.
  • Contribute to programmatic updates, process improvement initiatives, and implementation of program changes.
  • Partner with the Program Leads and evaluation team, as appropriate, to support accurate data collection and reporting and to use information to improve program performance.

Other

  • Perform other duties as assigned

Work Hours:

  • Please note that this position requires some after-hours and weekend shifts to provide full coverage for our resource access hotline. Hours may shift on a weekly basis.

Master's degree in psychology, counseling, marriage and family therapy, or social work and relevant licensure (or eligible to be licensed within 12 months) within the State of Missouri.

Education: LCSW or LPC.

title: Field Specialist in Agricultural Business and Urban Agriculture – Jefferson County, MO
description:
Hiring Department

University of Missouri (MU) Office of Extension and Engagement

Agricultural and Business Policy Program

Job Description

MU TITLE: Assistant/Associate/Full Extension Professional

LOCATION: Hillsboro, Missouri, and primarily serves Jefferson, St. Charles, St. Louis Counties and the City of St. Louis in the Urban East Region with additional service across the state as needed.

Specialist Emphasis

The emphasis area for this position is Agricultural Business and Urban Agriculture. This position will plan, teach, and evaluate educational programs that help farm and food businesses start, grow, and succeed in the St. Louis area. The position will mainly serve Jefferson, St. Charles, St. Louis Counties and the City of St. Louis in the Urban East Region.

This position will focus on business planning, marketing, risk management, and related support for urban and nearby agricultural businesses. The specialist may work with urban farms, small farms, market gardeners, beginning farmers, nonprofit agriculture groups, community farms, food entrepreneurs, local food businesses, value-added food producers, and other agricultural businesses that serve city and metro-area markets.

MU Extension Agricultural Business programs help people make better business decisions. Topics may include farm and business financial management, business plans, budgets, marketing plans, feasibility studies, pricing, recordkeeping, taxes, regulations, risk management, access to loans or grants, land access, leases, farm transition, value-added agriculture, and tools that help businesses start, expand, diversify, or become more profitable.

The specialist should also help clients understand and use new technologies that fit urban agriculture. This may include controlled-environment agriculture, high tunnels, small-scale irrigation systems, hydroponics, aquaponics, sensors, farm management software, online marketing tools, digital recordkeeping, food safety technology, and other tools that help urban farms improve production, efficiency, marketing, and profitability.

The specialist should provide technical assistance, often with state specialists and local partners. This work may support business plans, marketing plans, feasibility studies, surveys, enterprise analysis, grant or loan readiness, and other tools needed by producers, entrepreneurs, organizations, and agricultural businesses. The specialist will also help connect clients with the right regional and statewide partners when new business or economic development opportunities arise.

Educational programs may include in-person workshops, urban farm tours, field demonstrations, one-on-one visits, short courses, technical assistance projects, online programs, publications, decision tools, and media. Programs should provide research-based information that local clients can use. Strong programming will combine agricultural business knowledge with a clear understanding of the opportunities and challenges facing urban agriculture in a large metro area.

This position involves interacting with the agricultural and food systems community, including producers, farm families, urban growers, entrepreneurs, community organizations, industry representatives, local food system partners, municipalities, economic development organizations, local and statewide elected officials, and University colleagues from Missouri and the Midwest.

This position is a 12-month, ranked, non-tenure track appointment at the rank of assistant, associate, or full Extension Professional. Rank will be determined at the time of the appointment based on qualifications and experience in accordance with the MU Extension faculty standards. This position will hold the working title of Field Specialist in Agricultural Business and Urban Agriculture.

As a Field Specialist, your workload distribution at appointment will be 90% Extension Teaching and 10% Traditional Service.

This appointment is renewable annually at the discretion of the University and workload distribution may change at the discretion of Extension leadership. Circumstances affecting continued employment include, but are not limited to, work performance, fund availability, and educational priorities.

CORE DUTIES OF MU EXTENSION SPECIALISTS

MU Extension Specialists deliver the University of Missouri to all Missourians. They serve all Missourians by bringing research-based solutions to work on local problems. MU Extension Specialists teach new and foundational concepts, link people to resources, support partner organizations, participate in research, train volunteers, evaluate programs, foster innovation, and serve communities. MU Extension Specialists work as a team to expand educational attainment, foster economic development, and improve health outcomes. These core duties fall into three major areas:

Educate, Create, and Connect.

  • Educate. MU Extension specialists design, conduct, and evaluate educational programs. MU Extension specialists teach research-based information via meetings, in-person, and online courses, continuing education classes, technical assistance, volunteer training, media, websites, consultation, and other educational methods. They provide educational programs that support the individual, organizational, and community goals of Missouri’s learners and clients.
  • Create. MU Extension specialists develop innovative and research-informed educational products, services, materials, and other scholarly works. These include curricula, publications, presentations, educational tools, websites, and similar resources. MU Extension specialists obtain and use extramural funding to support creative works. MU Extension specialists contribute to the scholarship of Extension and Engagement by evaluating programs that result in learning and behavior changes that impact individuals and communities.
  • Connect. MU Extension specialists engage with learners, stakeholders, volunteers, and communities, including county extension councils, government officials and agencies, partners, and University and professional organizations. MU Extension specialists listen and respond with care. MU Extension specialists intentionally foster engaged partnerships and robust connections to the wide array of programs offered by the whole University of Missouri System.

Professional Expectations

  • Engage with stakeholders in all coverage counties to identify educational needs and then collaborate with appropriate internal and external partners to meet programming needs, incorporating timely marketing strategies.
  • Create an annual plan-of-work that reflects local needs and aligns with statewide program area efforts. Provide a monthly report for assigned county extension councils, supervisors, county commissioners and others, regarding programmatic efforts. Attend at least one county extension council meeting each month and provide a program review with feedback and analysis for the respective coverage area.
  • Collaborate with campus-based specialists on research projects and then deliver findings from those efforts via demonstrations, field days, courses, workshops, consultations, publications, and appropriate media.
  • Effectively work with supervisors, other specialists, and local leaders to complete administrative tasks as needed to support county efforts.
  • Demonstrate competency in communication, educational programming, subject matter knowledge, educational delivery, volunteer management, grant acquisition, teamwork, interpersonal relations, organization knowledge, leadership, and professionalism.
  • Offer timely, research-based information during times of natural disasters or unexpected catastrophic events.
  • Represent the University of Missouri on boards and committees for assigned program area.
  • Participate in professional development events to improve both technical and leadership skills.
  • Other duties and responsibilities as assigned to support the mission of MU Extension.

Additional Expectations

  • MU Extension Specialists travel regularly throughout Missouri and occasionally to out-of-state locations. MU Extension requires specialists to have a valid Missouri driver’s license, a legally operating vehicle, and wireless telephone/data service for university use. MU Extension specialists receive reimbursement for approved travel expenses, per University of Missouri policy.
  • MU Extension programs often occur outside of normal business hours. MU Extension Specialists should expect to attend these events as needed to meet the needs of learners, clients, and stakeholders.

MU EXTENSION LEADERSHIP RECEIVED

The Senior Program Director for Agriculture and Environment provides overall programmatic leadership. Programmatic supervision comes from the Education Director for the Agricultural and Business Policy Program with administrative oversight from the Regional Director for the Urban East Region.

MU EXTENSION INFORMATION

The University of Missouri (MU) Office of Extension and Engagement’s distinct land-grant mission is to improve lives, communities, and economies by producing relevant, reliable, and responsive educational strategies throughout Missouri. Our dedicated and knowledgeable specialists and staff collaborate with researchers and community leaders to develop and deliver programs that address the needs of Missourians, including educational attainment, economic development, and healthy people. For more information about MU Extension and Engagement, please visit .

UNIVERSITY INFORMATION

The University of Missouri, also known as Mizzou and MU, is the Flagship University of the four-campus University of Missouri System. It is one of the state’s land-grant universities. MU’s comprehensive undergraduate programs and its graduate, professional, and research programs attract an annual enrollment of more than 30,000 students. MU Extension and Engagement programs are located on all four campuses and in 114 counties and St. Louis city.

Qualifications

Academic qualifications include an earned master’s degree, MBA, Ph.D., or other applicable terminal degree in agricultural economics, agricultural business, agricultural marketing, business administration, business management, finance, urban agriculture, food systems, community development, or a closely related field at time of appointment.

Candidates will be evaluated on:

Knowledge of agricultural business, farm financial management, enterprise development, marketing, risk management, and/or local food systems.

Experience working with diverse audiences, including producers, entrepreneurs, community organizations, public agencies, nonprofit organizations, and agricultural or food-based businesses.

Understanding of urban agriculture, small-scale farming, local food systems, direct marketing, and the opportunities and constraints facing agricultural enterprises in metropolitan areas.

Ability to provide practical technical assistance in business plans, marketing plans, feasibility studies, enterprise budgets, pricing strategies, recordkeeping, grant or financing readiness, and related decision-making tools.

Effective and innovative teaching strategies that engage others, including strong listening, written, and oral communication skills.

Ability to collaborate with Extension colleagues, community partners, local governments, economic development organizations, and agricultural support entities.

Anticipated Hiring Range

This position offers a minimum starting salary of $58,000, with the final salary determined based on the candidate’s qualifications and experience.

Application Materials

Complete the brief online application and be prepared to upload:

• Cover Letter

• Resume/CV

• Copies of all unofficial academic transcripts, and

• a list of 3-5 references

For questions regarding the online application process contact MUHR@missouri.edu or call 573.882.7976. For technical problems with the online application process contact Helpdesk@missouri.edu or call 573.882.5000.

title: Library Information Specialist Music/Media Late Night and Weekend Supervisor, University Libraries
description:
Hiring Department

University Libraries

Job Description

This .75 FTE position works at the Music/Media desk on the ground floor of the Miller Nichols Library and reports to the Head of Music/Media. This position is in charge of the Music/Media area and ground floor during work shifts, provides circulation assistance and basic reference service, independently applies policies and procedures, indirectly supervises student assistants, and performs other Music/Media duties. This position also works with security officers assigned to the building, Circulation Services, and the UMKC Police to maintain a safe, secure environment for library patrons and is responsible for closing the Music/Media Library Thursday-Sunday.

Position Duties:

Provides friendly, efficient assistance to patrons and resolves problems in the Music/Media unit that cannot be resolved at lower levels (i.e. by student assistants.) Independently applies and interprets policies and procedures at point of need. Refers problems that cannot be resolved at the LIS level to a Music/Media LIS SR or the Head of Music/Media. This will generally be a referral for resolution at a later time due to the position’s work schedule.

Oversees Music/Media desk functions and assists/oversees student assistants in providing services at this desk, communicating effectively with library patrons, supervisor, and other library staff.

  • Answers directional and circulation questions.
  • Assists patrons with printing, scanning, and basic production software issues in the Music/Media lab, including lifting paper reams, stooping and bending to troubleshoot printer problems, etc.
  • Answers basic music, media, and dance reference questions. Recognizes and refers questions that require additional expertise.
  • Maintains the safety and security of the Miller Nichols Library ground floor, including the MNL north entrance, during scheduled shifts. Works with security officer assigned to building, Circulation Services, and UMKC Police to maintain safe, secure environment for library patrons. Provides backup support to first floor circulation desk in safety and security issues. Stays current on training and privacy guidelines related to access to all MNL security cameras, consulting them in case of security issues. Reports facility issues during scheduled shift. Secures ground floor at closing.
  • Documents and communicates situations and issues that occur during work shifts to Music/Media and other colleagues, in accordance with Libraries and Music/Media policies and procedures, including the Libraries’ Safe and Respectful Environment policy.
  • Performs detail-oriented project work, following detailed written and oral instructions, completing repetitive work accurately, and differentiating detailed information. Stays current with Microsoft Office software, especially Excel, producing and/or reviewing a variety of library materials, written correspondence, reports, and related materials in both electronic and hard copy form.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

Professional development and service:

  • Participates on appropriate committees and professional development as defined by and with the approval of their Supervisor.
  • Maintains sufficient expertise in skills and proficiencies required by the position.

Shift

This position works Thursday-Sunday and is responsible for supervising the Music/Media desk during work hours and closing the Music/Media Library Thursday-Sunday. Hours fluctuate during breaks/intersessions and the eight-week summer session. The position will occasionally cover other shifts in the absence of other employees. Any permanent schedule changes must be approved by the Supervisor. This position’s hours are:

  • Fall & Spring semesters:
    • Thursday, 4:15 p.m. – 12:15 a.m.
    • Friday, 2:15 p.m. – 10:15 p.m.
    • Saturday, 4:15 p.m. – 10:15 p.m.
    • Sunday, 4:15 p.m. – 12:15 a.m.
  • Eight-week summer session:
    • Sunday: 2:15 p.m. - 10:15 p.m.
    • Thursday, 2:15 p.m. – 10:15 p.m.
    • Friday, 10:15 a.m. – 6:15 p.m.
    • Saturday, 12:15 p.m. – 6:15 p.m.
  • Intersessions (4 weeks Dec/Jan, 1 week spring break, 3 weeks May, 3 weeks Aug):
    • Tuesday: 11:15 a.m. - 7:15 p.m.
    • Wednesday: 11:15 a.m. - 7:15 p.m.
    • Thursday, 11:15 a.m. – 7:15 p.m.
    • Friday, 12:15 p.m. – 6:15 p.m.

Minimum Qualifications

High school diploma or equivalent and at least 2 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessary.

Preferred Qualifications

  • One to two years’ experience in a library setting
  • Successful supervisory experience
  • Successful customer service experience
  • Knowledge of music and the performing arts, including the ability to read music, at a level usually acquired through formal study or education

Anticipated Hiring Range

The anticipated hiring range for this position has been established as $16.56 -$18.00/hourly. In addition, this position is eligible for a $1.00 shift differential for eligible hours. See HR-213 Shift Differential for more information. Salary is determined by a variety of factors, including but not limited to, the individual’s particular combination of education, skills, and experience, as well as organizational requirements.

Your total compensation goes beyond the number on your paycheck. The University of Missouri provides generous leave, health plans, and retirement contributions that add to your bottom line.

Grade: Salary Plan # 006
University Title: LIBRARY INFORMATION SPECIALIST
To review the University of Missouri’s Staff Compensation Structure you can view the Job Code detail page. Internal applicants can determine their university title by accessing the Talent Profile tile in myHR.

Application Deadline

Application review will begin on October 12, 2026. Applications will be accepted until this position is filled.


Sponsorship Information

Employment visa sponsorship is not available for this position.

Other Information

Supervisory Authority:

In the absence of other Music/Media staff members, indirectly supervises Music/Media Student Assistants including assigning tasks and training on basic skills. Provides input to the Music/Media Daytime Supervisor regarding student assistant performance during late night and weekend shifts.

Community Information

Kansas City offers the best of both worlds—a vibrant, urban community with Midwestern appeal. The city’s rich history and its modern-day, innovative thinking come together to create an eclectic group of neighborhoods that offer a little something for everyone. From thriving arts districts, an energetic downtown nightlife, casual to upscale shopping and champion sports teams, you will have no problem making yourself at home. Of course, one of Kansas City’s biggest claims to fame is its food, especially its world-famous barbecue. Foodies will delight in the culinary scene found throughout the city. title: Unity Construct System Administrator
description:
Hiring Department

Operations Administration

Job Description

The Unity Construct System Administrator will serve as the primary contact for MU Campus Unity Connect users. This role is responsible for system configuration, modification of data fields and templates, providing support and training to both internal and external users, and addressing user needs in a timely and professional manner. Additionally, the Administrator will collaborate with system-level Unity Construct teams, campus PeopleSoft programmers, and vendor-contracted staff to ensure smooth operation and integration of the Unity Construct system. The role includes report development, data extraction, and adherence to MU and System policies.

Key Responsibilities:

1. Unity Construct System Responsibilities: Set up and manage projects within Unity Construct.
Maintain and update templates (documents, budgets, schedules, mail merges, etc.).
Implement MU-specific configuration changes as needed.
Collaborate with fiscal staff and programmers to maintain the PeopleSoft/Unity Construct interface.
Provide technical support to users.
Review monthly and quarterly product release notes to stay updated on new functionalities.
Ensure system practices align with MU and System policies.

2. Training and Documentation:
Develop, update, and maintain training manuals specific to MU processes.
Deliver in-person and virtual training sessions for internal and external new users.
Provide ongoing refresher training and one-on-one training as needed.
Educate users on new product functionalities and system enhancements.

3. Reporting and Data Management:
Understand MU’s and the industry’s specific reporting and data requirements.
Develop recurring and ad hoc reports as requested.
Maintain ongoing reports and ensure timely delivery to MU and System leadership.

4. Communication and Collaboration:
Respond promptly and professionally to inquiries from internal users, co-workers, and external users.
Collaborate regularly with System Unity Construct Administrators and users to maintain consistent practices.
Build relationships with other power users at MU, System, and other universities to share best practices and gather system improvement insights.

5. Other Duties:
Perform additional tasks as assigned by leadership.

Shift

7:30 a.m. - 4:00 p.m., Monday thru Friday

Minimum Qualifications

A Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education and experience and at least 5 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessary

Preferred Qualifications

Prefer administrative experience with Unity Construct (e-Builder) and/or PeopleSoft accounting experience

Must possess and maintain a valid State of Missouri driver's license or a valid out-of-state driver's license with the understanding a Missouri driver's license must be obtained within the first six months of employment.

Salary Range: $74,000.00 - $85,000.00 per year

title: Fabric Estimator
description:
About The Role:

OCS is looking for an experienced Fabric Estimator with a strong background in construction fit-out, refurbishment and building-fabric projects.

Working closely with our Pre-Construction, Commercial, Design and Operational teams, you will manage estimates and tenders from the initial enquiry through to final submission and project handover.

You will prepare accurate, detailed and commercially competitive estimates across a range of fabric packages, including:

  • Internal fit-out and refurbishment
  • Partitions and ceilings
  • Flooring and finishes
  • Joinery
  • Decorations
  • Associated building works

Key Responsibilities

  • Review tender enquiries, drawings, specifications and contract documentation.
  • Complete detailed quantity take-offs for fabric, fit-out and refurbishment works.
  • Prepare accurate estimates covering labour, materials, plant and subcontractor packages.
  • Issue enquiries to suppliers and specialist subcontractors.
  • Analyse quotations and ensure all relevant costs are included within the tender.
  • Identify tender assumptions, exclusions, commercial risks and opportunities.
  • Attend site visits, tender review meetings and commercial discussions.
  • Contribute to bid strategy, value-engineering exercises and cost-saving proposals.
  • Prepare and submit accurate, compliant and competitive tenders within agreed deadlines.
  • Maintain reliable estimating records, cost information and tender documentation.
  • Develop effective relationships with clients, suppliers and subcontractors.
  • Produce clear handover information for successful tenders and present this to the project delivery team.
  • Support post-tender clarifications and negotiations when required.

About You

To be successful in this role, you will need:

  • Previous experience as an Estimator within the construction industry.
  • Demonstrable estimating experience across fit-out, refurbishment or building-fabric projects.
  • Strong knowledge of relevant construction methods, materials, labour requirements and subcontractor packages.
  • Experience completing quantity take-offs from technical drawings and specifications.
  • The ability to prepare detailed tender estimates and evaluate supplier and subcontractor quotations.
  • A good understanding of procurement, commercial risk and contract requirements.
  • Excellent attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple tender deadlines.
  • Confident communication skills when working with clients, operational teams and supply-chain partners.
  • Proficiency in estimating software and Microsoft Office, particularly Excel.

Desirable Experience

  • Experience estimating projects within healthcare or other live operational environments.
  • Previous main-contractor or M&E contractor experience.
  • Knowledge of value engineering and tender risk management.
  • A relevant construction, estimating or commercial qualification, such as an HNC, HND or degree.
  • Experience supporting tender presentations and post-tender interviews.

title: Document Controller
description:
About The Role:

We are looking for an experienced Document Controller to support the effective delivery of building services and project works. You will be responsible for managing and maintaining project documentation throughout the project lifecycle, ensuring information is accurate, controlled and issued in accordance with company and client requirements.

Key Responsibilities

  • Maintain project document control systems, registers and records.
  • Manage the receipt, distribution, filing and archiving of project documentation.
  • Control drawings, revisions and technical information, ensuring the latest versions are available.
  • Maintain drawing registers, transmittal logs and document trackers.
  • Track document submissions, reviews, approvals and outstanding actions.
  • Prepare document transmittals, status reports and project information.
  • Support project teams with reporting and general project administration.
  • Maintain information using EDMS platforms such as Aconex, Asite, Viewpoint, SharePoint, Procore or Autodesk Construction Cloud.
  • Support ISO 9001 processes, document audits and quality/compliance checks.
  • Liaise with clients, consultants, contractors and suppliers regarding documentation requirements.
  • Provide guidance to project teams on document control processes and procedures.
  • Coordinate project handover documentation, including as-built drawings and O&M manuals.
  • Ensure completed project records are accurately archived and retained.

About You

You will have previous Document Controller experience within construction, building services, engineering or FM, together with a good understanding of project documentation and information-management processes.

You will ideally have:

  • Previous experience using an electronic document management system (EDMS).
  • Experience controlling drawings, technical documents and revisions.
  • Knowledge of document registers, transmittals and approval workflows.
  • Experience supporting project handover and close-out documentation.
  • Good Microsoft Office skills.
  • Excellent attention to detail and organisational skills.
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to work with multiple project stakeholders.
  • An understanding of quality assurance and controlled-document processes.

Key Skills

Document Control | Version Control | Information Management | EDMS | Drawing Control | Quality Assurance | Project Administration | O&M Manuals | Project Handover | Stakeholder Management

title: POST DOCTORAL FELLOW- Chemistry #00098294
description:
Hiring Department

Chemistry

Job Description

The Department of Chemistry at Missouri S&T is seeking a highly motivated and accomplished Postdoctoral Fellow to join the research group of Dr. Pericles Stavropoulos. The successful candidate will contribute to advanced research projects requiring organic and inorganic synthesis and applications to atom/group-transfer catalysis along with mechanistic elucidation.


Key Responsibilities:

The successful candidate will design and execute synthetic organic chemistry reactions for the purpose of synthesizing suitable ligands. The candidate will further execute metalation reactions to generate potential catalysts and evaluate their efficacy in C-H amination reactions. The candidate will also participate in mechanistic investigations, involving physical organic/inorganic techniques. Responsibilities include purifying and characterizing reaction products using standard laboratory procedures (e.g., column purification, application of NMR, UV-vis, HPLC, MS, XRD) and maintaining precise laboratory records documenting experimental procedures. The candidate will assist in mentoring graduate and undergraduate researchers in the group and take a leading role in ensuring compliance will all safety protocols. The candidate will also participate in writing research manuscripts and grant applications.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications:

Candidates must possess a Ph.D. in Chemistry or a closely related field by the start of the appointment. Strong background in organic and inorganic synthesis is required and working knowledge of electrochemistry is desirable.

Preferred Qualifications:

Candidate will demonstrate a track record of research productivity as evidenced by quality publications in leading roles. Good written and verbal communication skills are expected, as well as demonstrated ability to conduct research independently and collaboratively.

Application Materials

Interested candidates can find details for the application process at the web address ; reference position number 00098294 and must submit all applications through this site.

Applications should consist of:

  • Cover letter outlining the applicant’s philosophy and goals on research, collegiality and collaboration
  • Current curriculum vitae that includes the applicant’s record of research
  • Contact information for at least five references

Handling of Application Materials

After initial review by the committee all uploaded materials may be shared with all faculty in the prospective home department. For affiliations and joint appointments materials may be shared with all faculty in all departments involved.

Application Deadline

Applications will be accepted until this position is filled.

Community Information

University Information
Missouri S&T is one of the nation's leading research universities with over 100-degree programs in 39 disciplines. It was founded in 1870 as one of the first technological institutions west of the Mississippi River. Located about 100 miles west of St. Louis in the vibrant community of Rolla, Missouri S&T is an accessible, safe, and friendly campus surrounded by Ozarks' scenery. Missouri S&T offers undergraduate degrees in engineering, the sciences, liberal arts, humanities, and business, with M.S. and Ph.D. programs available in many of the science and engineering programs. With over 7,000 students and 300 faculty, Missouri S&T is big enough to accommodate a broad population, yet small enough for individuals to build high visibility and impactful careers.

KUMMER COLLEGE
Established in 2022, The Kummer College serves as a pathbreaking model for social impact, technology transfer, and interdisciplinary collaboration within a future-oriented STEM-focused university. Supported by the Kummer Institute Foundation at Missouri S&T, this unique college integrates key academic, co-curricular, and administrative activities related to technology commercialization, business innovation and entrepreneurship, systems thinking, and economic development. Within The Kummer College lives several departments: Department of Business and Information Technology (BIT), Department of Economics, Department of Engineering Management and Systems Engineering (EMSE) and Kummer Student Programs.

COLLEGE of ENGINEERING & COMPUTING (CEC)
Missouri S&T’s College of Engineering and Computing is the largest of three colleges at S&T, accounting for approximately 80% of the total enrollment (about 4,500 undergraduates and 800 graduate students). The college includes more than 170 ranked faculty members who serve in 16 undergraduate programs, all with master’s and doctoral equivalents organized into nine academic departments. The college recently added a bachelor’s degree in biomedical engineering and a Ph.D. in bioengineering, both starting in fall 2024. Missouri S&T, supported by the College of Engineering and Computing, is nationally recognized for its career outcomes and ROI.

COLLEGE of ARTS, SCIENCES, & EDUCATION (CASE)
The College of Arts, Sciences, and Education is a catalyst of innovation, creativity, and discovery, where students and faculty work side-by-side to create and share knowledge and understanding. From arts and humanities to the natural and social sciences, the College of Arts, Sciences, and Education has a program for everyone. The College of Arts, Sciences, and Education (CASE) is made up of eleven units including Air Force ROTC, Army ROTC, Arts, Languages and Philosophy, Biological Sciences, Chemistry, English and Technical Communication, History and Political Science, Mathematics and Statistics, Physics, Psychological Science, and Education. The college is home to over 90 tenured/tenure-track and 44 non-tenure-track faculty members. CASE offers more than 85 different academic options including certificates, minors, bachelor’s, master’s, and doctoral degrees.

About Rolla
Rolla, Missouri offers several great advantages that help individuals enjoy a high quality of life. Rolla is an ideal place for families, with its low cost of living, excellent schools, safe neighborhoods, and a range of recreational activities suitable for all ages. The Ozark Scenic Riverways and beautiful landscapes offers abundant opportunities for outdoor enthusiasts of every lifestyle. With its vibrant community, Rolla hosts multiple events, concerts, art exhibitions, and theater performances throughout the year. The university’s Leach Theatre showcases nationally renowned performers for campus and community alike. Overall, living in Rolla offers a high quality of life with a supportive community, affordable living, beautiful natural surroundings, and numerous opportunities for personal and professional growth.

description:
Hiring Department

Office of Graduate Education

The Graduate Education office at Missouri S&T supports graduate students, postdoctoral scholars, faculty, and staff through advising, degree milestones, thesis and dissertation review, policy guidance, professional development, and administrative support through degree completion and postdoctoral success.

Job Description

The Graduate School is newly established effective August 1, 2026, marking a significant moment of transformation for graduate and postdoctoral education at Missouri S&T. As the school builds toward this new, centralized focus, structures and processes across the division will continue to evolve to best serve graduate students, postdoctoral scholars, and the broader academic community.

This position will provide comprehensive academic support and guidance to graduate students while ensuring the consistent application of university policies, degree requirements, and academic standards. The position serves as a lead source for thesis and dissertation preparation and formatting, supporting students and staff while contributing to the continuous improvement of graduate school processes and services.

Key Responsibilities:

Graduate Student Advising and Academic Progress

  • Advise graduate students regarding academic policies, degree requirements, procedures, and university resources in accordance with the Graduate Catalog, institutional policies, and Policy Memo II-20.
  • Develop and maintain degree audits based on approved plans of study and monitor student academic progress, enrollment status, and milestone completion to ensure compliance with university requirements.
  • Review active student records, analyze enrollment, milestone, and graduation reports, and communicate necessary actions to students to support timely progress toward degree completion.
  • Review graduation applications and audits to determine completion of degree and certificate requirements and approve or deny final degree audits based on university standards.
  • Communicate outstanding academic and graduation requirements to students and recommend solutions consistent with university regulations and best practices.
  • Process graduate student forms, records, and related documentation accurately and efficiently.

Department Support

  • Build collaborative relationships with faculty, staff, and campus partners to support graduate student success and efficient graduate education operations.

Lead Thesis and Dissertation Formatting and Support

Exercise judgment in determining whether documents should be returned to students for additional revisions or assigned to appropriate staff for further review and processing.

Policy Development, Campus Collaboration, and Process Improvement

  • Collaborate with team members and campus partners to develop policy and procedure recommendations for consideration by the Graduate Council and Graduate Faculty.

Perform other duties as assigned in support of graduate school operations and institutional goals.

A Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education and experience and at least 2 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessary

title: Radiochemist
description:
Hiring Department

University of Missouri Research Reactor (MURR)

Job Description

The University of Missouri Research Reactor (MURR) is seeking a Radiochemist to join our Innovative Development & Translation (ID&T) division. The ID&T division at MURR focuses on advancing radioisotope production methodologies with an emphasis on their translatability into current Good Manufacturing Practice (cGMP) standards. Core objectives of the ID&T division include: first, developing innovative and scalable radioisotope production techniques; second, optimizing and continuously improving existing isotope production lines at MURR to address any emergent issues; third, providing support to MURR’s research groups through a blend of technical expertise, collaborative projects, and tailored solutions; and fourth, evaluating new opportunities and managing new projects that will become the foundation of tomorrow’s growth and success.

This position will report to the Developmental Radiochemistry Senior Manager and will be responsible for developing radioisotope processing methods with a focus on radioisotope separations for the manufacturing of new cGMP medical radioisotopes to be used as Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs) in radiopharmaceutical formulations.


Key Duties Performed by This Position Will Include

• Design, implement, and optimize radioisotope production and separation methods using the University of Missouri Research Reactor.
• Lead radioisotope process development projects of moderate to high complexity and manage resources accordingly.
• Develop novel radioisotope manufacturing methodologies in collaboration with ID&T team members to ensure suitability for translation into current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP) compatible processes for medical grade radioisotope production.
• Conduct radioisotope separations to support the development of new radioisotope processes.
• Perform radioanalytical tests, and lead or assist in developing new quality control methods (e.g., gamma spectroscopy, ICP-MS, ICP-OES), including (radio)chromatography techniques (e.g., HPLC, IC, TLC).
• Collaborate with the members of other groups (i.e., Change Control & Translation, Developmental Engineering) within the Innovative Development & Translation division and other groups within MURR to understand the specific needs of each radioisotope development project.
• Lead or assist in developing SOPs and relevant technical documentation required for radioisotope process development and quality control methodologies.
• Perform research-grade radioisotope processing to produce high-quality radioisotope precursors to support researchers in MU and other research facilities across the US.
• Lead or assist in developing investigations and performing analyses to resolve issues that may arise in existing radiochemical production methodologies at MURR.
• Conduct detailed literature reviews to stay abreast of the latest advancements in isotope production, radiochemistry, radioisotope, and radiopharmaceutical development.
• Ensure compliance with all safety protocols and regulations related to radioisotope handling and production.
• Train staff on radiochemical procedures and safety protocols.


Successful candidates will be persuasive communicators with exceptional organizational and time management skills. They must demonstrate the following durable skills: leadership, character, collaboration, communication, creativity, critical thinking, mindfulness, growth mindset, and fortitude. Additionally, customer service, confidentiality, integrity, and a commitment to university values in their activities.

Must be available for reliable and consistent onsite work.

Shift

Monday through Friday, 8:00AM to 5:00PM

Minimum Qualifications

Doctoral degree in related/relevant area and at least 3 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessary.

Preferred Qualifications

• Ph.D. in Radiochemistry, Nuclear Chemistry, Radiopharmacy, Analytical Chemistry, or related field.
