title: ATHLETICS DIRECTOR #00031163
description:
Hiring Department

Athletics & Recreation- Division of Student Success

Job Description

Missouri University of Science and Technology (Missouri S&T) invites applications for the position of Director of Athletics and Recreation. The University seeks a dynamic, innovative, and student-centered leader to provide strategic, financial, operational, and administrative leadership for its comprehensive athletics and recreation enterprise.

The Director oversees 15 NCAA Division II varsity sports—nine men’s and six women’s—comprising approximately 500 student-athletes competing in the Great Lakes Valley Conference. Missouri S&T has a strong tradition of competitive and academic excellence, including 17 Academic All-America selections during the 2025–26 academic year—the most in NCAA Division II—and a school-record 381 Academic All-GLVC honorees.

Missouri S&T Athletics has experienced exceptional competitive and academic success in recent years, positioning the department among the premier NCAA Division II programs in the Great Lakes Valley Conference (GLVC). Over the past five years, the Miners have captured four conference championships, including the 2025 GLVC Baseball Tournament Championship, the 2025 GLVC Men's Basketball Regular Season Championship, the 2026 GLVC Baseball Regular Season Championship, and the inaugural 2026 GLVC Men's Volleyball Championship. During the 2025-26 academic year alone, 10 athletic programs advanced to conference or NCAA postseason competition, 22 student-athletes earned all-region honors, and 13 were named All-Americans. Missouri S&T also led all NCAA Division II institutions with 17 College Sports Communicators Academic All-America selections, extended its streak to 26 consecutive years with at least one Academic All-American, and established school records with 381 Academic All-GLVC honorees, 92 GLVC Distinguished Scholars, 48 Council of Presidents' Academic Excellence recipients, and 14 GLVC Team Academic Awards. These achievements reflect a department where competitive excellence and academic success are equally valued and consistently realized.

The Director also oversees the Student Recreation Center, fitness programs, club sports, intramural sports, informal recreation, and related services supporting a campus of approximately 7,200 students. The position has responsibility for the fiscal management, operations, maintenance, scheduling, safety, utilization, and long-term planning of Missouri S&T’s athletic and recreation facilities, fields, complexes, competition venues, practice spaces, and fitness areas.

Reporting to the Vice Chancellor for Student Success, the Director serves as the chief executive officer for Athletics and Recreation and leads approximately 13 administrators, 20 head and assistant coaches, and additional professional, support, and student staff.

Leadership Priorities

The Director will:

  • Establish and execute a clear strategic vision aligned with institutional, Student Success, and enrollment priorities.
  • Build a positive, accountable, collaborative, and high-performing organizational culture.
  • Recruit, supervise, develop, and evaluate coaches, administrators, and recreation professionals.
  • Champion student-athlete academic achievement, retention, graduation, career readiness, health, safety, and well-being.
  • Provide disciplined fiscal leadership, transparent budget management, effective internal controls, and timely operational execution.
  • Maintain a strong culture of NCAA Division II, GLVC, university, and institutional compliance.
  • Advance competitive excellence while supporting ethical conduct, sportsmanship, and student development.
  • Provide strategic oversight for recreation, fitness, club sports, intramurals, and informal recreation.
  • Lead athletic and recreation facility operations, maintenance planning, capital priorities, and space utilization.
  • Partner with Enrollment Management on recruiting, scholarship strategy, roster planning, yield, and retention.
  • Collaborate with University Advancement to strengthen fundraising, alumni engagement, sponsorships, and revenue generation.
  • Serve as a visible and effective ambassador with students, employees, alumni, donors, community members, the GLVC, and the NCAA.

Minimum Qualifications

Minimum qualifications include a master’s degree in a relevant field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience, and at least seven years of progressively responsible professional experience from which comparable leadership and administrative skills have been acquired.

The successful candidate will be a visible, accessible, and engaged leader who demonstrates integrity, sound judgment, emotional intelligence, fiscal responsibility, operational excellence, transparent communication, and strong follow-through.

Preferred Qualifications

Preferred candidates will demonstrate significant leadership experience within collegiate athletics, including success in personnel supervision, financial management, NCAA compliance, facilities operations, strategic planning, fundraising, student-athlete success, recreation programming, organizational change, and the development of a positive workplace culture.

Anticipated Hiring Range

The anticipated hiring range for this position has been established as up to $120,000 annually, commensurate with qualifications and experience.

Salary is determined by a variety of factors, including but not limited to, the individual’s particular combination of education, skills, and experience, as well as organizational requirements.

Your total compensation goes beyond the number on your paycheck. The University of Missouri provides generous leave, health plans, and retirement contributions that add to your bottom line.

title: Youth Services Coordinator
company: Community Health Action of Staten Island
description:
Community Health Action of Staten Island (CHASI) drives dramatic improvements in the health of New Yorkers by feeding people who are hungry, healing families broken apart by violence, and bridging the gaps between people and the compassionate health care they deserve. CHASI provides outreach, education, prevention, and direct support services for populations most affected by health disparities – people with low or no income, low-income people with chronic illnesses, people with criminal justice involvement, people who use drugs, domestic violence survivors, people of color, and the LGBTQ community.

POSITION SUMMARY:

The Youth Services Coordinator leads day-to-day operations for “Level Up SI,” CHASI's trauma-informed, recovery-oriented program for Staten Island youth ages 12 through 17. The coordinator supervises Youth Engagement Specialists, monitors quality and reporting, and ensures safe, welcoming, non-stigmatizing, developmentally appropriate programming. Regular after school, evening, and weekend availability is required. Proposed program hours are Tuesday through Saturday 12pm-8pm.


DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:

Program Operations and Supervision

  • Coordinate daily operations, staffing, schedules, groups, workshops, recreation, outings, supplies, technology, and readiness of the youth space.
  • Maintain at least two trained youth-serving staff during operating hours and the required 1:8 staff-to-youth ratio; monitor attendance and capacity.
  • Lead delivery of the 12-week curriculum covering peer relationships, digital wellness, creative arts, leadership, mindfulness, nutrition, and workforce readiness.
  • Supervise, coach, and support Youth Engagement Specialists; coordinate onboarding, training, reflective supervision, staff development, and approved relief coverage.

Safety, Quality, and Documentation

  • Ensure active supervision and compliance with youth protection, mandated reporting, confidentiality, professional boundaries, emergency response, incident reporting, and approved de-escalation practices.
  • Confirm consent, emergency-contact, staffing, and activity-approval requirements for off-site programming; restrict access to authorized youth, families, staff, and approved visitors.
  • Monitor required screening, State Central Registry clearances, training completion, program quality, contract compliance, and corrective follow-up.
  • Maintain accurate records for attendance, activities, outreach, referrals, incidents, youth feedback, membership forms, and required reports; collaborate with Data and Quality staff.

Youth Voice and Community Engagement

  • Establish and coordinate the Youth Advisory Board, facilitate quarterly meetings, document recommendations, and incorporate approved feedback into program improvement.
  • Coordinate outreach, presentations, referral pathways, and partnerships with schools, community organizations, healthcare providers, coalitions, CHASI programs, and other partners.
  • Work with Communications and youth to develop culturally responsive, developmentally appropriate, youth-informed, and non-stigmatizing materials.
  • Participate in meetings, training, quality-improvement activities, and approved community events; perform all functions in alignment with CHASI values and other duties as assigned.

title: Mobile Response Officer
description:
About The Role:

Days of Working: This role requires full flexibility to support operational needs around Glasgow, working 4 on 4 off shift pattern including days, nights and weekends.

We are currently seeking a reliable and professional Mobile Response Officer to join our team. This dynamic role involves attending alarm activations, conducting site inspections, carrying out mobile patrols, and responding to emergencies to ensure the safety and security of our clients' premises.

The successful candidate will work independently across multiple locations, acting as a visible security presence while delivering a responsive and professional service. This role requires strong decision-making skills, excellent communication, and the ability to remain calm under pressure.

As part of your role, your key responsibilities will include, but are not limited to:

  • Respond promptly to alarm activations and conduct thorough site investigations in accordance with company procedures.
  • Perform regular mobile patrols, security checks, and inspections across assigned locations.
  • Complete locking and unlocking procedures at client sites, ensuring premises are secured correctly.
  • Conduct vacant property inspections to ensure client properties remain secure and compliant with insurance requirements.
  • Respond appropriately to incidents, emergencies, and security concerns, taking necessary action and escalating where required.
  • Maintain a visible and professional presence to deter unauthorised access, criminal activity, and anti-social behaviour.
  • Accurately complete incident reports, patrol records, and all required security documentation.
  • Communicate effectively with clients, colleagues, and the Control Room, providing timely updates on incidents and operational matters.
  • Ensure compliance with company policies, assignment instructions, and Health & Safety requirements at all times.
  • Deliver excellent customer service and maintain positive working relationships with clients and stakeholders.

The ideal candidate should meet the following criteria:

  • Must have Right to Work in the UK and ability to pass an enhanced DBS and BS7858 security clearance
  • A calid SIA Licence.
  • Full UK Driving Licence with a good driving record*
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to work independently and use initiative.
  • Excellent problem-solving and decision-making abilities.
  • Ability to remain calm and professional in challenging situations.
  • Flexible approach to working hours, including nights, weekends, and public holidays.
Desirable:
  • Previous experience within a mobile security, keyholding, or response role.
  • Experience undertaking alarm response and property inspections.
  • Knowledge of security reporting systems and mobile patrol procedures.

title: Senior Engineer
description:
About The Role:

We are seeking an experienced Multi-Skilled Engineer with a background in industrial laundry operations, ideally within a high-volume commercial laundry serving the aviation, hospitality, healthcare, or manufacturing sectors.

This role is based within a large airline laundry facility responsible for processing and maintaining linen and textiles for major airline customers. Candidates should have experience maintaining, fault-finding, and repairing industrial laundry equipment and production systems in a fast-paced, 24/7 operational environment.

Working Pattern

This position operates on a 4 days on / 4 days off rotating shift pattern, consisting of 12-hour shifts:

  • Days 1 & 2: 5:45am to 5:45pm
  • Days 3 & 4: 5:45pm to 5:45am
  • Followed by 4 days off

Candidates must be comfortable working both day and night shifts.

The Ideal Candidate

  • Previous experience working within an industrial or commercial laundry environment.
  • Experience maintaining equipment such as industrial washers, dryers, tunnel washers, ironers, press systems, conveyors, garment handling equipment, folding systems, pumps, motors, and steam generation/distribution systems.
  • Proven electrical and mechanical fault-finding experience within a fast-paced production environment.
  • Excellent communication skills, both verbal and written.
  • Electrical installation and maintenance experience.
  • Mechanical fabrication and maintenance experience.
  • Electronic fault finding to component level.
  • Strong problem-solving and analytical skills.
  • Ability to make informed decisions and work independently.
  • Ability to build effective working relationships at all levels.
  • High attention to detail.
  • Self-motivated, flexible, and responsive to business needs.
  • Ability to work under pressure in a 24/7 operational environment.

Education & Experience

  • Must hold a recognised engineering qualification relevant to the role (Electrical or Mechanical City & Guilds, NVQ Level 3, HNC/HND, or equivalent).
  • Time-served apprenticeship preferred.
  • Multi-skilled engineer with both electrical and mechanical competence.
  • Experience with pneumatics, hydraulics, steam systems, conveyors, process machinery, and automated production equipment.
  • Previous experience within a commercial laundry processing airline linen and textiles would be highly advantageous.

About the Site

The successful candidate will join a large commercial laundry operation providing textile and linen services to the airline industry. The facility operates around the clock, processing high volumes of airline bedding, towels, uniforms, and other onboard textile products, requiring a proactive and safety-focused engineering team to maintain maximum operational uptime.

title: Student Financial Services Coordinator
description:
Hiring Department

Student Financial Aid

Job Description

JOB SUMMARY

This position serves as a primary point of contact for students, families, and visitors, providing guidance and support related to student accounts, financial aid, and university services. The role reviews, analyzes, and processes student financial and account information; accepts in-person and mailed payments; and responds to a broad range of inquiries. The position applies knowledge of university policies, procedures, and financial aid processes, including FAFSA, to provide accurate information and effective assistance. The incumbent is expected to deliver timely, professional customer service and contribute to a positive student experience.


PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES

Customer Service and Campus Resource Support - 30%

  • Serve as the first point of contact for students, prospective students, families, and visitors in person and by telephone.
  • Provide professional, student-centered service and maintain a welcoming environment for all customers.
  • Assess individual needs and connect students and visitors with the appropriate department or campus resource.

Student Account and Financial Aid Guidance - 45%

  • Review and analyze student account and financial information to respond accurately to questions and requests.
  • Advise current and prospective students and their families regarding student accounts, financial aid processes, and FAFSA requirements.
  • Explain applicable university policies, procedures, services, account activity, and available next steps.

Payment Processing and Recordkeeping - 15%

  • Process student payments received in person and through the mail in accordance with established procedures.
  • Maintain accurate documentation and records of payments, student interactions, requests, and outcomes.
  • Protect the accuracy and confidentiality of student financial and account information while completing transactions and account-related work.

Issue Resolution and Communication - 10%

  • Research and resolve student concerns, complaints, and account issues in a timely and effective manner.
  • Communicate clearly and professionally with students, families, faculty, staff, and campus partners regarding questions and resolutions.
  • Escalate complex or unresolved matters to the appropriate department or supervisor and provide relevant documentation for follow-up.

As with all positions, may perform other job-related responsibilities as needed to support departmental and campus-wide needs.


CORE COMPETENCIES

  • Student-centered customer service
  • Student account and financial aid knowledge
  • Analytical review and problem resolution
  • Payment processing and record accuracy
  • Clear communication and attention to detail


WORKING CONDITIONS & PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

Work is primarily performed in an onsite office and customer service environment with frequent interaction with students, families, visitors, faculty, and staff. The role requires regular use of a computer and telephone, review and processing of detailed financial information, and handling of in-person and mailed payments. The position involves sustained attention to detail, frequent communication, and the ability to manage a high volume of inquiries, including during peak service periods.


SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Ability to manage multiple tasks and prioritize effectively in a fast-paced environment
  • Proficiency with office software and student information management systems
  • Strong attention to detail and problem-solving skills
  • Excellent customer service and interpersonal skills

title: Assistant Director of Stewardship & Hospitality
description:
Hiring Department

Intercollegiate Athletics

Job Description

The University of Missouri Department of Athletics is seeking a service-oriented, organized, and detail-focused professional to serve as the Assistant Director of Stewardship & Hospitality. Reporting to the Senior Director of Hospitality & Premium Experiences, this position provides support in the planning, coordination, and execution of stewardship, hospitality, donor recognition, and engagement initiatives for the Mizzou Athletics Fund.

This position will play an important role in delivering exceptional experiences for members of the Mizzou Leadership Circle (MLC), premium seating holders, and other key supporters of Missouri Athletics. Serving as a key operational partner to the Senior Director, the Assistant Director will assist in executing a comprehensive stewardship and recognition program while supporting donor events, premium hospitality, game day experiences, event participation strategies, and post-event stewardship efforts that strengthen donor relationships and encourage long-term philanthropic support.

The Assistant Director will help advance the Mizzou Athletics Fund's commitment to delivering a best-in-class donor experience by supporting innovative stewardship initiatives, exceptional hospitality, and meaningful engagement opportunities that foster lifelong relationships with Missouri Athletics supporters.

Key Responsibilities
1. Stewardship and Donor Recognition (35%)
• Assist the Senior Director in executing a comprehensive donor stewardship and recognition program for the Mizzou Athletics Fund, with a primary emphasis on the Mizzou Leadership Circle (MLC).
• Support donor recognition initiatives, including donor signage, recognition displays, naming opportunities, plaques, stewardship communications, and other recognition efforts.
• Assist in coordinating donor appreciation initiatives, stewardship gifts, and recognition programs that celebrate philanthropic support and donor loyalty.
• Help maintain stewardship calendars, donor recognition inventories, and benefit fulfillment schedules.
• Coordinate stewardship fulfillment to ensure donors receive timely, meaningful, and personalized recognition.
• Assist in developing stewardship touchpoints before and after donor events that reinforce the impact of philanthropy and strengthen donor relationships.

2. Hospitality and Event Support (35%)
• Assist in planning and executing MLC special events, premium hospitality experiences, and stewardship events.
• Support premium game day hospitality operations for football, men's basketball, and other athletic events, with a primary focus on delivering exceptional experiences for MLC members.
• Coordinate event logistics, including invitations, registrations, catering, venue setup, signage, staffing, volunteer coordination, and post-event follow-up.
• Support event marketing, invitations, and outreach efforts designed to maximize attendance and engagement among MLC members and invited donors.
• Track event participation and attendance, identify engagement trends, and provide recommendations to enhance future donor experiences.
• Coordinate post-event stewardship activities, including thank-you communications, donor follow-up, photography, surveys, and benefit fulfillment.
• Collaborate with the Marketing and Communications teams to promote donor events, MLC initiatives, and stewardship experiences through social media, digital communications, photography, and other storytelling opportunities that highlight the impact of philanthropy.
• Assist in developing event communications and promotional materials that increase awareness, drive participation, and enhance the visibility of MLC programming and donor engagement initiatives.
• Assist with premium hospitality operations during athletic events.
• Support the development and execution of unique hospitality experiences and engagement opportunities that strengthen donor affinity and encourage continued participation.

3. Donor Experience & Collaboration (20%)
• Support the Senior Director in delivering an exceptional donor experience for MLC members, premium seating holders, and other Mizzou Athletics Fund supporters.
• Assist in coordinating MLC benefits, hospitality offerings, and engagement opportunities throughout the year.
• Collaborate with development officers to support stewardship plans, donor engagement opportunities, and hospitality experiences for assigned prospects and donors.
• Partner with development officers and the Senior Director of Hospitality & Premium Experiences to create customized stewardship plans and unique donor experiences for the Athletics Department's highest-level supporters.
• Assist in coordinating personalized hospitality opportunities, behind-the-scenes experiences, coach interactions, facility tours, and other exclusive engagement opportunities designed to recognize and steward leadership donors.
• Work closely with Annual Giving, Development, Ticket Operations, Marketing, Communications, and External Relations to ensure a seamless donor experience.
• Respond to donor requests related to stewardship, hospitality, event participation, and donor recognition in a timely, professional, and service-oriented manner.
• Support initiatives that increase MLC participation, deepen donor engagement, and create meaningful opportunities for supporters to connect with Missouri Athletics throughout the year.
• Continuously identify opportunities to enhance the donor experience by developing creative hospitality, recognition, and engagement initiatives that strengthen relationships with MLC members and inspire continued philanthropic support.

4. Administrative Support & Special Projects (10%)
• Maintain accurate records of event participation, stewardship activities, donor engagement, hospitality utilization, and recognition initiatives.
• Prepare event summaries and participation reports to evaluate attendance, donor engagement, and opportunities for continuous improvement.
• Assist with budget tracking, vendor coordination, event logistics, and stewardship project management as assigned.
• Represent the Mizzou Athletics Fund at donor events, athletic contests, and community functions.
• Perform other duties and special projects as assigned in support of the mission of the Mizzou Athletics Fund.

Shift

Monday-Friday 8:00am-5:00pm; Nights, Weekends, and Travel as required.

Minimum Qualifications

A Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education and experience and at least 2 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessary.

Preferred Qualifications

Prior experience executing large scale events and/or working in premium services is preferred.

title: Authorities and Catalog Management Library Associate, UMKC University Libraries
description:
Hiring Department

Cataloging & Resource Management/Special Collections and Archives

University of Missouri - Kansas City

For more information about University Libraries, visit:

Job Description

The Authorities and Catalog Management Library Associate supports the quality and consistency of bibliographic, authority, and metadata records within the UM System shared catalog and the UMKC institutional repository. The position holds primary responsibility for catalog maintenance and related special projects. Responsibilities also include complex copy and original cataloging of physical and electronic formats (excluding music) for UMKC Libraries, including LaBudde Special Collections and University Archives. Working under the guidance of the Head of Cataloging & Resource Management and in coordination with other cataloging staff, this position applies national, UM System, and local standards, procedures, and workflows to complete assigned cataloging and metadata tasks, assists with authority control processes, and contributes to enrichment and remediation projects. The position relies on documented practices and guidance from faculty librarians to address complex issues.

The position collaborates with colleagues across UMKC Libraries and the UM System to provide accurate and consistent access to library resources, while following established practices and identifying opportunities for workflow efficiencies. The position requires knowledge of cataloging, the ability to work independently, and reports to the Head of Cataloging & Resource Management.

Authorities and Catalog Data Management

  • Receive Backstage reports via UM System as assigned, resolve new, duplicate, blind, and invalid headings, and update bibliographic and authority records accordingly to ensure accuracy and consistency in the UM System shared catalog.
  • Along with the Head of CRM and other personnel as needed, serves as a UMKC representative at MERLIN Quality Control Committee meetings and participates in online discussions.
  • Serve as the primary contact for catalog maintenance questions from within UMKC Libraries and UM System colleagues within established guidelines and refer complex or policy-related issues to faculty librarians for guidance.
  • Execute batch record updates, imports, and exports in the UM System shared catalog and related systems such as OCLC.
  • Utilize tools (e.g., MarcEdit, Bulk Edit) to perform catalog data maintenance tasks and gain workflow efficiencies.
  • Support catalog data enrichment and remediation projects using reporting tools and predefined queries as available.
  • Assist with testing new releases and applying features to cataloging workflows in collaboration with departmental, library-wide, and UM System colleagues.
  • Manage withdrawals, including missing and long-missing items, and assist Copy Cataloger & Finishing Supervisor with processing transfers, added copies, and reinstatements as needed.

Cataloging & Metadata

  • Provide complex copy and original cataloging of physical and electronic monographs and serials, including but not limited to monographic continuations, selected special collections materials, and electronic theses/dissertations (ETDs), following local, UM System, and national standards.
  • Assist in maintaining the integrity of the UM System catalog and OCLC and enhance resource discovery through accurate descriptive cataloging, authorized access points, including subject and genre/form headings, and controlled and linked data vocabularies as appropriate.
  • Employ established cataloging policies and suggest workflow improvements.
  • Create and maintain descriptive metadata for the UMKC institutional repository and supply controlled vocabularies (e.g., LCSH) for electronic theses and dissertations and selected materials, adding materials to OCLC and the UM System shared catalog as appropriate.
  • Provide finishing support to the Copy Cataloger and Finishing Supervisor for physical materials cataloged for UMKC Libraries, including the Law Library, as needed.
  • Provide bindery support to the Copy Cataloger and Finishing Supervisor as needed.

Documentation Support

  • Document cataloging procedures and workflows as assigned to support consistency across the department and UM System.

General Responsibilities

  • Attend and participate in department, division, all-staff, and system-wide meetings or discussions as assigned.
  • Engage in continuing education activities to maintain knowledge of cataloging practices and emerging tools.

Qualifications

Minimum qualifications:

  • A Bachelor’s degree in a related field or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Minimum of three years’ of relevant experience in cataloging, metadata, or technical services.
  • Working knowledge of cataloging standards (e.g., RDA, MARC) and controlled vocabularies.
  • Experience with a library services platform or integrated library system.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience with FOLIO applications (Inventory, Data Import/Export, Bulk Edit, Lists).
  • Familiarity with authority control practices and workflows.
  • Experience with batch processing tools (e.g., MarcEdit).
  • Basic familiarity with linked data concepts.

Anticipated Hiring Range

The anticipated hiring range for this position has been established as $22.10-$25.00/hourly.

Salary is determined by a variety of factors, including but not limited to, the individual’s particular combination of education, skills, and experience, as well as organizational requirements.

Your total compensation goes beyond the number on your paycheck. The University of Missouri provides generous leave, health plans, and retirement contributions that add to your bottom line.

Application Materials

To be considered, you must complete the application at including Legal Name, US employment eligibility, and current contact information. Upload all application materials (a letter of interest, curriculum vitae, a list of references).

If you are experiencing technical problems, please email umpshrsupport@umsystem.edu.

For questions about the position, please contact umkcfacultysearch@umkc.edu include the Job Identification number 61383 and name of the position.

Application Deadline

The application deadline is 10/22/2026.

Employment visa sponsorship is not available for this position.

Other Information

This position typically works a 40-hour week, Monday through Friday, between 7:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. at Miller Nichols Library and may provide training or guidance to student assistants or staff as needed.

This is a full-time,12 month, benefit eligible, academic position.

title: Graduate Admissions Advisor
description:
Hiring Department

Graduate School

Job Description

JOB SUMMARY

The Graduate Admissions Advisor supports prospective and newly admitted graduate students throughout the application, admissions, and enrollment process. The position reviews and processes graduate applications in Slate, provides applicant communication and technical assistance, and collaborates with graduate program directors and campus partners to resolve admissions-related matters. The role leads the planning and execution of graduate student events and contributes to programming focused on student engagement, retention, and connection to Graduate School resources. The incumbent maintains accurate and confidential student records, supports data integrity, and contributes to the continuous improvement of graduate admissions and student success operations.


PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES

Graduate Admissions Advising and Application Processing - 35%

· Review and process graduate applications in Slate and interpret application materials and academic records in accordance with established admissions practices.

· Advise prospective and newly admitted graduate students throughout the application and admissions process through email, telephone, and in-person interactions.

· Provide timely, accurate, and student-centered guidance regarding application requirements, status, next steps, and available Graduate School resources.

Slate Support, Records, and Process Improvement - 25%

· Troubleshoot application issues in Slate and provide technical guidance to applicants and graduate program directors using the platform.

· Maintain accurate and confidential student records in compliance with FERPA and institutional policy and support the integrity of admissions data in Slate.

· Identify workflow concerns and participate in training, team meetings, and continuous improvement efforts related to graduate admissions processes.

Graduate Student Events and Success Programming - 25%

· Lead the planning and execution of graduate student events, including coordination of timelines, communications, logistics, and campus resources.

· Develop and support programming that promotes graduate student engagement, retention, and connection to Graduate School services and resources.

· Manage event planning responsibilities alongside cyclical admissions deadlines and other concurrent priorities.

Campus Collaboration and Student Communication - 15%

· Collaborate with graduate program directors and campus partners on application review, admitted student communication, and event logistics.

· Communicate professionally with students, faculty, and staff and provide consistent follow-up on admissions, enrollment, and student success matters.

· Coordinate information and next steps across campus partners to support students from application through enrollment.


WORKING CONDITIONS & PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

Work is primarily performed in an office environment with regular interaction with prospective and admitted students, faculty, staff, graduate program directors, and campus partners. The role requires frequent use of a computer, telephone, Slate, and standard office software, as well as sustained review of detailed application and academic information. The position involves managing multiple concurrent priorities across cyclical admissions deadlines and ongoing event planning and may require participation in graduate student events.


SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, given the applicant-facing and program director-facing nature of the work

Planning and Design provides MU with facility designs that optimize quality, timeliness, and cost effectiveness. Under the direction of the Director of Planning, Design and Construction, the Senior Project Manager provides professional engineering direction and project management for design and construction projects.

title: Youth Program Associate II (part-time) - Madison County
description:
Hiring Department

University of Missouri (MU) Office of Extension and Engagement

4-H Center for Youth Development - Madison County

Job Description

MU TITLE: Educational Program Associate II

LOCATION: Madison County - Fredericktown, MO

The University of Missouri (MU) Office of Extension and Engagement’s distinct land-grant mission is to improve lives, communities, and economies by producing relevant, reliable, and responsive educational strategies throughout Missouri. Our dedicated and knowledgeable faculty and staff collaborate with researchers and community leaders to develop and deliver programs that address the needs of Missourians including: educational attainment; environmental concerns; community, economic, business and workforce development; global food systems; and health systems. For more information about MU Extension and Engagement, please visit

The University of Missouri Extension 4-H Center for Youth Development provides leadership and expertise with developing communities of young people across Missouri who are learning citizenship, leadership, and life skills. 4-H is publicly supported by county, state, and federal partners, as well as private resources to enrich the learning experiences of both youth and adults. For more information about 4-H, visit

This position will assist in the planning, management, and support of 4-H Youth Development programs in assigned geographic area, under the guidance and supervision of the 4-H Youth Development Specialist/Educator.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES

  • Advocate for positive youth development in the community and MU Extension.
  • Build and expand external local partnerships to grow the 4-H program in the county, including but not limited to Schools, Community Centers, and other Youth serving organizations.
  • Build and expand internal partnerships to grow the 4-H program in the county, including partnerships among other UM Colleges and Missouri Extension programs: Agriculture & Environment, Business and Community, Health and Human Science.
  • Assist with coordination and planning, management, marketing, implementing (including teaching) and evaluation (including reporting) of researched based curriculum that has an emphasis on Leadership and Civic Engagement, STEM, Healthy Living, Agriculture and Natural Resources, as well as other career exploration topics. Including curriculums offered face to face activities and online.
  • Build capacity amongst volunteers and community partners, fostering developmental relationships to contribute to program growth.
  • Engage and empower volunteers and community partners to effectively implement 4-H programs across all delivery modes.
  • Develop leadership capacity among youth.
  • Assist in the management of financial and in-kind resources.
  • Coordinate and/or conduct educational events, contests, camps, and programs utilizing a positive youth development approach.
  • Contribute to the statewide effort to impact the lives of all Missourians positively including promotion of state and national events and contests.
  • Report accomplishments and impacts to appropriate sources including supervisor, funders, and stakeholders.
  • Assist with record keeping and report preparation of 4-H Youth Development Programs.
  • Ensure that individuals in the county can participate in extension programs.
  • Participate in training and professional development opportunities for continued in knowledge, skills, and abilities as it is related to the 4-H Youth Development program.
  • Ability to travel and work flexible hours, including some evenings and weekends, is required to fulfill assigned responsibilities.
  • As with all positions, involvement with other duties and responsibilities may be expected in order to support the mission and purpose of MU Extension.

LEADERSHIP RECEIVED AND EXERCISED

Administrative supervision is received from the assigned Field Specialist/Educator in 4-H Youth Development. This position is not responsible for supervision.

CORE ATTRIBUTES FOR MU EXTENSION STAFF

  • Exhibit a high personal standard of excellence, be an effective team player, and demonstrate civility and respect for all.
  • Engage stakeholders and learners; maintain positive interpersonal relationships and exhibit effective written and oral communication skills.
  • Operate with minimal guidance and be a self-directed learner who is flexible and adaptable to changing environments.
  • Ensure all youth and adults in the county have an ability to participate in extension programs which offer a safe environment.

UNIVERSITY INFORMATION

The University of Missouri, also known as Mizzou and MU, is the Flagship University of the four-campus University of Missouri system. It is the state’s land-grant university and one of the most comprehensive universities in the United States. title: Senior Research Scientist - Influenza Aerosol and Transmission Biology (Dual Posted with Job ID 61376)
description:
Hiring Department

Life Sciences Center.

Job Description

The Center for Influenza and Emerging Infectious Diseases (CIEID) at the University of Missouri is seeking a highly motivated Research Scientist or Senior Research Scientist to strengthen and help lead an expanding interdisciplinary research program in influenza aerosol biology and airborne transmission. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to assume a central scientific leadership role in a multidisciplinary P01 program focused on influenza transmission as part of the NIAID Influenza Transmission Research Consortium (ITRC), as well as complementary NIH R01-supported research on influenza transmission. Together, these programs integrate human studies, controlled animal transmission models, aerosol science, virology, immunology, engineering, and quantitative analysis.

A major goal of the transmission program is to understand why infected hosts differ in the amount and infectivity of virus released into aerosols and why exposure results in infection in some recipients but not others. The scientist will help define the mechanisms that govern influenza transmission by integrating viral, host, immune, aerosol, and environmental factors across human studies and controlled animal models. Research will encompass viral determinants of transmission, infectious virus shedding, aerosol generation and characterization, recipient susceptibility, particle transport and airflow, and other mechanisms governing airborne transmission. We are particularly interested in candidates with expertise in aerosol science, respiratory transmission, engineering, or related areas who can provide scientific and technical leadership and advance interdisciplinary transmission research across the P01 and R01 programs.

Major Responsibilities
• Provide scientific leadership for interdisciplinary research on influenza aerosol biology and airborne transmission, guiding experimental strategy, study design, scientific execution, and integration across human and animal studies. Provide scientific guidance and mentorship to postdoctoral fellows, graduate students, and research staff.
• Lead the scientific design and execution of influenza transmission studies across human studies and controlled animal models, working closely with study coordinators and research teams.
• Provide hands-on participation, as scientifically appropriate, in animal infection and exposure studies, aerosol sampling, specimen collection, and related experimental procedures.
• Investigate viral, host, immune, aerosol, and environmental determinants of infectious virus shedding, aerosol generation, recipient susceptibility, and airborne transmission.
• Lead and advance experimental approaches for studying respiratory aerosols and airborne transmission, including aerosol characterization, particle-size distributions, infectious virus content and stability, bioaerosol collection, and aerosol instrumentation, with emphasis on method development, optimization, validation, and troubleshooting.
• Contribute to studies of airflow, particle transport, aerosol behavior, and other physical and quantitative mechanisms of airborne transmission by working with engineering and modeling teams as appropriate to the scientist’s expertise and individual projects.
• Integrate aerosol, virologic, immunologic, clinical, environmental, and transmission data; analyze and interpret research findings; and contribute substantially to manuscripts, presentations, progress reports, grant applications, and collaborative publications. At the Senior Research Scientist level, assume greater responsibility for scientific project leadership, cross-project scientific integration, mentoring, and development of new research directions.

Research Environment
The Center for Influenza and Emerging Infectious Diseases (CIEID) at the University of Missouri provides a highly collaborative environment for interdisciplinary research on influenza and other emerging respiratory viruses. The Center brings together investigators with expertise in virology, immunology, aerosol science, engineering, animal models, genomics, computational biology, and public health, creating a strong environment for studying influenza transmission across disciplinary boundaries. The program draws on expertise and resources across the School of Medicine, College of Veterinary Medicine, College of Engineering, College of Agriculture, Food and Natural Resources, Bond Life Sciences Center, and Institute for Data Science and Informatics, providing extensive opportunities for cross-disciplinary collaboration. The research program has access to newly established ABSL-2 animal transmission facilities, BSL-3 and ABSL-3 biocontainment facilities, aerosol sampling and engineering capabilities, advanced laboratory automation systems, and institutional core facilities supporting genomics, proteomics, metabolomics, imaging, bioinformatics, and computational biology.

A multidisciplinary P01 program focused on influenza transmission as part of the NIAID Influenza Transmission Research Consortium (ITRC), together with complementary NIH R01-supported research, provides opportunities to integrate human studies with controlled swine and ferret transmission models, develop new approaches for measuring infectious aerosols, and define the mechanisms that govern airborne influenza transmission. The successful candidate will have substantial opportunities for scientific leadership, cross-project scientific integration, interdisciplinary collaboration, publication, grant development, mentoring, and career growth within this expanding influenza transmission research program.

Shift

Monday thru Friday, 8:00 a.m. – 5:00 p.m.; with occasional evening/weekend work depending on experiment needs

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in related/relevant area and at least 4 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessary

Preferred Qualifications

  • PhD, DVM, MD, or equivalent degree in aerosol science, bioaerosol science, environmental or occupational health, engineering, virology, microbiology, immunology, veterinary sciences, infectious diseases, biomedical sciences, or a related discipline.
  • Postdoctoral or equivalent research experience is preferred; the level of appointment will be commensurate with experience and demonstrated scientific independence.
  • Candidates with expertise in aerosol science, aerosol biology, or related areas are encouraged to apply even if their prior work was not specifically focused on influenza.
  • For appointment at the Senior Research Scientist level, evidence of scientific leadership, mentoring, and a strong record of research productivity is expected.
  • Strong quantitative, organizational, communication, and scientific writing skills and the ability to work effectively in a multidisciplinary team.

Anticipated Hiring Range

Salary Range: $60,944.00 - $112,230.00 annually. Competitive salary and benefits will be commensurate with experience and qualifications.

The Bond Life Sciences Center at the University of Missouri is a dynamic hub where groundbreaking research meets real-world impact. Designed to foster interdisciplinary collaboration, our state-of-the-art facility brings together experts in diverse fields—engineers, cancer biologists, plant scientists, and IT specialists—all working towards a common goal: to save lives, reduce costs, and enhance everyday life for Missourians and people around the globe.

Our Mission:

Our innovative research not only addresses pressing challenges in human and animal health, the environment, and agriculture, but it also translates into meaningful improvements in the lives of individuals everywhere. We also strive to share our findings with the public, ensuring that our discoveries resonate far beyond the lab in a language anyone can understand through our blog, Decoding Science, events for the public, social media and more.

description:
About The Role:

Shift Pattern: Monday to Thursday: 07:00–16:00 and Friday: 07:00–13:00 The role also includes participation in the site's on-call rota, approximately 1 week in every 6 weeks, providing out-of-hours support when required.
We are seeking an experienced, hands-on Building Facilities Supervisor to lead and support a multi-disciplinary facilities maintenance team. This is a working supervisor / tools-based role, requiring the successful candidate to combine strong technical ability with proven experience in supervising, motivating and coordinating a team.

The role is responsible for supporting the effective delivery of planned preventative maintenance (PPM), reactive maintenance, fault containment and completion of works, while maintaining high standards of safety, quality and customer service.

The Building Facilities Supervisor will work closely with facilities management, engineers, contractors and other stakeholders to ensure maintenance activities are completed safely, efficiently and within agreed timescales.

Key Responsibilities
  • Act as a hands-on working supervisor, carrying out maintenance activities while providing day-to-day leadership and direction to the engineering and facilities team.
  • Supervise and coordinate a multi-disciplinary team, ensuring workloads are appropriately allocated, prioritised and completed.
  • Support the planning, management and delivery of the site's PPM programme, ensuring scheduled tasks are completed within required timescales.
  • Coordinate and respond to reactive maintenance requests and breakdowns, ensuring faults are made safe, contained and progressed through to full completion.
  • Provide technical support and guidance to team members when diagnosing faults and determining appropriate repairs.
  • Monitor outstanding works and ensure jobs are followed through to completion rather than remaining at temporary containment.
  • Ensure maintenance records, job updates and relevant documentation are completed accurately and in a timely manner.
  • Identify additional works arising from PPM inspections, reactive maintenance and general site observations.
  • Support the preparation of quotations for additional and remedial works, including identifying labour, materials and access requirements.
  • Carry out approved additional works and customer requests as required.
  • Coordinate with specialist contractors and suppliers where works cannot be completed by the in-house team.
  • Assist with the ordering and control of materials, tools and equipment required to complete works.
  • Maintain good communication with customers and stakeholders, providing clear updates on progress, delays and completion of works.
  • Promote a strong health and safety culture, ensuring safe systems of work, risk assessments, method statements and site procedures are followed.
  • Support management with team performance, workload planning, technical issues and continuous improvement.
  • Provide appropriate support and guidance to engineers, apprentices and other team members to develop capability across the team.
  • Experience and Skills Required

    The successful candidate should have:
  • Previous experience in a Facilities Supervisor, Maintenance Supervisor, Lead Engineer or similar role within a building or facilities maintenance environment.
  • Demonstrable experience of leading and supervising a team.
  • Strong hands-on maintenance experience with the ability and willingness to work on the tools alongside the team.
  • Experience working within a multi-disciplinary maintenance environment.
  • Good understanding of planned preventative maintenance (PPM) and reactive maintenance processes.
  • Experience managing faults from initial response and containment through to permanent repair and completion.
  • Ability to prioritise workloads and coordinate engineers effectively in a busy operational environment.
  • Experience identifying additional/remedial works and supporting the preparation of quotations.
  • Good understanding of health and safety requirements within a facilities maintenance environment.
  • Strong fault-finding and problem-solving skills.
  • Good communication and customer service skills.
  • Ability to work independently while also contributing effectively as part of the wider facilities management team.
  • Relevant technical/trade qualifications or equivalent demonstrable experience.
  • Working Hours & On-Call

    Role Purpose

    The overall purpose of the position is to provide strong hands-on technical leadership to the facilities team, ensuring that planned and reactive maintenance is delivered safely, efficiently and to a high standard. The supervisor will help ensure issues are properly managed from initial identification through containment, repair and final completion, while supporting the wider facilities operation and responding positively to additional customer requirements.

title: DIRECTOR OF GRADUATE AND INTERNATIONAL ADMISSIONS #00065331
description:
Hiring Department

The Graduate School

The Graduate School is newly established effective August 1, 2026, marking a significant moment of transformation for graduate and postdoctoral studies at Missouri S&T. As the School builds toward this new, centralized focus, structures and processes across the Graduate and International Admissions team will continue to evolve to best serve graduate students, postdoctoral scholars, and the broader academic community.

Job Description

Reporting to the Founding Dean of the Graduate School and Vice Provost of Graduate and Postdoctoral Studies, the Director of Graduate and International Admissions provides strategic leadership for domestic, international, and online graduate recruitment and admissions, as well as international undergraduate recruitment and admissions at Missouri University of Science and Technology (Missouri S&T).

The Director leads the Office of Graduate and International Admissions and develops data-informed enrollment strategies to support sustainable enrollment growth and institutional priorities. The Director oversees admissions operations, recruitment and yield strategies, staff and budget management, enrollment partnerships, and continuous improvement of admissions processes while collaborating closely with academic programs, university leadership, and campus partners.

Responsibilities

  • Provide strategic and administrative leadership for the Office of Graduate and International Admissions, including supervision, hiring, training, performance management, professional development, workload planning, and establishment of departmental priorities and service standards.
  • Develop, implement, and assess comprehensive enrollment strategies for domestic, international, and online graduate students and international undergraduate students, aligned with institutional enrollment goals and academic priorities.
  • Oversee graduate and international undergraduate admissions operations, policies, procedures, and workflows to ensure accurate, timely, consistent, and student-centered application review and decision processes.
  • Establish and monitor enrollment goals, key performance indicators, conversion and yield rates, forecasts, and other measures of recruitment and admissions effectiveness; use data, market research, and enrollment trends to inform strategy and resource allocation.
  • Lead recruitment and yield initiatives across master's, doctoral, online, and international populations, including recruitment travel, events, webinars, campus visits, fellowship recruitment, and prospective and admitted student engagement.
  • Build strong partnerships with graduate program coordinators, department chairs, faculty, college leadership, and other academic stakeholders to establish enrollment priorities, develop program-specific recruitment strategies, and support applicant conversion and enrollment.
  • Lead the development and continuous improvement of admissions technology, CRM workflows, communications, reporting, automation, and business processes in partnership with systems and operations staff.
  • Identify and develop enrollment opportunities through university partnerships, pathway and collaborative academic programs, sponsored student programs, recruitment organizations, and other domestic and international partnerships.
  • Collaborate with Marketing and Communications and academic programs to develop targeted, multichannel recruitment and yield campaigns and ensure websites, communications, and recruitment materials effectively support enrollment goals.
  • Manage the Office of Graduate and International Admissions budget, including recruitment investments, travel, events, marketing, professional development, and other operational expenditures; evaluate effectiveness and return on investment.
  • Advise Graduate School and university leadership on graduate enrollment trends, recruitment opportunities, admissions policies, operational challenges, and emerging issues affecting enrollment.
  • Represent Missouri S&T and the Graduate School at recruitment events, conferences, partner institutions, and other external engagements.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Shift

Monday-Friday, 8am-4:30pm; Possibility of some weekend and evening work

Minimum Qualifications

A master's degree or an equivalent combination of education and experience and at least 7 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessary

Preferred Qualifications

  • Five to seven years of progressively responsible experience in graduate admissions, recruitment, enrollment management, or a related higher education field, including at least three years of experience supervising and developing professional staff.
  • Demonstrated success developing, implementing, and assessing data-informed recruitment, admissions, enrollment, and yield strategies for multiple student populations and delivery modalities.
  • Experience managing admissions operations, policies, processes, technology, and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Demonstrated ability to analyze enrollment data, identify trends, develop forecasts, and translate findings into actionable strategies.
  • Experience developing recruitment campaigns, partnerships, and programs that contribute to institutional enrollment goals.
  • Understanding of graduate education and the recruitment and enrollment needs of master's, doctoral, online, and international students.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead complex, cross-functional initiatives and build effective relationships with faculty, academic leadership, university administrators, staff, students, and external partners.
  • Excellent written and oral communication, presentation, organizational, project management, and interpersonal skills.
  • Demonstrated cultural competency, sound judgment, diplomacy, and ability to manage multiple priorities in a complex higher education environment.
  • Experience with CRM and student information systems, preferably Slate and PeopleSoft, and proficiency with Microsoft Office.

title: Field Specialist in Agricultural Business – Benton County, MO
description:
Hiring Department

University of Missouri (MU) Office of Extension and Engagement

Agricultural and Business Policy Program

Job Description

MU TITLE: Assistant/Associate/Full Extension Professional

LOCATION: Warsaw, Missouri, and primarily serves Benton, Cass, Cooper, Johnson, Henry,

Moniteau and Morgan Counties in the West Central Region, with additional service across the state

as needed.

Specialist Emphasis

This position is responsible for planning, implementing, and evaluating educational programs that support agricultural and agribusiness development and expansion in ways that improve Missourian’s quality of life and enhance the economic viability of Missouri enterprises while protecting the environment and the state’s natural resources. These efforts may involve:

  • Assisting agricultural operators and agribusinesses with decision-making, financial management, taxes, and risk mitigation as they start, expand, or diversify their businesses,
  • Assessing new business opportunities and emerging economic issues faced by producers, landowners, and businesses,
  • Offering technical assistance contracts, often in collaboration with state specialists, that support efforts such as business plans, marketing plans, feasibility studies, surveys, etc., and
  • Connecting appropriate regional and state partners with an agricultural business owner when an economic development opportunity arises.

Effective specialists will apply interdisciplinary knowledge and collaborate with respective regional producer groups, state and local agricultural support entities, and other relevant organizations to leverage efforts and funding opportunities.

This position is a 12-month, ranked, non-tenure track appointment at the rank of assistant, associate, or full Extension Professional. Rank will be determined at the time of the appointment based on qualifications and experience in accordance with the MU Extension faculty standards. This position will hold a working title of Field Specialist in Agricultural Business.

As a Field Specialist, your workload distribution at appointment will be 90% Extension Teaching and 10% Traditional Service.

This appointment is renewable annually at the discretion of the University and workload distribution may change at the discretion of Extension leadership. Circumstances affecting continued employment include, but are not limited to, work performance, fund availability, and educational priorities.

CORE DUTIES OF MU EXTENSION SPECIALISTS

MU Extension Specialists deliver the University of Missouri to all Missourians. They serve all Missourians by bringing research-based solutions to work on local problems. MU Extension Specialists teach new and foundational concepts, link people to resources, support partner organizations, participate in research, train volunteers, evaluate programs, foster innovation, and serve communities. MU Extension Specialists work as a team to expand educational attainment, foster economic development, and improve health outcomes. These core duties fall into three major areas:

Educate, Create, and Connect.

  • Educate. MU Extension specialists design, conduct, and evaluate educational programs. MU Extension specialists teach research-based information via meetings, in-person, and online courses, continuing education classes, technical assistance, volunteer training, media, websites, consultation, and other educational methods. They provide educational programs that support the individual, organizational, and community goals of Missouri’s learners and clients.
  • Create. MU Extension specialists develop innovative and research-informed educational products, services, materials, and other scholarly works. These include curricula, publications, presentations, educational tools, websites, and similar resources. MU Extension specialists obtain and use extramural funding to support creative works. MU Extension specialists contribute to the scholarship of Extension and Engagement by evaluating programs that result in learning and behavior changes that impact individuals and communities.
  • Connect. MU Extension specialists engage with learners, stakeholders, volunteers, and communities, including county extension councils, government officials and agencies, partners, and University and professional organizations. MU Extension specialists listen and respond with care. MU Extension specialists intentionally foster engaged partnerships and robust connections to the wide array of programs offered by the whole University of Missouri System.

Professional Expectations

  • Engage with stakeholders in all coverage counties to identify educational needs and then collaborate with appropriate internal and external partners to meet programming needs, incorporating timely marketing strategies.
  • Create an annual plan-of-work that reflects local needs and aligns with statewide program area efforts. Provide a monthly report for assigned county extension councils, supervisors, county commissioners and others, regarding programmatic efforts. Attend at least one county extension council meeting each month and provide a program review with feedback and analysis for the respective coverage area.
  • Collaborate with campus-based specialists on research projects and then deliver findings from those efforts via demonstrations, field days, courses, workshops, consultations, publications, and appropriate media.
  • Effectively work with supervisors, other specialists, and local leaders to complete administrative tasks as needed to support county efforts.
  • Demonstrate competency in communication, educational programming, subject matter knowledge, educational delivery, volunteer management, grant acquisition, teamwork, interpersonal relations, organization knowledge, leadership, and professionalism.
  • Offer timely, research-based information during times of natural disasters or unexpected catastrophic events.
  • Represent the University of Missouri on boards and committees for assigned program area.
  • Participate in professional development events to improve both technical and leadership skills.
  • Other duties and responsibilities as assigned to support the mission of MU Extension.

Additional Expectations

  • MU Extension Specialists travel regularly throughout Missouri and occasionally to out-of-state locations. MU Extension requires specialists to have a valid Missouri driver’s license, a legally operating vehicle, and wireless telephone/data service for university use. MU Extension specialists receive reimbursement for approved travel expenses, per University of Missouri policy.
  • MU Extension programs often occur outside of normal business hours. MU Extension Specialists should expect to attend these events as needed to meet the needs of learners, clients, and stakeholders.

MU EXTENSION LEADERSHIP RECEIVED

The Senior Program Director for Agriculture and Environment provides overall programmatic leadership. Programmatic supervision comes from the Education Director for the Agricultural and Business Policy Program with administrative oversight from the Regional Director for the West Central Region.

MU EXTENSION INFORMATION

The University of Missouri (MU) Office of Extension and Engagement’s distinct land-grant mission is to improve lives, communities, and economies by producing relevant, reliable, and responsive educational strategies throughout Missouri. Our dedicated and knowledgeable specialists and staff collaborate with researchers and community leaders to develop and deliver programs that address the needs of Missourians, including educational attainment, economic development, and healthy people. For more information about MU Extension and Engagement, please visit .

UNIVERSITY INFORMATION

The University of Missouri, also known as Mizzou and MU, is the Flagship University of the four-campus University of Missouri System. It is one of the state’s land-grant universities. MU’s comprehensive undergraduate programs and its graduate, professional, and research programs attract an annual enrollment of more than 30,000 students. MU Extension and Engagement programs are located on all four campuses and in 114 counties and St. Louis city.

Qualifications

An earned Master’s or other applicable terminal degrees MBA or Ph.D. in agricultural economics, agricultural business, agricultural marketing, business administration, business management or related field at time of appointment.

Experience working with a variety of audiences.

title: Health Sciences Career Coach, UMKC Career Services
description:
Hiring Department

UMKC Career Services empowers students and alumni to achieve career success through career exploration, experiential learning, professional development, employer engagement, and job search support. The office provides career coaching, career-readiness programming, internship and employment resources, employer networking opportunities, and career education that prepare students to successfully transition from college to meaningful careers. Career Services also supports students in pursuing undergraduate research, graduate education, and prestigious national competitive awards and scholarships by providing guidance on application development, personal statements, interviews, and experiential opportunities that enhance academic and professional growth. Through innovative programs and strategic partnerships, Career Services advances student success, retention, career readiness, and post-graduate outcomes.

Job Description

Career Coaches in UMKC Career Services support students and alumni as they explore career paths, prepare for internships, employment, graduate school, and other professional opportunities, and build the skills needed for long-term career success. This Career Coach position will work primarily with students majoring in the health sciences, providing targeted support aligned with their academic programs, career goals, and professional pathways. They provide individualized and group career coaching, deliver workshops and presentations, collaborate with academic units and campus partners, and connect students with resources, employers, and experiences that strengthen career readiness.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Promote an integrated and engaging career development program.
  • Provide individual and group career coaching for undergraduate students, graduate students, and alumni; assist students with career preparation, employment searches, and internship or career-related opportunities.
  • Assist students with developing professional skills, including resume writing, graduate school research and applications, job and internship searches, interview preparation, and professional networking.
  • Serve as the liaison for assigned academic units by collaborating with student groups, academic departments, and administrative departments to develop industry-specific programming, student preparation resources, and communication opportunities for students.
  • Develop and coordinate career-related educational programs for classes, student organizations, prospective student groups, and others as appropriate; collaborate with faculty and campus partners to develop and deliver programs and communications.
  • Assist with recruiting, selecting, and training undergraduate Peer Career Coaches.
  • Accurately document interactions with students and graduates in the career services database.
  • Collaborate with the employer relations team to connect students and academic programs with relevant employers, jobs, and internships.

Minimum Qualifications

A Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education and experience, and at least 2 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired, is necessary.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master's degree in Higher Education Administration, Student Affairs, Counseling, Education, or a related field.
  • Experience advising, mentoring, coaching, teaching, or providing student support services to undergraduate students, particularly those pursuing health sciences, healthcare, public health, pre-professional, or related academic and career pathways.
  • Familiarity with health sciences career pathways, experiential learning opportunities, graduate or professional school application processes, and professional expectations in healthcare-related fields.
  • Experience designing and delivering career-related workshops, programs, or presentations.
  • Ability to build effective working relationships with faculty, academic advisors, employers, alumni, and campus partners to support student career readiness.
  • Experience using technology platforms or career services systems to deliver student support, career coaching, or employment-related services.
  • Strong written, presentation, and interpersonal communication skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to work effectively with and serve students from diverse backgrounds.
  • Knowledge of career development, college recruiting, or professional association standards such as NACE, NCDA, or related career-focused organizations.

title: Development Director
description:
Overview

Since our founding in 1924, we've cut cardiovascular disease deaths in half, but there is still so much more to do. To overcome today’s biggest health challenges and accelerate this progress, we need passionate individuals like you. Join our movement, be part of the progress, and help ensure a healthier future for all. You matter, and so does the impact you can make with us.

We are currently hiring a Development Director in our Southeast Michigan market. The Director will generate revenue for our Heart of Ann Arbor-Jackson fundraising campaign. This campaign includes our signature Ann Arbor-Jackson Heart Ball event. We have a fast-paced sales type of environment with the main responsibility of driving revenue in support of our mission. We offer a base salary with the potential to earn an incentive up to 25% of your base pay. The potential incentive is based on achieving certain revenue targets and triggers.

The Association offers many resources to help you maintain work-life harmonization through your changing needs and life situations. To help you be successful, you will have access to Heart U, our award-winning corporate university, as well as additional training and support, locally.

#TheAHALife is more than a company culture; it is our way of life. It embodies our commitment to work-life harmonization and is guided by our core values where our employees can thrive both personally and professionally. Discover why you will Be Seen. Be Heard. Be Valued at the American Heart Association by following us on LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X, and at heart.jobs.

Responsibilities

  • Generate revenue by prospecting and securing local corporate sponsorship and individual donations. Achieve revenue goals by building and maintaining relationships with corporate partners and donors.
  • Build and maintain a pipeline of prospective corporate sponsors and donors by conducting research that matches to the campaign goals and the Association's mission.
  • Develop and present proposals and accompanying materials to secure revenue and volunteer engagement.
  • Recruit and be responsible for executive volunteer leadership and volunteer committees.
  • Lead and engage new individual membership for our Cor Vitae giving society, in partnership with other appropriate fundraising staff. Includes planning and implementing regular engagement events for members.
  • Plan and implement events in collaboration with internal and external partners.
  • Manage and maintain accurate volunteer and supporter information within our customer relationship management (CRM) system and Microsoft platforms, ensuring data is current and up to date.
  • Work with a Communications Director to support and promote campaign communication plans.
  • Lead fundraising strategies for the Leaders of Impact campaign to achieve and exceed revenue goal.
  • Identify and engage individuals with the potential to create significant impact through fundraising, awareness-building, community influence, and long-term volunteer leadership.
  • Provide exceptional, personalized support to campaign participants throughout their fundraising journey, ensuring they are valued, celebrated, and set up for success.
  • Identify and engage individuals with the potential to create significant impact through fundraising.
  • In addition to managing the Ann Arbor-Jackson Heart Ball and Leaders of Impact, the Director will support the Go Red for Women and Detroit Heart Ball campaign, as the need arises.

Qualifications

3 years of relevant experience in fundraising, sales, or other related experience

  • University/College degree or equivalent experience
  • Ability to do daily local travel up to 75% and some overnight trips as needed; requires access to reliable transportation at all times on an immediate basis
  • Ability to lift and/or move large objects (such as boxes) with the expectation that heavier items would be broken down into smaller components or requesting additional assistance may be required before lifting and/or moving
  • Must have at least basic knowledge and skill/proficiency with Microsoft Office

Here are some of the preferred experience and skills we are seeking:

  • Experience managing and cultivating high-level leaders at the C-Suite level
  • Knowledge of corporate and community networks

Compensation & Benefits

The American Heart Association invests in its people. Here are the main components of our total rewards package. Visit Rewards & Benefits to see more details.

  • Compensation – Our goal is to ensure you have a competitive base salary. That’s why we regularly review the market value of jobs and make adjustments, as needed.
  • Performance and Recognition – You are rewarded for achieving success through annual salary planning and incentive programs; this position is incentive eligible based on achieving certain targets.
  • Benefits – We offer a wide array of benefits including medical, dental, vision, disability, and life insurance, along with a robust retirement program that includes an employer match and automatic contribution. As a mark of our commitment to employee well-being, we also offer an employee assistance program, employee wellness program and telemedicine, and medical consultation.
  • Professional Development – You can join one of our many Employee Resource Groups (ERG) or be a mentor/mentee in our professional mentoring program. Heart U is the Association’s national online university, with more than 100,000 resources designed to meet your needs and busy schedule.
  • Work-Life Harmonization – The Association offers Paid Time Off (PTO) at a minimum of 16 days per year for new employees. The number of days will increase based on seniority level. You will also have a total of 12 paid holidays off each year, which includes several days off at the end of the year.
  • Tuition Assistance - We support the career development of all employees. This program provides financial assistance to employees who wish to further their education and career in relation to their current duties and responsibilities, or for potential future positions in the organization.
