title: Regional Engineering Supervisor
description:
About The Role:

We are looking for an experienced Regional Engineering Supervisor to lead and support multi-skilled engineering teams across the region.

You will be responsible for operational performance, technical standards, compliance, team development and customer relationships, ensuring services are delivered safely and in line with contractual SLAs and KPIs.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead, supervise and coordinate regional engineers across the GEO2 region.
  • Ensure resources and skill sets are effectively deployed across sites.
  • Build strong working relationships with customers and key stakeholders.
  • Monitor planned and reactive maintenance performance against SLAs and KPIs.
  • Act as a technical escalation point for complex faults and critical incidents.
  • Coach, mentor and develop engineers to improve performance and retention.
  • Manage engineering rotas and on-call coverage.
  • Audit workmanship, housekeeping and service quality.
  • Manage and monitor subcontractor performance and safe systems of work.
  • Ensure all PPM activities are completed within agreed timescales.
  • Take ownership of statutory compliance, inspections, testing and certification.
  • Undertake LV, CS and PS Authorised Person responsibilities where appointed.
  • Promote a strong health, safety and compliance culture through audits and toolbox talks.
  • Review operational data, identify trends and implement corrective action plans.
  • Support continuous improvement across maintenance, scheduling and asset management.
  • Identify opportunities to improve energy efficiency and operational resilience.
  • Produce performance and compliance reports for senior management.
  • Ensure teams have the tools, training and support required to deliver a safe and effective service.

About You

You will be an experienced technical services professional with a strong background in hard services Facilities Management and building services engineering.

You will ideally have:

  • At least 5 years' experience in Technical Services management or supervision.

title: Business Counselor – St. Louis City and St. Louis County
description:
Hiring Department

University of Missouri (MU) Office of Extension and Engagement

MU Extension’s Business Development Program

Job Description

MU TITLE: Extension Instructor

LOCATION: St. Louis, Missouri, primarily serves St. Louis County along with St. Louis City, Jefferson, and

St. Charles counties, with additional service across the state as needed.

HEADQUARTERED: Missouri Small Business Development Center – St. Louis, MO

MU Extension’s Business Development Program is an important component of the state’s economic development strategy and the University of Missouri’s economic development mission by providing education and assistance to entrepreneurs throughout Missouri. This includes serving as the Lead Center for the Missouri Small Business Development Center (SBDC) network, as well as operating centers in St. Louis and Columbia. For more information about the Missouri Small Business Development Center network, visit For more information about MU

Extension, visit

Educator Emphasis

The primary purpose of an SBDC counselor is to transform Missouri business and industry through education, technical assistance, and collaboration by working with entrepreneurs in small to medium size companies to improve bottom-line performance. As a Business Counselor, you will plan, implement, and evaluate educational programs and services for entrepreneurs utilizing research-based knowledge on a range of topics, including business growth, strategic planning, technology development, government contracting, marketing, management, finance, capital formation, operations, human resources, business start-up and business growth/sustainability, as well as in other timely topics relating to entrepreneurship and business growth.

This position primarily serves as a business educator and counselor for entrepreneurs and business owners in the St. Louis region. Counselors should have an emphasis in finance, management, marketing, product commercialization, product development, and/or growth management. Successful business counselors are able to transform this expertise into practical knowledge and solutions for their clients and students.

This position is a 12-month unranked academic position. This position will have a MU Title of Extension Instructor with the working title of Business Counselor.

As a Business Counselor, your workload distribution at appointment will be 90% Extension Teaching and 10% Traditional Service.

This appointment is renewable annually at the discretion of the University and workload distribution may change at the discretion of Extension leadership. Circumstances affecting continued employment

include, but are not limited to, work performance, fund availability, and educational priorities.

Program Specialization: A Business Counselor is responsible for providing educational programming and business coaching to entrepreneurs and new companies in starting, growing, and operating business ventures that result in economic and societal outcomes. Develop and provide high-quality educational programs that are consistent with the MU Extension mission, are research-and evidence-based, and resulting in learning and behavioral changes that positively impact the economy and society.

Key responsibilities of a MU Extension Business Counselor include:

Client Consultation and Technical Assistance

  • Provide business coaching to entrepreneurs and new companies, while also developing and providing high-quality educational programs that are consistent with the MU Extension mission, are research-and evidence-based, and foster learning and appropriate behavioral changes.
  • Serve as a critical link between Missouri companies and the faculty, research staff, and students in regional and statewide higher-education institutions.
  • Facilitate significant economic impact by achieving or exceeding goals in new sales, new jobs, business investments, quality and quantity of stakeholder relations, revenue generation, and well as other program-specific metrics.
  • Regularly collect qualitative and quantitative data to evaluate the impact of educational programs and services.
  • Conduct in-depth research and provide technical assistance to support clients; serve as a mentor on complex topics; perform a lead role in analyzing client needs and assessing the effectiveness of client action plans; and provide technical feedback to clients.

Program Support and Administrative Leadership

  • Participate in interdisciplinary teams, committees, and task forces and work with faculty and staff throughout Missouri to carry out the mission of MU Extension and the Missouri Small Business Development Centers.
  • Develop and maintain external strategic partnerships to ensure effective program outreach in support of organizational goals and objectives.
  • Serve on various ad hoc committees, task forces and teams engaged in product development planning or process implementation for the Missouri SBDC. Participate in regional planning efforts and assist in the implementation of a plan for the Missouri SBDC in St. Louis.
  • Travel to client sites, events, and training activities as budget allows. Attend outreach events to build awareness of SBDC services. Actively work to build awareness of SBDC services through speaking engagements, collaboration of regional training initiatives, or other events.

CORE DUTIES OF MU EXTENSION EDUCATORS

MU Extension Educators deliver the University of Missouri to all Missourians. They serve all Missourians by bringing research-based solutions to work on local problems. MU Extension Educators teach new and foundational concepts, link people to resources, support partner organizations, participate in research, train volunteers, evaluate programs, foster innovation, and serve communities. MU Extension Educators work as a team to expand educational attainment, foster economic development, and improve health outcomes. These core duties fall into three major areas:

Educate, Create, and Connect.

  • Educate. MU Extension educators design, conduct, and evaluate educational programs. MU Extension educators teach research-based information via meetings, in-person and online courses, continuing education classes, technical assistance, volunteer training, media, websites, consultation, and other educational methods. They provide inclusive educational programs that support Missouri's learners and clients' individual, organizational, and community goals.
  • Create. MU Extension educators develop innovative and research-informed educational products, services, materials, and other scholarly works. These include curricula, publications, presentations, educational tools, websites, and similar resources. MU Extension educators obtain and use extramural funding to support creative works. MU Extension educators contribute to the scholarship of Extension and Engagement by evaluating programs that result in learning and behavior changes that impact individuals and communities.
  • Connect. MU Extension educators engage with learners, stakeholders, volunteers, and communities, including county extension councils, government officials and agencies, partners, and University and professional organizations. MU Extension educators listen and respond with care. MU Extension educators intentionally engage partnerships and robust connections to the vast array of programs offered by the University of Missouri System.

Professional Expectations

  • Engage with stakeholders in all counties to identify educational needs and then collaborate with appropriate internal and external partners to meet those needs.
  • Create an annual plan of work that reflects local needs and aligns with statewide program area efforts. Provide a monthly report to county extension councils, supervisors, county commissioners, and others regarding programmatic efforts. Attend at least one county extension council each month and provide an oral update on program efforts at that meeting.
  • Collaborate with campus-based specialists on research projects and then deliver findings from those efforts via demonstrations, field days, courses, workshops, consultations, publications, and appropriate media.
  • Effectively work with supervisors, specialists, and local leaders to complete administrative tasks as needed.
  • Demonstrate competency in communication, educational programming, subject matter knowledge, educational delivery, volunteer management, grant acquisition, teamwork, interpersonal relations, organization knowledge, leadership, and professionalism.
  • Offer timely, research-based information during times of natural disasters or similar events.
  • Represent the University of Missouri on boards and committees as assigned.
  • Participate in professional development events to improve both technical and leadership skills.
  • Other duties and responsibilities as assigned to support the mission of MU Extension.

Additional Expectations

  • MU Extension Educators regularly travel throughout Missouri and occasionally to out-of-state locations. MU Extension requires educators to have a valid Missouri driver’s license, a legally operating vehicle, and wireless telephone/data service for University use. MU Extension Educators receive reimbursement for approved travel expenses, per University of Missouri policy.
  • MU Extension programs often occur outside of regular business hours. MU Extension educators should expect to attend these events as needed to meet the needs of learners, clients, and stakeholders.

LEADERSHIP RECEIVED AND EXERCISED

The Senior Program Director for Business & Community provides overall programmatic leadership.

Programmatic supervision comes from the Business Development Education Director and administrative oversight from the Missouri SBDC in St. Louis Regional Director.

MU EXTENSION INFORMATION

The University of Missouri (MU) Office of Extension and Engagement’s distinct land-grant mission is to improve lives, communities, and economies by producing relevant, reliable, and responsive educational strategies throughout Missouri. Our dedicated and knowledgeable specialists and staff collaborate with researchers and community leaders to develop and deliver programs that address the needs of Missourians, including educational attainment, economic development, and healthy people. For more information about MU Extension and Engagement, please visit .

UNIVERSITY INFORMATION

The University of Missouri, also known as Mizzou and MU, is the Flagship University of the four-campus University of Missouri system. It is the state’s land-grant university and one of the most comprehensive universities in the United States. MU’s broad undergraduate programs and its’ graduate, professional and research programs attract annual enrollment of more than 30,000 students. MU is centrally located in Columbia, MO, which is consistently ranked as one of America’s most livable cities. MU Extension programs are located on all four campuses and in 114 counties and St. Louis city.

Qualifications

An earned bachelor’s degree in business, engineering, business education, or related area with appropriate coursework exhibited is required at the time of appointment.

Candidates will be evaluated on:

  • Degree in business, engineering, business education, or related area with appropriate coursework exhibited.
  • Years of experience in business management, marketing, or finance. Related areas include government procurement, marketing, finance, accounting, management, human resources, operations management, e-commerce, or entrepreneurship.
  • Demonstrated ability in applying and transferring research-based knowledge in the above subject matter areas.
  • The ideal candidate will also have successful experiences in operating and managing a business, providing consulting, and/or owning a business, sales, banking and/or lending experience.
  • Ideal candidates will also hold a master’s degree from an accredited institution in business, engineering, business education, or related areas.
  • A knowledge of financial analysis and comparisons and the ability to communicate those reports is desired.
  • Effective and innovative teaching strategies that engage others, including strong listening, written, and oral communication skills. Must be able to integrate new and emerging technology into teaching strategies.
  • Experience in designing, conducting, and evaluating educational programs, and applying research-based knowledge in subject matter areas related to community cooperation and collaboration, capacity assessment and action planning, needs assessment, citizen participation, leadership, resource management and volunteerism is desired.

Anticipated Hiring Range

This position offers a minimum starting salary of $60,000, with the final salary determined based on the candidate’s qualifications and experience.

Application Materials

Complete the brief online application and be prepared to upload:

  • Cover Letter
  • Resume/CV
  • Copies of all academic transcripts, and
  • a list of 3-5 references

For questions regarding the online application process contact MUHR@missouri.edu or call 573.882.7976. For technical problems with the online application process contact Helpdesk@missouri.edu or call 573.882.5000.

Sponsorship Information

Employment visa sponsorship is not available for this position.

Benefit Eligibility

This position is eligible for University benefits. As part of your total compensation, the University offers a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental and vision plans, retirement, and educational fee discounts for all four UM System campuses. For additional information on University benefits, please visit the Faculty & Staff Benefits website at

title: Research Scientist - (Dual Posted with Job ID 61378)
description:
Hiring Department

Life Sciences Center

Job Description

The Center for Influenza and Emerging Infectious Diseases (CIEID) at the University of Missouri is seeking a highly motivated Research Scientist or Senior Research Scientist to strengthen and help lead an expanding interdisciplinary research program in influenza aerosol biology and airborne transmission. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to assume a central scientific leadership role in a multidisciplinary P01 program focused on influenza transmission as part of the NIAID Influenza Transmission Research Consortium (ITRC), as well as complementary NIH R01-supported research on influenza transmission. Together, these programs integrate human studies, controlled animal transmission models, aerosol science, virology, immunology, engineering, and quantitative analysis.

A major goal of the transmission program is to understand why infected hosts differ in the amount and infectivity of virus released into aerosols and why exposure results in infection in some recipients but not others. The scientist will help define the mechanisms that govern influenza transmission by integrating viral, host, immune, aerosol, and environmental factors across human studies and controlled animal models. Research will encompass viral determinants of transmission, infectious virus shedding, aerosol generation and characterization, recipient susceptibility, particle transport and airflow, and other mechanisms governing airborne transmission. We are particularly interested in candidates with expertise in aerosol science, respiratory transmission, engineering, or related areas who can provide scientific and technical leadership and advance interdisciplinary transmission research across the P01 and R01 programs.

Major Responsibilities
• Provide scientific leadership for interdisciplinary research on influenza aerosol biology and airborne transmission, guiding experimental strategy, study design, scientific execution, and integration across human and animal studies. Provide scientific guidance and mentorship to postdoctoral fellows, graduate students, and research staff.
• Lead the scientific design and execution of influenza transmission studies across human studies and controlled animal models, working closely with study coordinators and research teams.
• Provide hands-on participation, as scientifically appropriate, in animal infection and exposure studies, aerosol sampling, specimen collection, and related experimental procedures.
• Investigate viral, host, immune, aerosol, and environmental determinants of infectious virus shedding, aerosol generation, recipient susceptibility, and airborne transmission.
• Lead and advance experimental approaches for studying respiratory aerosols and airborne transmission, including aerosol characterization, particle-size distributions, infectious virus content and stability, bioaerosol collection, and aerosol instrumentation, with emphasis on method development, optimization, validation, and troubleshooting.
• Contribute to studies of airflow, particle transport, aerosol behavior, and other physical and quantitative mechanisms of airborne transmission by working with engineering and modeling teams as appropriate to the scientist’s expertise and individual projects.
• Integrate aerosol, virologic, immunologic, clinical, environmental, and transmission data; analyze and interpret research findings; and contribute substantially to manuscripts, presentations, progress reports, grant applications, and collaborative publications. At the Senior Research Scientist level, assume greater responsibility for scientific project leadership, cross-project scientific integration, mentoring, and development of new research directions.

Research Environment
The Center for Influenza and Emerging Infectious Diseases (CIEID) at the University of Missouri provides a highly collaborative environment for interdisciplinary research on influenza and other emerging respiratory viruses. The Center brings together investigators with expertise in virology, immunology, aerosol science, engineering, animal models, genomics, computational biology, and public health, creating a strong environment for studying influenza transmission across disciplinary boundaries. The program draws on expertise and resources across the School of Medicine, College of Veterinary Medicine, College of Engineering, College of Agriculture, Food and Natural Resources, Bond Life Sciences Center, and Institute for Data Science and Informatics, providing extensive opportunities for cross-disciplinary collaboration. The research program has access to newly established ABSL-2 animal transmission facilities, BSL-3 and ABSL-3 biocontainment facilities, aerosol sampling and engineering capabilities, advanced laboratory automation systems, and institutional core facilities supporting genomics, proteomics, metabolomics, imaging, bioinformatics, and computational biology.

A multidisciplinary P01 program focused on influenza transmission as part of the NIAID Influenza Transmission Research Consortium (ITRC), together with complementary NIH R01-supported research, provides opportunities to integrate human studies with controlled swine and ferret transmission models, develop new approaches for measuring infectious aerosols, and define the mechanisms that govern airborne influenza transmission. The successful candidate will have substantial opportunities for scientific leadership, cross-project scientific integration, interdisciplinary collaboration, publication, grant development, mentoring, and career growth within this expanding influenza transmission research program.

Shift

Monday thru Friday, 8:00 a.m. – 5:00 p.m.; with occasional evening/weekend work depending on experiment needs.

Minimum Qualifications

A Bachelor's degree in related/ relevant area and at least 3 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessary

Preferred Qualifications

• PhD, DVM, MD, or equivalent degree in aerosol science, bioaerosol science, environmental or occupational health, engineering, virology, microbiology, immunology, veterinary sciences, infectious diseases, biomedical sciences, or a related discipline.
• Postdoctoral or equivalent research experience is preferred; the level of appointment will be commensurate with experience and demonstrated scientific independence.
• Candidates with expertise in aerosol science, aerosol biology, or related areas are encouraged to apply even if their prior work was not specifically focused on influenza.

Anticipated Hiring Range

Salary Range: $53,976.00 - $98,072.00 Competitive salary and benefits will be commensurate with experience and qualifications.

description:
Hiring Department

University Physicians

Job Description

#upjobs
This is a dual posting with job ID 59698. The final title will depend on the qualifications of the final candidate.
Review complex clinical documentation and diagnostic results timely to accurately assign codes for diagnoses (ICD-10-CM), procedures (CPT), and applicable modifiers for services provided to assure maximum reimbursement and regulatory compliance.
Assist in the audit of medical records in order to identify potential problems with the coding and reimbursement process such as edits, denials, appeal letter, etc.
Act as liaison between third party payers and assigned departments in order to coordinate all aspects of professional coding.
Provide assistance to faculty, residents and department staff in the standards of medical record documentation and coding of medical records.
Assist in the presentation of training sessions for faculty, residents and staff to inform them of changes made to Medicare billing, federal laws and regulations, and other specific standards and guidelines regarding clinical documentation requirements, procedure and diagnosis coding.
Comply with applicable organization policies; i.e. Quality Assurance, Working Remote, Productivity, etc.
Remote working options available.

Shift

Monday – Friday

Minimum Qualifications

Completion of a coding certification program or equivalent training to obtain certification using ICD-10-CM, ICD-10-PCS, and the CPT-4 coding systems. One (1) year of related medical records coding experience may be substituted.

One of the following certifications within one (1) year as a condition of continued employment in this job classification:

-- Certified Coding Associate (CCA)
-- Certified Coding Specialist (CCS)
-- Registered Health Information Technician (RHIT)
-- Registered Health Information Administrator (RHIA) by the American Health Information Management Association (AHIMA); or

-- Certified Professional Coder (CPC/CPC-A)
-- Certified Outpatient Coder (COC/COC-A)
-- Certified Inpatient Coder (CIC/CIC-A) by the American Academy of Professional Coders (AAPC); or

Specialty certification per the department needs such as:
-- Radiation Oncology Certified Coder (ROCC) by the American Medical Accounting and Consulting Inc (AMAC)

Anticipated Hiring Range

Salary Range: $20.58 - $32.49 hourly
Grade: PAT - 6A

title: Oracle Analytics Cloud (OAC) Developer & Administrator
description:
Are you looking to take the next step in your career as an Oracle Analytics Cloud (OAC) Developer & Administrator? Let's chat and see if we are a good match!


Opportunity:

Virtual Service Operations is searching for an Oracle Analytics Cloud (OAC) Developer & Administrator to join our team. The OAC Developer & Administrator will play a key role in the organization’s transition from Oracle Analytics Server (OAS) to Oracle Analytics Cloud (OAC). This individual will be responsible for developing analytics content in OAC—including reports, dashboards, and data models—while also administering and maintaining the OAC environment. The ideal candidate has hands-on experience performing OAS-to-OAC migrations, including working with RPD models, BAR files, and semantic model conversions.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Develop and maintain reports, dashboards, analyses, and data visualizations in Oracle Analytics Cloud.
  • Administer OAC, including user provisioning, application configuration, performance monitoring, and security management.
  • Troubleshoot data model, performance, and access issues across the OAC environment.
  • Collaborate with data engineering, infrastructure, and business stakeholders to ensure analytics solutions meet project objectives.
  • Document technical processes, semantic model changes, and migration procedures for long-term supportability.
  • Support and execute the migration from OAS to OAC, including: Exporting OAS RPD into BAR files, Importing BAR files into OAC to create/maintain the semantic model and Validating and remediating semantic model changes post-migration

Required Qualifications:

  • 3–5 years of experience developing analytics content using Oracle Analytics Cloud (OAC) or Oracle Analytics Server (OAS).
  • Hands-on experience exporting RPDs to BAR files and importing BAR packages into OAC.
    Strong understanding of OAC semantic models, including subject areas, joins, hierarchies, and data modeling concepts.
  • Experience with OAC administration, including user/role management, application configuration, and environment monitoring.
  • Proficiency in SQL and understanding of relational data structures.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience working with Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), particularly analytics-related services.
  • Hands-on experience with Oracle Data Integration (ODI), Oracle Data Integrator Cloud (ODI-C), Oracle Data Integration Platform Cloud, or comparable ETL/ELT tools such as Informatica, Talend, or DataStage.
  • Advanced SQL skills, including query optimization, performance tuning, and working with complex data models.
  • Prior involvement in full lifecycle migrations from OAS to OAC.
  • Familiarity with data warehousing concepts and modern cloud-based data pipelines

title: Desk Attendant (Student)
description:
Hiring Department

Residential Life - Student Affairs

Job Description

MU Housing, a department within the Division of Student Affairs, provides a world-class housing experience by engaging students within an innovative and educational environment that supports best on-campus housing practices and promotes student success.

This position is customer service centric. Desk Attendants are part of a team that represents the student spirit of MU Housing, serving as the initial contact point through various customer interaction mediums that include all hall information desks, along with email and phone communication.

Desk Attendants are responsible for the day-to-day operations of the hall information desks. This includes organizing and sorting mail and packages; managing the room keys, spare keys, access cards, and other front desk resources for the respective hall; maintaining the appearance of the desks and lobby areas; and other functions necessary for the success of the MU Housing. Desk Attendants are an extension of the MU Housing brand and are on hand to offer guidance and information on MU Housing and Mizzou to residents, prospective students, visitors, faculty, staff, administrators, and alumni.

Desk Attendants are required to work during campus holidays and closures, with the exception of Thanksgiving, Winter, and Spring Breaks. This includes days such as Labor Day, Veterans Day, and MLK Jr. Day.

This appointment also requires that you attend the following paid mandatory orientation and training sessions:

  • Spring 2027 Training: Training is mandatory and is scheduled for January 14 – 15, 2027*.

*Dates are subject to change.

Essential Functions

Desk Attendants may perform some or all of the responsibilities listed below and may be assigned to support one or more service areas within MU Housing.

  • Provide outstanding service to residents, guests, and campus partners by creating a welcoming and supportive environment. Greet individuals entering the building, engage positively with residents, and build meaningful connections through everyday interactions.
  • Support front desk operations by reviewing and completing communication logs, completing shift checklists, conducting nightly key inventories, answering phone calls, monitoring the front desk email account, and maintaining a clean, organized, and professional workspace.
  • Accurately sort, organize, and distribute mail and packages for residents. Assist with locating misplaced items and follow all applicable University procedures, as well as federal and state laws related to mail and package handling.
  • Assist residents with submitting maintenance requests and connecting with appropriate campus resources.
  • Serve as an important communication link between residents, professional staff, and student staff by sharing concerns, suggestions, and information related to the daily operation of MU Housing.
  • Manage room keys, temporary keys, access cards, and other building access resources. Assist with basic lock and ID card troubleshooting and facilitate key card checkouts for authorized University personnel when needed.
  • Represent MU Housing and the University of Missouri in a positive and professional manner. Develop knowledge of Housing, Student Affairs, and campus resources to effectively assist residents and connect them with available support services.
  • Safeguard confidential student and University information. Complete FERPA training prior to beginning Desk Attendant training and comply with FERPA requirements when handling student information and records.
  • Understand and comply with all applicable University policies and procedures, as well as federal, state, and local laws related to job responsibilities, including laws governing the handling of mail and packages.
  • Seek guidance from a supervisor when questions arise regarding policies, procedures, legal requirements, or workplace expectations.

Additional Responsibilities

  • Complete required training on MU Housing operations, University resources, customer service practices, FERPA requirements, and appropriate service delivery methods.
  • Attend and actively participate in all required training sessions, staff meetings, and department workshops.
  • Assist with special projects, events, and initiatives that enhance services and the resident experience within MU Housing.
  • Demonstrate professionalism, accountability, and a commitment to supporting the mission and values of MU Housing and Student Affairs.
  • As with all positions, additional duties and responsibilities may be assigned to support the ongoing operations, goals, and mission of MU Housing and Student Affairs.

Anticipated Hiring Range

title: Psychologist - RSVP Clinician
description:
Hiring Department

The MU Counseling Center - MU Student Health and Well-Being

Job Description

POSITION IS ALSO POSTED AS A SR. COUNSELOR UNDER JOB ID #61350. ONLY ONE WILL BE HIRED.

The MU Counseling Center is part of the MU Student Health and Well-Being unit, which includes the Counseling Center, Student Health Center, and Wellness Resource Center. The Center is an APA-accredited doctoral internship site and serves the MU student community. The Relationship and Sexual Violence Prevention Program (RSVP) is a program embedded within Student Health and Well-Being. RSVP case management and clinical services are embedded within the Counseling Center, while outreach and prevention efforts are embedded within the Wellness Resource Center. The staff seek professionals to join a team who are engaged in efforts to enhance campus services to better support all students.

The successful candidate will promote the well-being of Mizzou students through the provision of high-quality case management and clinical services (including brief individual therapy, group therapy, and crisis counseling) for university students with a special focus on survivors of sexual assault, relationship violence, and stalking. These presenting concerns often overlap with various psychological, academic and interpersonal concerns. The RSVP clinician will work collaboratively with other mental health providers, medical staff, and outreach and health promotion staff in Student Health and Well-being. Competence and experience in the treatment of a wide variety of diagnoses and life problems in addition to relationship and sexual violence is required.

Job Duties Include:

  • Provide confidential case management, brief individual therapy, group counseling, and crisis intervention services to students, with a special focus on survivors of sexual assault, relationship violence, and stalking as part of the Relationship and Sexual Violence Prevention Program (RSVP).
    • Conduct RSVP Brief Screening assessments for students seeking RSVP related clinical services and connect to appropriate case management and on-going clinical services as needed.
    • Provide case management services depending on individual needs of the student, including but not limited to safety planning, assisting with referral needs, providing resources, and trauma-specific psychoeducation.
    • Provide brief therapy to students referred for on-going clinical services.
    • Perform crisis and consultation services during regular business hours that require complex clinical decision-making.
    • Maintain timely, accurate, and complete documentation of all service contacts as required by Center policies and procedures and state laws.
    • Develop and facilitate RSVP related group therapy.
  • Provide prevention and outreach services centered around relationship violence, sexual assault prevention, impacts of interpersonal violence, and other related topics.
    • Work closely with the RSVP Health Educator at the Wellness Resource Center (WRC) and other WRC Health Educators and staff to develop and provide prevention and outreach services on campus.
    • Foster relationships with key campus contacts for the purpose of developing and implementing programmatic interventions that result in student participation.
  • Coordinate with other campus offices that work with survivors – such as the Student Health Center, MU Police Department, Student Accountability and Support, Care Team, and Office of Institutional Equity (OIE).
  • Coordinate with community partners who also serve survivors in the larger Columbia area and make referrals and connections as needed.
  • Become familiar with the Clery Act (20 U.S.C. 1092(f)) and the Violence Against Women Act (VAWA) and related federal requirements for universities and colleges, including programming, service provision, and reporting.
  • May conduct supervision and training for post-doctoral residents, doctoral interns in our APA-accredited doctoral internship, post-MA fellows, and graduate students in training (as allowed by licensure status).
  • Contribute as a member of the MUCC team to the development and implementation of goals, philosophies, policies, and procedures that support the psychological needs of Mizzou students and cultivate a culture of well-being on campus. Serve on relevant MUCC and/or University committees as requested.

The successful candidate will possess strong interpersonal, oral, and written skills; value a multifaceted approach involving linked clinical and training efforts; demonstrate the ability to work collaboratively with colleagues, campus partners, and student groups; exhibit interpersonal flexibility with a sense of humor; understand the importance of life balance and have a strong commitment to the developmental perspective of counseling services.

Shift

Monday through Friday, 8:00am - 5:00pm

This position may require evening and weekend hours supporting activities and programs within the department. Occasionally division and campus projects may require additional hours outside of your normal schedule.

Minimum Qualifications

Doctorate degree in Psychology and licensure (or eligibility to be licensed) as a Psychologist within the State of Missouri.

Preferred Qualifications

Two or more years of post-degree experience working with sexual assault, relationship violence, and stalking. Must be fully licensed to practice independently as a Licensed Psychologist in the state of Missouri and licensure must be maintained as a requirement for employment. Provisional Licensure is not accepted.

While candidates should not exclude themselves from consideration for a position, preference will be given to applicants who also have extensive experience providing case management and clinical services to survivors of relationship and sexual violence. Additionally, a minimum of one year of clinical experience working in a college counseling center (this may include practica, internship or fellowship experience) or with a college aged population is desired.

Anticipated Hiring Range

Salary Range: $60,944 - $112,320 per year

title: Field Specialist in Regional Economic Development – Howell County, MO
description:
Hiring Department

University of Missouri (MU) Office of Extension and Engagement

Business & Community Extension

Job Description

MU TITLE: Assistant/Associate/Full Extension Professional

LOCATION: West Plains, Missouri, and primarily serves Howell, Texas, Wright, Douglas, Ozark, Shannon and Oregon Counties in Southwest Region with additional service across the state as needed.

Specialist Emphasis

This position is responsible for planning, implementing and evaluating regional economic development educational programs that support and complement existing economic development efforts in Missouri communities. These efforts may involve:

  • Developing and facilitating educational trainings that strengthen regional leaders’ capacity to foster economic prosperity
  • Developing economic development guides and materials on topics such as tourism, understanding your region’s economic drivers, and strengthening community support of entrepreneurs, housing trends. Etc.
  • Facilitating forums and conferences that bring regional and community partners together to foster economic development opportunities
  • Offering technical assistance contracts, often in collaboration with other state specialists, that support efforts such as; business surveys, tourism assessments, broadband ambassador training, etc.
  • Connecting and convening appropriate regional and state partners with community leaders to address economic development opportunities and challenges

Effective specialists will apply interdisciplinary knowledge related to general community, economic, business and workforce development needs in the counties served. Educational programs may consist of facilitated workshops, publishing guides or regional reports, technical assistance, and online programming that provide research-based material to local clients aligned with state specialists and Extension colleagues.

Effective specialists will work in close collaboration with their respective Regional Planning Commissions, state and local economic development departments, workforce boards, and other relevant organizations to leverage efforts and funding opportunities.

This position is a 12-month, ranked, non-tenure track appointment at the rank of assistant, associate, or full Extension Professional. Rank will be determined at the time of the appointment based on qualifications and experience in accordance with the MU Extension faculty standards. This position will hold the working title of Field Specialist in Regional Economic Development.

As a Field Specialist, your workload distribution at appointment will be 90% Extension Teaching and 10% Traditional Service.

This appointment is renewable annually at the discretion of the University and workload distribution may change at the discretion of Extension leadership. Circumstances affecting continued employment include, but are not limited to, work performance, fund availability, and educational priorities.

CORE DUTIES OF MU EXTENSION SPECIALISTS

MU Extension Specialists deliver the University of Missouri to all Missourians. They serve all Missourians by bringing research-based solutions to work on local problems. MU Extension Specialists teach new and foundational concepts, link people to resources, support partner organizations, participate in research, train volunteers, evaluate programs, foster innovation, and serve communities. MU Extension Specialists work as a team to expand educational attainment, foster economic development, and improve health outcomes. These core duties fall into three major areas:

Educate, Create, and Connect.

  • Educate. MU Extension specialists design, conduct, and evaluate educational programs. MU Extension specialists teach research-based information via meetings, in-person, and online courses, continuing education classes, technical assistance, volunteer training, media, websites, consultation, and other educational methods. They provide educational programs that support the individual, organizational, and community goals of Missouri’s learners and clients.
  • Create. MU Extension specialists develop innovative and research-informed educational products, services, materials, and other scholarly works. These include curricula, publications, presentations, educational tools, websites, and similar resources. MU Extension specialists obtain and use extramural funding to support creative works. MU Extension specialists contribute to the scholarship of Extension and Engagement by evaluating programs that result in learning and behavior changes that impact individuals and communities.
  • Connect. MU Extension specialists engage with learners, stakeholders, volunteers, and communities, including county extension councils, government officials and agencies, partners, and University and professional organizations. MU Extension specialists listen and respond with care. MU Extension specialists intentionally foster engaged partnerships and robust connections to the wide array of programs offered by the whole University of Missouri System.

Professional Expectations

  • Engage with stakeholders in all coverage counties to identify educational needs and then collaborate with appropriate internal and external partners to meet programming needs, incorporating timely marketing strategies.
  • Create an annual plan-of-work that reflects local needs and aligns with statewide program area efforts. Provide a monthly report for assigned county extension councils, supervisors, county commissioners and others, regarding programmatic efforts. Attend at least one county extension council meeting each month and provide a program review with feedback and analysis for the respective coverage area.
  • Collaborate with campus-based specialists on research projects and then deliver findings from those efforts via demonstrations, field days, courses, workshops, consultations, publications, and appropriate media.
  • Effectively work with supervisors, other specialists, and local leaders to complete administrative tasks as needed to support county efforts.
  • Demonstrate competency in communication, educational programming, subject matter knowledge, educational delivery, volunteer management, grant acquisition, teamwork, interpersonal relations, organization knowledge, leadership, and professionalism.
  • Offer timely, research-based information during times of natural disasters or unexpected catastrophic events.
  • Represent the University of Missouri on boards and committees for assigned program area.
  • Participate in professional development events to improve both technical and leadership skills.
  • Other duties and responsibilities as assigned to support the mission of MU Extension.

Additional Expectations

  • MU Extension Specialists travel regularly throughout Missouri and occasionally to out-of-state locations. MU Extension requires specialists to have a valid Missouri driver’s license, a legally operating vehicle, and wireless telephone/data service for university use. MU Extension specialists receive reimbursement for approved travel expenses, per University of Missouri policy.
  • MU Extension programs often occur outside of normal business hours. MU Extension Specialists should expect to attend these events as needed to meet the needs of learners, clients, and stakeholders.

MU EXTENSION LEADERSHIP RECEIVED

The Senior Program Director for Business & Community provides overall programmatic leadership. Programmatic supervision comes from the Regional Economic Development Educational Director and administrative oversight from the Southwest Regional Director.

MU EXTENSION INFORMATION

The University of Missouri (MU) Office of Extension and Engagement’s distinct land-grant mission is to improve lives, communities, and economies by producing relevant, reliable, and responsive educational strategies throughout Missouri. Our dedicated and knowledgeable specialists and staff collaborate with researchers and community leaders to develop and deliver programs that address the needs of Missourians, including educational attainment, economic development, and healthy people. For more information about MU Extension and Engagement, please visit .

UNIVERSITY INFORMATION

The University of Missouri, also known as Mizzou and MU, is the Flagship University of the four-campus University of Missouri System. It is one of the state’s land-grant universities. MU’s comprehensive undergraduate programs and its graduate, professional, and research programs attract an annual enrollment of more than 30,000 students. MU Extension and Engagement programs are located on all four campuses and in 114 counties and St. Louis city.

Qualifications

An earned PhD or master’s degree at time of appointment.

Candidates will be evaluated on:

Degree in economics, urban or regional planning, business, finance, economic development, sociology, public policy or closely related field.

Coursework demonstrating knowledge of economic development strategies and data analysis skills.

Experience in the field of economic development, business or financial analysis.

Demonstrated capability to translate research into educational programs in regional economic development for audiences of all age groups is critical.

The ability to exhibit effective and innovative teaching strategies that engage others, including strong listening and written and oral communication skills.

This position offers a minimum starting salary of $58,000, with the final salary determined based on the candidate’s qualifications and experience.

• Cover Letter

• a list of 3-5 references

For questions regarding the online application process contact MUHR@missouri.edu or call 573.882.7976. For technical problems with the online application process contact Helpdesk@missouri.edu or call 573.882.5000.

title: Learning Specialist Rural Scholars & Pathways
description:
Hiring Department

Department of School of Medicine Expansion

Job Description

This position is responsible for developing, implementing, and evaluating academic support services that promote the success of undergraduate pathway participants and medical students. The role provides individualized coaching, learning strategy instruction, and examination preparation designed to improve academic readiness, matriculation, retention, progression, and licensure outcomes. Emphasis is placed on supporting learners from rural and nontraditional backgrounds. The position contributes to the School of Medicine's strategic priorities by strengthening the physician workforce pipeline and supporting the preparation of physicians who will serve communities across Missouri.

Core Responsibilities:

Provide Individualized Academic Coaching and Student Success Support – 30%

Provide longitudinal academic coaching and learning support for students across pathway, pre-admission, and medical education programs. Develop individualized strategies that strengthen study skills, time management, self-directed learning, and academic performance. Support learners through academic challenges, educational transitions, and key progression milestones using evidence-based interventions.

Support Entrance and Licensure Examination Preparation – 20%

Guide students in preparing for high-stakes examinations, including the MCAT, USMLE Step 1, and USMLE Step 2 CK. Assist learners in developing personalized study plans, preparation timelines, and effective test-taking strategies. Monitor readiness through performance metrics and provide targeted support to enhance examination outcomes.

Develop and Deliver Academic Success Programming and Resources – 15%

Design, implement, and evaluate workshops, presentations, and educational resources that promote academic success, learning effectiveness, resilience, and examination readiness. Create scalable programming that supports learners across multiple stages of the educational continuum.

Monitor Academic Performance and Conduct Proactive Outreach – 15%

Utilize academic performance data and referral processes to identify learners who may benefit from additional support. Conduct timely outreach and implement targeted interventions that promote academic progression, engagement, retention, and student success.

Collaborate with Faculty, Staff, and Academic Leaders – 10%

Partner with Student Affairs, faculty, pathway program leaders, and curriculum stakeholders to align academic support services with learner needs and institutional goals. Participate in initiatives that strengthen student success, educational outcomes, and workforce development objectives.

Support Cross-Campus Services, Assessment, and Continuous Improvement – 10%

Coordinate academic support services across the Columbia and Springfield campuses to ensure equitable access and consistent delivery. Collect, analyze, and report student success metrics to support program evaluation, accreditation activities, continuous quality improvement, and strategic decision-making.

Monday – Friday
8:00 a.m. – 5:00 p.m.

A Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education and experience and at least 3 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessary

Education: Bachelor’s degree

The University of Missouri School of Medicine is entering a period of strategic growth and innovation, highlighted by the UM Board of Curators’ approval to expand the Springfield clinical campus into a full four-year medical program. This expansion will increase total enrollment across Columbia and Springfield to more than 670 medical students and strengthen the university’s commitment to addressing Missouri’s physician shortage, particularly in rural regions. Beginning in 2027, first-year students will be welcomed to the Springfield campus, with fully identical curricula delivered across both sites through shared faculty, expanded simulation resources, and bi-directional livestreamed instruction. This milestone underscores the university’s broader mission to enhance statewide access to high-quality medical education and clinical care.

Complementing this statewide investment, the School of Medicine’s MOmentum curriculum redesign is transforming how future physicians are trained. MOmentum builds on MU’s long-standing learner-centered approach by integrating cutting-edge technology, innovative teaching strategies, and comprehensive support systems to create a dynamic and effective learning environment. The redesigned curriculum emphasizes evidence-based education, active learning, individualized support, early clinical exposure, and the development of lifelong, self-directed learners prepared to navigate an increasingly complex health care landscape. Through MOmentum, the School of Medicine is charting a bold path forward, ensuring students graduate with the advanced skills, adaptability, and patient-centered mindset needed to excel in modern medicine.

title: Program Manager - Wan Lab
description:
Hiring Department

Bond Life Sciences Center

Job Description

The Program Manager will provide program management and administrative leadership for multidisciplinary research programs within the NextGen Center for Influenza and Emerging Infectious Diseases (CIEID), with primary responsibility for coordinating a major NIH Program Project (P01) on influenza transmission and supporting the Center Director’s broader portfolio of research funded by federal agencies, such as NIH, NSF, and USDA, as well as industry-sponsored and collaborative research programs.

Reporting to the Center Director, the incumbent will coordinate research activities across investigators, projects, cores, study teams, and administrative units; track milestones and deliverables; facilitate communication and meetings, monitor program timelines; and support timely completion of sponsor requirements. The position will work closely with scientific investigators, human and animal study coordinators, laboratory management, research staff, institutional offices, and external collaborators.

The Program Manager will provide the organizational framework needed to keep complex, multidisciplinary research programs aligned and progressing efficiently while allowing investigators and scientific staff to focus on scientific leadership and research execution. This is a research administration and program management position and does not require laboratory experimentation or independent scientific interpretation of research data.

Key responsibilities include:
• Manage day-to-day program operations for the NIH P01 and other major research programs by maintaining integrated project plans, timelines, milestones, deliverables, and action items and identifying issues that may affect program progress.
• Coordinate activities across P01 projects and cores and other collaborative research programs, working with investigators, human and animal study coordinators, laboratory management, research staff, administrative offices, and external collaborators.
• Organize and facilitate program meetings, investigator meetings, and sponsor-related activities; prepare agendas and program materials; document decisions and action items; and follow up with responsible team members to support timely completion.
• Track sponsor requirements, reporting deadlines, research milestones, and other program deliverables and work with investigators and administrative partners to address delays, dependencies, or operational issues.
• Coordinate preparation of NIH progress reports, sponsor updates, program documentation, and other required deliverables by gathering information from investigators and project teams and supporting accurate and timely submission.
• Support the Center Director in managing the broader research portfolio by maintaining an overview of active and planned projects, major deadlines, collaborative activities, and program priorities.
• Facilitate communication and coordination among scientific teams, study coordinators, laboratory management, institutional research and administrative offices, and external partners to strengthen interdisciplinary research activities within CIEID.

Bachelor's degree in life sciences, biomedical sciences, business administration, public administration, project management, or related field; advanced degree (MS, MPH, MBA, PhD, or equivalent) preferred.

Experience in research program management, sponsored research, project management, clinical or translational research operations, or coordination of complex multidisciplinary programs is preferred.

Experience with NIH-funded research, including multi-project awards, is highly desirable.
Strong organizational, communication, problem-solving, and project-management skills, with demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities, track deadlines and deliverables, and work effectively with investigators, research staff, administrators, and external collaborators.

title: Credentialing Specialist II
description:
Hiring Department

Department of Family & Community Medicine

Job Description

Credentialing Specialist II

The Departments of Family and Community Medicine, Radiology, and Radiation Oncology are seeking a highly organized, detail-oriented Credentialing Specialist to provide comprehensive credentialing, compliance, and administrative support for physicians, advanced practice providers, and other healthcare professionals. This position plays a critical role in ensuring clinicians maintain the credentials, licenses, privileges, and regulatory requirements necessary to support the School of Medicine's mission of excellence in patient care, education, research, and engagement.

The Credentialing Specialist serves as the primary resource for credentialing and privileging activities, collaborating with department leadership, medical staff offices, healthcare organizations, and external agencies to ensure accurate, timely, and compliant credentialing processes.

This is an exciting opportunity for an individual who thrives in a fast-paced healthcare environment and enjoys managing complex processes that directly support exceptional patient care, clinician onboarding, and regulatory compliance.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Coordinate and oversee the initial credentialing, privileging, and recredentialing processes for physicians, advanced practice providers, and other clinical providers.
  • Maintain credentialing records and files for medical staff members, advanced practice professionals, and affiliated providers in accordance with institutional, regulatory, and accreditation requirements.
  • Prepare, review, and submit credentialing applications and supporting documentation to healthcare systems, medical staff offices, regulatory agencies, and payer organizations to ensure timely approvals and compliance.
  • Coordinate provider credentialing activities with MU Health Care, University Physicians, the VA, Mercy, and other affiliated healthcare organizations.
  • Monitor provider licensure, certifications, registrations, privileges, prescribing authorities, and other required credentials to ensure ongoing compliance and timely renewals.
  • Create, maintain, and track Collaborative Practice Agreements and other required provider documentation.
  • Manage and track Ongoing Professional Practice Evaluation (OPPE) and Focused Professional Practice Evaluation (FPPE) reporting activities.
  • Utilize Medical Staff Office systems and other designated databases to maintain credentialing data, generate provider rosters, compliance reports, and operational metrics.
  • Prepare and maintain reports related to credentialing, privileging, and provider compliance.
  • Monitor regulatory, accreditation, and institutional requirements and assist with maintaining departmental compliance standards.
  • Safeguard the confidentiality, accuracy, and integrity of all credentialing information, provider records, and verification processes.
  • Serve as a key point of contact for providers, department leadership, Medical Staff Offices, healthcare organizations, and external agencies, ensuring effective communication throughout the credentialing process.
  • Identify and resolve credentialing-related issues and escalate concerns to appropriate leadership as needed.
  • Support departmental operations through additional duties and special projects as assigned.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Strong organizational skills and exceptional attention to detail.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines in a fast-paced healthcare environment.
  • Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and exercise sound judgment when handling sensitive information.
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with a variety of internal and external stakeholders.

Impact of the Position

This position is essential to maintaining clinician compliance, facilitating timely onboarding and recredentialing, supporting patient care operations, and ensuring adherence to regulatory and accreditation standards. The Credentialing Specialist helps mitigate compliance risk, prevents lapses in clinical privileges and licenses, and supports uninterrupted clinical services across multiple departments and healthcare organizations.

Shift

Monday – Friday
8:00 a.m. – 5:00 p.m.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in business, health administration, finance, or an equivalent combination of education and experience from which comparable knowledge, skills, and abilities can be acquired.

Two (2) years of experience with graduate medical education, medical staff credentialing, HR, provider enrollment, or work that involves confirming work history, education, training, background, and/or reference checks, or similar experience.

Anticipated Hiring Range

Salary Range: $22.00 - $34.74 hourly
Grade: PAT - 007

Internal applicants can determine their university title by accessing the Talent Profile tile in myHR.

Application Materials

In addition to the Online Application, please provide Resume and cover letter.

This position is eligible for University benefits. As part of your total compensation, the University offers a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental and vision plans, retirement, paid time off, short- and long-term disability, paid parental leave, paid caregiver leave, and educational fee discounts for all four UM System campuses. description:
Hiring Department

If you would like to learn more about the Resident Advisor positions, additional information can be found at

TO BE CONSIDERED FOR THE AY 2027-2028 RESIDENT ADVISOR POSITION, YOU MUST APPLY FOR BOTH SPRING 2027 AND AY2027-2028.

MU Housing - Student Affairs

Job Description

MU Housing, a department within the division of Student Affairs, provides a world-class housing experience by engaging students within an innovative and educational environment that supports best on-campus housing practices and promotes student success.

Resident Advisors (RAs) are focused on building community within the residence halls. RAs serve as mentors and leaders within the halls by having a robust knowledge of the University of Missouri and MU Housing. Resident Advisors will connect residents to leadership, service and involvement opportunities on campus. As agents of the University, Resident Advisors are part of a team that strives to support and know their residents, while also creating a strong sense of belonging within the halls and on campus. Resident Advisors serve as ambassadors for MU Housing, the Division of Student Affairs and Mizzou and must serve as positive members of the university community while in their positions.

Resident Advisors are a presence in the halls. They are responsible for setting and role modeling expectations on their respective floors by abiding by and enforcing MU Housing and University guidelines and procedures. Resident Advisors help create a positive community in the hall by managing conflict between roommates and residents. They also have a thorough understanding of emergency protocols and the opening and closing procedures.

Resident Advisors are expected to be a positive brand ambassador for MU Housing by communicating the benefits of living in the halls, while also promoting employment opportunities within the department. Resident Advisors assist with contracting in their position; this includes tabling, working, and planning hall events and having conversations with residents about living in MU Housing.

MU Housing is a 365/24/7 operation, and RA presence is required to provide exceptional services and experiences for our residents. Resident Advisors may be required to complete tasks in the residence halls during scheduled academic breaks and university closures.

Resident Advisors are required to arrive early in August and January to participate in annual RA training, Mizzou Move-In and Welcome Week activities. They are also required to stay late in December and May to assist with closing hall operations for the semester and academic year.

Essential Functions

Resident Advisors will perform the duties listed below and may be assigned to operate in one or more service areas or functions.

Community Development and Sense of Belonging

  • Spend time on the floor to build community within their respective floors, halls and neighborhood by making residents feel welcome.
  • Support and know the residents living on their floor and in their building.
  • Build relationships with their residents by getting to know who they are and establishing how they can mentor them.
  • Be a presence in the halls by spending time in common areas and being social.
  • Plan and attend events within the hall/neighborhood, and support programs and initiatives put on by MU Housing, Student Affairs and Mizzou.
  • Maintain extensive knowledge about the University of Missouri, academic programs and involvement opportunities on campus.
  • Connect residents to leadership, service, involvement and employment opportunities on campus and within the department.
  • Support the academic mission of the University by fostering an integrative learning environment through the facilitation of programming.
  • Collaborate with campus partners and programs to support already existing events and initiatives. Support relationships across campus to avoid duplicating efforts.
  • Act as a leader on the floor and within the respective hall.
  • Manage and mediate conflict between residents and roommates.

On-Call, Operational, and Administrative Responsibilities

  • Provide operational and administrative support for the residence hall.
  • Serve in an on-call duty rotation overnight and as situations arise (with regard to class schedule).
  • Understand and carry out emergency procedures and crisis response.
  • Understand, abide by and enforce policies and procedures for MU Housing.
  • Be responsible for the cleanliness of communal spaces and, potentially, incidents involving bodily fluids.
  • Act as situationally critical staff and follow instructions for dealing with situations that impact the residence halls.

Required Attendance and Participation

Resident Advisors are expected and required to arrive to and depart campus, as well as participate in, the following in accordance with the dates outlined below:

January 14, 2027: RA Winter Training Check-In (arrive by 8pm)

January 14-17, 2027: RA Winter Training (anticipate required participation between 8am-7pm)

May 17, 2027: End of Year Hall Closing (anticipate departure after 10am)

ALL DATES AND TIMES ARE SUBJECT TO CHANGEALL DATES AND TIMES ARE SUBJECT TO CHANGE

  • Attend weekly RA staff meetings.
  • Attend one-on-one meetings as scheduled by the supervisor.
  • Attend RA and other training and activities as required by MU Housing.
  • Training is a mandatory part of your appointment and failure to attend training may result in appointment action up to and including termination from the appointment.

  • As with all positions, involvement with other duties and responsibilities is expected in order to serve and maintain our departmental and Student Affairs mission.

Anticipated Hiring Range

Compensation includes a single residence hall room and a top-tier dining meal plan for the term of the appointment. RAs are required to maintain 100% occupancy in their university-provided room, suite and/or apartment. The university housing assignment is decided at the discretion of MU Housing.

Shift

Average hours per week: 20 (hours may vary)

This position may require evening and weekend hours supporting activities and programs within the department. Occasionally division and campus projects may require additional hours outside of your normal schedule.

Minimum Qualifications

  • To be eligible for a student title, an individual must be enrolled at the University of Missouri during the term of the housing contract and RA appointment.
  • Enrollment in the summer session is not required if the student was enrolled in the Spring semester and is pre-enrolled for the Fall semester.
  • Selection is contingent upon successful results of an Office of Institutional Equity and Office of Student Accountability & Support check and review by the office of the Vice Chancellor for Student Affairs.
  • Applicants must be in good standing with MU Housing and the University.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Lived in MU Housing for 2 semesters prior to start of the appointment.

Job Description

Perform skilled work on a technical level in the HVAC field involving repair and maintenance of HVAC systems or other trade areas relating to repair and preventative maintenance of buildings, equipment and fixtures. May perform All work is subject to spot checking and inspection for conformance to specifications and accepted standards of the trade.

Key Responsibilities

  • HVAC:
    • Perform preventative maintenance on rotating equipment including pumps, air compressors, fans and air handling units with the goal of assuring a minimum of 90 days of reliable, trouble free operations.
    • Monitor pre- and final-filter loading conditions and replace when necessary to maintain good indoor air quality in campus buildings.
    • Monitor bearing conditions with infrared temperature gun.
    • Check and maintain auto-lube systems of high RPM equipment.
    • Monitor drive belts wear condition and judge when replacement is required.
    • Monitor shave conditions and diagnose and replace when excessive wear is found.
    • Diagnose and report need for major repairs to pumps, air compressors and fans to supervisor.
    • Survey campus equipment periodically to confirm equipment data regarding motor types, sizes, sheaves, belts and filters are correct.
    • Prepare documentation required to make the preventative maintenance program effective.
    • Utilize testing equipment such as laser sheave and shaft alignment tools, electrical multi-meters, and Magnehelic gauges to check that equipment is operating properly.
  • Other preventative maintenance:
    • Make scheduled inspections of buildings, structures and adjoining grounds to detect defects and signs of deterioration.
    • Determine necessary repairs and undertake such maintenance and repairs as are within scope of responsibility.
    • Report other deficiencies to superior.
    • Make preliminary inspections of work where work orders do not clearly indicate scope of repair required.
    • Perform routine carpentry repairs as assigned or as indicated from inspections: nail down loose boards, repair door hardware, replace worn or rotten floor boards, remove and replace siding, replace portions of wall board and ceilings, repair fireproofing surfaces; tighten or replace loosened supports and planks, replace or repair door knobs, brackets, racks, etc.
    • Use such hand tools, power equipment and materials as are common to the carpentry trade.
    • Perform minor electrical tasks: replace light bulbs, fluorescent lights, ballasts and fuses.
    • Make minor interior wiring repairs, replace and make minor motor repairs and adjustments.
    • Replace sockets, plugs and outlets; maintain such equipment as fans, motors, heating appliances, elevators and light fixtures.
    • Test circuits for continuity and proper connections. Use such hand tools, equipment and materials as are common to the electrical trade.
    • Perform routine interior and exterior plumbing tasks: cover exposed sections of pipe, clear simple stoppages, check and repair defective plumbing parts, make replacement connections on air, gas and water lines, and fixtures such as water closets, lavatories, showers, sinks and heaters.
    • Use such hand tools, power equipment and materials as are common to the plumbing trade.
    • Conduct preventive maintenance of equipment such as oiling moving parts, motor bearings, fans, cleaning or replacing filters, etc.
    • Inspect equipment to detect worn or damaged parts.
    • Replace or assist in the repair of same.
    • May perform touch up painting in areas where repairs are made; assist other craftsmen as directed; drive truck when needed.
  • Clean, maintain, safely operate and properly store all tools and equipment.
  • Observe and enforce all safety requirements related to equipment operation.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Shift

Monday-Friday, 8:00am-4:30pm

Minimum Qualifications

  • HVAC:
    • Two years of experience and training in preventative maintenance of rotating equipment.
  • Other preventative maintenance:
    • Three years of experience in building trades or building mechanical maintenance, or equivalent
      competence.
  • All personnel:
    • A high school diploma or equivalent combination of education and experience from which
      comparable knowledge, skills and abilities can be acquired is required.
    • Skill in maintenance and use of tools, equipment and materials of the trade.
    • Possession of a valid motor vehicle driver’s license may be required.
    • Ability on a daily basis to:
      • Grasp, lift, maneuver, rotate and otherwise use small to large trade tools and equipment.
      • Grasp, lift, carry and set down heavy objects weighing from 50-80 pounds.
      • Grasp, turn, twist, pull, push, lift and otherwise move equipment, controls, parts, etc.
      • Visually assess maintenance, construction and repair needs.
      • Climb and work from ladders, scaffolding, and stairs.

Anticipated Hiring Range

The anticipated hiring range for this position has been established as $15.60-$20.50 hourly.

About the Role

We are seeking a highly organised and proactive Security Admin to support our operational teams and ensure the effective delivery of security services across multiple contracts. This is a fast-paced role requiring strong attention to detail, excellent communication skills, and the ability to make informed decisions under pressure.

Working closely with Operations Managers, frontline security personnel, subcontractors, and the Operations Director, you will play a key role in maintaining service delivery standards, managing staffing requirements, and supporting out-of-hours operations.

Key Responsibilities

  • Schedule and deploy security personnel to ensure all contracted hours are covered accurately.
  • Maintain staffing levels across all contracts and respond quickly to operational changes.
  • Monitor out-of-hours activity and support the health, safety, and welfare of all deployed staff.
  • Ensure service delivery standards and key performance indicators (KPIs) are consistently achieved.
  • Maintain accurate records within the Smart Task system and other internal platforms.
  • Communicate operational updates and scheduling changes to security personnel.
  • Monitor bookings, check calls, attendance, and shift compliance, escalating any concerns where required.
  • Manage and escalate incidents, sickness, absenteeism, and operational issues in a timely manner.
  • Respond efficiently to client requests and last-minute changes.
  • Escalate client complaints to the appropriate management team and ensure prompt resolution.
  • Produce daily operational reports and hand over outstanding tasks to the relevant personnel.
  • Create ad hoc sites within company systems and complete associated assignment instructions and risk assessments.
  • Prepare cost models, business documentation, and administrative submissions as required.
  • Archive completed sites and maintain system accuracy.
  • Carry out payroll and billing reconciliations to ensure accurate pay and charge processes.

What We're Looking For

Essential Requirements

  • Valid SIA Licence.
  • Ability to pass or hold a valid DBS check.
  • Exceptional attendance and reliability.
  • Strong attention to detail and accuracy.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to work under pressure and meet tight deadlines.
  • Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office applications.
  • Strong organisational and problem-solving skills.
  • Professional and customer-focused approach.

Desirable

  • Previous experience within the security industry.
  • Experience in scheduling, workforce planning, or control room operations.
  • Knowledge of Smart Task or similar workforce management systems.

What Success Looks Like

As a Security Admin, you will ensure staffing requirements are met, operational systems remain accurate, and both clients and frontline teams receive excellent support. Your ability to manage competing priorities, communicate effectively, and maintain high standards of administration will be critical to the success of the role.

Additional Information

The duties listed above are not exhaustive and may be amended to meet business needs. The successful candidate will be expected to undertake responsibilities of a similar nature where required.

Reporting Structure

The Security Admin reports directly to the North, Midlands and K9 Operations Director.

Confidentiality

This role requires a high level of discretion and professionalism. The successful candidate will handle sensitive business and personnel information and must maintain strict confidentiality at all times.
