title: Digital Learning Designer
description:
About The Role:

As a Digital Learning Designer, you will join our Learning & Development team to design and create engaging, accessible and effective digital learning experiences for colleagues across OCS.

Working closely with your line manager, you will explore learning needs, brainstorm ideas and develop creative solutions to challenges brought to the team. Projects will vary widely, from eLearning on topics such as safeguarding or Modern Slavery, to supporting new systems and wider Learning & Development initiatives.

The role goes beyond eLearning. You will also create resources such as videos, guides, manuals, presentations, forms and job aids, helping to identify the right solution for each learning need.

OCS is a fast-paced organisation, so you will need to be comfortable managing multiple projects, working with stakeholders and subject matter experts, and adapting to changing priorities.

This role is suited to someone with relevant L&D, training or content creation experience who is looking to further develop their career in digital learning.

Key Responsibilities

Digital Learning Design & Development

  • Design and develop engaging eLearning and digital learning resources for colleagues across OCS.
  • Work closely with your line manager to brainstorm ideas and develop creative solutions to learning needs and challenges brought to the Digital Learning team.
  • Explore the purpose, audience and desired outcome of learning requests to help identify the most appropriate solution.
  • Recognise that eLearning may not always be the best solution and contribute ideas for alternative approaches where appropriate.
  • Use tools such as Articulate 360 to create interactive and engaging eLearning experiences.
  • Create and edit video-based learning content using tools such as Synthesia.
  • Develop additional learning resources including guides, manuals, presentations, job aids, digital forms and supporting documents.
  • Turn complex or technical information into learning that is clear, practical and easy to understand.
  • Consider the needs of the learner throughout the design process, including accessibility, usability and different levels of digital confidence.
  • Bring creativity and new ideas to projects while ensuring learning meets the intended business need.
  • Review and update existing learning content to ensure it remains accurate, relevant and effective.
  • Explore new tools and technologies, including AI, that could enhance how learning content is designed and delivered.

About You

We're looking for someone with previous experience or knowledge of Learning & Development who is ready to develop their career within digital learning.

You'll have experience creating learning, training or digital resources, with a creative approach and an interest in designing engaging and effective learning experiences.

Essential Criteria

  • Previous experience within Learning & Development, Human Resources, training or a similar people-focused area, or relevant exposure to Learning & Development or workplace learning.
  • Previous experience creating learning, training or digital resources, with examples of content you have developed.
  • A genuine interest in digital learning, eLearning and learning design.
  • Creative thinking and the ability to contribute ideas and potential solutions.
  • Good written communication skills and strong attention to detail.
  • Confidence using digital technology and learning new systems and tools.
  • Experience using Microsoft 365 applications.
  • Good organisation skills and the ability to manage multiple pieces of work at the same time.
  • Ability to take ownership of your workload and work independently when required.
  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced environment where priorities and deadlines can change.
  • An understanding of the importance of creating inclusive and accessible learning experiences for different audiences.

Desirable Criteria

  • Previous experience using Articulate 360, including Storyline or Rise.
  • Experience using Synthesia or other video creation and editing tools.
  • Experience using eLearning authoring or digital content creation tools.
  • An understanding of learning design or instructional design principles.
  • Experience working with subject matter experts to develop learning or training resources.
  • Experience using Learning Management Systems.
  • Experience using Microsoft Forms.
  • Experience using AI or emerging technologies to support content creation.

Previous experience with Articulate, Synthesia or other eLearning creation tools would be a strong advantage. However, we're also interested in candidates who have relevant L&D experience and can demonstrate that they have already created effective learning or training resources using other tools.

What Success Looks Like

Success means creating engaging learning that genuinely helps colleagues understand and apply what they need to know.

You'll work closely with your line manager to solve problems, develop ideas and turn learning needs into effective solutions. As you develop, you'll take increasing ownership of projects from initial request through to design, development and launch.

You'll bring creativity, curiosity and new ideas to the team, while managing your workload effectively and building strong relationships with stakeholders.

title: Dean, Henry W. Bloch School of Management
description:
Hiring Department

Henry W. Bloch School of Management

The Bloch School was founded in 1953 and endowed by Henry Bloch in 1986. Henry W. Bloch is the co-founder of tax empire H&R Block and is considered one of the world's greatest entrepreneurs. He is not only the Bloch School benefactor but also the role model for what we teach: he embodies the philosophy of working hard, generating wealth and success, and completing the continuum by giving back to the community through philanthropy and social entrepreneurship. The Bloch School of Management continues to benefit from the generous and steadfast support of the Marion and Henry Bloch Family Foundation, which plays an important role in advancing the School’s pursuit of excellence.

Undergraduate and graduate students can pursue degrees across five academic areas including Accountancy, Entrepreneurship and Management, Finance, Marketing and Supply Chain Management, and Public Affairs. The Bloch School of Management is the only school in the Kansas City region accredited by both AACSB and NASPAA. The Bloch School’s business administration programs are accredited by AACSB International (Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business), and the public administration programs are accredited by the Network of Schools of Public Policy, Affairs, and Administration (NASPAA).

Job Description

The University of Missouri–Kansas City (UMKC) invites applications and nominations for the position of dean of the Henry W. Bloch School of Management. Given its distinguished academic foundation and an exceptional trajectory today, this is an extraordinary opportunity to bring a bold and innovative leader to the School at a pivotal moment in UMKC history. This search comes at a time of significant institutional momentum and offers the next dean an important opportunity to advance excellence in education, entrepreneurship, and innovation at UMKC, a dynamic urban research university with deep connections to the Kansas City community.

With UMKC’s recent achievement of the Carnegie R1 designation, its partnership with the National Science Foundation to develop a critical materials crossroads with an estimated $40B economic impact on the region over the next decade, expanded academic programs and degree offerings and the recent launch of a comprehensive capital campaign, the time to join UMKC as a dean could not be better.

The Henry W. Bloch School of Management is home to a robust collection of academic programs and institutes that offer first-class educational experiences to our students—whether first time-to-college or executives. Guided by the priorities of the Bloch School Strategic Plan, the School offers tailored programming for well-defined career paths, hands-on learning opportunities with regional partners, and a network for accessing coveted positions. Bloch faculty and staff are deeply engaged in both teaching and scholarship, providing its students with rich experiential learning opportunities, including consulting, internships, and community-based projects. Academic innovation abounds with new programs being launched in the past two years, including a graduate certificate in Public Policy Analysis, two emphasis areas in the BBA (sports management, and risk management & insurance) and a STEM-designated MBA in Business Analytics.

Entrepreneurship is woven throughout the School and University, where it is reinforced in the Bloch Consulting Lab, the Levitt Social Entrepreneurship Challenge, the Regnier mentoring initiative, and the Regnier Venture Creation Challenge. UMKC is also home to KCSourceLink and the national Innovation Center, providing students and faculty opportunities to support business and economic development across the country.

Within the broader comprehensive University there are plenty of opportunities for collaboration, including the state-of-the-art Robert W. Plaster Free Enterprise and Research Center, which provides world-class laboratories, maker spaces, and innovation studios coupled with exceptional equipment that provides students, faculty and industry alike with hands-on opportunities to innovate and discover.

Buoyed with a talented and dedicated team of faculty, staff, students and administrators, the next dean will have the opportunity to capitalize on the School’s existing strengths to play a dynamic role in expanding corporate and non-profit partnerships and economic development through our region and state.

Key Responsibilities of the Dean:

  • Provide visionary leadership to advance the Bloch School’s mission, strategic priorities, growth, and long-term distinction.
  • Promote excellence in teaching, research, service, and student learning across undergraduate, graduate, and professional programs
  • Advance student success, workforce readiness, and career outcomes through innovative, experiential, and industry-connected learning opportunities.
  • Lead strategic planning and steward fiscal, human, and physical resources in alignment with institutional priorities and opportunities.
  • Build/nurture an internal culture of collaboration, support and accountability, with a strong external lens.
  • Recruit, develop, evaluate, and retain outstanding faculty and staff while supporting their professional growth and leadership development.
  • Strengthen the School’s research enterprise by leveraging UMKC’s R1 status, supporting scholarly excellence, and expanding interdisciplinary and externally funded research.
  • Oversee and enhance the effectiveness of School-based academic, research, and outreach centers and initiatives.
  • Promote entrepreneurship, innovation, commercialization, and industry engagement to advance the School’s impact and regional relevance.
  • Model engagement and collaboration with the business and civic community, based on proven experience identifying and leveraging opportunities.
  • Serve as a visible and compelling ambassador for the Bloch School and UMKC, strengthening the School’s reputation, visibility, and influence locally, nationally, and globally.
  • Cultivate philanthropic support and strategic partnerships with alumni, donors, corporations, foundations, and community leaders to advance the School’s priorities and impact.
  • Represent the School in university governance and build strong relationships across UMKC and with external stakeholders to advance collaboration and shared success.
  • Cultivate and steward strong, enduring relationships with the Marion and Henry Bloch Family Foundation, the Regnier family, and other key benefactors, honoring their longstanding commitment to the School while engaging them as partners in advancing the School’s mission and strategic priorities.

View the full position profile on the UM System Executive Search website.

Qualifications

Basic Qualifications:

  • Possess a terminal degree in their respective discipline with an academic record warranting a tenured appointment at the rank of Professor
  • Demonstrated experience in strategic academic leadership at a comparable university

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Support shared governance practices by working collaboratively with divisions and elevating the voices of faculty, staff and students
  • Proven experience building an internal culture of collaboration, support and accountability, with a strong external lens
  • Demonstrate the ability to manage the complexities of a large academic unit budget
  • Demonstrate the ability to manage and lead faculty and personnel from a broad range of business disciplines
  • Possess experience in academic, philanthropic, and outreach efforts
  • Demonstrate a commitment to engage and collaborate with the business and civic, with experience and a strong understanding of the opportunities and responsibilities of leading an urban-serving university
  • Show capacity to build upon the mission and vision of the Bloch School of Management consistent with the UMKC mission, vision, and strategic plan
  • Possess knowledge of business workforce opportunities at the regional, state, and national levels
  • Show a record of integrity and fairness in dealing with peers, faculty, staff, and students
  • A desire to initiate and build partnerships with industry and business leaders on academic and research innovations
  • Show the ability to serve as a role model for ethical business leadership and advocate for the School at the University, community, and state levels
  • Provide strategic leadership for enrollment and retention, strengthening recruitment pipelines, the student experience, persistence, and degree completion across undergraduate, graduate, and professional programs

Anticipated Hiring Range

Salary will be competitive and commensurate with qualifications and experience.

Application Materials

Candidates should include a CV/resume and a letter of interest that addresses the key areas described above.

Later in the search process, additional information may be sought from interested candidates, along with names and contact information for at least 5 references. Candidates will be notified before references are contacted.

Application Deadline

The application deadline for this position is January 20, 2027.

Applications will be reviewed immediately upon receipt, and considered on an ongoing basis.

Tim McIntosh, Senior Director of Recruitment
Marilyn Green, Senior Recruiting Consultant

Community Information

Kansas City, Missouri (KC or KCMO) is the largest city in the U.S. state of Missouri by population and area. Most of the city lies within Jackson County, and other portions spill into Clay, Platte, and Cass counties. It is the central city of the Kansas City metropolitan area, which straddles the Missouri–Kansas state line and has a population of 2,392,035. As of the 2020 census, the city had a population of 508,090, making it the 37th most-populous city in the United States, as well as the sixth-most populous city in the Midwest. Kansas City was founded in the 1830s as a port on the Missouri River at its confluence with the Kansas River from the west. On June 1, 1850, the town of Kansas was incorporated; shortly after came the establishment of the Kansas Territory. Confusion between the two ensued, and the name Kansas City was assigned to distinguish them soon after.


Sitting on Missouri's western boundary with Kansas, with Downtown near the confluence of the Kansas and Missouri Rivers, the city encompasses about 319.03 square miles (826.3 km2), making it the 25th largest city by total area in the United States. It is one of Jackson County's two seats, along with the major satellite city of Independence, and its other major Missouri suburbs include Blue Springs, Lee's Summit, Raytown, and Liberty. Its major Kansas suburbs include Overland Park, Olathe, Lenexa, and Kansas City, Kansas.


The city is composed of several neighborhoods, including the River Market District, 18th and Vine District, and Country Club Plaza. description:

MU Police Department.

Transport lost & found and other large items for the department.
Set-up and remove closed campus signs.
Assist with finger printing, bicycle registration, and computer registration.
Deliver departmental mail and correspondences to campus, courts, and similar groups.
Check and keep up with room reservation list.

title: Strategic Communications Consultant - Office of Strategic Initiatives
description:
Hiring Department

Office of Strategic Initiatives (OSIN) at the University of Missouri-Kansas City (UMKC).

Job Description

The Visual Communications & Design Consultant is a hands-on creative professional responsible for producing high-quality visual and digital communications that supports the U.S. National Science Foundation (NSF) Critical Materials Crossroads (CMC) Engine and the University of Missouri – Kansas City (UMKC) Office of Strategic Initiatives (OSI).

The position is primarily focused on visual campaign development, including PowerPoint presentation design, graphic design, website development and maintenance, and social media content creation. The individual will take provided content, concepts, data, and direction and turn them into polished, professional materials appropriate for internal and external audiences.

This position requires strong print and digital production skills, attention to detail, creativity, responsiveness, and the ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines. The successful candidate will be comfortable moving quickly from request to execution, developing materials independently, incorporating feedback, and delivering finished products that meet university and project standards.

ROLES

  1. Presentation Designer
  2. Graphic Designer & Visual Content Creator
  3. Website Developer & Content Manager
  4. Social Media Content Creator
  5. Digital Asset & Brand Coordinator

RESPONSIBILITIES

  1. Presentation Design & Production
    • Responsible for creating, formatting, and improving professional PowerPoint presentations for research, programmatic, executive, stakeholder, and external audiences
  2. Graphic Design, Visual Content & Campaign Development
    • Responsible for producing graphics, diagrams, infographics, charts, figures, and other visual materials that clearly communicate technical, research, and programmatic information for Critical Materials Crossroads engineering, finance, business, workforce, research and development, and operations teams. Campaign development to encompass multi-channel strategies that include both print and digital outreach from form building and email campaigns to event collateral and channel tracking and maintenance
  3. Website Development & Maintenance
    • Responsible for developing, updating, and maintaining CMC and OSI website pages and digital content to ensure information is current, visually engaging, functional, accessible, and aligned with university standards.
  4. Social Media Content Development
    • Responsible for creating visual and written content for CMC social media channels that highlights programs, research, events, accomplishments, opportunities, and other organizational activities.
  5. Brand & Digital Asset Management
    • Responsible for consistently applying CMC, NSF, and university branding and maintaining organized templates, graphics, photographs, presentations, and other digital assets.
  6. Security & Compliance
    • Responsible for appropriately handling project information, research materials, photographs, digital assets, and other content in accordance with university requirements.
  7. Other Duties as Required
    • Provides additional graphic design, presentation, marketing, conference and events, web, social media, and communications production support as organizational needs evolve.

DUTIES

  • PowerPoint & Presentation Design
    • Create polished PowerPoint presentations from outlines, written content, existing presentations, data, and other source materials
    • Develop presentation templates, slide layouts, graphics, diagrams, and visual storytelling elements
    • Redesign and improve existing presentations for clarity, consistency, readability, and visual impact
    • Translate complex information into clear visual formats appropriate for technical and nontechnical audiences
    • Create charts, process diagrams, timelines, roadmaps, organizational graphics, and other presentation visuals
    • Ensure presentations consistently follow applicable brand and formatting standards
    • Prepare presentation materials for meetings, conferences, proposals, stakeholder briefings, and other events
    • Make timely revisions based on stakeholder feedback
  • Graphic Design & Visual Content
    • Design graphics, infographics, diagrams, figures, posters, one-pagers, flyers, signage, reports, and other communications materials
    • Create visual assets for proposals, websites, presentations, social media, events, and external communications
    • Improve researcher- or staff-developed graphics so they are visually consistent and presentation-ready
    • Develop reusable templates and design elements to improve efficiency and consistency.
    • Resize and adapt graphics for multiple digital and print formats
    • Prepare production-ready files for digital distribution and printing
  • Website Development & Maintenance
    • Develop and update website pages using approved university platforms and tools
    • Maintain current website content, graphics, photographs, links, documents, and other digital assets
    • Create new webpages and page layouts as program needs evolve
    • Format web content for readability, usability, and visual consistency
    • Support improvements to website navigation and user experience
    • Coordinate website updates, corrections, announcements, events, and other time-sensitive content
    • Ensure website content meets applicable accessibility and university requirements
    • Perform routine quality checks to identify outdated content, broken links, formatting issues, and other needed updates
    • Coordinate with university technical teams when changes require additional system or administrative support
  • Social Media & Digital Content
    • Create social media graphics, posts, announcements, event promotions, researcher highlights, project updates, and other digital content
    • Develop content from information provided by program staff, researchers, leadership, and other stakeholders
    • Adapt content and graphics for different social media platforms
    • Maintain a consistent visual identity across social media channels
    • Schedule and publish approved social media content
    • Maintain a social media content calendar aligned with program activities, events, announcements, and milestones
    • Monitor basic engagement metrics and use results to inform future content
    • Maintain organized files of approved photographs, graphics, captions, and other reusable social media assets
  • Project & Asset Management
    • Manage multiple concurrent design and communications requests
    • Track assigned projects, deadlines, revisions, approvals, and final deliverables
    • Maintain organized source files and final production files
    • Maintain presentation, graphic, website, and social media templates
    • Create, maintain, and update data collection forms embedded in websites or Emma emails for conferences and events
    • Archive completed materials so they can be easily located and reused
    • Coordinate with stakeholders to obtain necessary content, data, photographs, logos, approvals, and other inputs
    • Communicate proactively when information or approvals are needed to meet a deadline

EXPECTATIONS

The Visual Communications & Digital Design Consultant is expected to:

  • Be a hands-on producer. The position is expected to personally create, edit, and deliver presentations, graphics, webpages, social media content, and related materials
  • Work efficiently from direction and source materials. The individual should be able to receive an objective, content, data, or rough concept and develop a polished product without requiring extensive direction at every stage
  • Produce professional, accurate work. Materials should be visually polished, consistent, proofread, and ready for their intended audience
  • Meet deadlines. The position must be comfortable working in a deadline-driven environment where priorities may change quickly, particularly around proposals, events, announcements, presentations, and external communications
  • Manage multiple requests simultaneously. The individual should maintain an organized workflow and communicate clearly regarding deadlines, competing priorities, and required inputs
  • Be responsive to feedback. The individual should incorporate edits efficiently and work through revisions until materials are approved
  • Maintain brand consistency. All materials should appropriately follow university, program, sponsor, and other applicable branding requirements
  • Use AI and emerging design tools appropriately. AI-assisted tools may be used to improve productivity and creative development when appropriate, while maintaining accuracy, originality, confidentiality, and compliance with university requirements
  • Maintain organized digital assets. Working files, final products, templates, photographs, graphics, and other assets should be maintained in an organized and reusable manner
  • Protect sensitive information. Research, proposal, institutional, and other nonpublic information must be handled appropriately

NOTE: This position is grant funded and contingent on continued grant funding.

Minimum Qualifications

  • A Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education and experience and at least 2 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessary.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Security Clearance.

Preferred Qualifications

STRONGLY PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s degree in Graphic Design, Visual Communication, Digital Media, Web Design, Communications, Marketing, or a related field
  • Demonstrated professional experience in graphic design and digital content production
  • Strong portfolio demonstrating presentation design, graphic design, and digital communications capabilities
  • Advanced proficiency with Microsoft PowerPoint
  • Mastery of the Adobe Creative Suite
  • Experience creating graphics, diagrams, infographics, and other visual communications
  • Experience developing or maintaining websites using a content management system
  • Mastery of WordPress to support website development and troubleshooting
  • Experience developing content for social media and digital communications
  • Strong attention to detail, organization, and file management
  • Ability to manage multiple assignments and meet deadlines

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience developing executive, technical, research, or proposal presentations
  • Experience creating visual communications for scientific, engineering, financial and business, research, or technology-focused audiences
  • Advanced PowerPoint design and data visualization skills
  • Experience with website content management systems and front-end web design
  • Experience managing organizational social media accounts and content calendars
  • Experience with social media scheduling and analytics tools
  • Experience with photography, video editing, animation, or motion graphics
  • Familiarity with AI-assisted design and content-development tools
  • Understanding of ADA, Section 508, and WCAG accessibility requirements
  • Experience developing reusable templates, brand systems, and asset management systems
  • Experience working in a university, research, government, nonprofit, or similarly complex organization

  • A background in cleaning would be advantageous, but full training is required
  • Attention to detail and thoroughness in completing tasks.

title: Senior Project Manager
description:
About The Role:

Region: Based in Stirling office - covering Scotland, North England & Ireland

Working Hours: Monday to Thursday 08:00-17:00 & Friday 08:00-15:30

A Senior Project Manager will be a solution driven individual that can demonstrate a willingness to engage, drive and complete projects and where required understand and seek the necessary support to drive these projects to completion. These projects will be varied in size, scope, and complexity and this requires a flexible approach with a “can do” mindset.

Frameworks Division has a healthy pipeline of projects via our multiple client frameworks such as Home Office, Scottish Power and Scottish Water.

The individual must be able to demonstrate a varied background of successfully delivering construction projects and have a background in either Electrical, Mechanical or Building Fabric (or a mixed variety of all).

This individual will be responsible for the delivery of multidisciplinary projects across HVAC, M&E and Fit-Out/Building Fabric elements within live operational buildings specific to our client base which includes:

  • Understanding of cradle to grave Project Management - Delivery of Projects from conception through to completion in conjunction with the Regional Operations Manager.
  • Efficiency - Ensure the utilisation and efficiency of the resource within the projects team on every project

Experience & Skills

  • Minimum 5 years’ experience carrying out project delivery of this nature.
  • Mechanical, Electrical or Building Fabric experience is essential
  • Experience in office refurbishment / fit out projects up to £5m
  • Current position as a Project Manager looking to advance in career
  • Self-motivated person / absolute ability to work on own initiative and recognise the need for assistance and resource planning
  • Ability to develop, manage and empower a team
  • Deadline driven and committed to the same
  • Committed to personnel and team development and progression
  • Effective interpersonal skills
  • Excellent communication skills including written and verbal
  • PC literate with a working knowledge of Microsoft suite of software, including Teams, Outlook, Excel, Word, Project and Powerpoint
  • Ability to develop and manage a construction programme throughout the project lifespan

Personal Qualities

  • Flexible approach to all work activities (travel between various UK locations)
  • Ability to work calmly and efficiently in a pressurised environment.
  • Excellent customer service skills / Professional manner.
  • Confident, enthusiastic, and reliable.
  • Understanding of all legislative requirements that impact on the business and client activities and all employees

This role may include but not be limited to the various facets of project management in many forms, such as:

Client facing

  • Liaising and working in conjunction with the potential for numerous client/stakeholders and their various perspectives, throughout all aspects of the project. Thus, having an empathetic view of client needs.
  • Developing client’s requirements to produce a project specific proposal, fundamentally answering the clients scope ask.
  • Managing project specific costs to meet the client budget and programme.
  • Agreeing measurable KPI’s for each project.
  • Ensure client satisfaction.

Resource Management

  • Management of and development of project teams.
  • Effectively manage staff/labour under their control to maximise efficiencies.
  • Empower our employees with targets and goals to maximise their and OCS potential.
  • Control of supply chain partners.
  • Contract mobilisation and operational support.
  • Ensuring all project personnel possess the necessary skills and have the appropriate training opportunities to carry out their job functions. (e.g., Confined Space)
  • Interface with internal business functions (e.g., commercial, H&S Team, procurement)

Engineering

  • Understand client scope, develop the same, drive solutions and proposals including development of costs in conjunction with the wider OCS team.
  • Engagement with supply chain partners and sub-contractors to maximise the solutions.
  • Delivery of design and build projects.

Project Delivery

  • Ensuring compliance with all aspects of health & safety legislation to protect the client and the business.
  • Organise and chair and record all relevant project meetings.
  • Management of all building services installations.
  • Delivery of projects within timescale and budget.
  • Continuous improvement in line with the client’s requirements

Commercial

  • Develop knowledge of various contract, including NEC and other forms of contract.
  • Programme financial control.
  • Ability to maximise opportunities and improve margin returns.
  • Understand and develop contract change mechanisms and report these in a timeous manner to deliver the contract.

title: Area Relief Officer
description:
About The Role:

Days of Working: This is a mobile, multi-site role, requiring flexibility to support operational needs around Romford Magistrates Court, shift patterns will vary depending on site requirements.

As an Area Relief Officer, you will play a key role in maintaining a safe, secure and welcoming environment across a group of court and tribunal sites. You will be responsible for overseeing access control, monitoring activity and responding to incidents, ensuring that all visitors, staff and service users are supported in a professional and respectful manner.

You will work 40 hours per week, Monday to Friday, across sites within a defined radius of your core base. Shift patterns may vary depending on operational requirements, and you may be asked to provide cover at nearby sites. This is a daytime role with no night shifts. This is a mobile, multi-site role, requiring flexibility to support operational needs across a defined area. You will work closely with colleagues and the wider court service to deliver a high standard of security and customer service.

As part of your role, your key responsibilities will include, but are not limited to:

  • Flexibility to support multiple sites within a defined area
  • Provide a professional, welcoming and customer‑focused service to all court users
  • Control access to buildings, ensuring security procedures are followed at all times
  • Operate security equipment including CCTV, x‑ray machines and handheld metal detectors*
  • Conduct searches in line with site procedures
  • Patrol public and restricted areas, maintaining regular communication with control points
  • Respond promptly and effectively to alarms, incidents and security concerns
  • Accurately record and report all incidents and activities
  • Support safe and secure movement of people within the building
  • Maintain high standards of professionalism and compliance at all times

The ideal candidate should meet the following criteria:

  • Must have Right to Work in the UK and ability to pass an enhanced DBS and BS7858 security clearance**
  • A valid SIA Licence and relevant security experience
  • Full UK driving licence and use of own vehicle*
  • Strong communication and customer service skills
  • A professional, reliable and detail‑focused approach
  • Ability to work across multiple locations and adapt to changing priorities
  • Good understanding of security procedures and health & safety practices
  • Ability to remain calm and respond effectively in challenging situations

Desirable:

  • Experience working within public sector or regulated environments
  • Experience using security systems such as CCTV and screening equipment

Additional Benefits

⭐ Guaranteed 40 hours per week with additional earning potential through overtime at enhanced rates

💷 £1 per hour Attendance Allowance (subject to criteria)

🚗 Travel and mileage support, with expenses reimbursed

🚀 Funded training, development opportunities and a clear pathway to recognised qualifications

🤝 Work as part of a professional and supportive team within the Courts & Tribunals Service

* location specific
** This position is open only to candidates with an unrestricted right to work in the UK. Visa sponsorship is not available for this role.

title: Educational Program Coordinator
description:
Hiring Department

The eMINTS National Center (eMINTS) at the University of Missouri (MU)

Job Description

The eMINTS National Center (eMINTS) at the University of Missouri (MU) provides comprehensive programs of professional learning that help K-12 schools prepare students for a modern digital-age society. Our instructional model supports high-quality lesson design, promotes authentic learning, empowers technology-rich learning environments, and builds community among students and teachers. eMINTS classrooms are technology-rich environments where students tackle authentic, real-world problems, collaborate with others, and become savvy consumers of information and producers of new knowledge.

eMINTS is seeking an innovative, creative and energetic candidate to design and deliver eMINTS programs and professional learning in and out of Missouri. The person selected for this position will work remotely along with the rest of the eMINTS staff. Therefore, residing in Columbia, MO is not required. The start date is flexible through January 2027.

Duties:

  • Participate in writing federal, state or local grants as a lead or assistant.
  • Lead or support the implementation of one or more grants, including actively recruiting participants.
  • Deliver teacher, instructional trainer, and administrator professional learning in face-to-face, online, and blended formats.
  • Deliver professional learning that is active, hands-on, and engaging.
  • Support eMINTS participants through coaching, consulting and collaboration.
  • Seamlessly integrate a variety of technologies including Google for Educators and Chromebooks in the delivery of adult learning experiences.
  • Stay current on best engaging instructional practices in education, including the usage of educational technologies in classroom settings.
  • Develop effective professional learning materials and build a variety of support documents and websites to support eMINTS professional learning programs.
  • Work efficiently and effectively on collaborative teams to develop programs and materials in face-to-face meetings and from a distance using video conferencing technologies.
  • Build and maintain rapport and relationships with customers on behalf of eMINTS.
  • Represent eMINTS and MU at local, state, and national conferences by presenting and networking.
  • Travel to local, state, and national locations to provide professional learning and support which will include periodic one to five overnight stays.

Shift

Monday-Friday, 8:00am-5:00pm

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and experience and at least 2 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessary.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Masters degree in education or a related field
  • Minimum of three years of teaching experience in K-12 or related field
  • Demonstration of effective instructional practices related to student-centered, authentic learning and technology integration
  • Understanding and addressing the needs of adult learners with designing and facilitating professional learning
  • Strong written and oral communication skills
  • Coaching and mentoring skills that support adult professional learning
  • Effective use of technology to enhance professional learning and classroom instruction
  • Strong facilitation and presentation skills
  • Self-starter with the ability to work independently and collaboratively with minimal supervision
  • Flexible daily schedule to accommodate travel and duties outside regular business hours (when applicable)
  • Willing to travel to local, state, and national school locations and conferences
  • Entrepreneurial spirit as eMINTS creates and develops new products from grant work that can be commercialized in the educational market
  • Experience with Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, and learning management systems
  • A passion for helping students learn and developing teachers’ professional practice
  • Experience with creating and writing professional learning materials for adults and designing high-quality lessons for students
  • Three or more years of experience of delivering professional learning and supporting teachers
  • An understanding of federal, state, or local grants and an ability to create compelling research questions and narratives related to programs that could be written into a grant
  • Experience with writing grant proposals and/or managing grants

Anticipated Hiring Range

Salary Range: $58,000 - $65,000 per year

Grade: GGS 009

University Title: Educational Program Specialist

Internal applicants can determine their University title by accessing the Talent Profile tile in myHR.

Sponsorship Information

Employment visa sponsorship is not available for this position.

Benefit Eligibility

title: Director of Student Health Services, UMKC Division of Student Affairs
description:
Hiring Department

The University of Missouri-Kansas City Health Services department is dedicated to promoting the physical health and well-being of students through comprehensive, compassionate care. The department offers primary care services, preventive health programs, immunizations, health education, and wellness resources designed to support students throughout their academic journey.

To learn more about our mission, visit our website:

Job Description

The Director of Student Health Services serves as a vital member of the Student Health Services and Division of Student Affairs leadership teams, leading the university's student health center in supporting the diverse health and wellness needs of UMKC students. This position is responsible for the strategic, operational, financial, and personnel management of the health center and plays a critical role in fostering a healthy campus community that promotes student success.

Key Responsibilities:


• Assess, diagnose, treat, and manage patients, including mental health, and other acute & chronic conditions, within the scope of Advanced Practice Nursing.
• Manage quality assurance programs for health services.
• Supervise and participate in development and implementation of health and wellness programs as a part of outreach to the campus community, which includes student orientations.
• Participate in University meetings, projects, and committees as assigned.
• Develop patient education programs and materials.
• Develop, and maintain clinic policies and procedures.
• Establish and monitor contracts with, and services provided by, University Physician Associates, medical supply companies, laboratories, and pharmaceutical companies.
• Management of the Electronic Medical Records System, including monitoring functionality and problem solving.
• Assist with coordination of medical crisis response procedures for the university community.
• Manage and maintain the Student Health and Wellness web pages related to medical services.
• Participate in University/Division meetings, projects and committees as assigned while collaborating with other University offices.
• Provide supervision and direction for multidisciplinary staff including administrative, provider level, and clinical support staff.
• Maintain adequate staffing and scheduling of vacation. Approve time sheets and vacation requests for all staff.
• Assist with cost analysis to determine clinic pricing for visits, medications, and laboratory testing.
• Advise CHTD Director and Fiscal Officer on health-related budget planning processes and purchases.
• Work collaboratively with multidisciplinary staff. Specifically, the willingness and ability to function as an integral team member within the department (Counseling, Health Services, Student Recreation) and the Student Affairs Division.
• Supervise medical staff, provide timely direction, feedback, and conduct annual performance appraisals.
• Competency and commitment to providing and sustaining services and environment that is inclusive to a diverse college population.
• Work collaboratively with the Dean of Students and the CARE team.

Minimum Qualifications

A master’s degree in a relevant area, and 8 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired OR a bachelor's degree in a relevant area and 10 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessary.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Masters in Relevant Area. DNP, PA, or MSN required, and Advanced Practice Nursing Licensure in the state of Missouri. Preferred specializations: Family Nurse Practitioner, Primary Care Practitioner
  • Five or more years’ experience as an Advanced Practice Nurse, or Physician Assistant with some component of managerial experience.
  • BLS Certification.
  • Proficiency with an Electronic Medical Record System.
  • Experience working in a college health setting.

Anticipated Hiring Range

The anticipated hiring range for this position has been established as starting at $135,000 annually.

Salary is determined by a variety of factors, including but not limited to, the individual’s particular combination of education, skills, and experience, as well as organizational requirements.

Your total compensation goes beyond the number on your paycheck. The University of Missouri provides generous leave, health plans, and retirement contributions that add to your bottom line.

Grade: GGS12
University Title: SENIOR DIRECTOR
To review the University of Missouri’s Staff Compensation Structure you can view the Job Code detail page. Internal applicants can determine their university title by accessing the Talent Profile tile in myHR.

Application Materials

Applicants must submit a current cover letter and updated curriculum vitae (CV) outlining their qualifications, relevant experience, and interest in the position.

Application Deadline

Applications will be accepted until this position is filled.

Sponsorship Information

Employment visa sponsorship is not available for this position.

Community Information

Kansas City offers the best of both worlds—a vibrant, urban community with Midwestern appeal. The city’s rich history and its modern-day, innovative thinking come together to create an eclectic group of neighborhoods that offer a little something for everyone. From thriving arts districts, an energetic downtown nightlife, casual to upscale shopping and champion sports teams, you will have no problem making yourself at home. Of course, one of Kansas City’s biggest claims to fame is its food, especially its world-famous barbecue. Foodies will delight in the culinary scene found throughout the city. Ranging from award-winning chefs to cozy pizza joints, Kansas City definitely is not lacking any flavor.

UMKC’s campuses are conveniently nestled in the middle of all the action. Volker Campus is just minutes from the legendary Country Club Plaza, perfect for shopping or restaurants for lunch or after-work happy hours. Surrounded by hip neighborhoods and eateries, the Health Sciences Campus is located downtown near University Health Truman Medical Center and Children’s Mercy Hospital.

UMKC is proud to be “Kansas City’s university,” and the campus and its people celebrate all the characteristics of the surrounding community. To learn more about life in Kansas City and find more resources, visit VisitKC.com.

description:
About The Role:

Days of Working: This position will be based at Central Family Court, working Monday - Friday 1200 - 2000pm.

As a Security Officer, you will play a key role in maintaining a safe, secure and welcoming environment within a designated court or tribunal building. You will be responsible for overseeing access control, monitoring activity and responding to incidents, ensuring that all visitors, staff and service users are supported in a professional and respectful manner.

This is a site-based role, where you will work closely with colleagues and the wider court service to deliver a consistently high standard of security and customer service.

As part of your role, your key responsibilities will include, but are not limited to:

  • Provide a professional, welcoming and customer‑focused service to all court users
  • Control access to the building, ensuring security procedures are followed at all times
  • Operate security equipment including CCTV, x‑ray machines and handheld metal detectors*
  • Conduct searches in line with site procedures
  • Monitor public and restricted areas, maintaining regular communication with control points
  • Respond promptly and effectively to alarms, incidents and security concerns
  • Accurately record and report all incidents and activities
  • Support the safe and secure movement of people within the building
  • Maintain high standards of professionalism and compliance at all times

  • Must have Right to Work in the UK and ability to pass an enhanced DBS and BS7858 security clearance**
  • A valid SIA Licence and relevant security experience
  • Strong communication and customer service skills
  • A professional, reliable and detail‑focused approach
  • Good understanding of security procedures and health & safety practices
  • Ability to remain calm and respond effectively in challenging situations

As a Security Officer, you will play a key role in maintaining a safe, secure and welcoming environment within a designated court or tribunal building. You will be responsible for overseeing access control, monitoring activity and responding to incidents, ensuring that all visitors, staff and service users are supported in a professional and respectful manner.

  • Accurately record and report all incidents and activities

  • Strong communication and customer service skills
  • A professional, reliable and detail‑focused approach

  • Ability to remain calm and respond effectively in challenging situations

Desirable:

  • Experience working within public sector or regulated environments

title: [2] Ranked ASSISTANT/ASSOCIATE CLINICAL PROFESSORS of ENDODONTICS / UMKC School of Dentistry
description:
Hiring Department

UNIVERSITY of MISSOURI-KANSAS CITY

SCHOOL of DENTISTRY

Department of Endodontics

The UMKC School of Dentistry, founded in 1881, is the only public dental school in Missouri and Kansas, offering eight fully accredited programs, including advanced education in general dentistry, endodontics, periodontics, and orthodontics and dentofacial orthopedics. Located on UMKC’s Health Sciences Campus alongside the Schools of Medicine, Pharmacy, and Nursing and Health Studies, the School provides outstanding education, extensive hands-on clinical training, and real-world community service. Each year, students and faculty deliver care to more than 56,000 patients, while shaping the future of oral health through innovation in teaching, research, and clinical practice. About Us - UMKC School of Dentistry | UMKC

UMKC is rated R1 by the Carnegie Research Classification of Institutions of Higher Education. The UMKC Dental School is a partner of the UMKC Health Sciences District. The District strives to be a premier academic health district, engaging in cutting-edge biomedical research and entrepreneurship, delivering state-of-the-science health care, and educating the next generation of health care professionals. UMKC provides unique opportunities for research and health care collaboration across its Schools of: Medicine, Dentistry, Nursing & Health Studies, and Pharmacy as well as University Health physicians, regional health care institutions, and the University of Missouri System’s NextGen Data Science and Analytics Innovation Center.

Endodontics - Advanced Education Programs - Academic Programs - UMKC School of Dentistry | UMKC

Job Description

The UMKC School of Dentistry seeks to fill two faculty positions in the Department of Endodontics at the rank of Assistant/Associate Clinical Professor. Opportunity for ranked promotion is provided.

The faculty will have primary responsibilities in the education and clinical supervision of DDS students in the field of Endodontics. There is an opportunity for additional compensation in clinical practice for qualified candidates.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

DDS or DMD degree or a foreign equivalent professional dental degree

Demonstrated clinical experience in contemporary endodontic diagnosis and treatment, including root canal therapy, endodontic retreatment, and management of pulpal and periapical disease, with the ability to teach and supervise predoctoral dental students in a clinical environment.

Applicants must be eligible for and obtain the appropriate Missouri Dental License prior to starting their employment. For more information about licensing, visit .

Preferred Qualifications

Completion of advanced training in endodontics.

Anticipated Hiring Range

Rank and salary are commensurate with qualifications, experience and evidence of success in externally funded research. This is a 12-month, benefit-eligible, full-time (0.8 - 1.0 FTE) non-tenure track faculty appointment, eligible for ranked promotion.

Your total compensation goes beyond the number on your paycheck. The University of Missouri provides generous leave, health plans, tuition discounts at all 4 UM System campuses for full-time employees and qualifying dependents, and retirement contributions that add to your bottom line. Our academic workloads and schedules promote a positive work/life balance.

Application Materials

Application Materials (ERecruit Field)

For consideration, you must apply online at Careers - Human Resources | University of Missouri-Kansas City, click Academic Positions/Prospective Employees (Job Opening ID 61212).

  • Complete the job application including Legal Name, US employment eligibility, questionnaire, and current contact information.
  • Application materials
    • Letter of interest which provides your qualifications and experience for a ranked clinical faculty position
    • Curriculum vitae
    • Names, complete and current contact information for at least 5 professional references
      • These references can remain confidential for most of the application process.

Please combine all application materials into one PDF or Microsoft Word document and upload as your resume attachments. Limit document name to 50 characters and do not include any special characters (e.g., /, &, %, etc.).

  • If you are experiencing technical problems during application, please email umpshrsupport@umsystem.edu .
  • For questions and correspondence about the position, please contact umkcfacultysearch@umkc.edu including the Job Identification number including job identification number 61212.
  • Reasonable accommodations may be requested during the application and recruitment process. If you need an accommodation, please contact the Office of Equity and Title IX at (816) 235-6910.

Official higher education transcripts will be required for candidates advancing as finalists. We will contact references for finalists; candidates will receive prior notification if references will be contacted. Selected candidate will be required to pass a criminal background check prior to employment.

Handling of Application Materials

After initial review by the committee all uploaded materials may be shared with all faculty in the prospective home department and faculty in all departments involved.

Application Deadline

Review of applications begins upon receipt; the position remains open until a qualified candidate is hired.

Sponsorship Information

Employment visa sponsorship may be available for candidates currently in the United States in H-1B status or other work-authorized status.

Other Information

UMKC is a public, urban, research university with more than 15,000 undergraduate, graduate, and professional students. It is part of the larger University of Missouri System. Our university is committed to being a model urban university that is recognized for our partnerships with surrounding urban communities to effectively foster a healthy, safe, and more economically secure quality of life. University of Missouri-Kansas City

Kansas City is a multifarious and vibrant community with an affordable cost of living. Our UMKC campuses are centered in the hubs of business activity, cultural arts, (some great barbeque and ethnic cuisine!) and health science research engagement for both campuses. As one of the largest cities in Missouri, we are home to national championship sports teams, a rich history of cultural arts and music, NASCAR racing, a new international airport, and a community that is very engaged with and supportive of our university initiatives. Our beautiful state has rolling hills, rivers, lakes, and long bike/hiking trails for those that enjoy time in the great outdoors, all within an easy drive. Kansas City offers something for everyone! Visit Kansas City: Find Events, Things to Do & More

UMKC is proud to be “Kansas City’s university,” and the campus and its people celebrate all the characteristics of the surrounding community.

title: Educational Resource Coach – Center for Child Well-Being (location: Southeast – Cape Girardeau, Poplar Bluff, New Madrid)
description:
Hiring Department

Department of Psychiatry

Job Description

The Center for Child Well-Being, housed within the Department of Psychiatry in the University of Missouri School of Medicine, seeks an Educational Resource Coach to support Early Childhood Programs, including the Infant & Early Childhood Mental Health (iECMH) Initiative.

This position will be based regionally in the southeast part of Missouri (e.g., Cape Girardeau, Poplar Bluff, New Madrid) and will require regular travel both regionally and statewide.

We are seeking a candidate with a strong background in early education and/or extensive experience working with children ages 0–5 who have atypical mental, behavioral, and/or physical development.

About the Center

The Center for Child Well-Being drives positive change for children and families through innovative programs, collaborative community partnerships, and strategic capacity building. Guided by our mission to improve outcomes for young children and their families, we envision a future where all children have a strong foundation for lifelong health.

Working at the Center means being part of a passionate, collaborative team committed to impact. Staff are supported in their professional growth, empowered to contribute meaningfully, and engaged in work that is purpose-driven and community-centered. Join us in shaping a more responsive and resilient childhood systems landscape across Missouri!

Key Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

  • Provide on-site consultation and coaching to early childhood programs in East Missouri, focused on social-emotional learning within a Multi-Tiered System of Support (MTSS) framework. Support implementation of Tier 1 (universal supports), Tier 2 (targeted supports), and Tier 3 (individualized intensive interventions).
  • Maintain fidelity to iECMH Scope of Work per project standard operating procedures, including timely and accurate documentation of all project activities (e.g., site visit documentation).
  • Maintain up-to-date knowledge of best practices, state mandates, and emerging trends in early childhood mental health and education in Missouri.
  • Deliver and contribute to the development of in-person and virtual training sessions for diverse stakeholders on early childhood mental health and social-emotional learning.
  • Contribute to project management and project development initiatives as assigned.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Shift

Monday – Friday
8:00 a.m. – 5:00 p.m.
Occasional nights and weekends to accommodate trainings.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and experience and at least 2 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessary.

Preferred Qualifications

Education: Master’s degree in Early Childhood Education, Special Education, Psychology (clinical or developmental), or other related field.
Credentials: State certification or licensure in education, mental health, or a related field
Years of Experience: 3 or more years of experience in early childhood education settings preferred
Additional Training: Experience with evidence-based frameworks such as the Pyramid Model, Conscious Discipline, trauma-informed care, etc.

Anticipated Hiring Range

Salary Range: $55,000 - $65,000 annually
Grade: GGS - 9E

title: TigerSwim Instructor (Student)
description:
Hiring Department

MizzouRec Services and Facilities is a department within the Division of Student Affairs that provides quality leisure experiences to all members of the campus community, primarily Mizzou students. Through our facilities and programs, we strive to bring our members and guests an environment that inspires and promotes a healthy, active lifestyle. MizzouRec enhances the student experience by creating a sense of “third place” and belonging with its vast services, facilities, and programming — in addition to its unique connection to campus history and traditions.

Job Description

NOTE: Students hired under this posting will be employed as both a TigerSwim Group Lesson Instructor and Private Lesson Instructor.

Summary

TigerSwim Lesson Instructors plan and teach the American Red Cross Learn-to-Swim program for swim lesson participants ages 6 months through adult. Instructors provide leadership and guidance of skills during class through attentiveness to each participant’s swimming and learning needs. TigerSwim Instructors must effectively and safely instruct group and private swim lessons for all age and skill levels. Previous swimming instructor experience is highly recommended. Candidates must have strong communication and decision-making skills, as well as knowledge and application of teaching swimming and water safety skills. American Red Cross Water Safety Instructor certification is recommended but not required.

Essential Functions

  • Greet and communicate with all members and guests participating in the Tiger Swim Program associated with their assigned level.
  • Instruct classes based on the American Red Cross curriculum in the MizzouRec Aquatic Center.
  • The instructor must be able to teach all levels of swim strokes required by the Red Cross Learn-to-Swim Program.
  • Instructors should feel comfortable teaching individuals ranging from 6 months to adult in an indoor pool at varying depths.
  • Be able to demonstrate swim strokes in the water as well as on land.
  • Ensure participant safety by enforcing and communicating all Aquatic Center policies and procedures.
  • Be able to quickly and effectively respond to the Aquatic Center Emergency Action plan when activated, and assist Aquatic staff as needed, while ensuring safety of the participants.
  • Be readily available to instruct private lessons as assigned by the Aquatic Coordinator for Programming.
  • Communicate effectively to assigned private lesson inquiries and remain in communication with the family for on-going private lessons.
  • Adhere to all University, MizzouRec, Team Mizzou, and area specific guidelines.
  • As with all positions, involvement with other duties and responsibilities is expected in order to serve the customer and maintain the MizzouRec mission.

Anticipated Hiring Range

Private Lessons: $19.35, paid on a bi-weekly basis.

Group Lessons: $15.40, paid on a bi-weekly basis.

Shift

Average hours per week: 6-8.

2.5-hour shifts Monday/Wednesday or Tuesday/Thursday:

title: Assistant Director, Alumni Engagement
description:
Hiring Department

Alumni Activities

Job Description

JOB SUMMARY

Reporting to the Director, Alumni Engagement, the Assistant Director, Alumni Engagement is responsible for leading and directing operational activities, programs and/or communications strategies related to increasing alumni engagement with UMSL. This position will work closely with the Alumni Engagement team, campus partners and the UMSL Alumni Association volunteers to implement key alumni engagement programs that support the university’s strategic goals.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES

Alumni Engagement & Relationship Development 35%

  • Works with Director of Alumni Engagement to develop and execute strategically aligned alumni engagement plans utilizing a combination of data analysis and university priority setting resources.
  • Collaborates with Advancement colleagues, faculty, and staff to develop and maintain alumni engagement and affinity programs within identified colleges and departments.
  • Identifies alumni to participate in programs and attend events and coordinate follow-up with Alumni Engagement Officer.
  • Identifies and refers alumni and friends to appropriate giving programs: annual giving, mid-level giving, major and planned gifts. In some cases, they may solicit alumni directly.
  • Sources and applies new and emerging best practices and industry standards to achieve personal and team goals.

Alumni Event and Program Management 35%

  • Plans events and activities that connect alumni to the University and to each other aligned with Campaign and Strategic Plan priorities.
  • Leads Alumni Volunteer programming including identifying impactful volunteer opportunities across campus; works to communicate opportunities to and recruit interested alumni.
  • Optimizes and works within a defined budget for events and programs, adhering to all UM System, UMSL, and Advancement purchasing policies. Tracks expenditures towards budget and submits and pays invoices and bills in a timely and accurate manner.
  • Serves as liaison and leads assigned UMSL Alumni Association committees including setting agendas and meeting materials, writing and submitting meeting minutes and facilitating action items.

Planning, Performance & Execution 30%

  • Participates in assigned university leadership-level meetings on campus and Alumni Association board meetings, with the ability to fully represent the Office of Alumni Engagement and the UMSL Alumni Association through effective meeting preparation, management, and communications.
  • Prepares and delivers presentations to internal and external groups; articulates messages, ideas and information effectively in both written and verbal communications.
  • Enters contact reports and other data into CRM in a timely and accurate manner. Critically evaluates data and pulls reports to utilize for decision making.
  • Travels locally and regionally for alumni meetings and activities. Update project plans with status updates on assigned activities including escalating blocks to project managers as needed.
  • Achieve annual performance goals in collaboration with the supervisor, demonstrating progress toward strategic engagement and advancement objectives.

As with all positions, other job-related responsibilities may be performed as needed to support departmental and campus-wide needs.

WORKING CONDITIONS & PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

Work is performed in a variety of environments with regular interaction with alumni, current and prospective donors, and community leaders. The role requires travel, evenings, and weekends, and the ability to maintain professionalism and composure in potentially stressful situations. The position involves sustained attention, multitasking, decision-making, and clear judgement.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

None

Shift

40 hours per week/M-F; some nights and weekends required.

Minimum Qualifications

"A Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education and experience and at least 4 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessary

  • Strong organizational, project management and communication skills (both verbal and written); an ability to communicate complex issues and maintain open communication channels with relevant stakeholders.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint).
  • High level of initiative, proven ability to work independently, attention to detail, good time-management skills and ability to work within deadlines.
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality around sensitive and private data.
  • Ability to take direction and work collaboratively within a team and university setting.

OCS is recruiting Chaperone Technicians to join our Technical Services team supporting the EOS contract.

This is a mobile role combining chaperone and escorting responsibilities with general building-fabric maintenance across designated government sites.

You will escort contractors and other authorised personnel while they are working on site, as well as undertaking planned and reactive maintenance. You will help ensure that sites remain safe, compliant and maintained to a high standard.

The role will require travel across your designated region, and you will also participate in the contract’s callout rota.

Key Responsibilities

  • Carry out chaperone and escorting duties across designated sites.
  • Escort contractors and authorised personnel while they complete work within secure environments and report remedial works to the engineers and supervisors
  • Plan, inspect and complete repairs and preventative maintenance.
  • Respond to breakdowns and reactive maintenance requirements promptly.
  • Complete delegated reactive work orders and planned preventative maintenance within agreed budgets, quality standards and contractual SLAs and KPIs.
  • Undertake basic general building-fabric and maintenance repairs.
  • Complete basic carpentry, plumbing, painting and decorating, masonry, locksmith and ceiling-grid or tile repairs where required
  • Provide general handyman services, including relevant L8 duties.
  • Support and assist the wider maintenance team (supervisor and engineers) with other facilities-related work when required.
  • Ensure an appropriate safe system of work is in place before starting each activity.
  • Make sure all work is completed safely and that sites are maintained to the required standards.
  • Liaise with subcontractors, cleaning teams and security colleagues to support the effective management of each site.
  • Maintain accurate records and update work orders using the provided tablet and systems.
  • Support out of hours work where required (with relevant notice)

Job Description

MU TITLE: Educational Program Associate I

LOCATION: Dent County - Salem, MO

The University of Missouri (MU) Office of Extension and Engagement’s distinct land-grant mission is to improve lives, communities, and economies by producing relevant, reliable, and responsive educational strategies throughout Missouri. Our dedicated and knowledgeable faculty and staff collaborate with researchers and community leaders to develop and deliver programs that address the needs of Missourians including: educational attainment; environmental concerns; community, economic, business and workforce development; global food systems; and health systems. For more information about MU Extension and Engagement, please visit

The University of Missouri Extension 4-H Center for Youth Development provides leadership and expertise with developing communities of young people across Missouri who are learning citizenship, leadership, and life skills. 4-H is publicly supported by county, state, and federal partners, as well as private resources to enrich the learning experiences of both youth and adults. For more information about 4-H, visit

This position will assist in the planning, management, and support of 4-H Youth Development programs in assigned geographic area, under the guidance and supervision of the 4-H Youth Development Specialist/Educator.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES

  • Advocate for positive youth development in the community and MU Extension.
  • Build and expand external local partnerships to grow the 4-H program in the county, including but not limited to Schools, Community Centers, and other Youth serving organizations.
  • Build and expand internal partnerships to grow the 4-H program in the county, including partnerships among other UM Colleges and Missouri Extension programs: Agriculture & Environment, Business and Community, Health and Human Science.
  • Assist with coordination and planning, management, marketing, implementing (including teaching) and evaluation (including reporting) of researched based curriculum that has an emphasis on Leadership and Civic Engagement, STEM, Healthy Living, Agriculture and Natural Resources, as well as other career exploration topics. Including curriculums offered face to face activities and online.
  • Build capacity amongst volunteers and community partners, fostering developmental relationships to contribute to program growth.
  • Engage and empower volunteers and community partners to effectively implement 4-H programs across all delivery modes.
  • Develop leadership capacity among youth.
  • Assist in the management of financial and in-kind resources.
  • Coordinate and/or conduct educational events, contests, camps, and programs utilizing a positive youth development approach.
  • Contribute to the statewide effort to impact the lives of all Missourians positively including promotion of state and national events and contests.
  • Report accomplishments and impacts to appropriate sources including supervisor, funders, and stakeholders.
  • Assist with record keeping and report preparation of 4-H Youth Development Programs.
  • Ensure that individuals in the county can participate in extension programs.
  • Participate in training and professional development opportunities for continued in knowledge, skills, and abilities as it is related to the 4-H Youth Development program.
  • Ability to travel and work flexible hours, including some evenings and weekends, is required to fulfill assigned responsibilities.
  • As with all positions, involvement with other duties and responsibilities may be expected in order to support the mission and purpose of MU Extension.

LEADERSHIP RECEIVED AND EXERCISED

Administrative supervision is received from the assigned Field Specialist/Educator in 4-H Youth Development. This position is not responsible for supervision.

  • Engage stakeholders and learners; maintain positive interpersonal relationships and exhibit effective written and oral communication skills.

The University of Missouri, also known as Mizzou and MU, is the Flagship University of the four-campus University of Missouri system. description:
Hiring Department

This position will be part of the UMKC Information Services Team with a dotted line to the School of Dentistry.

Job Description

The Support Systems Administrator (Expert) provides advanced technical leadership and hands-on support for a highly specialized academic and clinical dental environment. This role leads the design, integration, and optimization of systems supporting advanced graphics, 3D dental imaging, digital dentistry workflows, and enterprise clinical platforms.

This position requires deep technical expertise, strong judgment, and a willingness to explore emerging technologies in a production setting. An individual in this role is expected to take initiative, guide technical direction, mentor others, and operate effectively in a fast-paced, evolving environment where adaptability and thoughtful risk-taking are essential.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Set up, configure, and maintain 3D scanners, mills, and associated digital dentistry hardware.
  • Manage Group Policy Objects (GPOs) and user permissions and resources, including network shares and printers, across clinical and academic systems.
  • Set up and maintain physical and virtual server environments, storage systems, and structured data environments, ensuring optimal performance, security, and availability.
  • Administer electronic dental record (EHR) systems, including axiUm, Ortho II, Viewpoint, and Dentrix, with emphasis on integration, reporting, and performance.
  • Administer MiPacs PACS x-ray storage and imaging systems.
  • Write advanced scripts using PowerShell and Python for server provisioning, automation, and configuration management.
  • Lead incident management, including root-cause analysis and long-term remediation, including development of, testing, and maintenance of disaster recovery (DR) and business continuity plans, including regular validation and improvement.
  • Document system changes, configurations, and updates to ensure accountability and continuity.
  • Coordinate with IT staff and institutional partners on complex troubleshooting and system improvements.
  • Mentor and guide junior IT staff, providing technical direction and knowledge sharing.

Secondary Responsibilities

  • Contribute to system integration efforts across dental, academic, and enterprise platforms.
  • Participate in evaluation and implementation of new clinical, instructional, and imaging technologies.
  • Manage user access, permissions, and credentialing across multiple systems.
  • Monitor system performance, respond to alerts, and proactively address risks.
  • Image and deploy computers, including specialized high-performance and imaging workstations.
  • Administer and troubleshoot printer queues and print services.
  • Install, support, and maintain research computers, specialized devices, and non-standard hardware configurations.
  • Provide in-person and remote support for faculty, staff, and students using tools such as Bomgar.
  • Provide ExamSoft online testing support for students and faculty.

8:00am - 5:00pm, Monday through Friday

  • Experience building and supporting high-performance workstations, including systems optimized for graphics, rendering, or imaging workloads.
  • Advanced experience with Windows server and workstation environments.
  • High level of technical judgment and the ability to operate independently on complex issues.
  • A builder and optimizer mindset—comfortable designing, modifying, and improving systems.
  • Willingness to take calculated, thoughtful risks to advance technical capability.
  • Thrives in a fast-paced, rapidly changing environment with evolving priorities.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities, especially in ambiguous situations.
  • Effective communicator who can translate technical concepts for diverse audiences.
  • Resourceful, curious, and proactive in identifying opportunities for improvement.
  • Have a driver's license, cell phone with data, and be able to lift 40 lbs.

  • Strong expertise in Active Directory, Group Policy, identity management, and enterprise configuration.
  • Extensive experience with scripting and automation, including Windows PowerShell and related tools, as well as Python.

  • Demonstrated ability to mentor, guide, and elevate colleagues.
