title: Postdoctoral Research Fellow – Patch-Clamp Electrophysiology, Ion Channels, and Renal/Vascular Physiology
description:
Hiring Department

Roy Blunt NextGen Precision Health Center, University of Missouri, Columbia

Job Description

A Postdoctoral Research Fellow position is available for a highly motivated scientist with strong hands-on experience in patch-clamp electrophysiology to study ion channel and G-protein–coupled receptor signaling in vascular and kidney cells.

The laboratory investigates the molecular and physiological mechanisms regulating ion channel function, calcium signaling, vascular reactivity, hypertension, and kidney injury. Ongoing studies combine electrophysiology with molecular, cellular, and functional approaches to understand the regulation of ion channels and related signaling pathways in renal and vascular cells.

The successful candidate will have opportunities to lead mechanistic studies, publish high-quality research, present findings at scientific meetings, contribute to grant-funded projects, and develop toward an independent research career.

All duties and research activities will be conducted in accordance with institutional policies, ethical research standards, and applicable federal regulations.

Qualifications

Applicants should have:

A PhD, MD/PhD, or equivalent doctoral degree in physiology, pharmacology, neuroscience, biophysics, molecular biology, or a related field

Candidates will be evaluated on:

Demonstrated expertise in patch-clamp electrophysiology
Experience with molecular and cellular biology techniques
A strong record of research productivity and peer-reviewed publications
Strong analytical, communication, and scientific writing skills
The ability to work independently and collaboratively in a multidisciplinary research environment
Candidates should be highly motivated, technically rigorous, dependable, and genuinely interested in electrophysiology and ion channel biology.
Additional experience with ion channel physiology, calcium imaging, vascular smooth muscle or endothelial cells, renal cells, transgenic rodent models, or pressure/wire myography would be advantageous but is not required.

description:
Hiring Department

University of Missouri (MU) Office of Extension and Engagement.

Job Description

MU TITLE: Assistant/Associate/Full Extension Professional

LOCATION: Primarily serves the counties of Carroll, Caldwell, Chariton, Lafayette, Livingston, Ray, and Saline Counties in the Northwest Region. Location determined within assigned counties.

The University of Missouri (MU) Office of Extension and Engagement’s distinct land-grant mission is to

improve lives, communities, and economies by producing relevant, reliable, and responsive educational

strategies throughout Missouri. University of Missouri is an academic community of faculty, staff, and

students. We seek individuals who are committed to this goal and our core campus values of respect,

responsibility, discovery, and excellence. Our dedicated and knowledgeable faculty and staff collaborate with

researchers and community leaders to develop and deliver programs that address needs of Missourians

including educational attainment; environmental concerns; community, economic, business and workforce

development; global food systems; and health systems. For more information about

MU Extension and Engagement, please visit .

MU Extension faculty are commonly known as Specialists, with titles indicating geographic focus and programmatic specialization. Specialists coordinate educational opportunities that enable businesses, farms, families, and communities to strengthen the economy and enhance quality of life. Additionally, specialists create partnerships with civic and business organizations, educational institutions, local leaders, and key stakeholders to identify priorities, increase resources, and determine how research-based education can best meet the needs of residents.

This position is a 12-month, ranked, non-tenure track appointment at the rank of assistant, associate, or full Extension Professional. Rank will be determined at the time of appointment based on qualifications and experience in accordance with the MU Extension faculty standards. This position will hold a working title of Extension Engagement Specialist.

As an Extension Engagement Specialist, your workload distribution at appointment will be 40% Extension Teaching and 40% Extension Service, and 20% Administrative Activity.

This appointment is renewable annually at the discretion of the University and workload distribution may change at the discretion of Extension leadership. Circumstances affecting continued employment include, but are not limited to, work performance, fund availability, and educational priorities.

Essentials Duties

20% Administrative Leadership

  • Collaborate with the Regional Director to develop a plan for the region, to engage county extension councils and support them in fulfillment of their statutory responsibilities.
  • Collaborate with County Extension Councils in navigating their statutory responsibilities and requirements.
  • Collaborate with the County Extension Councils to share in the oversite of office staff and provide support in implementing best practices for managing operations, finance, and human resources including standard and ad hoc reporting as needed and/or required.

40% Extension Service

  • Attend a sufficient number of council meetings in assigned counties to support councils in conducting effective and efficient meetings and following up on action items as appropriate.
  • Attend Regional Advisory Council meetings and communicate information to County Extension Councils.

40% Extension Teaching

  • Non-credit extension programming or continuing education teaching activities delivered to external audiences.
  • Work with extension faculty and staff to ensure appropriate programming is provided in each county.

Professional Expectations

  • All Extension Faculty, regardless of appointment category or type, are expected to demonstrate competency in Communication, Educational Programming and Knowledge of Subject Matter, Information and Education Delivery, Interpersonal Relations, Knowledge of Organization, Leadership, Organizational Management, and Professionalism.

  • Actively participate in professional development opportunities to continuously improve skills and increase research-based knowledge including interdisciplinary teams, committees, and task forces. Work with faculty and staff located in county offices, across program disciplines and regions, with boards and organizations and other campuses throughout Missouri with a positive outlook, high personal standard of excellence, and passion for the mission, vision, and values of MU Extension.
  • Specialists travel throughout Missouri regularly, using their own transportation, with occasional travel out of state. title: Senior Program Coordinator for Graduate Medical Education, UMKC School of Medicine
description:
Hiring Department

Department of Graduate Medical Education

University of Missouri - Kansas City

School of Medicine

Job Description

Produces, coordinates and implements various departmental training curriculum and may oversee specific departmental education programs. This would include, but is not limited to, planning and assessing educational needs as well as evaluating and updating program materials and manuals on an ongoing basis.

  • Performs a variety of assignments that impact the Educational Support function
  • Understands key departmental objectives and uses this understanding to accomplish/complete educational support projects/initiatives
  • Implements educational support plans, providing guidance and oversight as necessary
  • Solves problems in straightforward situations
  • Analyzes potential solutions using experience, judgments and precedence, providing input and recommendations
  • Impacts the quality of own work and the work of others on the team, ensuring efficiency, productivity, compliance, etc.
  • Explains complex information to others in a way that is understandable
  • May serve as a liason with faculty, staff, trainers, and/or other internal and external constituents

Professional Development Oversight:

  • Design, implement, and evaluate professional development programs for program coordinators, program leadership, and faculty members.
  • Identify and address gaps in knowledge, skills, and competencies by creating tailored learning opportunities that align with the needs of the institution.
  • Foster a culture of continuous learning and self-improvement by providing educational resources, workshops, and mentorship opportunities.

Training Innovation & Curriculum Development:

  • Develop and implement training models using innovative educational techniques, technologies, and methodologies.
  • Integrate New Innovations Knowledge Center learning, e-learning platforms, and other digital tools to enhance the educational experience.
  • Collaborate with faculty, staff, and other key stakeholders to develop curricula to ensure alignment with current ACGME standards and best practices.

Management & Coordination:

  • Coordinate and manage all aspects of the GME training programs, including scheduling, logistics, and resource allocation.
  • Support the onboarding process for new residents and fellows, ensuring that training objectives are clearly communicated and supported through the residency tracking system.
  • Organize onboarding and orientation events.
  • Update GME’s marketing and website content as needed.
  • Evaluation & Continuous Improvement:
    • Administer evaluations on the effectiveness of professional development and training programs.
    • Review feedback from participants, faculty, and other stakeholders to identify areas for improvement and implement adjustments.
    • Stay current with advancements in medical education and related technologies, ensuring that GME programs incorporate the latest evidence-based practices.

Stakeholder Engagement & Collaboration:

  • Function as a liaison between the GME office, residency/fellowship programs, faculty, and external stakeholders to foster collaboration and share best practices.
  • Represent the GME department at internal and external meetings, conferences, and committees.
  • Provide administrative and operational support for institutional GME committees, meetings, and strategic initiatives.
  • Develop and distribute monthly communications to residents/fellows, Program Directors, and Program Coordinators regarding GME updates, deadlines, policies, and institutional initiatives.

Compliance & Accreditation:

  • Ensure all GME programs comply with ACGME (Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education) and other relevant accrediting bodies’ standards and guidelines.
  • Assist with preparation for accreditation visits and audits, ensuring all necessary documentation and reports are up to date.
  • Assist with institutional oversight and quality improvement projects, including review and monitoring of ACGME Accreditation Data System (ADS) updates, Annual Program Evaluations (APEs), and other program-level submissions.
  • Oversee PLA submission process
  • May oversee and provide guidance to others in completing educational support duties.
  • Other duties assigned

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and experience and at least 3 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessary

Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree required, master’s degree in education, Healthcare Administration, or related field preferred.
  • A minimum of 3 years of experience in medical education, GME management, or related professional development roles.
  • Strong background in curriculum development, training program management, and assessment.
  • Expertise in educational technologies, including e-learning platforms, residency management platforms, and digital training tools.
  • Excellent communication, organizational, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across diverse teams and with all levels of staff.
  • Knowledge of ACGME and other accreditation standards and requirements.
  • Ability to adapt quickly to new challenges and a continuously evolving healthcare environment
  • TAGME Certification preferred.
  • Familiarity with project management software.
  • Experience with data analytics and program evaluation techniques
  • Possesses expanded conceptual knowledge of the Educational Support function and broadens capabilities.

Anticipated Hiring Range

The anticipated hiring range for this position has been established as $67,000 - $80,000 annually.

Salary is determined by a variety of factors, including but not limited to, the individual’s particular combination of education, skills, and experience, as well as organizational requirements.

Your total compensation goes beyond the number on your paycheck. The University of Missouri provides generous leave, health plans, and retirement contributions that add to your bottom line.

title: Cluster Relief Officer
description:
About The Role:

Days of Working: This is a multi-site role based around Chelmsford, working 40 hours per week, shifts will be varied and between the hours of 0700 and 1830

As a Cluster Relief Officer, you will play a key role in maintaining a safe, secure and welcoming environment across a group of court and tribunal buildings within a defined area. You will be responsible for overseeing access control, monitoring activity and responding to incidents, ensuring that all visitors, staff and service users are supported in a professional and respectful manner.

You will work closely with colleagues and the wider court service to deliver a consistently high standard of security and customer service, supporting different locations based on operational requirements.

  • Control access to buildings, ensuring security procedures are followed at all times
  • Operate security equipment including CCTV, x‑ray machines and handheld metal detectors*

  • Monitor public and restricted areas, maintaining regular communication with control points
  • Patrol multiple court locations within your assigned cluster
  • Respond promptly and effectively to alarms, incidents and security concerns
  • Accurately record and report all incidents and activities
  • Support the safe and secure movement of people within the buildings

  • Strong communication and customer service skills
  • A professional, reliable and detail‑focused approach
  • Good understanding of security procedures and health & safety practices
  • Ability to remain calm and respond effectively in challenging situations
  • Flexibility to travel between multiple sites within a defined area

Desirable:

  • Experience using security systems such as CCTV and screening equipment

title: Resident Advisor (New) AY27-28 (Student)
description:
Hiring Department

Residential Life - Student Affairs

Job Description

If you would like to learn more about the Resident Advisor positions, additional information can be found at .

Residential Life – Student Affairs

Summary

Resident Advisors (RAs) are focused on building community within the residence halls. RAs serve as mentors and leaders within the halls by having a robust knowledge of the University of Missouri and MU Housing. Resident Advisors will connect residents to leadership, service, and involvement opportunities on campus.

As agents of the University, Resident Advisors are part of a team that strives to support and know their residents, while also creating a strong sense of belonging within the halls and on campus. Resident Advisors serve as ambassadors for MU Housing, the Division of Student Affairs and Mizzou and must serve as positive members of the university community while in their positions.

Resident Advisors are a presence in the halls. They are responsible for setting and role modeling expectations on their respective floors by abiding by and enforcing MU Housing and University guidelines and procedures. Resident Advisors help create a positive community in the hall by managing conflict between roommates and residents. They also have a thorough understanding of emergency protocols and the opening and closing procedures.

Resident Advisors are expected to be a positive brand ambassador for MU Housing by communicating the benefits of living in the halls, while also promoting employment opportunities within the department. Resident Advisors assist with contracting in their position; this may include but is not limited to tabling, working, and planning hall events and having conversations with residents about living with MU Housing.

MU Housing is a 365/24/7 operation, and RA presence is required in order to provide exceptional services and experiences for our residents. Resident Advisors may be required to complete tasks in the residence halls during scheduled academic breaks and university closures.

Resident Advisors are required to arrive early in August to participate in annual RA training, Mizzou Move-In, and Welcome Week activities. They are also required to stay late in December and May to assist with closing hall operations for the semester and academic year.

Essential Functions

Resident Advisors will perform some or all of the duties listed below and may be assigned to operate in one or more service areas or functions.

Community Development and Sense of Belonging

  • Spend time on the floor to build community within their respective floors, halls, and neighborhood by making residents feel welcome.
  • Support and know the residents living on their floor and in their building.
  • Build relationships with their residents by getting to know who they are and establishing how they can mentor them.
  • Be a presence in the halls by spending time in common areas and being social.
  • Plan and attend events within the hall/neighborhood, and support programs and initiatives put on by MU Housing, Student Affairs and Mizzou.
  • Maintain extensive knowledge about the University of Missouri, academic programs, and involvement opportunities on campus.
  • Connect residents to leadership, service, involvement, and employment opportunities on campus and within the department.
  • Support the academic mission of the University by fostering an integrative learning environment through the facilitation of programming.
  • Collaborate with campus partners and programs to support already existing events and initiatives. Support relationships across campus to avoid duplicating efforts.
  • Act as a leader on the floor and within the respective hall.
  • Manage and mediate conflict between residents and roommates.

On-Call, Operational, and Administrative Responsibilities

Provide operational and administrative support for the residence hall.

Serve in an on-call duty rotation overnight and as situations arise, with regard to class schedule.

Understand and carry out emergency procedures and crisis response.

Understand, abide by and enforce policies and procedures for MU Housing.

Be responsible for the cleanliness of communal spaces and, potentially, incidents involving bodily fluids.

Required Attendance and Participation

RAs are expected and required to arrive to and depart campus, as well as participate in, the following in accordance with the dates outlined below:

  • July 30th – August 1st , 2027: RA Move-In Weekend
  • Aug. 1st-7th, 2027: RA August Training
    • Anticipate required participation between 8 AM – 7 PM daily
  • Aug. 7th, 2027: Early Arrivals Move-In
    • Anticipate required participation between 7 AM – 7 PM
  • Aug. 8th-10th, 2027: Move-In Preparation
  • Aug. 11-12th, 2027: Mizzou Move-In
    • Anticipate required participation between 7 AM – 8 PM
  • Dec. 13, 2027: Winter Recess
    • Anticipate departure after 10 AM
  • Jan. 12, 2028: RA Winter Training Check-In
    • Arrive by 8 PM
  • Jan. 12-15, 2028: RA Winter Training
    • Anticipate required participation between 8 AM – 7 PM
  • May 15, 2028: End of Year Hall Closing
    • Anticipate departure after 10 AM

ALL DATES AND TIMES ARE SUBJECT TO CHANGE

  • Attend weekly RA staff meetings.
  • Attend one-on-one meetings as scheduled by the supervisor.
  • Attend RA and other training and activities as required by MU Housing.
    • These include, but are not limited to, Orientation, August RA Training, Mizzou Move-In (Early Arrival, First Years, and Returning Students), Winter Break Move-Out, January RA Training, and Academic Year Move-Out/Hall Closures.

Training is a mandatory part of your appointment and failure to attend training may result in appointment action up to and including termination from the appointment. Having previously completed training does not exempt you from further training.

As with all positions, involvement with other duties and responsibilities is expected in order to serve and maintain our departmental and Student Affairs mission.

Additional Responsibilities

Act as situationally critical staff and follow instructions for dealing with situations that impact the residence halls.

Receive training on a wide variety of MU programs and offerings and appropriate delivery methods.

Attend and participate in periodic RA meetings and all training sessions scheduled by the supervisor and MU Housing.

As with all positions, involvement with other duties and responsibilities is expected in order to serve and maintain our departmental and Student Affairs mission.

Background Check

Following the application process, the MU Housing team will review all submitted materials and select candidates for the 2027–2028 academic year. Please note that any offer of appointment is contingent upon successful completion of a criminal background check, in accordance with policies at University of Missouri. Candidates who receive an offer will be provided with additional information and instructions regarding the background check process at that time.

For questions about the selection or background check process, please contact musahr@missouri.edu.

Anticipated Hiring Range

Compensation includes a single residence hall room and a top-tier dining meal plan for the term of the appointment. RAs are required to maintain 100% occupancy in their university-provided room, suite, and/or apartment. The university housing assignment is decided at the discretion of MU Housing.

Shift

The RA role requires on average a commitment of 20 hours per week; however, hours may vary based on department needs; and this role may include evening and/or weekend commitments.

Minimum Qualifications

  • To be eligible for a student title, an individual must be enrolled at the University of Missouri at all times during the term of the housing contract and RA appointment.
  • Selection is contingent upon successful results of a student employment record review conducted by Student Affairs Human Resources, Residential Life, the Office of Student
    Accountability and Support, and the Office of Institutional Equity.
  • Selection is also contingent on successful results of a background check.
  • Applicants must be in good standing with MU Housing and the University.
  • Maintain a 2.75 minimum GPA for both the semester and cumulative GPA.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Lived in MU Housing for 2 semesters prior to start of the appointment.
  • Primary consideration will be given to applicants with a 3.2 GPA or above.
  • Excellent relationship-building skills and a passion for helping others feel connected to campus
  • Enthusiasm for involvement, Residential Life, Student Affairs, and Mizzou
  • Enjoyment in being a leader
  • Possess strong organizational skills
  • Good time-management skills
  • Reliable and dependable
  • Good communication skills
  • Sense of commitment to the department
  • Ability to work with a variety of people
  • Able to manage and mediate conflict in a variety of situations
  • Ability to function in a team setting, where they will have to collaborate with others to plan events, accomplish hall operations and administrative tasks and support residents
  • Passion for educating others informally and formally
  • Ability to understand, interpret and communicate guidelines to ensure the safety and well-being of residents

Application Materials

Complete application, and upload the following:
• Résumé
• cover letter
• 3 references, Please submit your references contact information here: https://missouri.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_0pIEZhweRNezB8W your references will receive an email from MU Housing.

Other Information

Housing Requirements
Must live in an assigned residence hall for the duration of service.

If you intend to live on campus regardless of whether you receive a Resident Advisor appointment or not, please fill out a housing application here: https://housing.missouri.edu/renew. If you only plan to live on campus if you are appointed a Resident Advisor position, please do not complete a housing contract. More information on what you need to do to complete your housing contract if you are selected for a Resident Advisor appointment will be communicated to you.

Essential Functions, Responsibilities and Duties

By embracing the Mizzou Student Affairs T.I.G.E.R.S. Learning Framework, Resident Advisors will complement their academic learning with practical experiences that allow them to gain and articulate essential skills.


T = Thoughtful

I = Inviting

G = Giving

E = Empowered

R = Resilient

S = Self-Aware

Mizzou Resident Advisors are THOUGHTFUL:

  • Spending time on the floor to build community within their respective floors, halls and residential neighborhoods by making residents feel welcome.
  • Supporting and understanding the residents living on their floor and in their building.
  • Building relationships with their residents by getting to know them and mentor them.
  • Being a presence in the halls by engaging with residents in common areas and being approachable.
  • Maintaining extensive knowledge about the University of Missouri, academic programs and involvement opportunities on campus.
  • Facilitating one-on-one Tiger Chats (intentional conversations) with each resident on their floor twice a semester.
  • Assisting with student follow-ups for New Student Check-In each semester.
  • Completing room inspections, and participating in hall closing and opening procedures.

Mizzou Resident Advisors are INVITING:

  • Promoting an inviting environment by planning and attending events within the hall/neighborhood and supporting initiatives from MU Housing, Student Affairs and Mizzou.
  • Connecting residents to leadership, service, involvement and employment opportunities on campus, fostering an environment of engagement.
  • Exhibiting respect for all individuals and being open-minded, non-judgmental in interactions.
  • Engaging in critical conversations that are respectful and understanding of differing points of view.
  • Facilitating shared living agreements between roommates at the beginning of each semester.
  • Designing door decorations for each resident twice a semester and creating monthly bulletin boards on various topics.
  • Promoting active engagement with the hall council and assisting in hall-wide and neighborhood events.

Mizzou Resident Advisors are GIVING:

  • Acting as a leader on the floor and within the hall, managing and mediating conflicts between residents, roommates and/or suitemates.
  • Supporting the academic mission of the University by fostering an integrative learning environment through programming.
  • Collaborating with campus partners to support existing events and initiatives, avoiding duplication of efforts.
  • Providing a variety of social and educational programs and events for residents.
  • Inspiring residents to share their passions and be actively involved in hall functions.
  • Planning and hosting community events to engage residents based on residents’ needs and interests.

Mizzou Resident Advisors are EMPOWERED:

  • Actively supporting and guiding residents, connecting them to leadership and involvement opportunities.
  • Being a proactive leader on their floor and within the hall, taking initiative in conflict management and community building.
  • Serving in an on-call duty rotation and understanding, abiding by and enforcing policies and procedures for MU Housing and the University.
  • Attending RA weekly staff meetings and weekly one-on-one meetings with their supervisor, sharing key issues, concerns or updates about their residents and community.
  • Demonstrating good judgment, integrity, and reliability in all aspects of the role.

Mizzou Resident Advisors are RESILIENT:

  • Attending and participating in all scheduled training and meetings, demonstrating flexibility and commitment to handling the demands of the RA role effectively.
  • Managing the cleanliness of communal spaces and addressing incidents professionally and calmly.
  • Understanding and executing emergency procedures and crisis response, adapting effectively to challenges as they arise.

Mizzou Resident Advisors are SELF-AWARE:

  • Recognizing their strengths and limitations, working to cultivate their strengths and addressing areas for improvement through personal and professional growth.
  • Balancing the demands of the RA role with personal life and academic responsibilities effectively.
  • Maintaining self-awareness and adaptability, taking initiative and serving as a positive role model within the community and on campus.
  • Engaging in continuous personal growth through feedback and training opportunities

Benefit Eligibility

This is a student position and is not eligible for University benefits.

The University of Missouri is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

description:
Hiring Department

MO Institute of Mental Health

Job Description

Missouri Institute of Mental Health

Overdose Prevention Supply Distribution Specialist I

Overdose Prevention Supply Distribution Specialist (4299 - Program/Project Support I)

Position Description

The Addiction Science Team at University of Missouri- St. Louis, Missouri Institute of Mental Health (UMSL-MIMH) conducts grant implementation and evaluation services for several federally and state-funded research and service grants focused on substance use prevention, treatment, and recovery efforts across Missouri. The Addiction Science Team focuses on supporting individuals who use drugs and our communities through program design, implementation, research, evaluation, capacity-building and training. We envision a Missouri where people who use drugs are healthy and supported within their communities through rapid access to meaningful, high-quality services and supports, the ability to easily navigate a variety of paths to wellness, and freedom from preventable illness and death.

We are currently looking for a dedicated, flexible, knowledgeable, and compassionate individual to help us assemble, pack, ship, and track naloxone, drug checking strips, and other critical supplies to support people who use drugs across Missouri.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Perform warehouse and inventory operations to support statewide supply distribution under the direction of the Director of Supply Distribution and Senior Operations and Logistics Lead
  • Receive, stock, pack, and assemble supplies into complex kits (e.g., naloxone, drug checking supplies, wound care, withdrawal care) according to standardized packing lists and quality control guidelines
  • Prepare shipments for carrier pickup (e.g., UPS) and community-based distribution via local events
  • Organize, track, and rearrange onsite supply inventory to ensure efficient operations
  • Prepare and fulfill orders for local organizations and statewide partners, including coordinating shipment schedules and ensuring timely delivery
  • Attend occasional distribution events or local deliveries to transport and distribute supplies as needed; statewide travel may be required
  • Manage inventory organization within multiple storage areas across multiple buildings, including shelving, bin systems, and palletize
  • Support documentation and monthly, quarterly, and annual reporting related to inventory levels, distribution activity, and supply deployment
  • Coordinate with internal teams to support distribution needs, including communication related to supply availability, restocking timelines, and shipment status
  • Maintain a clean, organized, and safe warehouse and working environments in compliance with organizational policies and norms
  • Perform other warehouse, logistics, or inventory-related duties as assigned
  • Provide as-needed support to team members working on substance use and addiction training curricula and communications to partner organizations
  • Attend all required Addiction Science team events, including but not limited to internal teamwide meetings, monthly research presentations, and operational project meetings
  • Demonstrate a high level of organization and dependability

Reports to: Casey Johnson, Director of Supply Distribution

Funding expectations: This position is currently funded through a combination of grant funding through the State of Missouri. Current grant funding is annual with expectations for renewals.

The candidate will be expected to abide by the Collected Rules and Regulations of the University System.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Ability to frequently lift and move boxes weighing up to 57 lbs.
  • Ability to use pallet jack with minimal training.
  • Possess at least a moderate understanding of substance use disorder--particularly opioid use disorder-- and the role of evidence-based strategies in combating the overdose crisis.
  • Possess a high level of curiosity, humility, organization, flexibility, and self-direction.
  • Able to navigate Zoom Video Conference systems and Microsoft Outlook Calendar.

This is a strategic leadership role requiring a strong track record in Facilities Management, contract management, stakeholder engagement, and financial accountability.

Key Responsibilities
As Account Director for one of our prestigious clients, your responsibilities will include, but are not limited to:

  • Providing overall leadership and direction for the Facilities Management contract.
  • Taking full accountability for contract performance, including P&L management, budget control, and commercial outcomes.
  • Ensuring the successful delivery of integrated FM services in line with contractual commitments, KPIs, and SLAs.

  • Driving operational excellence, service innovation, and continuous improvement initiatives across all service streams.

  • Ensuring full compliance with Health & Safety legislation, company policies, and regulatory requirements.
  • Managing risk, business continuity planning, and service resilience across the contract.
  • Identifying opportunities for cost efficiencies, value creation, and service enhancement.
  • Leading contract governance processes, including business reviews, performance reporting, and strategic planning.
  • Managing supplier and subcontractor performance to ensure high standards of service delivery.
  • Supporting growth opportunities, contract retention, and change management initiatives.
  • Ensuring effective communication and timely escalation of operational, commercial, or reputational risks.

The Ideal Candidate

  • A relevant degree or professional qualification in Facilities Management, Business Management, or a related discipline.
  • Significant senior leadership experience within a Facilities Management environment.
  • Proven experience managing large, complex, multi-service FM contracts.
  • Demonstrable success in P&L management, commercial performance, and budget accountability.
  • Strong client-facing experience with a proven ability to build and develop executive-level stakeholder relationships.
  • Experience managing large, geographically dispersed teams and driving high performance.

title: Drainage Engineer
description:
About The Role:

OCS is looking for an experienced Drainage Engineer to join our team supporting a leading UK broadcasting and media organisation.

You will be responsible for the operation, maintenance, monitoring and repair of environmental water and drainage systems across the site, ensuring systems remain safe, compliant and fully operational.

The role requires strong practical engineering knowledge, particularly across water treatment, water systems, drainage and associated equipment.

Key Responsibilities

  • Monitor and maintain building water systems in line with ACOP L8, HSG 274 Parts 1, 2 and 3, Water Fittings Regulations and relevant site procedures.
  • Inspect, fault-find and repair water treatment equipment, including water softeners, dosing pumps and associated systems.
  • Carry out monitoring and maintenance of environmental water systems and equipment.
  • Undertake drainage maintenance, including:
    • Foul drainage systems
    • Grease traps
    • Penstocks
    • Gullies
    • Soil stacks
    • Sump pumps
    • Interceptors
  • Carry out CCTV/camera surveys of drainage systems when required.
  • Clean, inspect, fault-find and arrange remedial works on drainage, interceptors, sump pumps and associated equipment.
  • Respond to environmental water issues, including Legionella risks, flooding, drainage issues and public health concerns.
  • Maintain accurate water and environmental system logbooks and records.
  • Liaise with specialist contractors and subcontractors to resolve water and environmental system issues.
  • Review and update relevant drawings, schematics and system documentation.
  • Ensure high-risk activities, including sump and interceptor cleaning, are carried out in accordance with approved RAMS, Safe Systems of Work and Permit to Work procedures.
  • Identify faults and escalate issues where specialist support or further remedial works are required.
  • Support the delivery of planned and reactive maintenance activities across the site.
  • Maintain a high standard of housekeeping and ensure work areas are left safe and clean.

Health, Safety & Compliance

  • Follow all OCS health, safety, environmental and compliance procedures.
  • Work in accordance with approved RAMS, Safe Systems of Work and Permit to Work requirements.
  • Report accidents, near misses, hazards and unsafe conditions through the appropriate systems.
  • Complete all mandatory training and maintain required competency levels.
  • Use all required PPE and safety equipment.
  • Ensure work is completed in accordance with current legislation, industry standards and site procedures.
  • Be willing to undertake First Aid training and associated duties where required.

Contractor & Supply Chain Management

  • Liaise with subcontractors and specialist contractors working on water and environmental systems.
  • Monitor subcontractor performance and ensure work is completed safely, to specification and within agreed timescales.
  • Provide feedback on contractor performance and identify opportunities to improve service delivery.
  • Identify opportunities to bring suitable outsourced services in-house where appropriate.

Client & Customer Service

  • Build and maintain a professional working relationship with the client, site teams and end users.
  • Respond promptly and professionally to water and environmental system issues.
  • Maintain clear communication with relevant stakeholders throughout planned and reactive works.
  • Ensure actions arising from inspections, faults and client feedback are recorded and followed through to completion.
  • Support the delivery of agreed service levels, KPIs and SLAs.

IT & Administration

  • Maintain accurate maintenance records, logbooks and reports.
  • Use relevant CAFM, maintenance and reporting systems effectively.
  • Maintain proficiency in Microsoft Office, including Word and Excel.
  • Produce clear and concise written reports where required.

Person Specification

Essential

  • Practical engineering experience within water systems, water treatment, plumbing or environmental services.
  • Knowledge of domestic and commercial water systems.
  • Experience working with equipment such as water softeners, pumps and dosing systems.
  • Understanding of Legionella control and the risks associated with water systems.
  • Good understanding of safe working practices and Permit to Work procedures.
  • Ability to fault-find and undertake practical maintenance activities.
  • Good written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a wider engineering team.
  • Good IT skills, including Microsoft Word and Excel.
  • Full UK driving licence preferred.

Desirable / Advantageous

  • Experience of cooling tower operation and maintenance.
  • Legionella/Legionnaires' disease training, including cooling tower awareness.
  • Water Fittings Regulations and backflow prevention training, such as BPEC.
  • TMV maintenance training.
  • Confined Space training.
  • Relevant City & Guilds or equivalent water systems qualifications.
  • Experience working within a large commercial, industrial or critical environment.

Personal Attributes

  • Practical and solutions-focused approach.
  • Strong attention to detail.
  • Organised and able to prioritise workload effectively.
  • Comfortable making decisions and working with limited supervision.
  • Reliable and professional approach.
  • Able to communicate effectively with clients, colleagues and contractors.
  • Flexible approach to working hours and operational requirements.
  • Committed to maintaining high standards of safety, compliance and customer service.

title: Dietician
description:
About The Role:

Days of Working: This position is based in South Warwickshire Clinical Services, working across Warwickshire, Leamington and community Trusts. Hours are part-time, Monday - Friday (20 hours per week).

We are recruiting for a Dietitian to support OCS Public Sector catering and facilities services across healthcare environments. This is a rewarding opportunity to help shape nutritional care and food provision, ensuring safe, inclusive, and therapeutic dietary services for service users.

Working closely with catering teams, healthcare professionals, service stakeholders, and service users, you will play a key role in maintaining high standards of nutritional care, food quality, compliance, and service delivery. If you are passionate about improving lives through nutrition and enjoy working in a collaborative environment, we'd love to hear from you.

As part of your role, your key responsibilities will include, but are not limited to:

Food provision

  • Provide recipe analysis, nutritional assessment, and development using dietary analysis software and catering information systems.
  • Maintain and review a database of standard recipes for patient, resident, staff, and retail food provision where applicable.
  • Assign and/or verify dietary coding for meals, dishes, and food items offered through catering services, including retail and vending outlets where relevant.
  • Develop and review menus and recipes in partnership with catering management teams and relevant healthcare professionals.
  • Ensure that all standard, modified, and therapeutic diets can be provided safely, accurately, and in a timely manner, meeting both dietary and personal requirements.
  • Support the development of food-related information and menu resources suitable for diverse service user needs, including accessible, pictorial, and multilingual materials where appropriate.

Professional Advice and Liaison

  • Act as a source of nutritional and catering-related dietetic expertise.
  • Build and maintain relationships with professional dietetic bodies, catering groups, and industry networks to ensure awareness of current legislation, guidance, and best practice.
  • Provide specialist dietetic advice and support to OCS Public Sector teams when required.
  • Work collaboratively with catering, clinical, operational, and quality teams to promote best practice in food provision and nutrition.
Monitoring and Compliance
  • Lead audits and monitoring activities relating to catering standards, nutritional compliance, food safety, and contractual requirements.
  • Support routine food service reviews, including assessment of portion control, food presentation, service standards, dining environments, and service user experience.
  • Monitor compliance against relevant legislation, guidance, quality standards, and client requirements.
  • Contribute to the achievement of quality inspection outcomes, including PLACE, CQC standards, and other applicable regulatory frameworks.
  • Produce recommendations and action plans to support continuous improvement.
Training and Development
  • Ensure staff involved in food provision receive appropriate training in nutrition, allergens, therapeutic diets, and feeding practices.
  • Work closely with chefs, catering managers, and operational teams to support the production of nutritionally appropriate meals.
  • Develop, source, and deliver nutrition-related training materials and sessions.
  • Promote awareness of nutritional care and dietary requirements across operational teams.

The ideal candidate should meet the following criteria:

  • Must have Right to Work in the UK and willingness to go through DBS checks if successful in this role.
  • BSc Nutrition & Dietetics or equivalent recognised degree, plus a Postgraduate Diploma in Dietetics (or recognised equivalent qualification).
  • Registered Dietitian with the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC).
  • Strong understanding of nutritional standards, therapeutic diets, food service operations, and healthcare catering.
  • Experience working collaboratively with multidisciplinary teams.
  • Effective communication, training, and stakeholder engagement skills.
Desirable:
  • Full membership of the British Dietetic Association (BDA).
  • Previous experience supporting catering services within healthcare, public sector, or regulated environments.
  • Experience of conducting audits and supporting compliance against quality standards and regulatory requirements.

description:
Hiring Department

MU Energy Management

Job Description

Powering Mizzou’s Future

At MU Energy Management, we don’t just keep the lights on — we energize the future. Our team is responsible for producing, purchasing, and delivering essential utility services across the University of Missouri campus. At the heart of our operations is the cutting-edge Combined Cooling, Heating, and Power Plant (CCHP), which generates steam, chilled water, and electricity to heat, cool, and energize more than 17 million square feet of academic, research, athletic, and healthcare facilities.

Beyond providing utility services to the campus, Energy Management also installs and manages cutting-edge Building Automation Systems that optimize energy consumption across the university. Building Automation systems include HVAC Controls, Lighting Controls, Electronic Locking, Keycard Access, and Security Camera Systems.

Our mission is to provide cost-effective, reliable, and resilient utility services that empower the University to excel in its academic and research goals.

If you are passionate about energy, innovation, and resiliency, join a team that keeps Mizzou running — and thriving.

Position: Building Controls System Technician – Security Systems

Nature and Level of Work:

Perform skilled work at a journey level in the installation, low voltage cabling and wiring, operation, maintenance, service and repair of building automation systems for security cameras, card access systems, security systems and panic/duress systems.

Key Responsibilities:

Installs, maintains, repairs, and tests campus security systems, including video surveillance cameras, electronic access control systems, panic alarms, duress alarms, and related field devices.

Troubleshoots and resolves issues involving security system hardware, devices, controllers, electronic locking mechanisms, and associated equipment.

Coordinates with Information Technology staff on system integrations, network connectivity, device commissioning, and software-related issues.

Responds to service requests, equipment failures, and emergency calls to restore system functionality in a timely manner.
Assists with security system upgrades, renovations, and new installations across campus facilities.

Conducts inspections and acceptance testing of newly installed or modified security systems.

Ensures work is performed in accordance with applicable codes, regulations, university standards, and manufacturer specifications.

Coordinates with other campus departments to support campus safety and security operations.

Provides technical guidance to lower-level technicians.

May serve as lead technician on small to medium-sized projects.

Demonstrates knowledge of electronic access control systems, video surveillance equipment, panic and duress alarm systems, and physical security technologies.

Performs other related duties as assigned.

Shift

7:00 - 3:30, M-F

Minimum Qualifications

Personnel in the Building Controls System Technician employee development program:
• This job is a promotional step from a Building Controls Technician II, and requires successful completion of skill assessments and 1.5 years of experience as a Building Controls System Technician II.
All Personnel:
• A high school graduate with one year of university or technical training in electronics, electrical engineering or an equivalent combination of education and experience from which comparable knowledge and abilities can be acquired is necessary.
• Three years of experience in the skilled maintenance, installation and repair of distributed automation systems for buildings and associated electrical and pneumatic control equipment or two years completion of technical training.
- During the first six months of employment, must complete the same skills assessment required of a Building Controls Systems Technician II as outlined in the Building Controls System Technician Employee Development Program.
• Knowledge of building codes is preferred.
• Skill in use and operation of tools, equipment and materials necessary to complete the essential functions of the job.
• Ability to read blueprints, drawings, schematics and wiring diagrams.
• A valid State of Missouri Driver’s License must be held and maintained by incumbents in the position.
• A person working in this classification will need to:
- Grasp, lift, carry and set down objects of moderate weight (50 lbs.) on a regular basis
- Grasp, lift and pull electrical/electronic cabling and wiring on a regular basis
- Climb and work from ladders, scaffolding and staging on an occasional basis
- Ability to get into and work in hot, moist, confined spaces on an occasional basis

Preferred Qualifications

Three years of experience in the installation and maintenance of building automation security cameras, card access systems, and security systems. Must be able to work from ladders and mobile elevated work platforms.

title: Director of Visitor Services - The National Musuem of Toys and Miniatures
description:
Hiring Department

University of Missouri - Kansas City
The National Museum of Toys and Miniatures

The National Museum of Toys and Miniatures (T/m) is a Kansas City treasure and a nationally recognized cultural institution. Home to the world’s largest collection of fine-scale miniatures and one of the nation’s largest collections of historically significant antique toys, T/m invites visitors of every age to experience wonder, spark imagination, and connect with history through the art of play.

Founded in 1982 on the beautiful campus of the University of Missouri–Kansas City, T/m has grown to more than 33,000 square feet of exhibit space and a collection of over 100,000 objects. Our mission—to educate, inspire, and delight—drives everything we do, from the galleries we design to the team we build. We are a high-performing, collaborative, and joyful place to work, and we are growing.

Job Description

The Opportunity

T/m is entering an exciting new chapter. With growing attendance, a strengthening earned revenue base, and a leadership team committed to building an institution that matches the quality of its collection, we are ready to make a transformational investment: formal, senior leadership for Visitor Services.

We are looking for a Director of Visitor Services who understands that every visitor encounter is a strategic act. The right candidate will see the front door not as a threshold to manage, but as the beginning of a relationship to build. They will be equally at home setting a membership conversion strategy, coaching a visitor services associate through a difficult guest interaction, curating the store to reflect our current exhibition, and reporting visitor experience data for our board meetings.

This role owns the full arc of the T/m visit: from arrival to departure and what happens after. It is a senior leadership position, a revenue ownership position, and an experience design position, all at once. If you are energized by the intersection of hospitality, strategy, and mission, and you want to help make one of Kansas City’s most beloved institutions even better, we want to meet you.

Role Overview

The Director of Visitor Services serves as the senior leader for all visitor-facing operations at T/m. As a core member of the senior leadership team, this individual is responsible for designing and delivering an intentional visitor experience, leading and developing the Visitor Services team, and owning key earned revenue lines including the Museum Store and facility rentals.

This role operates at the intersection of strategic leadership and day-to-day execution, moving fluidly between big-picture vision and ground-level presence. The Director of Visitor Services will champion a culture of warmth, excellence, and genuine hospitality, one that reflects T/m’s identity and deepens the visitor’s connection to the institution. They will also serve as a collaborative institutional partner, working closely with the Executive Director, Development, Learning & Engagement, and Marketing to ensure the visitor experience is woven into every aspect of institutional strategy.

Core Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership & Visitor Experience Design

  • Develop and lead the long-range strategy for T/m’s visitor experience, aligned with the institution’s strategic plan and the goal of building a visitor-to-member-to-donor pipeline.
  • Serve as the institutional voice for the visitor in every planning conversation, ensuring that curatorial, programmatic, marketing, and operational decisions are evaluated through the lens of visitor impact.
  • Design the full arc of the T/m visit, arrival, orientation, gallery experience, store, and departure, with intention and consistency.
  • Establish and maintain service standards, visitor interaction protocols, and operational procedures that reflect T/m’s values and brand.
  • Use visitor data, surveys, and observation to continuously improve the experience and report findings to leadership.
  • Serve as a senior member of the leadership team; actively participate in institutional planning, cross-departmental collaboration, and shared responsibility for organizational outcomes.

Team Leadership & Developmental Delegation

  • Lead, supervise, and develop the Visitor Services team, including part-time associates and front-of-house staff.
  • Build and maintain a staffing model that ensures excellent coverage across open hours, programs, and events, with enough depth to absorb the unexpected.
  • Practice intentional developmental delegation: assigning ownership of meaningful work, building team capacity, and coaching toward increasing responsibility.
  • Conduct regular one-on-ones, performance check-ins, and annual evaluations; create individualized development plans for each direct report.
  • Foster a positive, high-performing team culture grounded in hospitality, accountability, and mutual respect.
  • Model T/m’s values in every aspect of leadership: in how you communicate, how you handle challenges, and how you show up for your team.

Museum Store Ownership & Earned Revenue Management

  • Own the Museum Store end-to-end: merchandising strategy, vendor relationships, inventory management, buying decisions, and gross profit performance.
  • Set annual store revenue and gross profit goals; monitor performance and adjust strategy as needed throughout the year.
  • Ensure the store experience is integrated with and reflective of current exhibitions, T/m’s brand, and visitor identity.
  • Manage all point-of-sale systems and cash management processes; ensure accurate daily reconciliation and reporting.
  • Oversee admission revenue operations, including ticket pricing implementation, front desk procedures, and accurate recordkeeping across all ticketing platforms.
  • Track and report earned revenue metrics to the Executive Director and Board with transparency and strategic context.

Membership Conversion & the Visitor Pipeline

  • Own the on-site membership conversion experience: ensure every eligible visitor interaction includes a warm, compelling membership invitation.
  • Partner with Development to build and execute a visitor-to-member-to-donor pipeline, understanding T/m’s visitors as future donors, not just admissions.
  • Use data to track membership attachment rates, conversion trends, and renewal performance; work with Development on strategies to improve each.
  • Ensure front-of-house staff are trained, motivated, and equipped to serve as genuine ambassadors for membership.

Events & Rental Operations

  • Serve as the operational lead for all T/m facility rentals and private events, in partnership with the Director of Development and Development Associate.
  • Own day-of execution for events: staffing, setup, visitor flow, and guest experience from arrival to close.
  • Develop and maintain operational protocols for events that ensure a consistent, high-quality experience for rental clients without disrupting regular museum operations.
  • Collaborate with Development on event pricing, calendar management, and growth strategy; contribute operational insight to the annual rental ROI analysis.
  • Maintain awareness of rental market trends and visitor services best practices in the cultural institution sector.

Operational & Budgetary Oversight

  • Create and manage the Visitor Services department operating budget with fiscal responsibility and strategic intent.
  • Ensure departmental operations run efficiently, with clear workflows, staff accountability, and on-time delivery.
  • Maintain records, reporting, and documentation consistent with institutional requirements and UMKC systems.
  • Manage vendor relationships related to visitor services operations, including POS systems, ticketing platforms, and store suppliers.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications

A Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education and experience and at least 5 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessary.

Preferred Qualifications

  • 5–7 years of experience in visitor services, retail management, hospitality, or cultural institution operations, with increasing responsibility.
  • At least 2 years of demonstrated experience supervising and developing paid staff.
  • Proven experience managing retail operations, including buying, merchandising, inventory management, and margin performance.
  • Demonstrated data fluency: comfort setting measurable goals, tracking performance, and using metrics to inform decisions.
  • Experience with point-of-sale systems, ticketing platforms, and cash management processes.
  • Proven ability to lead cross-functional collaboration and work as part of a senior leadership team.
  • Experience with event operations or facility rental management strongly preferred.
  • Strong business acumen, including experience managing departmental budgets.

The Ideal Candidate Brings

  • Genuine enthusiasm for T/m’s mission, and a deep belief that the visitor experience is one of the most important things a cultural institution can get right.
  • A hospitality mindset paired with strategic instincts: you care about how every guest feels, and you also think in pipelines, conversion rates, and return visits.
  • The ability to think strategically and execute tactically, moving seamlessly between vision and ground-level presence.
  • Strong communication skills, both written and verbal, with the presence and confidence to represent Visitor Services at the leadership table and in the community.
  • High emotional intelligence and the self-awareness to lead with humility, adaptability, and grace.
  • A coaching mindset: genuine investment in the development and success of the people you lead.
  • Retail fluency: you see a store as a curated experience, not a display case, and you know how to make it perform.
  • Professional maturity and a track record of owning outcomes, meeting deadlines, and following through.
  • Positivity, creativity, and a readiness to make a real difference at one of Kansas City’s most beloved institutions.

Anticipated Hiring Range

The anticipated hiring range for this position has been established as up to $79,000 annually.

Salary is determined by a variety of factors, including but not limited to, the individual’s particular combination of education, skills, and experience, as well as organizational requirements.

Your total compensation goes beyond the number on your paycheck. The University of Missouri provides generous leave, health plans, and retirement contributions that add to your bottom line.

Other Information

What Success Looks Like

In this role, success means leading a Visitor Services department that is stable, intentional, and excellent. It means your team shows up with warmth and professionalism because you’ve built a culture where those things are expected and supported. It means the Museum Store is a curated, mission-aligned experience, not a gift shop. It means membership conversion is increasing because every visitor feels genuinely invited to belong. It means events run smoothly and clients come back. And it means you are a trusted, collaborative member of the senior leadership team who advocates for the visitor in every room you’re in—and makes the whole institution better for it.

Community Information

Kansas City offers the best of both worlds—a vibrant, urban community with Midwestern appeal. The city’s rich history and its modern-day, innovative thinking come together to create an eclectic group of neighborhoods that offer a little something for everyone. From thriving arts districts, an energetic downtown nightlife, casual to upscale shopping and champion sports teams, you will have no problem making yourself at home. Of course, one of Kansas City’s biggest claims to fame is its food, especially its world-famous barbecue. Foodies will delight in the culinary scene found throughout the city. Ranging from award-winning chefs to cozy pizza joints, Kansas City definitely is not lacking any flavor.

UMKC’s campuses are conveniently nestled in the middle of all the action. Volker Campus is just minutes from the legendary Country Club Plaza, perfect for shopping or restaurants for lunch or after-work happy hours. Surrounded by hip neighborhoods and eateries, the Health Sciences Campus is located downtown near University Health Truman Medical Center and Children’s Mercy Hospital.

UMKC is proud to be “Kansas City’s university,” and the campus and its people celebrate all the characteristics of the surrounding community. To learn more about life in Kansas City and find more resources, visit VisitKC.com.

title: Facility & Event Operations Frontline (STUDENT)
description:
Hiring Department

MizzouRec Services and Facilities provide quality leisure experiences to all members of the campus community, primarily Mizzou students. Through our facilities and programs, we strive to bring our members and guests an environment that inspires and promotes a healthy, active lifestyle.

MizzouRec enhances the student experience by creating a sense of “third place” and belonging with its vast services, facilities and programming — in addition to its unique connection to campus history and traditions.

Job Description

Facility & Event Operations Frontline are responsible for supporting the safe, welcoming, and effective operation of the MU Student Recreation Complex. Individuals in this position will interact with members, guests, event clients, and department staff and must be friendly and professional in all interactions. Frontline provide service to our members at our equipment checkout station, assist with commercial laundry service, monitor activity spaces, and provide emergency aid when needed. Frontline also support event and reservation operations by reviewing and monitoring scheduled reservations, assist with event setup and teardown, maintain event spaces and equipment, serve as a resource for clients and guests, and communicate event needs to appropriate staff.

DUTIES INCLUDE (but not limited to):

  • Enforcing all MizzouRec guidelines and policies with members, guests, and Team Mizzou staff
  • Overseeing open recreation activities, facility spaces, and space reservations during scheduled hours
  • Utilizing facility management software to issue equipment and staff uniforms, complete tasks, track usage, and access reservation/event information.
  • Monitoring the facility and events to ensure cleanliness, safety, and appropriate use by all groups and users
  • Providing customer service and responding to needs from members, guests, event clients, and staff.
  • Conducting setup and teardown of event spaces and equipment according to event diagrams, reservation details, and established procedures.
  • Maintaining facility and event equipment by cleaning, sanitizing, and disinfecting equipment as needed and reporting equipment concerns.
  • Submitting work orders for equipment and facility issues as they arise
  • Controlling and running commercial laundry operations
  • Maintaining a clean environment for members in General and Rothwell Locker Rooms, as well as stocking product & towels
  • Responding to medical emergencies and other situations according to established emergency action plans and level of training.
  • Communicating with Team Mizzou Staff, Leads, and Coordinators
  • Attending all staff meetings and trainings
  • Adhering to all University, MizzouRec, Team Mizzou, and area specific guidelines
  • As with all positions, involvement with other duties and responsibilities is expected in order to serve the customer and maintain the MizzouRec mission.

title: Continuous Posting: Supplemental Instruction Adjunct, UMKC International Center for Supplemental Instruction
description:
Hiring Department

Academic Support & Mentoring

International Center for Supplemental Instruction (ICSI)

Job Description

The International Center for Supplemental Instruction (ICSI) SI Associate Adjunct serves as a dedicated point of contact and source of support for SI programs that are currently accredited or are working toward ICSI accreditation. The position provides individualized guidance to help programs strengthen their implementation of SI, maintain accreditation standards, and address areas where additional support or development may be needed.

The position also supports the dissemination of SI best practices across the United States and internationally through training, consultation, and professional development. The position interfaces with higher education professionals and organizations from across the United States and around the world for the purposes of advancing the work and reach of ICSI and supporting revenue-generating activities that directly support Academic Support and Mentoring (ASM) programming.

Roles and Responsibilities

  • Serve as a point person for assigned SI programs, providing guidance and support throughout the assigned term.
  • Be matched with up to 10 accredited SI programs and conduct at least one check-in with each assigned program during the service term to learn about their progress, identify areas where support may be helpful, and connect programs with appropriate ICSI resources.
  • Coach SI programs that are not yet meeting accreditation standards, helping programs develop practical strategies to strengthen their SI implementation.
  • Support programs aspiring to become ICSI-accredited by providing guidance as they work toward meeting accreditation expectations.
  • Train and provide consultation to higher education professionals from the United States and around the world regarding the implementation, development, supervision, and sustainability of Supplemental Instruction.
  • Provide online training and consultation related to SI program leadership, implementation, supervision, and best practices.
  • Support the dissemination of ICSI best practices and resources across the United States and internationally.
  • Share practical expertise and experience with institutions seeking to strengthen, develop, or expand their SI programs.
  • Organize and facilitate ICSI events, trainings, webinars, and other professional development opportunities as requested.
  • Interface with higher education professionals, institutions, and organizations to identify opportunities for training, consultation, and other ICSI services.
  • Contribute to activities that support the continued growth of ICSI and its revenue-generating services, which directly support ASM programming.
  • Review SI Leader Microcredential candidates and provide feedback as part of the ICSI credentialing process.
  • Contribute to ICSI projects and initiatives as assigned based on the individual's expertise and organizational needs.
  • Represent ICSI in a professional and collegial manner when working with institutions, organizations, and higher education professionals.
  • Connect SI programs and higher education professionals with appropriate ICSI resources, expertise, and opportunities for continued professional development.
  • Provide constructive, practical, and collegial feedback to SI programs and professionals to support continuous improvement and high-quality SI implementation.
  • Organize and facilitate events and other activities as requested by ICSI leadership.

Part time, not eligible for benefits. Anticipated FTE will be .25 per contract (approximately 10 hours); FTE may be more but will always be less than .74 FTE (approximately 28 hours).

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education and experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired.
  • Completion of the Advanced SI Supervisor Training conducted by the International Center for Supplemental Instruction.
  • At least four years of experience working in SI program leadership at a higher education institution.
  • Active and in-good-standing membership on the US SI Advisory Board as an SI Associate for at least two years.
  • Demonstrated knowledge, experience, and commitment necessary to provide effective support to SI programs in accordance with ICSI standards.
  • Demonstrated knowledge and experience with Supplemental Instruction.
  • Demonstrated ability to provide training, consultation, and support to higher education professionals.
  • Ability to effectively communicate and facilitate training in an online environment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master's degree or higher in Education, Psychology, Higher Education, or another related field.
  • Working knowledge of student development and/or learning theory.
  • Experience providing professional development, training, or consultation to higher education professionals.
  • Experience working with institutions or organizations outside the individual's home institution.
  • Experience with program development, accreditation, assessment, or continuous improvement.

Anticipated Hiring Range

Supplemental Instruction Adjuncts will be compensated at a rate of $31.25 per hour for work performed under the terms of their appointment.

Application Materials

To be considered, you must complete the application at including Legal Name, US employment eligibility, and current contact information. Upload all application materials (a letter of interest, curriculum vitae, a list of references).

If you are experiencing technical problems, please email umpshrsupport@umsystem.edu.

For questions about the position, please contact umkcfacultysearch@umkc.edu include the Job Identification number 61171 and name of the position.

Handling of Application Materials

After initial review by the committee all uploaded materials may be shared with all faculty in the prospective home department. For affiliations and joint appointments materials may be shared with all faculty in all departments involved.

Sponsorship Information

Employment visa sponsorship is not available for this position.

Community Information

Kansas City offers the best of both worlds—a vibrant, urban community with Midwestern appeal. The city’s rich history and its modern-day, innovative thinking come together to create an eclectic group of neighborhoods that offer a little something for everyone. From thriving arts districts, an energetic downtown nightlife, casual to upscale shopping and champion sports teams, you will have no problem making yourself at home. Of course, one of Kansas City’s biggest claims to fame is its food, especially its world-famous barbecue. Foodies will delight in the culinary scene found throughout the city. Ranging from award-winning chefs to cozy pizza joints, Kansas City definitely is not lacking any flavor.

UMKC’s campuses are conveniently nestled in the middle of all the action. Volker Campus is just minutes from the legendary Country Club Plaza, perfect for shopping or restaurants for lunch or after-work happy hours. Surrounded by hip neighborhoods and eateries, the Health Sciences Campus is located downtown near University Health Truman Medical Center and Children’s Mercy Hospital.

UMKC is proud to be “Kansas City’s university,” and the campus and its people celebrate all the characteristics of the surrounding community. To learn more about life in Kansas City and find more resources, visit VisitKC.com.

Role Purpose

OCS are looking for a hands-on Mobile Technician role that bridges operational cleaning support with basic mechanical troubleshooting and fixes for machinery used across our food production and distribution contracts. You’ll help keep our equipment safe, clean, and running by completing hygiene tasks, first-line fault finding, minor repairs, and supporting planned maintenance, all while maintaining high standards of food safety and site compliance.

This is not an industrial cleaning role and not a manufacturing role - it’s an on-the-ground, mobile operational support role focused on equipment uptime, hygiene, and quick-turn resolution.

Key Responsibilities

• Perform targeted cleaning of production and distribution equipment in line with SOPs, including hygiene resets and documentation.

• Use and store chemicals safely under COSHH requirements and maintain correct PPE use.

• Support deep‑clean activities during shutdowns and peak periods.

• Diagnose and complete minor mechanical fixes such as belt adjustments, sensor cleaning, and clearing jams.

• Assist with simple PPM tasks including lubrication, inspections, and filter changes.

• Escalate issues outside scope and support engineers or contractors during call‑outs.

• Record all work accurately in maintenance logs or CMMS systems.

• Work within food‑site rules including GMP, allergen control, tool control, and hygiene zoning.

• Follow LOTO, permit‑to‑work processes, and complete dynamic risk assessments and near‑miss reporting.

• Maintain van stock of consumables, parts, and cleaning materials.

• Build effective working relationships with production, engineering, hygiene, and QA teams.

• Use mechanical skills confidently with hand tools and basic component replacement.

• Travel between sites with flexibility for shifts and varied environments; full UK licence required.

• Work safely with chemicals, in chilled or ambient warehouse settings, and undertake physical tasks up to 20kg.

• Advantageous experience includes basic electrical checks, LOTO awareness, CMMS use, Food Safety Level 2, and FLT/MEWP or PAT certification.

Tools, Equipment & PPE Provided

• Company van

• Basic tool kit and consumables.

• Uniform and task-appropriate PPE.

• Induction covering food site rules, GMP, allergen awareness, COSHH, manual handling, and LOTO awareness.

• Task training for site-specific equipment, SOPs, and documentation standards.

• Shadowing period with experienced technicians/engineers/hygiene leads.

description:
About The Role:

Working Hours: Monday to Friday 8am to 4.30pm

About the Role

We are looking for a skilled and motivated Refrigeration & Air Conditioning Engineer to join our mobile technical services team. You will be responsible for the maintenance, repair and some installation works of a wide range of air conditioning, refrigeration, and mechanical systems across commercial sites.

Key Responsibilities

As a Mobile Refrigeration & Air Conditioning Engineer, you will be responsible for delivering high-quality technical services across a range of commercial environments. Your duties will include:

Technical Service & Maintenance

  • Carry out planned and reactive maintenance, servicing, and repairs on:
  • Split air conditioning systems
  • VRV/VRF systems
  • Air Handling Units (AHUs) and heat pumps
  • Commercial refrigeration equipment, including chilled cabinets, multidecks and light commercial systems

Compliance & Standards

  • Work in accordance with industry regulations, technical standards, and manufacturer guidelines.
  • Ensure all work complies with F-Gas & ODS regulations, Permit to Work procedures, and Health & Safety protocols.
  • Maintain safe working practices at all times, including when working at heights or in confined spaces.

Documentation & Reporting

Accurately complete:

  • Inspection reports
  • Maintenance logs

Communication & Collaboration

Research Participation:

Training and Education:

Administrative Duties:
