Job Description

The University of Missouri Research Reactor (MURR) is seeking a Senior Supervisor - Production position that will oversee the Non-Carrier Added Lutecium production team. This position will report to the Manager - Production. The Senior Supervisor - Production will play a critical role in the regular and successful production of Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) Isotopes This position will be responsible for a team of Technicians that conduct the processes involved with the production and release of these critical isotopes.

Key Duties Performed by This Position Will Include

• Supervise and develop a high-performing production team, including assigning work, setting priorities and expectations, delegating responsibilities, providing routine feedback, completing performance appraisals, coaching and mentoring direct reports, and assisting with hiring and onboarding.
• Oversee end-to-end cGMP and related production processes, ensuring complex process steps are coordinated effectively and production commitments to customers and patients are met.
• Promote a safety-conscious, quality-focused, positive, and collaborative work environment through daily leadership, communication, and professional interactions.
• Support a strong quality culture by reinforcing compliance with procedures, good documentation practices, data integrity expectations, and timely escalation of quality or process concerns.
• Monitor process performance, including key performance indicators, budget awareness, staffing needs, scheduling, inventory management, and reagent preparation.
• Coordinate with peers and site leadership to align production activities with departmental, quality, safety, regulatory, and organizational priorities.
• Drive continuous improvement, change management, process robustness, efficiency gains, and waste reduction while maintaining compliance with quality and regulatory expectations.
• Identify, assess, escalate, investigate, and support resolution of critical production issues within required timelines using established procedures, root cause analysis, CAPA processes, corrective action implementation, and effectiveness verification.
• Participate in cross-functional meetings with Production, Quality Assurance, Quality Control, Regulatory Affairs, Development/Translation, Radiation Protection, Shipping, Finance, Reactor Operations, and Safety to provide production updates, share feedback, and support aligned decision-making.
• Author, review, and revise technical documentation, including SOPs, change controls, deviations, and related production records.
• Perform other duties as assigned to support production operations, quality objectives, departmental priorities, and site goals.

The Project Manager – Expert provides strategic leadership and project management expertise for Information Technology Services’ Campus Relations and Communications team. This position leads and manages complex projects, related project groups, and project portfolios by evaluating priorities, resource requirements, financial considerations, risks, and alignment with organizational goals. The role develops and maintains a centralized leadership project portfolio to support project planning, task management, reporting, and product delivery. This position also serves as a subject matter expert and mentor, promoting consistent project management practices and effective collaboration among leadership, functional teams, clients, and project stakeholders.


PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES

Project and Portfolio Planning – 40%

• Develop comprehensive project plans addressing scope, budget, schedule, quality, resources, risks, communications, change management, and procurement.

• Build and maintain collaborative project workspaces and a centralized leadership portfolio for projects, tasks, and deliverables.

• Evaluate projects and portfolio priorities based on strategic goals, funding, resource availability, operational needs, and other organizational constraints.

• Coordinate with functional managers to identify project resources, establish availability, maintain resource calendars, and assign project responsibilities.

• Support procurement activities and coordinate required technology security reviews or audits.


Project Governance and Authorization – 25%

• Prepare project charters defining business requirements, objectives, scope, anticipated outcomes, resource needs, and key stakeholders.

• Obtain review, approval, and priority assignment from functional leadership, executive sponsors, and business leaders.

• Coordinate project requirements and dependencies with affected functional directors, managers, and stakeholders.

• Partner with fiscal management to develop funding estimates for capital and other applicable projects.

• Provide project management guidance, mentoring, and subject matter expertise to project teams and organizational leaders.


Project Execution, Monitoring, and Control – 20%

• Establish project baselines and manage project execution in accordance with approved scope, budget, schedule, and quality expectations.

• Maintain project schedules, monitor progress, and prepare clear and timely status reports for leadership review.

About The Role:

Days of Working: Flexible Locations | Varied Shifts | SIA Licence Required

Purpose of the Role:

As a Retail Security Officer, you’ll play a key role in maintaining a safe and secure environment for customers, staff, and stock across multiple retail locations. You’ll act as a visible deterrent to criminal activity, deliver excellent customer service, and respond effectively to incidents. title: Field Specialist in Agronomy and Assistant Director of the Wurdack Extension and Education Center
description:
Hiring Department

University of Missouri (MU) Office of Extension and Engagement

MU Extension’s Agriculture and Environment program

MU Extension's Plant Health & Technology program

Job Description

MU TITLE: Assistant/Associate/Full Extension Professional

LOCATION: Steelville, Missouri and primarily serves Crawford, Dent and Phelps counties in the East Central Region with additional service across the state as needed.

Specialist Emphasis

The emphasis area for this position is agronomy, which includes the science of crops, forages, soils, weeds, insects, and pathogens. The position involves planning, implementing, and evaluating educational programs. Examples of agronomic programs in MU Extension include soil testing, precision agriculture, crop and hay production, pest monitoring, grazing systems, pesticide application, weed management, and disease management. The position also involves interacting with the farming community, including agronomic commodity groups, industry representatives, farm families, other university colleagues, and local and statewide elected officials.

Wurdack Extension and Education Center - Responsibilities

Working under the leadership of the Wurdack Extension and Education Center Director, this position serves as Assistant Director and provides leadership for educational programming while assisting with selected farm and facility operations. The Assistant Director works closely with the Director to help ensure the Center is effectively used for MU Extension education, demonstrations, applied research and stakeholder engagement.

The Assistant Director helps coordinate field days, workshops, demonstrations, tours and other educational activities at the Center. This includes connecting Extension field specialists, state specialists, researchers, agricultural organizations and other partners with opportunities to conduct programs and demonstrations at Wurdack. The position also helps identify new programming opportunities that benefit farmers, landowners, livestock producers, forest managers and natural resource professionals.

In coordination with the Director, the Assistant Director supports selected daily farm and facility activities. Responsibilities may include coordinating fieldwork, supervising seasonal and temporary employees as assigned, supporting equipment and facility maintenance, helping implement research and demonstration projects, coordinating event logistics and promoting a safe and productive work environment.

The Center Director retains overall responsibility for the management, budget, personnel and strategic direction of the Wurdack Extension and Education Center. The Assistant Director provides additional leadership and operational support as assigned and serves as a key partner in expanding the Center’s educational use and impact.

This position is a 12-month, ranked, non-tenure track appointment at the rank of assistant, associate, or full Extension Professional. Rank will be determined at the time of the appointment based on qualifications and experience in accordance with the MU Extension faculty standards. This position will hold the working title of Field Specialist In Agronomy and Assistant Director of the Wurdack Extension and Education Center.

The workload distribution at appointment will be 65% Extension Teaching, 25% Wurdack EEC leadership and 10% Traditional Service.

This appointment is renewable annually at the discretion of the University and workload distribution may change at the discretion of Extension leadership. Circumstances affecting continued employment include, but are not limited to, work performance, fund availability, and educational priorities.

CORE DUTIES OF MU EXTENSION SPECIALISTS

MU Extension Specialists deliver the University of Missouri to all Missourians. They serve all Missourians by bringing research-based solutions to work on local problems. MU Extension Specialists teach new and foundational concepts, link people to resources, support partner organizations, participate in research, train volunteers, evaluate programs, foster innovation, and serve communities. MU Extension Specialists work as a team to expand educational attainment, foster economic development, and improve health outcomes. These core duties fall into three major areas:

Educate, Create, and Connect.

  • Educate. MU Extension specialists design, conduct, and evaluate educational programs. MU Extension specialists teach research-based information via meetings, in-person and online courses, continuing education classes, technical assistance, volunteer training, media, websites, consultation, and other educational methods. They provide inclusive educational programs that support the individual, organizational, and community goals of Missouri’s learners and clients.
  • Create. MU Extension specialists develop innovative and research-informed educational products, services, materials, and other scholarly works. These include curricula, publications, presentations, educational tools, websites, and similar resources. MU Extension specialists obtain and use extramural funding to support creative works. MU Extension specialists contribute to the scholarship of Extension and Engagement by evaluating programs that result in learning and behavior changes that impact individuals and communities.
  • Connect. MU Extension specialists engage with learners, stakeholders, volunteers, and communities, including county extension councils, government officials and agencies, partners, and University and professional organizations. MU Extension specialists listen and respond with care. MU Extension specialists intentionally foster engaged partnerships and robust connections to the wide array of programs offered by the whole University of Missouri System.

Professional Expectations

  • Engage with councils, commissions, legislators, and stakeholders in all coverage counties to identify educational needs and then collaborate with appropriate internal and external partners to meet those needs.
  • Create an annual action plan that reflects local needs and aligns with statewide program area efforts. Provide a monthly report of impact to county extension council assigned, supervisors, county commissioners and others, regarding programmatic efforts. Attend at least one county extension council meeting each month and provide an oral update on program efforts.
  • Collaborate with campus-based specialists on research projects and then deliver findings from those efforts via demonstrations, field days, courses, workshops, consultations, publications, and appropriate media.
  • Work in collaboration with other specialist in counties of responsibility to serve the needs of the headquartered county, ensuring counties receive promotional materials in advance of programming.
  • Effectively work with supervisors, other specialists, and local leaders to complete administrative tasks as needed.
  • Demonstrate competency in communication, educational programming, subject matter knowledge, educational delivery, volunteer management, grant acquisition, teamwork, interpersonal relations, organization knowledge, leadership, and professionalism.
  • Offer timely, research-based information during times of natural disasters or similar events.
  • Represent the University of Missouri on boards and committees as assigned.
  • Participate in professional development events to improve both technical and leadership skills.
  • Conduct all activities per the Civil Rights Acts, Title IX, Rehabilitation, Americans with Disabilities Act, and local, state, and regional affirmative action plans.
  • Other duties and responsibilities as assigned to support the mission of MU Extension.

Additional Expectations

  • MU Extension Specialists travel regularly throughout Missouri and occasionally to out-of-state locations. MU Extension requires specialists to have a valid Missouri driver’s license, a legally operating vehicle, and wireless telephone/data service for university use. MU Extension specialists receive reimbursement for approved travel expenses, per University of Missouri policy.
  • MU Extension programs often occur outside of normal business hours. MU Extension Specialists should expect to attend these events as needed to meet the needs of learners, clients, and stakeholders.

MU EXTENSION LEADERSHIP RECEIVED

The Senior Program Director for Agriculture & Environment provides overall programmatic leadership. Programmatic supervision comes from the Education Director for the Plant Health & Technology program area and administrative oversight from the Regional Director for the East Central region.

MU EXTENSION INFORMATION

The University of Missouri (MU) Office of Extension and Engagement’s distinct land-grant mission is to improve lives, communities, and economies by producing relevant, reliable, and responsive educational strategies throughout Missouri. Our dedicated and knowledgeable specialists and staff collaborate with researchers and community leaders to develop and deliver programs that address the needs of Missourians, including educational attainment, economic development, and healthy people. For more information about MU Extension and Engagement, please visit .

UNIVERSITY INFORMATION

The University of Missouri, also known as Mizzou and MU, is the Flagship University of the four-campus University of Missouri System. It is one of the state’s land-grant universities. MU’s comprehensive undergraduate programs and its graduate, professional, and research programs attract an annual enrollment of more than 30,000 students. MU Extension and Engagement programs are located on all four campuses and in 114 counties and St. Louis city.

Qualifications

An earned master’s or Ph.D. with appropriate coursework demonstrating knowledge of Agronomy, Plant Sciences, Crop Sciences, Soil Sciences at the time of appointment.

Candidates will be evaluated on:

Oral and written communication skills.

Anticipated Hiring Range

This position offers a minimum starting salary of $65,000, with the final salary determined based on the candidate’s qualifications and experience.

title: Research Specialist I
description:
Hiring Department

Department of Psychological Sciences in the College of Arts & Science.

Job Description

This position provides research and administrative support for a research study led by Dr. Timothy Trull that examines patterns of alcohol use during the transition to legal drinking age. The study uses smartphone-based data collection, ecological momentary assessments, and portable breathalyzer readings to gather real-time behavioral data.

This position will assist with participant recruitment and coordination, support data collection and management, process participant payments, and help ensure adherence to research protocols and compliance standards. The role requires strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to communicate effectively with study participants and team members.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Assist with participant recruitment, scheduling, and tracking. Maintain communication with potential and enrolled participants, screen individuals for eligibility, coordinate study visits and reminders, and ensure participant confidentiality and adherence to study protocols
  • Support data collection and management. Prepare study materials, distribute surveys through mobile platforms, collect and enter data, perform basic data checks, and flag irregularities for review by senior research staff
  • Assist with participant payments and documentation. Track compensation, prepare payment requests, and ensure records are complete and compliant with university policy
  • Provide routine study updates. Compile weekly recruitment and data tracking reports, and communicate participant compliance and project status to the project manager and principal investigator
  • General laboratory and research support. Maintain research files, order supplies, and assist other project staff with day-to-day operations as needed

The anticipated start date for this position is between January 2027 and July 2027. While the exact start date is flexible and will be determned in consultation with the selected candidate, the appointment is not expected to begin before January 2027 or after July 2027.

Shift

Monday - Friday, 8:00 AM - 5:00 PM.

Minimum Qualifications

A Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience and at least 1 year of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessary.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience working on research projects and/or recruitment is preferred.

Anticipated Hiring Range

Salary: $17.40 - $23.85 per hour

Grade: GGS 007

title: Electrical (HV/LV)
description:
About The Role:

OCS are looking for an enthusiastic and capable individual to form a key part of the team.

  • As part of a small team of technical specialists, provide the role of Technical Authority for all Electrical Systems on the BBC Account, supporting OCS delivery of the highest levels of technical service and support.
  • Provide technical guidance, leadership, advice and direction to OCS staff, BBC Customers and Supply Chain Partners (SCP) to ensure the BBC Account remains technically compliant
  • Collaboratively work alongside BBC Workplace team to achieve BBC’s short, medium and long-term technical strategies, providing OCS technical input and considerations.
  • Act as the authoritative technical point of contact for all Electrical system operating standards and performance requirements.
  • Champion continuous improvement for system performance, processes, procedures, and monitoring for the Electrical Systems.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Oversee the delivery of the electrical annual performance analysis and condition surveys, ensuring they are completed on time, to the required standard and findings are effectively communicated and acted upon.
  • Analyse electrical testing and inspection data: adjust and optimise maintenance routines based on historical trends.
  • Analyse complex electrical systems where required to understand faults and performance limitations and make recommendations to address short-falls and delivery improvements. Develop, introduce and maintain electrical operating instructions and related documents e.g. Standard Operation Procedures (SOP's) and logbooks that define the site electrical safety program.
  • Provide electrical subject matter expertise in support of deviation investigation, participation with Root Cause Analysis (RCA) activities. Also, where necessary introduce new ways of working to the site operations teams.
  • Provide control and assume overall responsibility for compliant electrical systems including statutory tasks, ensuring the OCS Compliance Manager is kept informed of status and performance of equipment.
  • Proactive engagement in LCAM electrical system reviews ensuring continuous improvement.
  • Ensure risks are appropriately documented and managed via OCS UK/ BBC systems.
  • Alongside the BBC Account Authorising Engineer, monitor all staff and SCP’s who service electrical systems ensuring they are suitably trained, certified and competent.
  • Conduct account Level 2 technical audits, alongside other members of the Engineering Pillar.
  • In conjunction with Operational Technical Leads, set, support and deliver professional electrical engineering standards, training requirements, competency standards (Knowledge, Skills & Experience) and support competency assessment delivery, where required.
  • Perform routine management monitoring to measure site program effectiveness.
  • Review data integrity in the client CAFM system to ensure statutory requirements are met or exceeded, ensure correct maintenance for all electrical assets is in place.
  • Conduct AP (HV/LV) duties as required.
  • Provide technical support to ensure necessary capital expenditure is prioritised and risks reduced.
  • Recommend improvement opportunities and champion implementation

Personal Specification:

Required

  • Electrical Engineering HNC or equivalent.
  • 18th Edition Regulations
  • In-depth technical and operational knowledge of Electricity at Work Regs, to allow operational control to be gained over compliance for electrical systems.
  • City & Guilds 2360 Part 1 & 2 or equivalent NVQ & C&G 2383 -18.
  • 5 years + experience of installation, testing and maintenance and operation of HV/LV distribution systems.
  • AP(HV/LV)

    Desired

  • C&G 2391-52 Inspection & Testing, & C&G 2396 Design & Verification of Electrical Installations
  • Electrical Engineering Degree.
  • Achieved or be working towards Chartered or Incorporated status.

title: TAB Technician I
description:
Hiring Department

Energy Management.

Job Description

Powering Mizzou’s Future

At MU Energy Management, we don’t just keep the lights on — we energize the future. Our team is responsible for producing, purchasing, and delivering essential utility services across the University of Missouri campus. At the heart of our operations is the cutting-edge Combined Cooling, Heating, and Power Plant (CCHP), which generates steam, chilled water, and electricity to heat, cool, and energize more than 17 million square feet of academic, research, athletic, and healthcare facilities.

Beyond providing utility services to the campus, Energy Management also installs and manages cutting-edge Building Automation Systems that optimize energy consumption across the university. Building Automation systems include HVAC Controls, Lighting Controls, Electronic Locking, Keycard Access, and Security Camera Systems.

Our mission is to provide cost-effective, reliable, and resilient utility services that empower the University to excel in its academic and research goals.

If you are passionate about energy, innovation, and resiliency, join a team that keeps Mizzou running — and thriving.

Position: TAB Technician I

Nature and Level of Work:

Perform entry level TAB Technician work for testing, adjusting, and balancing (TAB) of Heating, Ventilating, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) Systems.

Key Responsibilities:

Assist with collecting HVAC equipment nameplate data.

Assist with entering data into computerized TAB forms.

Assist with inspection of building construction to determine if equipment and devices are installed per the design allowing TAB work to be performed.

Notify the supervisor of any unresolved deficiencies in construction.

Assist with air and water measurements, calibration of devices, and adjusting dampers, valves and motor speeds.

Properly and safely use, clean, operate, store and maintain tools and TAB equipment.
Follow all safety and maintenance policies and procedures.

Perform other duties as assigned.

Work toward successfully completing all Skills Category training courses and tests for TAB Technician II.

Shift

7:00 AM – 3:30 PM / Monday-Friday.

Minimum Qualifications

Personnel in the TAB Technician employee development program:
• This classification is a promotion step from a TAB Technician II classification after successful completion of skill assessments and necessary experience. The minimum time a person must spend in the TAB Technician II classification is 2 years to qualify for this classification.

All personnel:
• High school diploma or a combination of education and experience from which comparable knowledge and abilities can be acquired is necessary.
• Five years actual work experience and training, including the equivalent of apprenticeship or vocational training, in the trade.
• Must pass a written test and skills assessment related to the specific trade being performed.
• Must have ability to follow safety procedures and work safely.
• Must have ability to read and interpret blueprints, plans, schematics and drawings.
• Must be skilled in maintenance and use of tools, equipment and materials associated with the TAB of HVAC systems.
• A person working in this classification will need, on a daily basis, to be able to:
- Grasp, lift, maneuver, rotate, and otherwise use small to large trades tools and equipment.
- Grasp, lift, carry, and set down heavy objects (80 lbs.).
- Grasp, turn, twist, pull, push, lift, and otherwise move equipment, controls, parts, etc.
- Climb and work from ladders, stairs, and scaffolding.
- Wear appropriate PPE while accomplishing assigned tasks.
• May be required to work occasional overtime, including weekends.
• May be required to possess a valid driver’s license, which will allow legal operation of a motor vehicle in the State of Missouri.

Preferred Qualifications

Prior experience with commercial HVAC maintenance, controls, commissioning or TAB is preferred. Must be able to work from ladders and mobile elevated work platforms.

A valid driver’s license which will allow the legal operation of a motor vehicle in the State of Missouri is required

Salary Range: $15.00 - $22.90 per hour

Grade: GGS E

title: Senior Director for Advancement – MURR
description:
Hiring Department

Advancement

Job Description

The University of Missouri seeks highly qualified applicants for a Sr. Director for Advancement for the MU Research Reactor (MURR). Reporting to the Assistant Vice Chancellor for Principal Gifts and Donor Strategy, the Sr. Director for Advancement will develop and cultivate a portfolio of individual and corporate/foundation principal-gift prospects, hone the case for support for NextGen MURR and related research and develop enterprises, and serve as a communication liaison between MU Advancement and MURR. The Sr. Director will foster collaboration between the Executive Director of the Research Reactor, the director of the NextGen MURR initiative, related campus entities, and MU Advancement to secure major and principal gifts for the current reactor, the NextGen project and related entities, and serve as the primary steward for such gifts.

POSITION RESPONSIBILITIES

• Drive the fundraising and stakeholder engagement efforts for NextGen MURR and related projects, reporting to both the Executive Director of MURR and the Assistant Vice Chancellor for Advancement – Principal Gifts and Donor Strategy.
• Proactively identify prospective individual and corporate/foundation donors capable of principal level support ($5M+) for the NextGen MURR facility.
• In cooperation with the Vice Chancellor for Advancement, the Assistant Vice Chancellor for Principal Gifts and Donor Strategy, and the Assistant Vice Chancellor for University Programs, develop and execute a fundraising plan that aligns MURR’s national breadth of interest with potential donor prospects, within and beyond MU’s donor base.
• Strategically partner with MURR leadership to develop philanthropic priorities and gift opportunities that will resonate with donors.
• Strategically partner with MURR Marketing and Communications to ensure consistent and effective message alignment for all stakeholders.
• Steward genuine relationships with the donors, alumni, partners, and stakeholders of the research reactor, communicating donor impact.
• Build an individual portfolio of principal-gift donors ($5m+), make substantive and meaningful contact (including phone, video, and face-to-face visits) with them, and successfully present proposals.

• Interpersonal:
o Exceptional interpersonal and communication skills, including the ability to build and foster a culture of trust, influence internal and external stakeholders, and network effectively in-person and digitally.
o Build consensus and resolve conflict while leveraging Mizzou Advancement’s commitment to a collaborative and effective work environment.
o Demonstrate competence around Mizzou’s core values of Respect, Responsibility, Discovery, and Excellence.


• Business:
o Ability to think strategically, synthesize broad information and communicate across all levels
o Intentionally and purposefully sets priorities and shifts processes, resources, and capital
o Propels aggressive results through proven business acumen and innovative thinking
o Analyzes team, donor, and unit needs and proposes forward-thinking solutions
o Quickly master’s new technical and business knowledge, serving as a chief storyteller of the MURR and NextGen MURR opportunities.


• Competencies:
o A passion for the mission of the University of Missouri, Mizzou Advancement, and the MU Research Reactor.
o Self-starter and strong sense of urgency, continuously motivates and inspires others to action.
o Intellectually curious & takes initiative to capitalize on opportunities
o Entrepreneurial spirit and ability to generate excitement to build fruitful working relationships with colleagues and donors
o A compassionate and empathic leader, thoughtful of environment, organizational cultures, and dynamics
o Self-aware with an accurate reflection of strengths and areas for improvement and is willing to growth and thrive
o Demonstrates leadership in difficult situations and uses effective management tactics, including mentoring, professional relationship building, and feedback channels

Shift

Monday-Friday, 8:00am-5:00pm

There is expected frequent travel and can include irregular working hours.

This is an on-campus role that will be housed within the NextGen MURR offices, with regular meetings expected at Reynolds Alumni Center and other locations on campus.

Minimum Qualifications

A Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education and experience and at least 6 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessary.

Preferred Qualifications

Preferred candidates will have a master’s degree, a minimum of five years of fundraising or transferrable skills, ideally within a university or research organization. Preference will be given to candidates with high proficiency in communications to best relay the potential presented by the NextGen MURR project..

Anticipated Hiring Range

Salary Range: $100,000 -120,000 per year

Grade: GGS 013

description:
Hiring Department

Thompson Center for Autism & Neurodevelopment

Job Description

In recognition of your impact and commitment, this position offers a $2,500 bonus after successful completion of training, and an additional $2,500 bonus after one year of employment following training.

Position Overview
We are seeking a dedicated and experienced Behavior Analyst to join our team in delivering high-quality behavioral intervention services for children and young adults (ages 18 months to 21 years) with autism spectrum disorders and other developmental disabilities. This role primarily involves clinic-based service delivery, with occasional opportunities for community-based services. The Behavior Analyst will design and implement individualized programs focused on both skill development (e.g., early intensive behavioral intervention) and behavior reduction (e.g., severe behavior clinic).
________________________________________
Key Responsibilities
• Design and implement individualized Behavior Intervention Plans (BIPs) using evidence-based Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) strategies.
• Monitor and evaluate client progress, using data to inform treatment adjustments and optimize outcomes.
• Provide clinic-based behavioral services, with flexibility for community-based delivery when needed.
• Deliver intensive skill-building interventions, including programs targeting early developmental milestones.
• Develop and oversee behavior reduction programs for clients with severe or challenging behaviors.
• Collaborate with families, caregivers, and multidisciplinary professionals (e.g., speech-language pathologists, occupational therapists) to ensure coordinated and comprehensive care.
• Train and supervise support staff in the application of ABA techniques, promoting high standards of care and professional growth.
• Maintain accurate records and documentation, including data collection, treatment plans, and progress reports.
________________________________________
Work Environment
This position is based primarily in a clinic setting, with occasional travel for community-based services. You will work as part of a collaborative and supportive multidisciplinary team dedicated to improving the lives of children and families.
________________________________________
This is a rewarding opportunity for a compassionate professional who is committed to making a meaningful difference through evidence-based behavioral interventions. Join our team and help shape brighter futures—while earning $5,000 in retention bonuses along the way.

Shift

Monday – Friday
8:00 a.m. – 5:00 p.m.

Minimum Qualifications

Master's degree in behavior analysis or a closely related field and at least 2 years of experience in child development. Licensure as required for position.

description:

  • Patrol multiple court locations within your assigned cluster

  • Accurately record and report all incidents and activities
  • Support the safe and secure movement of people within the buildings

The ideal candidate should meet the following criteria:

  • Strong communication and customer service skills

  • Good understanding of security procedures and health & safety practices
  • Ability to remain calm and respond effectively in challenging situations
  • Flexibility to travel between multiple sites within a defined area

title: Flight Test Intern (Dec 2026-Feb 2027)
description:
Company Overview

Imagine a piloted air taxi that takes off vertically, then quietly carries you and your fellow passengers over the congested city streets below, enabling you to spend more time with the people and places that matter most. At Joby, we've been working to make that dream a reality since 2009 and we're now in the final stages of certifying our aircraft with the FAA. With plans to launch our aircraft in the US and Dubai, we're now scaling manufacturing and preparing for the launch of our commercial service.

Overview

Joby Aviation is seeking passionate and driven interns to join our flight test team. This role requires a willingness to learn and develop a range of knowledge and skills that include developing flight test plans and reports for experimental CTOL/VTOL fly-by-wire aircraft, executing testing in a ground control station environment, test data analysis, flight test simulator development, and all other tasks related to development and certification flight test activities. A can-do attitude is essential for this fast-paced environment, where every team member relies on each other to perform at their highest potential. The position is based at Joby’s Marina facility.

Responsibilities

  • Expected to work in a safe manner in accordance with established operating procedures and practices
  • Other duties as assigned or required
  • Support the flight test team in a range of technical and administrative roles, including flight test planning, flight readiness reviews, flight briefs/debriefs and post-flight analysis
  • Participate in experimental flight testing as a crew member in the ground control station, or in test support functions
  • Perform simulator evaluations, development, and experimentation with and without pilot-in-the-loop
  • Help develop manuals and supporting documentation necessary to operate flight test vehicles
  • Complete required documentation in accordance with established company and FAA procedures
  • Responsible for observing all laws, regulations, and other applicable obligations wherever and whenever business is conducted on behalf of the company

Required

  • Undergraduate class standing of 3rd year or higher (or graduate student)
  • Has completed or is pursuing a Bachelor of Science in Aerospace, Mechanical, or Electrical Engineering (or equivalent)
  • Excellent computer skills – proficiency with day-to-day applications used for email, word processing, etc., as well as data analysis experience using MATLAB, Python, or similar
  • Excellent interpersonal skills to effectively communicate with colleagues across a wide range of technical disciplines
  • Must be able to work both independently and on a team, work extended hours, and travel as required
  • Read and speak English proficiently

Desired

  • Previous experimental flight test experience, preferably eVTOL or UAS-related
  • Hands-on experience in motor sports and/or electric vehicles (AIAA Design, Build, Fly; Formula SAE, etc.)

Additional Information

The pay range for undergraduate interns, which includes freshman to senior level students, is $22.00-$33.00/ hour. The pay range for graduate interns with a Bachelor, Master, and/or Ph.D. degree is $5,550 - $7,800/monthly.

Relocation Assistance: This position does not offer relocation assistance. Candidates must live in the immediate area or relocate at their own expense.

title: Head of Technical Services
description:
About The Role:

Hours of working: 08:00 - 17:00, Monday - Friday.

Job Purpose:

The Head of Technical Services is responsible for leading the delivery of technical support and service excellence across the maintenance on the account. The role ensures the safe, compliant, and efficient operation of all technical services, driving performance, reliability, and continuous improvement while maintaining strong client relationships and supporting the achievement of strategic business objective

What you'll do:

  • Be the technical lead for maintenance strategy, advice and delivery as well as RCA/Investigations, recruitment and technical planning
  • Manage in full the cost centre P&L aspects alongside the finance team
  • Provide technical consultancy as required by the Account Director and deputise for Account Director where required
  • Lead on the delivery of the account compliance programme.
  • Lead and direct operational efficiencies that will enhance operational effectiveness.
  • Provide technical advice on new buildings/assets and act as the Interface with projects, Asset Management and Operations for new building / asset handover. Manage the gap analysis and Risk Register for technical risks (including reporting of and transfer to Customer where appropriate).
  • Provide cost centre updates, financial reports and ad-hoc report requirements as required by the Account Director.
  • Contribute, support and Chair, when required, lead technical and management meetings.
  • Actively and positively promote the image of business at all times and to maintain good working relationships with clients, suppliers and other external parties.
  • Ensure that performance is consistent and satisfactory.
  • Establish a consistently positive working relationship with all clients and end users.
  • Ensure an effective feedback mechanism is in place to allow clients feedback to be monitored and actions logged and closed out.
  • Provide appropriate challenge and improvement to the customer through value propositions.
  • Be the intelligent supplier for the customer to improve their engineering/maintenance and asset base by bringing in UK industry best available practices.
  • Deliver your service in compliance with your allocated budget and manage the P&L for the cost centre.
  • Satisfy all contract deliverables.
  • Ensure compliance with all relevant end to end processes applicable to the role.

Who you'll be:

  • Chartered Engineering status and holding an engineering degree or equivalent qualification and a member of a relevant professional body e.g. IET.
  • A proven successful record of accomplishment working at Senior Engineering Operations Level, ideally gained within a regulated, manufacturing and high security environment.
  • Experience of working with quality management systems with a high degree of procedural, technical and HSE compliance.
  • A thorough knowledge of outsourced facilities services within the UK, including hard FM service lines and directly delivered complex projects including M&E, building and civils activities.
  • An effective and progressive leader with experience of directing and developing multi-disciplined engineering teams in highly regulated and demanding environments.
  • An experienced leader of change with the ability to lead and direct others towards acceptance of new business ideas, methods and working practices. A clear understanding of transformational leadership and an ability to change culture and behaviours.
  • Ability and experience in developing strong relationships with key customers to support account development and long-term sustainable and profitable tenure.
  • Understanding of Asset Management Strategy and ISO 55000 series best practice.
  • Experience in working with CMMS/CAFM systems, maintenance planning, scheduling and mitigation Management.
  • IT Literate including Word, Excel, Project, PowerPoint and Visio.
  • Key account management experience/education would be beneficial.

description:
About The Role:

Main Purpose:

To maintain the school premises to a high standard of cleanliness; required to clean all rooms, including classrooms, offices, toilets, cloakrooms, staircases, and all other areas in use.

This position is a term time post. You will be required to participate in the annual deep clean of the school for 3 weeks during the summer holidays.

Working Pattern:
Monday to Thursday 15:50 - 21:50
Friday 12.30 - 18:30

Key Responsibilities:

  • Overall responsibility for the practical organisation of the day-to-day cleaning operation.
  • In consultation with the Soft Services Area Supervisor, to identify the number of cleaning staff required to maintain a clean environment.
  • To monitor stock of cleaning equipment and materials, to ensure orders can be placed on a timely basis.
  • Update Maximo daily for any Misuse.
  • Maintain a flexible daily cleaning schedule of all internal areas of the school.
  • Ensure that identified key areas of the school receive priority in the schedule.
  • Liaise with the Head Janitor and review the weekly school calendar to identify lets and school events.
  • Liaise with school representative to ensure client satisfaction.
  • Daily checks of all areas of the school to ensure they are cleaned to a satisfactory standard and daily cleaning logs are completed for each work section.
  • Clean allocated areas to a high standard – including but not limited to: -
    • Vacuuming
    • Scrubber Drying
    • Damp Wiping
    • Stair Cleaning
    • Toilet Cleaning
  • Produce, on a monthly basis, official order forms for equipment, uniform and materials for authorisation by the Area Supervisor.
  • Produce a monthly report for the Area Supervisor.
  • Ensure that tools, equipment, and materials are available as and when required to ensure the effective delivery of the service.
  • Maintain a working knowledge of developments in cleaning equipment and materials and identify means by which the cleaning operation might be developed.
  • Conduct regular site audits to ensure that the specified standard of work is maintained.
  • Secure the building when there is no janitor present onsite.
  • Provide information to the Area Supervisor for the Training Log.
  • Ensure that all Health & Safety procedures are followed, in accordance with company policies.
  • Responsible for the day-to-day personnel management of the cleaning staff, and consulting with the Area Supervisor on any necessary formal procedure, including:
    • Develop and carry out induction procedures with all new staff.
    • Identify formal and informal training needs for all cleaning staff.
    • Complete cleaning staff Return to Work Interviews and any other HR paperwork required.
    • Organise appropriate training for all cleaning staff.
    • Carry out Staff CPD and new starter training.
    • In conjunction with the Area Supervisor, interview and recruit sufficient cleaning staff to cover the weekly budgeted cleaning hours.

Skills & Knowledge:

  • Supervisory experience in a cleaning environment, preferably in a PPP environment.
  • BICSc certification, or equivalent to an appropriate level, desirable.
  • Experience of operating a management system i.e. ISO 9001:2000, 14001, 18001.
  • Excellent prioritisation and multi-tasking skills.
  • A pro-active attitude.
  • Good IT/computer skills.
  • The ability to supervise operatives.
  • The ability to deliver in-house training.
  • Excellent communication skills including verbal and the written word.
  • The ability to form relationships with clients and to exceed customer expectation.
  • Approachable demeanour and a demonstrable commitment to team working.
  • A track record of delivering a similar role.
  • A commitment to continuing professional development in relation to themselves and their team members.

title: Research Assistant / Senior Research Assistant, Ophthalmology--Vision Research Center, UMKC School of Medicine
description:
Hiring Department

University of Missouri - Kansas City School of Medicine

Department of Ophthalmology

Vision Research Center

For more than 60 years, the Department of Ophthalmology has provided high-level care to patients with eye disease through innovative treatments, ground-breaking research, prevention strategies, community engagement and exemplary training for the next generation of ophthalmologists.

The Vision Research Center (VRC) at UMKC is the Department of Ophthalmology’s research arm, providing residents and fellows with comprehensive research opportunities, including basic research, translational research and clinical trials.

UMKC is rated R1 by the Carnegie Research Classification of Institutions of Higher Education.

Job Description

The Department of Ophthalmology seeks outstanding candidates for full-time Research Assistant or Senior Research Assistant positions at the University of Missouri-Kansas City School of Medicine. The selected candidates will be responsible for assisting with preclinical research, neuroscience, physiology, histology and microscopy experiments as part of newly NIH-funded research projects. This involves preparing biological and other specimens for imaging and neuroscience, preclinical, physiological and biochemical testing and to acquire and analyze related data. These positions will assist in maintaining preclinical research, physiology, histology and microscopy equipment, order routine supplies, prepare technical reports and archive data. This research position will be part of a highly qualified research group to advance ocular research in further hopes of developing cures/treatment for vision degenerative conditions.

This is a 12-month full-time contract, benefit eligible, unranked academic position.

Qualifications

To qualify as a Research Assistant, minimum qualifications include a Bachelor’s degree and 2 years of experience in neuroscience, preclinical research, physiology, histology and/or in microscopy techniques.

To qualify as a Senior Research Assistant, minimum qualifications include a Master’s degree in a related medical or field of science and 2+ years of experience in neuroscience, preclinical research, physiology, histology and/or in microscopy techniques.

Experience in preclinical research and physiology is a preferred qualification

Anticipated Hiring Range

The anticipated hiring range for this position has been established as $18-00 -$30.00/hourly.

Salary is determined by a variety of factors, including but not limited to, the individual’s particular combination of education, skills, and experience, as well as organizational requirements.

Your total compensation goes beyond the number on your paycheck. The University of Missouri provides generous leave, health plans, and retirement contributions that add to your bottom line.

Application Materials

For consideration, please apply online at / Searh for Job ID 61101.

Combine all application materials (personal letter of interest stating your experience in research with accompanying curriculum vitae, and a list of professional references) into one PDF or Microsoft Word document and upload as your resume attachment. Limit document name to 50 characters, do not include special characters, i.e. #,@, *, /, etc.

  • If you are experiencing technical problems during application, please email umpshrsupport@umsystem.edu .
  • For questions about the position, please contact Megan Florance florancem@umkc.edu, including the Job Identification number 61101 and name of the position.
  • Reasonable accommodations may be requested during the application and recruitment process. If you need an accommodation, please contact the Office of Equity and Title IX at (816) 235-1323.
  • All final candidates will be required to successfully pass a Criminal Background Check prior to beginning employment.

Application Deadline

Review of applications will begin upon receipt. Applications will be accepted until qualified candidates are hired.

Sponsorship Information

Employment visa sponsorship is not available for this position.

Community Information

UMKC is a public, urban, R1 research university with more than 15,000 undergraduate, graduate, and professional students. It is part of the larger University of Missouri System. Our university is committed to being a model urban university that is recognized for our partnerships with surrounding urban communities to effectively foster a healthy, safe, and more economically secure quality of life.

Kansas City is a vibrant community with an affordable cost of living. Our UMKC campuses are centered in the hubs of business activity, cultural arts, (some great barbeque and ethnic cuisine!) and health science research engagement for both campuses. As one of the largest cities in Missouri, we are home to national championship sports teams, a rich history of cultural arts and music, a new international airport, and a community that is very engaged with and supportive of our university initiatives. Our beautiful state has rolling hills, rivers, lakes, and long bike/hiking trails for those that enjoy time in the great outdoors. Kansas City offers something for everyone!

title: Events and Project Manager
description:
About us:

People Serving People is the largest and most comprehensive emergency shelter for families experiencing homelessness in Minnesota and a dedicated leader in homeless prevention. If you want to help transform communities and see families thrive, then People Serving People is the place for you.


What do we need:

The Events and Project Manager is the primary support for Advancement leadership in their fundraising and communications work in service to People Serving People’s mission. This role is critical to ensuring smooth and effective planning and execution of projects that support the Advancement team’s goals, including a comprehensive campaign. Primary responsibilities include project management for development and communications, and leading all Advancement events.

This is a hybrid role, with a minimum of 3 days per week in the office.


Responsibilities:

Project Management

  • Serve as the project manager for projects across the Advancement team, including email campaigns, events, and the creation and production of digital and print assets.
  • Serve as the primary administrator for the Advancement team's project management platform, including establishing timelines, developing project templates and forms, and ensuring that tasks are completed on time and projects are completed on budget.
  • Lead project meetings, provide progress reports, and facilitate communication between team members and stakeholders.
  • Manage vendor relationships as needed, ensuring successful delivery of products/deliverables, including managing logistics and processing invoices.


Events Management

  • Lead planning and serve as the primary person responsible for the execution of all Advancement events, including building and monitoring timelines, facilitating events-related meetings, securing catering, managing a budget, and on-site event execution.
  • Manage all events deliverables, including workflows for staff and vendors.
  • Lead event-related communication, including invitations, reminder and logistics emails, etc.


Operations and Data Management

  • Serve as Salesforce administrator back-up as needed, including entering gifts and generating donor acknowledgements.
  • Manage all third-party platforms utilized by the Advancement team to ensure that access, administration, and usage are consistent and accurate.
  • Establish and maintain Standard Operation Procedures (SOP) for Advancement, including identifying SOP gaps and leading solutions to address them.
  • Build campaign pages in Go Fund Me Pro/Classy and build MailChimp emails as needed.
  • Lead submission of Charity Navigator, Candid, Charities Review Council, and other related registrations.


Administrative Support

  • Provide back-up support for website and social media channels (e.g., creating and scheduling posts, making website updates) as needed.
  • Monitor various email inboxes to ensure timely responses to inquiries.
  • Other duties as assigned.

The Thompson Center for Autism and Neurodevelopment and the Department of Psychiatry in the School of Medicine at the University of Missouri-Columbia (MU) invite applications for an Assistant, Associate, or Full Professional Practice Professor position in Clinical Psychology.
The successful candidate will work primarily at the Thompson Center for Autism and Neurodevelopment, providing clinical psychology services to children with autism spectrum disorder and other neurodevelopmental conditions and their families.

The Thompson Center is a state-of-the-art facility dedicated to advancing clinical care, research, education, and training for individuals with autism and related neurodevelopmental conditions. Designed to promote interdisciplinary collaboration and innovative service delivery, the Center provides a modern, patient- and family-centered environment with advanced clinical spaces, technology, and resources. Faculty work alongside professionals from multiple disciplines, creating opportunities for collaboration, professional growth, and the delivery of high-quality, evidence-based care.

Responsibilities may include:
• Conducting comprehensive psychological and diagnostic assessments
• Providing evidence-based intervention services
• Collaborating with other clinical specialties as part of an interdisciplinary team
• Supervising and mentoring trainees, including predoctoral psychology interns and postdoctoral fellows
• Participating in research, scholarly activities, and other initiatives aligned with the mission of the Thompson Center and School of Medicine

This position offers an opportunity to combine clinical practice, teaching and supervision, interdisciplinary collaboration, and research within an academic medical center committed to improving outcomes for individuals with autism and other neurodevelopmental conditions.

title: Senior Counselor, UMKC Division of Student Affairs
description:
Hiring Department

The University of Missouri Kansas City Counseling Services

The University of Missouri-Kansas City Counseling Services is a dynamic, student-centered team dedicated to promoting the mental health, well-being, and success of the UMKC community. Through comprehensive counseling services, crisis support, consultation, prevention initiatives, and wellness programming, our team empowers students to thrive both personally and academically. As an APA-accredited training site, we are also committed to developing the next generation of mental health professionals while fostering a culture of collaboration, innovation, and inclusive care.

To learn more about our mission, visit our website:

Job Description

We are seeking two candidates who will provide a full range of clinical services including individual and group therapy, crisis intervention, outreach, consultation, assessment, supervision, and training. We are particularly interested in clinicians with expertise in trauma treatment, substance use disorder treatment, co-occurring mental health concerns, and recovery-oriented care. Service provision includes face-to-face and tele-psychological for a diverse university population, including students impacted by trauma, interpersonal violence, substance use, and complex clinical presentations.

The selected candidate will join a collaborative team at Counseling Services committed to providing evidence-based, culturally responsive, and trauma-informed care. Clinicians with specialized training in trauma-related therapies, substance use disorder treatment, recovery support services, prevention programming, motivational interviewing, harm reduction approaches, or integrated treatment approaches are strongly encouraged to apply.

In addition, this position will serve in a leadership role by acting as a liaison to key campus partners and collaborating across the university to promote student well-being, academic success, persistence, and holistic development. The successful candidate will demonstrate the ability to work collegially and collaboratively, bringing a team-oriented approach that fosters a culture of respect, partnership, and shared success. Responsibilities include providing consultation to faculty, staff, and students; developing and facilitating outreach, prevention, and educational programming; participating in university committees and interdisciplinary initiatives; and contributing to departmental training, supervision, and strategic priorities.

Essential Responsibilities

  • Provide individual counseling, group counseling, crisis intervention, consultation, and case management services to students.
  • Conduct clinical assessments, develop treatment plans, and provide evidence-based interventions for a broad range of mental health concerns.
  • Deliver services with a focus on ethical practice, cultural humility, and responsiveness to diverse identities and experiences.
  • Provide consultation to students, faculty, staff, parents, and campus partners regarding student mental health concerns and appropriate interventions.
  • Develop, coordinate, and facilitate outreach programs, workshops, trainings, and prevention initiatives that promote student well-being.
  • Participate in crisis response and risk assessment activities in accordance with departmental procedures.
  • Collaborate with campus departments, student organizations, and community partners to support student success and wellness.
  • Represent Counseling Services on university committees, task forces, and division initiatives as assigned.
  • Provide clinical supervision, training, mentoring, and consultation as appropriate based on licensure and position level.
  • Maintain accurate and timely clinical documentation in accordance with professional, legal, and ethical standards.
  • Demonstrate effectiveness in assessment and intervention with complex clinical presentations and diagnostic concerns.
  • Demonstrate knowledge of developmental issues impacting college students, including non-traditional student populations.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Shift

This position requires rare evening and weekend hours (e.g., for new student orientations or specialized outreach programming).

Minimum Qualifications

Master’s degree in psychology, counseling, marriage and family therapy, or social work and relevant licensure (or eligible to be licensed within 12 months) within the State of Missouri.

Preferred Qualifications

Specialized Clinical Expertise (Preferred)

UMKC Counseling Services is particularly interested in candidates with demonstrated expertise in one or more of the following areas:

  • Trauma treatment and trauma-informed care.
  • Treatment of PTSD, complex trauma, and trauma-related disorders.
  • Clinical work with survivors of sexual violence, interpersonal violence, stalking, discrimination, or other traumatic experiences.
  • Substance use assessment, treatment, prevention programming, and recovery support.
  • Co-occurring mental health and substance use disorders.
  • Evidence-based interventions such as Motivational Interviewing (MI), BASICS, Seeking Safety, CBT/ACT/DBT, harm reduction approaches, Cognitive Processing Therapy (CPT), Prolonged Exposure (PE), or related modalities.
  • Recovery-oriented systems of care and collegiate recovery support programs.

Additional Preferred Qualifications

  • A master’s degree in clinical or counseling psychology, or social work
  • Active full licensure as a Professional Counselor or obtain licensure in the State of Missouri within 12 months.
  • Clinical supervisory experience of master’s and/or Doctoral level trainees/interns.
  • Experience working in a college or university counseling center.
  • Advanced training or clinical experience in trauma-informed care and treatment.
  • Experience providing counseling services to survivors of interpersonal violence, sexual violence, stalking, or other traumatic experiences.

The anticipated hiring range for this position has been established as starting at $65,000 annually.

The UMKC School of Dentistry is looking for a reliable and self-motivated Clinical Technician II to work independently and in a team environment as part of our Dental Clinic Sterilization Team. title: SENIOR BUDGET ANALYST #00073340
description:
Hiring Department

Budget & Planning Services

Fiscal Services supports university operations through financial process management and guidance. The department works with campus units to ensure consistent fiscal practices. Positions involve financial processing, account support, and coordination with campus units.

Job Description

Missouri S&T is seeking a strategic financial professional to help shape the university's long-term financial future. As the Senior Budget Analyst this role is responsible for the accurate entry and maintenance of financial data, analyzing multiple budget scenarios, and organizing information into reports that support financial planning efforts. This role offers the opportunity to work across the university, collaborate with senior leaders.

Key Responsibilities:

Strategic Financial Planning

  • Develop and maintain multi-year financial projections that support the university's strategic and operational planning.
  • Analyze enrollment trends, revenue forecasts, capital investments, and other financial drivers to model future fiscal scenarios.
  • Maintain and update approved projections within the campus budgeting system.

Position Funding Management

  • Accurately enter and monitor position-level funding allocations to ensure accurate use of General Revenue Allocation (GRA) funding.
  • Maintain documentation of funding changes and verify financial adjustments are balanced and accurately recorded.

Financial Analysis & Decision Support

  • Produce recurring and ad hoc financial reports for university leadership.
  • Identify budget trends, evaluate financial performance, and communicate meaningful insights that support informed decision-making.
  • Develop dashboards, presentations, and executive summaries that translate financial data into actionable recommendations.

Budget Development & Administration

  • Support development of the annual operating budget by coordinating revenue estimates and personnel and operating expense projections.
  • Review departmental budget submissions for accuracy, consistency, and compliance with university guidelines.
  • Provide guidance and training to campus departments on budgeting processes and financial systems.
  • Identify year-over-year budget variances and partner with departments to resolve discrepancies.

Campus Collaboration

  • Partner with Fiscal Services leadership, divisional business officers, and campus administrators to collect, analyze, and interpret financial information.
  • Respond to data requests from the Controller's Office and other university stakeholders.
  • Serve as a trusted resource on budgeting tools, financial reporting, and institutional financial planning.

Strategic Initiatives & Special Projects

  • Support Finance leadership on complex financial analyses, strategic initiatives, and high-impact projects.
  • Assist in preparing budget books, executive presentations, financial communications, and other materials for campus leadership.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement efforts that enhance financial planning processes and reporting.


Minimum Qualifications

A Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education and experience and at least 5 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessary

Preferred Qualifications

  • Demonstrated experience in budgeting, financial analysis, and reporting, preferably in higher education
  • Experience utilizing PeopleSoft Queries, Power BI Reporting, Workday, and Cognos or other similar budget management and reporting tools
  • Proficient in business applications, such as MS Excel
  • Ability to compile, model, and analyze large data sets and make meaningful recommendations to management/leadership
  • Working knowledge of University Finance policies and procedures
  • Customer focused and excellent attention to detail

Anticipated Hiring Range

title: AP Shift Engineer
description:
About The Role:

The Shift Engineer (AP) / Lead Shift Engineer / Senior Shift Engineer is responsible for the safe operation, maintenance and resilience of critical engineering systems within a 24/7 broadcasting environment.

The role acts as an Authorised Person (AP), controlling permits, isolations, engineering risks and safe systems of work. Working a 4-on, 4-off days and nights shift pattern, the role provides 24/7 engineering support and deputises for the Engineering Supervisor or Technical Services Manager when required.

Key Tasks & Responsibilities

  • Lead the safe operation and maintenance of critical engineering plant and infrastructure.

  • Diagnose and resolve faults affecting critical systems, coordinating engineering responses to incidents and outages.

  • Provide technical guidance, support and mentoring to shift engineers.

  • Monitor critical alarms, system performance and operational risks, escalating issues where required.

  • Issue, manage and close Permits to Work and maintain associated permit and AP records.

  • Review and approve contractor RAMS and control high-risk maintenance activities.

  • Carry out and oversee safe isolation, reinstatement and return-to-service procedures.

  • Manage engineering impairments, temporary works and contractor access to critical systems.

  • Ensure all engineering activities comply with OCS/EMCOR and client safe systems of work.

  • Record time, activities and work orders accurately using the CAFM/work order management systems.


Critical Systems

Working knowledge of the following systems is required:

  • HVAC and chillers

  • Generators and UPS systems

  • Critical power and electrical distribution systems

  • Building Management Systems (BMS)

  • Fire alarm and fire suppression systems

  • Water systems


Qualifications, Skills & Experience

Essential

  • NVQ Level 3 in Mechanical or Electrical Engineering, or equivalent.

  • Relevant engineering apprenticeship or equivalent practical experience.

  • Experience working within a critical environment.

  • Experience issuing Permits to Work and managing safe systems of work.

  • Experience fault-finding and responding to engineering incidents in a 24/7 operational environment.


Authorisations

Candidates must hold, or be willing to obtain and maintain, one or more of the following AP appointments. Training will be provided where required:

  • AP Electrical

  • AP Mechanical

  • AP Water

  • AP Pressure Systems


Desirable

  • HNC/HND in an engineering discipline.

  • IOSH Managing Safely.

  • Multiple AP appointments.

  • Experience leading or supervising an engineering shift team.


About You

  • Safety-focused and committed to compliance.

  • Proactive and able to make sound decisions in a critical environment.

  • Able to lead and support engineers during incidents and operational activities.

  • Flexible and willing to provide additional shift cover at short notice when required.

  • Willing to develop technical knowledge and undertake additional training and authorisations.

title: Autism Clinician Scientist and Research Division Director - Thompson Center (NTT or T/TT)
description:
Hiring Department

Thompson Center for Autism & Neurodevelopment

Job Description

Autism Clinician Researcher & Research Division Director

Guru Har Krishan Saheb Professorship

Thompson Center for Autism & Neurodevelopment, University of Missouri

Open Rank, Open Track

The Thompson Center for Autism & Neurodevelopment at the University of Missouri is seeking a clinician-scientist to help shape the future of interdisciplinary autism research, clinical translation, and community impact. This is an opportunity to join a nationally recognized center during a period of major growth across clinical care, translational research, and statewide partnerships.

The ideal candidate will be a collaborative leader whose work advances understanding of autism spectrum disorder and related neurodevelopmental conditions through translational, clinical, implementation, or community-engaged research. Candidates with expertise spanning biological mechanisms, clinical characterization, intervention development, implementation science, outcomes research, biomarkers, neuroscience, or related areas are encouraged to apply.

The Research Division Director will play a central role in shaping and advancing the Thompson Center’s interdisciplinary research strategy, fostering collaboration across clinical and scientific domains, supporting clinician-scientists and trainees, and expanding the Center’s national research presence. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to help guide the future direction of one of the country’s most integrated autism and neurodevelopmental centers.

Clinical responsibilities will be tailored to the candidate’s discipline, expertise, and research portfolio. Protected research time, startup support, and leadership responsibilities will be commensurate with the candidate’s experience and role.

Facilities & Resources

The University of Missouri offers exceptional opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration as one of only six comprehensive public universities in the nation with medicine, veterinary medicine, agriculture, engineering, law, arts and sciences, and a research reactor on a single campus.

The Thompson Center for Autism & Neurodevelopment is a nationally recognized leader in autism and neurodevelopmental care, research, education, and community engagement. Housed in a recently expanded 74,000-square-foot facility, the Center integrates clinical care, research, and training to improve outcomes across the lifespan.

Its multidisciplinary team includes experts in developmental pediatrics, psychology, psychiatry, neurology, behavior analysis, speech-language pathology, occupational therapy, education, and social work. The Center’s collaborative model supports translational research, advanced phenotyping, longitudinal studies, and community-based implementation efforts, with partnerships spanning major initiatives such as SPARK, Simons Foundation, and NextGen Precision Health.

Closely connected to both the University of Missouri campus and MU Health Care, the Thompson Center provides access to diverse patient populations, statewide partnerships, and extensive research infrastructure. The holder of the Guru Har Krishan Saheb Professorship will benefit from the resources of the Thompson Center, School of Medicine, MU Health Care, NextGen Precision Health, and the broader University of Missouri research enterprise.

Educational Opportunities

The University of Missouri offers extensive educational and training opportunities through MD and PhD programs housed in the School of Medicine, including a campus-wide neuroscience PhD program, as well as programs within the College of Education and Human Development and the College of Health Sciences.

The Thompson Center plays a vital role in educating graduate students, postdoctoral fellows, residents, interns, and other trainees across disciplines. The successful candidate will hold an academic appointment aligned with their discipline and will be expected to actively contribute to education, mentorship, and trainee development, as well as participate in departmental and university service activities.

Candidacy

The ideal candidate will value interdisciplinary, team-based approaches to autism and neurodevelopmental research and demonstrate enthusiasm for building collaborative partnerships across clinical, scientific, and community settings.

The Thompson Center is particularly interested in candidates whose work bridges discovery, clinical application, dissemination, implementation, and meaningful real-world impact across the lifespan. Candidates interested in helping grow a collaborative and expanding autism research program are especially encouraged to apply.

The successful candidate will foster collaboration across disciplines, mentor trainees and junior investigators, and contribute to a culture of scientific rigor, innovation, and accountability.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications:

  • MD, MD/PhD, PhD, or equivalent degree in medicine, psychology, neuroscience, public health, or a related field
  • Clinical licensure in the state of Missouri (or eligibility/intention to obtain prior to start date, if applicable)

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Track record of research productivity and scholarly accomplishments
  • Demonstrated ability to establish or maintain an internationally recognized, externally funded research program
  • Strong publication record in peer-reviewed journals
  • Research focus relevant to autism spectrum disorder and related neurodevelopmental conditions
  • Experience leading interdisciplinary teams, programs, or research initiatives
  • Demonstrated leadership, mentorship, and administrative experience with diverse groups of individuals
  • Experience leading or contributing to complex clinical research infrastructure, data systems, translational research initiatives, or multi-site collaborations

Application Materials

In addition to completing the online application, candidates should be prepared to provide:

  • Cover Letter
  • Curriculum Vitae
  • Research Statement

Employment visa sponsorship may be available for candidates currently in the United States in H-1B status or other work-authorized status.

Columbia offers small-town friendliness with big city features and a high quality of life for people of all ages and interests. Founded on education and known as an ideal college town, its location also makes it an attractive spot for businesses and travelers. Located on Interstate 70 and U.S. Highway 63, Columbia is right in the middle of the state and the nation.
