description:
Hiring Department

Pre-Employment Transition Services Program

College of Education & Human Development

University of MO-Columbia

Job Description

Job Summary:
This position supports the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA) requirement for Vocational Rehabilitation (VR) to collaborate with Local Educational Agencies (LEA) to deliver Pre-Employment Transition Services (Pre-ETS) to students with disabilities in Missouri secondary schools. This role involves working closely with LEAs, VR, and community partners to prepare students for employment, post-secondary education, and independent living.

Key Responsibilities:
Job Exploration Counseling
• Develop and assess student career interests using tools like Missouri Connections.
• Provide insights on in-demand jobs and local labor markets.
• Help students identify and explore careers of interest in their communities or geographic regions.
• Facilitate learning through simulated work experiences in the classroom.

Postsecondary Education Counseling
• Guide students on college training options relevant to their career paths.
• Facilitate visits to college disability support services and educate on accommodations in higher education.
• Educate and assist students with financial aid processes.

Workplace Readiness Training
• Teach critical work skills such as punctuality, teamwork, and communication.
• Assist with transportation planning and financial literacy.
• Coordinate mock interviews, assist with resume development, and provide feedback when needed.

Work-Based Learning Experiences
• Collaborate with LEA staff, VR counselors, and local businesses to create work-based learning experiences in the school or community.
• Arrange job shadows, business tours, and guest speakers to introduce students to careers.
• Facilitate learning through volunteer experiences in the community.

Self-Advocacy & Peer Mentoring
• Promote self-determination and self-advocacy skills.
• Support peer mentoring opportunities, including Youth Leadership Forum.
• Facilitate real-life self-advocacy skill development.

Regional Assignment and Travel Requirements:
Pre-Employment Transition Services Specialists are assigned to specific high schools and service regions by the Pre-ETS Director based on programmatic, staffing, and service-delivery needs. Assignments may be modified or reassigned by the Director when necessary to meet the operational needs of the Pre-ETS Program.


Specialists are required to live within their designated service area and are responsible for providing services throughout all school districts and communities assigned.


Extensive travel is an essential and required function of this position. Specialists must be willing and able to travel up to 75–100% of their work time, as necessary, to assigned school districts, schools, businesses, community partners, student activities, meetings, and other locations necessary to fulfill the responsibilities of the position.


A valid Missouri driver's license, the ability to travel extensively, and flexibility in scheduling are required conditions of the position.

Requires home-office setup.

This position is not located in Columbia, MO; applicants must reside in the designated service area.

Shift

Flexible hours, Monday–Friday, 12-month appointment.

7:00 am to 3:30 pm, 7:30 am–4:00 pm, or 8:00 am to 4:30 pm, to align with school district schedules as approved by the Pre-Employment Transition Services Director.

Minimum Qualifications

Associate's degree in early childhood education, child development or related area or the equivalent combination of education and experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessary

A current MO teaching certificate or substitute teacher certification is required.

Preferred Qualifications

Preferred Qualifications:

• Education: Bachelor’s degree or master’s degree in education or related field preferred, with preference for Special Education certification.
• Experience: Minimum of 3–4 years, including at least two years in teaching or counseling, with frequent interaction with state agencies, school staff, and students in Missouri secondary schools.


• Preferred Skills:

Experience with transition-age youth, familiarity with disability programs (vocational rehabilitation, special education), career pathways, and strong skills in communication, organization, relationship-building, and leadership.

title: Building and Research Coordinator - MITC
description:
Hiring Department

University of Missouri, Research Reactor (MURR)

Job Description

MURR/MITC seeks a motivated, organized, and technically capable Building Leader to serve as the operational anchor of the MITC radiopharmaceutical research laboratories. This individual will coordinate day-to-day experimental activities across a multi-investigator, multidisciplinary research environment; ensure the safe and compliant operation of shared radiochemistry and radiopharmaceutical facilities; and serve as the primary liaison between faculty researchers and MURR operational units including Radiation Safety, Facilities, and Access Control.

The Building Leader plays a critical integrating role: bridging the needs of faculty-led research programs with the regulatory, safety, and facilities infrastructure of MURR and the University. Importantly, this individual will serve as an active leader and visible champion of nuclear safety culture within MITC, modeling the values of safety-conscious work environment (SCWE) principles, encouraging open reporting of safety concerns, and reinforcing the expectation that safety considerations are never subordinated to programmatic or research priorities. This position is well-suited to a detail-oriented STEM professional with hands-on laboratory experience who is equally committed to scientific excellence and an uncompromising safety culture.
Primary Responsibilities
Laboratory Operations and Safety
• Serve as a visible leader and active champion of nuclear safety culture within MITC laboratory spaces, modeling Safety-Conscious Work Environment (SCWE) principles
• Oversee safe day-to-day operation of shared MITC radiochemistry and radiopharmaceutical research laboratories
• Serve as primary point of contact for MURR Safety, Health Physics, and Radiation Safety Committee (RSC) matters pertaining to MITC laboratory spaces
• Support compliance with applicable radioactive material licenses and institutional safety programs
• Implement and monitor corrective actions, CAP items, and safety stand-down follow-up activities
• Coordinate with MURR and MU campus facilities on laboratory maintenance, equipment repair, infrastructure needs, and space management; prepare and track work orders
Research Coordination
• Coordinate experimental scheduling and shared equipment access across multiple faculty-led research programs
• Serve as a resource for faculty, postdoctoral researchers, and students navigating MURR access control procedures, safety training requirements, and operational protocols
• Facilitate access and training records of laboratory personnel in coordination with MURR Access Control
• Maintain laboratory inventory chemical stocks, and consumable supplies; coordinate procurement and waste disposal
Equipment and Training
• Train students, postdoctoral researchers, and visiting scientists in the proper use of shared laboratory instrumentation and radiochemical techniques
• Work with faculty to develop and maintain standard operating procedures (SOPs) for shared equipment, safety-critical operations, and routine laboratory workflows
• Coordinate preventive maintenance, calibration, and service for laboratory instrumentation in coordination with vendors and MURR facilities
Core and Animal Facility Coordination
• Coordination of animal research activities, including communication with campus animal facilities, IACUC compliance, and radioisotope use in animal protocols
• Support faculty in preparing and maintaining animal use protocols and radioactive material amendments related to preclinical imaging and therapy studies

Shift

Monday - Friday, 8AM - 5PM. This position involves routine work with open radioactive sources in controlled-access laboratory environments. Occasional coordination outside standard business hours may be needed to support time-sensitive experimental needs.

Minimum Qualifications

A Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience and at least 4 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessary.

Preferred Qualifications

• Graduate degree (M.S. or Ph.D.) in Radiochemistry, Nuclear Chemistry, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or a related field
• Hands-on experience with radiochemical synthesis, radiolabeling, or radiopharmaceutical production
• Familiarity with radioactive material licensing and radiation safety regulations (NRC/Agreement State)
• Experience with IACUC protocols, institutional animal care compliance, or in vivo radiotracer studies
• Prior experience in a multi-PI or shared research facility environment
• Proficiency with laboratory information management systems, work order platforms, or inventory management tools

Anticipated Hiring Range

Salary Range: $80,000.00 - $105,000.00 per year

Grade: GGS 011

University Title: Research Lab Manager

Internal applicants can determine their University title by accessing the Talent Profile tile in myHR.

Sponsorship Information

Other Information

About MURR and MITC

The University of Missouri Research Reactor (MURR) is the highest-flux university research reactor in the United States, operating at 10 MW with neutron fluxes up to 4.5 × 10¹4 n/cm²/sec. MURR supports a broad portfolio of research spanning nuclear analytical chemistry, radiopharmaceutical science, nuclear forensics, isotope production, and neutron scattering.

The Molecular Imaging and Theranostics Center (MITC) is a translational research facility embedded within MURR that develops and applies novel radiopharmaceuticals and molecular imaging agents for oncologic and other disease applications. MITC operates shared radiochemistry laboratories, radiopharmacy-grade production infrastructure, and preclinical imaging cores and animal research facilities on the MU campus.

Just a couple hours’ drive from St. Louis and Kansas City, Columbia is Boone County’s largest population center offering big-city culture, activities, and resources with a low cost of living. Columbia is home to a variety of restaurants and entertainment venues and hosts more than a dozen festivals each year. If you want to grow your career, continue your education, raise a family, and retire, Columbia is a good place to be!

title: Program Manager I Student Support Services - Special Events Coordinator
description:
Hiring Department

Tiger Garden -- Division of Plant Science & Technology

Job Description

The Special Events Coordinator is responsible for leading the planning, design, coordination, and execution of floral services for university events, weddings, special occasions, and on/off campus functions. This position combines expertise in floral design, business development, event management, and student mentorship to operate a successful floral program while providing hands-on educational experiences for college students pursuing careers in the floral and event industries.

The coordinator develops strategic partnerships with campus departments, alumni, community organizations, and external clients to expand the university's floral services and create real-world learning opportunities. This role serves as both an industry professional and educator, preparing students for successful careers through experiential learning, leadership development, and practical business experience.

Essential Responsibilities

Business Development & Client Relations

  • Develop and maintain strong relationships with university departments, alumni, donors, local businesses, and community organizations.
  • Market and promote university floral services to increase revenue and community engagement.
  • Consult with clients to determine floral needs, design concepts, budgets, and event logistics.
  • Prepare proposals, estimates, contracts, and invoices while ensuring exceptional customer service.
  • Identify new business opportunities that support the educational mission of the university.

Floral Design & Event Management

  • Design and produce floral arrangements for weddings, university ceremonies, conferences, donor events, athletic functions, and special occasions.
  • Coordinate all aspects of floral installation, delivery, setup, and event execution.
  • Develop creative floral concepts that align with client vision and event objectives.
  • Manage event timelines and collaborate with vendors, venue staff, and campus partners.
  • Ensure high standards of design quality, presentation, and customer satisfaction.

Budgeting & Financial Management

  • Develop and manage annual operating budgets.
  • Monitor revenues, expenses, inventory, and profitability of floral operations.
  • Purchase flowers, plants, hard goods, and supplies while maintaining cost-effective inventory practices.
  • Analyze financial performance and implement strategies to improve operational efficiency and revenue generation.

Student Leadership & Workforce Development

  • Recruit, supervise, mentor, and train college students employed within the floral program.
  • Provide hands-on instruction in floral design techniques, customer service, sales, event production, inventory management, and business operations.
  • Foster professional development by preparing students for careers in the floral, wedding, event planning, and horticulture industries.
  • Create meaningful experiential learning opportunities that integrate classroom knowledge with industry experience.
  • Evaluate student performance and encourage leadership, creativity, professionalism, and teamwork.

Program Operations

  • Oversee daily floral shop operations and maintain a safe, organized work environment.
  • Coordinate production schedules and staffing for multiple events simultaneously.
  • Ensure compliance with university policies and industry best practices.
  • Maintain equipment, floral inventory, and production facilities.

Shift

Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. - 5:00 p.m.

Minimum Qualifications

A Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education and experience and at least 2 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessary.

Preferred Qualifications

Preferred Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

  • Experience designing weddings and large-scale events.
  • Experience supervising, mentoring, or teaching college-aged students.
  • Knowledge of retail floral operations and inventory management.
  • Experience with event planning, sales, and contract management.
  • Professional floral design certification or industry credentials.
  • Experience working within higher education or experiential learning environments.
  • Advanced floral design and event production skills.
  • Business development and relationship-building expertise.
  • Budget planning and financial management.
  • Event planning and project coordination.
  • Leadership, coaching, and student mentorship.

description:

Campus Facilities Management (CFM)

Job Description

As a UMKC employee within the Boiler Operator position, you’ll belong to an engaged, diverse community and will get to interact and engage with faculty, staff, and students from a variety of backgrounds daily. UMKC offers many competitive benefits, including health, dental, life and other insurance plans; a comprehensive retirement program; and educational assistance and tuition reduction programs for employees and their spouse/dependents. You will have an assorted amount of work as a boiler operator who is responsible for covering both of our campus locations. You will have the opportunity to broaden your skillsets with the Campus Facilities Department as you will work side by side with other skilled trades such as HVAC, electrical and plumbing when needed. There is never a dull, typical day on campus as we have a wide variety of buildings within the realm of our residence halls This job could be just the refreshing change and new opportunity you are looking for, and we encourage you to apply and start a new adventure in your career.

Perform skilled work primarily involving maintenance, repair, and operation of boilers and other equipment related to heating and cooling. Review is accomplished through occasional spot-checking and observation of work for overall effectiveness. Functional contacts are limited primarily to co-workers with occasional contact with other University staff.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Periodically clean boilers inside and out, removing soot and other residue from floors, firesides, and boiler tubes, using electric tube cleaners, water hoses, and other hand tools. Inspect for excessive scaling, cracks or other defects. Disassemble and reassemble such parts as necessary to facilitate cleaning of the boiler and its working parts. Take boiler off line preparatory to overhaul and places boiler back online on completion of maintenance and repair.
  • Maintain freeze protection system. Maintain and properly respond to alarms from the automated system. May be required to evacuate a building in the event of a dangerous situation equipment, and painting floors, pipes, fixtures, and equipment in the power plant.
  • Check boilers on a day-to-day basis for proper functioning, detection of leaks or other problems, replaces or does minor repairs on defective or damaged parts. Make routine repairs on boilers, related equipment, and power plant fixtures. Replace packing, and some worn parts. Periodically overhaul solenoids, fans, and repairs leaks in water and steam lines and assist in major repairs as directed by your supervisor. Perform various cleaning and maintenance duties such as sweeping, dusting, vacuuming, lubricating equipment, and painting floors, pipes, fixtures, and equipment in the power plant.
  • May relieve or substitute for other positions performing all routine duties regularly assigned to such positions, typically involving maintenance duties. Read and record information from various gauges and instrumentation devices; manipulate controls to attain desired level.
  • Must be able to change system from gas fuel to fuel oil when required by the gas company. Maintain chemical treatment of boilers to keep boilers and pipes from deteriorating and as energy efficient as possible.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Shift

8:00am-4:00pm, Sunday through Thursday

Minimum Qualifications

  • High school graduate or equivalent; demonstrated skills may offset this requirement.
  • Knowledge of heating boilers with ability to operate boilers and associated equipment.
  • Knowledge and skill in the maintenance and use of tools, equipment, and materials used for general building maintenance.
  • Manual dexterity and physical coordination.
  • Ability to read blueprints, plans, drawings, wiring diagrams, and electrical codes.
  • Valid driver’s license required.

title: ERP Module Lead – Research Administration
description:
Hiring Department

ERP Project

Job Description

The University of Missouri ERP Forward Program strives to strengthen our administrative foundation to enable a greater focus on delivering enterprise-wide missions. The program will implement a new Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system along with supporting technology to streamline administrative processes, improve user experience, reinforce a primary system of record, and enable enterprise-wide compliance.

A successful candidate for this position in the ERP Forward Program will:
• Understand financial and research administration operations, business processes, and systems.
• Demonstrate strong analytical, documentation, and organizational skills.
• Communicate effectively with stakeholders across the University.
• Support continuous improvement through process evaluation and system innovation.

The ERP Forward Finance Workstream supports the University of Missouri’s financial systems and manages technology processes and functions that affect transaction processing, data reconciliation, reporting, system maintenance, and upgrades. The University is preparing to implement a new ERP system over the next three years, along with an Electronic Research Administration (ERA) platform that will be implemented first to support pre-award grants management. The Finance Workstream team will provide functional expertise for both efforts and will assume ownership of the ERA platform after implementation.

Reporting to the ERP Pillar Lead, this position serves as the functional lead for pre-award research administration systems with initial focus on implementing the University’s pre-award ERA platform. The role will document requirements, redesign processes, lead testing, and prepare the organization for adoption in coordination with stakeholders across all four campuses and the health system. It will work closely with the post-award functional lead, a peer role under the same manager, to support a seamless proposal-to-award-to-project lifecycle.

Following ERA go-live and stabilization, the position will retain ongoing functional ownership of the ERA platform in production. The position will also support the broader cloud ERP implementation where ERA, finance, research administration, reporting, data validation, integrations, or business process design intersects.

This position offers a substantive role in the implementation and long-term support of major University systems, with opportunities for growth as the ERA and ERP programs mature.

Key Responsibilities

ERA Implementation and Functional Leadership
• Own assigned workstreams for the ERA implementation, with primary responsibility for pre-award functionality and related business processes.
• Partner with Research Administration, Finance, Sponsored Programs, and Information Technology stakeholders across all four campuses and the health system to define requirements, redesign processes, and prepare for adoption.
• Guide pre-award process design for proposal development and budgeting, internal routing and approval, sponsor submission, and award intake.
• Lead functional design for ERA integrations with the University’s financial system of record (currently PeopleSoft), including data mapping, interface design, error handling, and the transition from PeopleSoft to the new cloud ERP, partnering with the post-award functional lead on the award handoff between the two systems.
• Maintain key implementation documentation, including process maps, configuration workbooks, security role definitions, data validation and testing materials, and functional decision records.
• Coordinate system integration, end-to-end, and user acceptance testing; manage defect triage and resolution with the implementation partner.
• Develop and deliver end-user training and change management activities across decentralized campus research administration offices.

ERA Production Support and Continuous Improvement
• Serve as the primary functional owner of the ERA platform after go-live, including configuration maintenance, security administration, user provisioning, and resolution of escalated user issues.
• Manage vendor’s SaaS release cycle impacts by assessing functional changes, coordinating regression testing, and communicating updates to campus users.
• Monitor ERA data quality and integration activity, resolve exceptions, and support ongoing reporting needs.
• Maintain end-user documentation and training resources, and identify opportunities to improve processes, configuration, and user experience after go-live.

ERP Implementation and Cross-System Alignment
• Support the cloud ERP implementation while maintaining ERA production responsibilities.
• Partner with ERP functional leads to validate requirements, solution designs, integrations, reporting, data conversion, and deployment readiness.
• Lead planning and testing for the transition of ERA financial integrations from PeopleSoft to the new cloud ERP, including interface redesign, cutover planning, and post-cutover reconciliation.
• Identify risks, issues, process gaps, and improvement opportunities that affect ERA, ERP, or the broader proposal-to-award-to-project lifecycle.

As with all positions, involvement with other duties and responsibilities may be expected to support the mission and purpose of the University of Missouri System.

Shift

M-F 8:00AM to 5:00PM

Minimum Qualifications

A bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and experience and at least 3 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessary.

Preferred Qualifications

• Direct experience in pre-award research administration or sponsored programs administration in higher education or an academic medical center.
• Experience implementing or administering an electronic research administration platform (for example Cayuse, Concourse Tech, Huron Research, Kuali Research, Novelution, or Streamlyne).
• Working knowledge of federal research administration requirements, including 2 CFR 200 (Uniform Guidance), sponsor submission systems such as Grants.gov, Research.gov, and NIH ASSIST, and F&A rate and cost share concepts.
• Experience with system implementation or conversion projects, including integrations, data mapping, and reconciliation between enterprise systems.
• Experience gathering and documenting business requirements and process flows, test planning and user acceptance testing.
• Experience with cloud-based enterprise systems, particularly SaaS platforms with vendor-driven release cycles.
• Experience supporting change management, developing training materials, and building consensus on standardized processes across decentralized units or multiple campuses.
• Ability to exercise sound judgment, manage complex cross-functional work, and translate business needs between research administration, finance, technical teams, vendors, and campus stakeholders.

title: Postdoctoral Research Fellow - Aerosol Biology of Influenza Transmission
description:
Hiring Department

The Center for Influenza and Emerging Infectious Diseases (CIEID) at the University of Missouri

Job Description

The Center for Influenza and Emerging Infectious Diseases (CIEID) at the University of Missouri is seeking a highly motivated Postdoctoral Research Fellow to join an interdisciplinary research program focused on the aerosol and airborne transmission biology of influenza viruses. The fellow will have the opportunity to play a central role in major NIH-supported research on influenza transmission, including a multidisciplinary P01 program as part of the NIAID Influenza Transmission Research Consortium (ITRC) and complementary NIH R01-supported research. A major goal of our research program is to understand why infected hosts differ in the amount and infectivity of virus released into aerosols, why exposure results in infection in some recipients but not others, and why different influenza viruses vary in their capacity for airborne transmission. We are particularly interested in candidates with expertise or strong research interests in aerosol science, aerosol biology, respiratory transmission, or related areas. Prior experience specifically with influenza is desirable but not required. The fellow will have opportunities to develop an independent research niche within this broad transmission program, with research directions tailored to the candidate’s expertise and career interests.

Research Focus and Responsibilities
• Design and conduct mechanistic studies of influenza transmission involving human studies and/or controlled animal models, as appropriate to the candidate’s expertise and research interests.
• Investigate viral, host, immune, and environmental determinants of infectious virus shedding, aerosol generation, recipient susceptibility, and airborne transmission.
• Study the generation, properties, transport, and fate of respiratory aerosols, including particle-size distributions, infectious virus content, aerosol stability, airflow, particle transport, and other factors relevant to transmission.
• Develop and apply experimental, engineering, and quantitative approaches to airborne transmission. Depending on the candidate’s expertise and research interests, these may include bioaerosol sampling, aerosol instrumentation, particle characterization, airflow measurements, computational fluid dynamics, and mathematical or mechanistic modeling.
• Integrate virologic, immunologic, aerosol, clinical, environmental, and transmission data to identify mechanisms and determinants of influenza transmission.
• Work collaboratively across virology, immunology, aerosol science, engineering, human studies, animal models, and quantitative modeling, while analyzing data and contributing to manuscripts, presentations, collaborative publications, and grant-related scientific activities.


Research Environment and Career Development
The Wan Influenza Systems Biology Laboratory and CIEID provide a collaborative environment spanning the School of Medicine, College of Veterinary Medicine, College of Engineering, Bond Life Sciences Center, and Institute for Data Science and Informatics. The research program has access to ABSL-2 transmission facilities, BSL-3 and ABSL-3 biocontainment facilities, aerosol sampling and engineering capabilities, laboratory automation, and institutional cores supporting genomics, imaging, proteomics, metabolomics, bioinformatics, and computational biology. Through the multidisciplinary P01 program as part of the NIAID Influenza Transmission Research Consortium (ITRC) and complementary R01-supported research, the fellow will have opportunities to work with investigators across aerosol science, virology, immunology, engineering, animal models, human studies, and quantitative modeling; develop an independent scientific niche in aerosol and airborne transmission biology; publish interdisciplinary work; contribute to major collaborative grants; and build expertise at the interface of aerosol science and infectious disease.

Qualifications

Qualifications
• PhD or equivalent doctoral degree in aerosol science, aerosol biology, environmental or occupational health, engineering, microbiology, virology, infectious diseases, or a related field. Research experience in aerosol science, respiratory or airborne pathogen transmission, or related experimental or quantitative systems is preferred. Prior experience specifically with influenza is desirable but not required.
• Strong quantitative, organizational, communication, and scientific writing skills and the ability to work effectively in a multidisciplinary team.

Application Materials

Must complete MU application as well as the below items.

Please send the following materials to Dr. Henry Wan through cieid@missouri.edu:
• Cover letter describing your research experience, interests, and career goals
• Curriculum vitae
• Contact information for at least two professional references

Application Deadline

https://mizzou.us/WorkatBondLSC

About Us:
The Bond Life Sciences Center at the University of Missouri is a dynamic hub where groundbreaking research meets real-world impact. Designed to foster interdisciplinary collaboration, our state-of-the-art facility brings together experts in diverse fields—engineers, cancer biologists, plant scientists, and IT specialists—all working towards a common goal: to save lives, reduce costs, and enhance everyday life for Missourians and people around the globe.

Our Mission:
We are committed to transforming scientific discoveries into actionable solutions. Our innovative research not only addresses pressing challenges in human and animal health, the environment, and agriculture, but it also translates into meaningful improvements in the lives of individuals everywhere. We also strive to share our findings with the public, ensuring that our discoveries resonate far beyond the lab in a language anyone can understand through our blog, Decoding Science, events for the public, social media and more.

Why Join Us?
At the Bond Life Sciences Center, you’ll be part of a vibrant community dedicated to making a difference. Our collaborative environment not only supports innovative research but also ensures that our discoveries lead to tangible benefits for society. Work in an award-winning facility designed for creativity and impact and contribute to a mission that truly changes lives.

title: SENIOR STRATEGIC COMMUNICATIONS CONSULTANT #00064616
description:
Hiring Department

Marketing & Communications

Job Description

Missouri University of Science and Technology (Missouri S&T) is looking for an exceptional communicator for the position of Senior Strategic Communications Consultant to work with leaders within our College of Engineering and Computing (CEC) as part of a central Communications, Outreach and Engagement team. This position requires talent, tact and tenacity, strong writing and storytelling skills, a collaborative mindset, the ability to influence others, political savvy, an enterprising outlook, and good doses of creativity, dauntless positivity in the face of difficulty, humor and humility.

This position reports to the director of strategic communications in the Marketing and Communications Department, with dotted-line reporting to either the vice provost and dean of the college or an associate dean of the college. The position works closely with other staff within Communications, Outreach and Engagement to achieve the college’s strategic goals.

Goals and Responsibilities

The person in this position will be responsible for collaboratively developing comprehensive college-level marketing and communications strategies in partnership with fellow marketing and communications staff and in collaboration with leaders, staff and faculty in the college. This will involve:

  • Developing effective external relations for the college in collaboration with the central marketing and communications
  • Advising the vice provost and dean, associate deans, and department chairs on communications strategies and outreach
  • Coordinating with development and alumni relations staff on alumni and donor relations communications and marketing
  • Developing written content for marketing materials that support the college’s marketing and visibility goals, including print and digital communications materials, such as news releases, print and electronic newsletters, and website content
  • Developing content for and managing college-level social media channels
  • Providing expertise and assistance for other staff within the college and departments who are responsible for mid- to high-level communications tasks, such as online content, newsletters, etc.
  • Positioning the vice provost and dean, associate deans, department chairs and other college faculty as thought leaders and influencers to enhance the university’s visibility and influence
  • Ensuring consistent messaging, brand identity and achievement of marketing goals between the college and the university at large
  • Along with the user interface and user experience designer (UX/UI designer), attending college-level meetings as co-liaison between the college and the marketing and communications department
  • Coordinating with UX/UI designer on user experience with CEC website and department websites

Tasks for CEC

  • News and feature writing on behalf of CEC, including press releases, CEC and university website articles, with a heavy emphasis on writing about CEC research.
  • Marketing materials for CEC.
  • U.S. News influencer marketing, including e-newsletter (6-8/year) and postcards of major announcements (new dean, etc.)
  • CEC social media posting (Facebook, Linkedin).
  • CEC internal communications (dean’s internal newsletter).
  • Strategic communications initiatives for the college.
  • Assist with departmental email newsletters (advise on content, edit copy, recommend stories, etc.)
  • Maintain contact and strong relations with CEC leaders, including department chairs.
  • Coordinate requests for print and digital marketing materials related to CEC and its academic departments.

Minimum Qualifications

A Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education and experience and at least 4 years of experience from which comparable knowledge and skills can be acquired is necessary

Anticipated Hiring Range

The anticipated hiring range for this position has been established as $60,944-$85,176 annually.

Salary is determined by a variety of factors, including but not limited to, the individual’s particular combination of education, skills, and experience, as well as organizational requirements.

Your total compensation goes beyond the number on your paycheck. The University of Missouri provides generous leave, health plans, and retirement contributions that add to your bottom line.

title: CHILLER TECHNICIAN II
description:
Hiring Department

Department of Energy Management

Job Description

Powering Mizzou’s Future
At MU Energy Management, we don’t just keep the lights on — we power the future. Our team is responsible for producing, purchasing, and delivering essential utility services across the University of Missouri campus. At the heart of our operations is the cutting-edge Combined Cooling, Heating, and Power Plant (CCHP), which generates steam, chilled water, and electricity to heat, cool, and energize more than 17 million square feet of academic, research, athletic, and healthcare facilities.

In addition to the CCHP Plant, we operate two chilled water district cooling loops with over 30 chillers and a total capacity of more than 34,000 tons. Our mission is to deliver cost-effective, reliable, and resilient utility services that support the University’s academic and research excellence.

If you are passionate about energy, innovation, and resiliency, join a team that keeps Mizzou running — and thriving.

__________________________________________________________________

Position: Chiller Technician II

Nature of Work

Perform skilled work on a journey level in the installation, maintenance, service and repair of refrigeration and air conditioning units, equipment, and systems. All work is subject to spot checking and inspections for conformance to specifications and accepted standards of the trade.

After required time and successful completion of skill assessments, this position can progress to Chiller Technician III.

Key Responsibilities:

• Perform repair, preventative maintenance, and operation of all mechanical and absorption air conditioning systems and refrigeration systems including air cooled, steam turbine driven and water-cooled systems. Use various tools: gauges, torches, vacuum pumps, drills, etc. in performing duties. Test and replace broken parts; check for and repair leaks; repair and adjust valves, fittings, and pipe connection; adjust refrigerant level of units; and service and lubricate units as required.

• Assist in, or perform major overhauls on absorption, steam turbine driven, centrifugal, and reciprocating chiller components and systems. Purchase parts, install refrigerant, perform moving, rigging, and handling heavy and expensive components and parts safely.

• Assist in, or evaluate complex factors and malfunctions in absorption, steam turbine driven, centrifugal, and reciprocating chiller systems and take corrective actions.

• Assist with on-the-job training of Chiller Tech I positions.

• Assist with design and construction of specialized tools and equipment to repair and maintain all types of chillers.

• Clean, maintain, safely operate and properly store all tools and equipment.

• Follow all safety policies and procedures including lock-out-tag-out. Wear all necessary PPE as job duties require.

• Prepare records, detailed reports, recommendations, cost estimates, prepare material orders, and similar information for supervisory and management use.

• Utilize asset management system for work orders, parts and repair tracking

• Perform other duties as assigned.

Supervision Received

• Administrative and functional supervision is received from a designated supervisor. Receives oral and written instructions daily/weekly outlining work to be performed. Work may be supplemented by diagrams and/or blueprints.

Supervision Exercised

• No supervision exercised, may provide instruction.

Shift

7:00 AM – 3:30 PM / Mon. – Fri.

Minimum Qualifications

• A high school graduate or an equivalent combination of education and experience from which comparable knowledge, skills, and abilities can be acquired is necessary.
• Four years of experience working with large chiller systems or a combination of two years of experience working with large chiller systems and four years of experience as a journey level refrigeration mechanic.
• Refrigerant certification as required by state and federal laws and course work in large chiller systems.
• Skill in use and operation of tools, equipment and materials necessary to complete the essential functions of the job.
• Ability to read blueprints, drawings, schematics and wiring diagrams and knowledge of building codes are required.
• A valid driver's license to operate a vehicle in the state of Missouri is required.
• Ability to grasp, lift, carry and set down heavy objects (75 lbs.) on a regular basis.
• Ability to climb and work from ladders, scaffolding and staging on an occasional basis.

Preferred Qualifications

Eight or more years’ experience operating and maintaining large (1000 ton) chiller systems.

Certification as an EPA Section 608 Universal Technician.

Experience operating and maintaining air cooled chillers up to and larger than 500 tons.

Experience operating and maintaining water cooled chillers up to and larger than 1000 tons.

Experience with cooling tower operation and maintenance.

Experience maintaining pumps, motors, and fans.

Must possess a valid driver’s license, which will allow legal operation of a motor vehicle in the State of Missouri.

Salary Range: $26 - $32 hourly

title: Field Specialist in Human Development – Gentry County, MO
description:
Hiring Department

University of Missouri (MU) Office of Extension and Engagement

Health & Human Sciences Extension

Job Description

MU TITLE: Assistant/Associate/Full Extension Professional

LOCATION: Albany, Missouri and primarily serves Daviess, DeKalb, Gentry, and Harrison Counties in Northwest Region, with additional service across the state as needed.

SPECIALIST EMPHASIS

The Human Development and Family Sciences Specialist is responsible for planning, implementing, and evaluating educational programs in parenting, family strengthening, mental health awareness, adolescence, aging and/or early childhood care and education.

This position is responsible for planning, implementing, and evaluating educational programs and services in the Extension Health and Human Sciences unit. The Health & Human Sciences Extension program promotes optimal well-being of individuals, families, and communities.

This position is a 12-month, ranked, non-tenure track appointment at the rank of assistant, associate, or full Extension Professional. Rank will be determined at the time of appointment based on qualifications and experience in accordance with the MU Extension faculty standards. This position will hold the working title of Field Specialist in Human Development.

As a Field Specialist, your workload distribution at appointment will be 90% Extension Teaching and 10% Traditional Service.

This appointment is renewable annually at the discretion of the University and workload distribution may change at the discretion of Extension leadership. Circumstances affecting continued employment include, but are not limited to, work performance, fund availability, and educational priorities.

CORE DUTIES OF MU EXTENSION SPECIALISTS

MU Extension Specialists deliver the University of Missouri to all Missourians. They serve all Missourians by bringing research-based solutions to work on local problems. MU Extension Specialists teach new and foundational concepts, link people to resources, support partner organizations, participate in research, train volunteers, evaluate programs, foster innovation, and serve communities. MU Extension Specialists work as a team to expand educational attainment, foster economic development, and improve health outcomes. These core duties fall into three major areas:

Educate, Create, and Connect.

  • Educate. MU Extension specialists design, conduct, and evaluate educational programs. MU Extension specialists teach research-based information via meetings, in-person and online courses, continuing education classes, technical assistance, volunteer training, media, websites, consultation, and other educational methods. They provide educational programs that support the individual, organizational, and community goals of Missouri’s learners and clients.
  • Create. MU Extension specialists develop innovative and research-informed educational products, services, materials, and other scholarly works. These include curricula, publications, presentations, educational tools, websites, and similar resources. MU Extension specialists obtain and use extramural funding to support creative works. MU Extension specialists contribute to the scholarship of Extension and Engagement by evaluating programs that result in learning and behavior changes that impact individuals and communities.
  • Connect. MU Extension specialists engage with learners, stakeholders, volunteers, and communities, including county extension councils, government officials and agencies, partners, and University and professional organizations. MU Extension specialists listen and respond with care. MU Extension specialists intentionally foster engaged partnerships and robust connections to the wide array of programs offered by the whole University of Missouri System.

Professional Expectations

  • Engage with councils, commissions, legislators, and stakeholders in all coverage counties to identify educational needs and then collaborate with appropriate internal and external partners to meet those needs.
  • Create an annual plan-of-work that reflects local needs and aligns with statewide program area efforts. Provide a monthly report of impact to county extension council assigned, supervisors, county commissioners and others, regarding programmatic efforts. Attend at least one county extension council meeting each month and provide an oral update on program efforts.
  • Collaborate with campus-based specialists on research projects and then deliver findings from those efforts via demonstrations, field days, courses, workshops, consultations, publications, and appropriate media.
  • Work in collaboration with other specialist in counties of responsibility to serve the needs of the headquartered county, ensuring counties receive promotional materials in advance of programming.
  • Effectively work with supervisors, other specialists, and local leaders to complete administrative tasks as needed.
  • Demonstrate competency in communication, educational programming, subject matter knowledge, educational delivery, volunteer management, grant acquisition, teamwork, interpersonal relations, organization knowledge, leadership, and professionalism.
  • Offer timely, research-based information during times of natural disasters or similar events.
  • Represent the University of Missouri on boards and committees as assigned.
  • Participate in professional development events to improve both technical and leadership skills.
  • Other duties and responsibilities as assigned to support the mission of MU Extension.

Additional Expectations

  • MU Extension programs often occur outside of normal business hours. MU Extension Specialists should expect to attend these events as needed to meet the needs of learners, clients, and stakeholders.
  • MU Extension Specialists travel regularly throughout Missouri and occasionally to out-of-state locations. MU Extension requires specialists to have a valid Missouri driver’s license, a legally operating vehicle, and wireless telephone/data service for university use. MU Extension specialists receive reimbursement for approved travel expenses, per University of Missouri policy.

MU EXTENSION LEADERSHIP RECEIVED

The Senior Program Director for Health & Human Sciences Extension provides overall programmatic leadership. Programmatic supervision comes from the Education Director for the Health & Human Sciences Extension and administrative oversight from the Regional Director for the Northwest Region.

MU EXTENSION INFORMATION

The University of Missouri (MU) Office of Extension and Engagement’s distinct land-grant mission is to improve lives, communities, and economies by producing relevant, reliable, and responsive educational strategies throughout Missouri. Our dedicated and knowledgeable specialists and staff collaborate with researchers and community leaders to develop and deliver programs that address the needs of Missourians, including educational attainment, economic development, and healthy people. For more information about MU Extension and Engagement, please visit .

UNIVERSITY INFORMATION

The University of Missouri, also known as Mizzou and MU, is the Flagship University of the four-campus University of Missouri System. It is one of the state’s land-grant universities. MU’s comprehensive undergraduate programs and its graduate, professional, and research programs attract an annual enrollment of more than 30,000 students. MU Extension and Engagement programs are located on all four campuses and in 114 counties and St. Louis city.

Qualifications

An earned PhD or master’s degree at time of appointment.

Candidates will be evaluated on:

  • Coursework exhibited in Human Development and Family Sciences or related areas.
  • Demonstrated ability to translate research into educational programs in parenting, family strengthening, mental health awareness, adolescence, aging and/or early childhood care and education for audiences of all age groups is critical.
  • Ideal candidates will also have successful experiences in youth and/or adult education.
  • Successful administrative and leadership experience, particularly in managing fiscal, human, and data resources, is preferred.
  • Effective and innovative teaching strategies that engage others, including strong listening, written, and oral communication skills.
  • The ability to integrate new and emerging technology into teaching strategies. Experience in designing, conducting, and evaluating educational programs, and applying research-based knowledge in subject matter areas related to community cooperation and collaboration, capacity assessment and action planning, needs assessment, citizen participation, leadership, resource management, and volunteerism is desired.

Anticipated Hiring Range

This position offers a minimum starting salary of $58,000, with the final salary determined based on the candidate’s qualifications and experience.

Application Materials

Complete the brief online application and be prepared to upload:

• Cover Letter

• Resume/CV

• Copies of all unofficial academic transcripts, and

• a list of 3-5 references

For questions regarding the online application process contact MUHR@missouri.edu or call 573.882.7976. For technical problems with the online application process contact Helpdesk@missouri.edu or call 573.882.5000.

Sponsorship Information

Employment visa sponsorship is not available for this position.

This position is eligible for University benefits. As part of your total compensation, the University offers a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental and vision plans, retirement, and educational fee discounts for all four UM System campuses. title: Resident Advisor (Returner) AY27-28 (Student)
description:
Hiring Department

This application is intended ONLY for current Resident Advisors. Current Resident Advisors must submit an updated HR application in order to be considered for a returner Resident Advisor position in the 2027-2028 academic year.

Current Resident Advisors who return for the 2027-2028 academic year will be assigned an RA housing assignment in late spring/early June. You will not select a room preference in the housing portal.

Job Description

Resident Advisors (RAs) are focused on building community within the residence halls. RAs serve as mentors and leaders within the halls by having a robust knowledge of the University of Missouri and MU Housing. Resident Advisors will connect residents to leadership, service, and involvement opportunities on campus.

As agents of the University, Resident Advisors are part of a team that strives to support and know their residents, while also creating a strong sense of belonging within the halls and on campus. Resident Advisors serve as ambassadors for MU Housing, the Division of Student Affairs and Mizzou and must serve as positive members of the university community while in their positions.

Resident Advisors are a presence in the halls. They are responsible for setting and role modeling expectations on their respective floors by abiding by and enforcing MU Housing and University guidelines and procedures. Resident Advisors help create a positive community in the hall by managing conflict between roommates and residents. They also have a thorough understanding of emergency protocols and the opening and closing procedures.

Resident Advisors are expected to be a positive brand ambassador for MU Housing by communicating the benefits of living in the halls, while also promoting employment opportunities within the department. Resident Advisors assist with contracting in their position; this may include but is not limited to tabling, working, and planning hall events and having conversations with residents about living with MU Housing.

MU Housing is a 365/24/7 operation, and RA presence is required in order to provide exceptional services and experiences for our residents. Resident Advisors may be required to complete tasks in the residence halls during scheduled academic breaks and university closures.

Resident Advisors are required to arrive early in August to participate in annual RA training, Mizzou Move-In, and Welcome Week activities. They are also required to stay late in December and May to assist with closing hall operations for the semester and academic year.

Essential Functions

Resident Advisors will perform some or all of the duties listed below and may be assigned to operate in one or more service areas or functions.

Community Development and Sense of Belonging

  • Spend time on the floor to build community within their respective floors, halls, and neighborhood by making residents feel welcome.
  • Support and know the residents living on their floor and in their building.
  • Build relationships with their residents by getting to know who they are and establishing how they can mentor them.
  • Be a presence in the halls by spending time in common areas and being social.
  • Plan and attend events within the hall/neighborhood, and support programs and initiatives put on by MU Housing, Student Affairs and Mizzou.
  • Maintain extensive knowledge about the University of Missouri, academic programs, and involvement opportunities on campus.
  • Connect residents to leadership, service, involvement, and employment opportunities on campus and within the department.
  • Support the academic mission of the University by fostering an integrative learning environment through the facilitation of programming.
  • Collaborate with campus partners and programs to support already existing events and initiatives. Support relationships across campus to avoid duplicating efforts.
  • Act as a leader on the floor and within the respective hall.
  • Manage and mediate conflict between residents and roommates.

On-Call, Operational, and Administrative Responsibilities

Provide operational and administrative support for the residence hall.

Serve in an on-call duty rotation overnight and as situations arise, with regard to class schedule.

Understand and carry out emergency procedures and crisis response.

Understand, abide by and enforce policies and procedures for MU Housing.

Be responsible for the cleanliness of communal spaces and, potentially, incidents involving bodily fluids.

Required Attendance and Participation

RAs are expected and required to arrive to and depart campus, as well as participate in, the following in accordance with the dates outlined below:

  • July 30th – August 1st , 2027: RA Move-In Weekend
  • Aug. 1st-7th, 2027: RA August Training
  • Anticipate required participation between 8 AM – 7 PM daily
  • Aug. 7th, 2027: Early Arrivals Move-In
    • Anticipate required participation between 7 AM – 7 PM
  • Aug. 8th-10th, 2027: Move-In Preparation
  • Aug. 11-12th, 2027: Mizzou Move-In
    • Anticipate required participation between 7 AM – 8 PM
  • Dec. 13, 2027: Winter Recess
    • Anticipate departure after 10 AM
  • Jan. 12, 2028: RA Winter Training Check-In
    • Arrive by 8 PM
  • Jan. 12-15, 2028: RA Winter Training
    • Anticipate required participation between 8 AM – 7 PM
  • May 15, 2028: End of Year Hall Closing
    • Anticipate departure after 10 AM

ALL DATES AND TIMES ARE SUBJECT TO CHANGE

  • Attend weekly RA staff meetings.
  • Attend one-on-one meetings as scheduled by the supervisor.
  • Attend RA and other training and activities as required by MU Housing.
    • These include, but are not limited to, Orientation, August RA Training, Mizzou Move-In (Early Arrival, First Years, and Returning Students), Winter Break Move-Out, January RA Training, and Academic Year Move-Out/Hall Closures.

Training is a mandatory part of your appointment and failure to attend training may result in appointment action up to and including termination from the appointment. Having previously completed training does not exempt you from further training.

As with all positions, involvement with other duties and responsibilities is expected in order to serve and maintain our departmental and Student Affairs mission.

Additional Responsibilities

Act as situationally critical staff and follow instructions for dealing with situations that impact the residence halls.

Receive training on a wide variety of MU programs and offerings and appropriate delivery methods.

Attend and participate in periodic RA meetings and all training sessions scheduled by the supervisor and MU Housing.

As with all positions, involvement with other duties and responsibilities is expected in order to serve and maintain our departmental and Student Affairs mission.

Background Check

Following the application process, the MU Housing team will review all submitted materials and select candidates for the 2027–2028 academic year. Please note that any offer of appointment is contingent upon successful completion of a criminal background check, in accordance with policies at University of Missouri. Candidates who receive an offer will be provided with additional information and instructions regarding the background check process at that time.

For questions about the selection or background check process, please contact musahr@missouri.edu.

Anticipated Hiring Range

Compensation includes a single residence hall room and a top-tier dining meal plan for the term of the appointment. RAs are required to maintain 100% occupancy in their university-provided room, suite, and/or apartment. The university housing assignment is decided at the discretion of MU Housing.

Shift

The RA role requires on average a commitment of 20 hours per week; however, hours may vary based on department needs; and this role may include evening and/or weekend commitments.

Minimum Qualifications

To be eligible for a student title, an individual must be enrolled at the University of Missouri at all times during the term of the housing contract and RA appointment.

Selection is contingent upon successful results of a student employment record review conducted by Student Affairs Human Resources, Residential Life, the Office of Student

Accountability and Support, and the Office of Institutional Equity. Selection is also contingent on successful results of a background check.

Applicants must be in good standing with MU Housing and the University

Maintain a 2.75 minimum GPA for both the semester and cumulative GPA.

Preferred Qualifications

Lived in MU Housing for 2 semesters prior to start of the appointment.

  • Primary consideration will be given to applicants with a 3.2 GPA or above.
  • Excellent relationship-building skills and a passion for helping others feel connected to campus
  • Enthusiasm for involvement, Residential Life, Student Affairs, and Mizzou
  • Enjoyment in being a leader
  • Possess strong organizational skills
  • Good time-management skills
  • Reliable and dependable
  • Good communication skills
  • Sense of commitment to the department
  • Ability to work with a variety of people
  • Able to manage and mediate conflict in a variety of situations

Ability to function in a team setting, where they will have to collaborate with others to plan events, accomplish hall operations and administrative tasks and support residents

Passion for educating others informally and formally

Ability to understand, interpret and communicate guidelines to ensure the safety and well-being of residents

Application Materials

Complete application, and upload the following:

Résumé

Cover letter

Benefit Eligibility

This is a student position and is not eligible for University benefits.

Equal Employment Opportunity

The University of Missouri is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

To request ADA accommodations, please call the Director of Accessibility and ADA at 573-884-7278.

As a Security Officer, you will play a key role in maintaining a safe, secure and welcoming environment within a designated court or tribunal building. title: Lead Family Navigator
description:
Hiring Department

Department of the Thompson Center.

Job Description

The Thompson Center for Autism and Neurodevelopment is a nationally recognized center dedicated to improving the lives of individuals with autism and other neurodevelopmental conditions through exceptional clinical care, research, education, and community engagement. Our interdisciplinary team is committed to providing comprehensive, family-centered services that support individuals across the lifespan. We are seeking a collaborative and innovative Lead Family Navigator to oversee our Family Navigation program and help ensure families receive timely, compassionate guidance as they access services through the Thompson Center.

Position Summary

The Lead Family Navigator provides leadership and oversight for the Family Navigation team while supporting continuous improvement of patient access processes. title: Cardiometabolic Resource & Referral Specialist – Center for Child Well-Being
description:
Hiring Department

Department of Psychiatry

Job Description

The Center for Child Well-Being, housed within the Department of Psychiatry, in collaboration with the Maternal-Fetal Care Center in the Department of Obstetrics, Gynecology, and Women’s Health, seeks two full-time Cardiometabolic Resource and Referral Specialists.

This full-time, grant-funded, exempt, on-site position supports pregnant and postpartum patients and the professionals who care for them by connecting callers with timely, accurate, and appropriate cardiometabolic and social-service resources throughout Missouri.

Required credential

Current Missouri licensure as a registered nurse (RN) or licensed practical nurse (LPN).

About the Center for Child Well-Being

The Center for Child Well-Being drives positive change for children and families through innovative programs, collaborative community partnerships, and strategic capacity building. Guided by our mission to improve outcomes for young children and their families, we envision a future where all children have a strong foundation for lifelong health.
Working at the Center means being part of a passionate, collaborative team committed to impact. Staff are supported in their professional growth, empowered to contribute meaningfully, and engaged in work that is purpose-driven and community-centered. Join us in shaping a more responsive and resilient childhood systems landscape across Missouri!

About the Maternal-Fetal Care Center (Department of Obstetrics, Gynecology, and Women's Health)

The Maternal-Fetal Care Center provides comprehensive, multidisciplinary care for women with high-risk pregnancies through an academic practice committed to excellence in patient care, education, research, and innovation. The Center brings together Maternal-Fetal Medicine specialists and a broad network of multidisciplinary partners, including General Obstetrics & Gynecology, Neonatology, Pediatric Subspecialties, Genetics, Cardiology, Anesthesiology, and other specialists, to provide coordinated care for complex maternal and fetal conditions. The Center’s comprehensive services include outpatient and inpatient maternal-fetal medicine consultation, a robust ultrasound program with an AIUM-accredited Ultrasound Unit and echo-certified sonographers, comprehensive genetics services, and specialized multidisciplinary programs such as the Cardio-Obstetrics. As an integral part of the University of Missouri School of Medicine, the Center also provides an outstanding educational environment for medical students, OB/GYN residents, and Maternal-Fetal Medicine fellows while advancing clinical research and innovation in high-risk obstetric care.

Key responsibilities

  • Respond to resource and referral requests received by telephone, email, or other program channels and complete a focused assessment of each caller’s needs.
  • Performs all activities in compliance with HIPAA, health and safety regulations, and organizational policies and procedures.
  • Identify and connect patients, families, and healthcare professionals with cardiometabolic, maternal-health, and community resources, including services related to hypertension, diabetes, nutrition, medication access, transportation, insurance, behavioral or mental health, and social needs. Conducts follow-up with patients and families as necessary and indicated.
  • Provides responsive, respectful, and service-oriented support, fostering engagement and satisfaction.
  • Provide warm handoffs, follow-up, and problem-solving support for complex or difficult-to-place referrals while maintaining appropriate role boundaries.
  • Develop and maintain accurate statewide resource information, with particular attention to availability, eligibility, waitlists, and access barriers in rural Missouri communities.
  • Coordinate closely with all appropriate members of the Maternal Health Access Project team, including but not limited to MHAP Cardiometabolic Program Lead, Nurse Health Educator, clinical consultants, Resource and Referral team. Develop strong relationships with external partners.
  • Document contacts, referrals, outcomes, and follow-up activities in program data systems and support reporting, quality-improvement, and evaluation activities.
  • Participate in outreach, education, team meetings, and continuous improvement of referral workflows and resource tools.
  • Protect confidential information and follow university, program, and applicable regulatory requirements.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Shift

Primarily 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m., Monday–Friday.

This position requires some after-hours and weekend shifts to provide full coverage for our resource access hotline. Hours may shift on a weekly basis.

Minimum Qualifications

Master's degree in psychology, counseling, marriage and family therapy, or social work and relevant licensure (or eligible to be licensed within 12 months) within the State of Missouri.

Preferred Qualifications

Education and experience: Experience in cardiometabolic and/or maternal health, particularly hypertension and diabetes management. Three years of related work experience is preferred.

Credentials: Current Missouri RN or LPN license.

Knowledge and skills: Familiarity with Missouri health and social-service systems, especially rural resources; experience with resource navigation, care coordination, telephone-based support, electronic documentation, and interdisciplinary teamwork; strong communication, organization, cultural responsiveness, and problem-solving skills.

title: Facilities Technician Level 1
description:
About The Role:

Working Pattern: This is a varied shift role comprising a mixture of early shifts 7am - 6pm or late shifts 10am - 9pm to cover park and hotel operations. The shifts cover park operations seven days a week.

The Facilities Maintenance Technician Level 1, is an entry level role. The team member would ideally have knowledge & skills that are relevant to the tasks. They may have qualifications or just have valuable experience in a maintenance
environment.

All Technician roles exist to ensure that safe and efficient park and hotels operation. They have complete hands-on role in the department which directly affects guest satisfaction with their actions, in terms of quality, safety and efficiency. The Facilities Maintenance Technician carries out all building maintenance related work around the resort including its two hotels, Adventure Golf and New Woodland Village. This will include reactive works, planned preventative maintenance, project work and modifications to existing installations. They will carry out a multitude of tasks including daily checks of play structures and uses their own initiative when problem solving.

Main Responsibilities:
  • The primarily responsibility of the role is to ensure that the safest possible environment exists for themselves, the team, contractors, visitors, and guests in the park. The job holder is responsible for ensuring any tools or machinery used around the park are always kept safe and in sight, with the honest belief that "nothing is safe enough".
  • The Facilities Maintenance Technician Level 1 will generally be paired up with a higher-level Technician while they are learning the role, they will be there to assist and learn the different aspects of the business.
  • Responding to reactive maintenance situations and carrying out the required corrective action. This can be in several
    situations such as, unit failure, building works, plumbing, catering equipment, electrical failures etc. They will carry out PPM’s (Planned Preventative Maintenance) this will be Weekly/Monthly/Annually duties but not limited to Q-Line checks, softener checking, meter readings, filter cleans, hotel room checks and furniture checks.
  • The technician will also be trained to carry out daily inspections on all play areas making sure they are safe for daily use.

    Skills, Experience & Qualifications:
  • Full right to work in the UK
  • Must hold a valid driving licence
  • A part of the job holder duties are to ensure that all paperwork is completed correctly, as a lot of building maintenance related documents are statutory requirements.
  • The main part of the role is using the asset management system (Infor) in which Departments or individuals ask for work to be completed, the work gets planned in by the Facilities Managers and then given to the Technician, with a time for completion.
  • The candidate would ideally prioritize and plan their own work, once they have some experience of working on site as certain time scales must be achieved.
  • As a Level 1, Knowledge of a Facilities Maintenance or Construction environment would be an advantage but not essential.
  • As this is an entry level role there would be opportunities to gain experience, knowledge and Qualifications when appropriate, including a trade apprenticeship if correct requirements are met.
